_rec.program: Master Programme Postdigital Lutherie
_rec.university: Kunstuniversität Linz (University of Art and Design Linz), in cooperation with Anton Bruckner Privatuniversität
_rec.degree: Master — four-semester international master programme (exact degree abbreviation not stated on the official pages; UNVERIFIED)
_rec.institutionType: Public art university (jointly with a private music university)
_rec.focus: Electronic Music / Live Electronics + Sound Design (postdigital musical-instrument design and performance)
_rec.language: CONFIRMED English. "Postdigital Lutherie is a four-semester english language master programme". Admission page, both language versions: "German skills are not required to join the programme. Our faculty can support German, Englisch and Spanish speaking students."
_rec.durationEcts: CONFIRMED 4 semesters (2 years). ECTS NOT PUBLISHED on either the English or German official page — UNVERIFIED (Austrian masters are normally 120).
_rec.whatYouStudy: "Postdigital Musical Instruments on the intersections between Design & Technology, Composition & Performance as well as Art- & Media-Theories." Students reconnect acoustic, electronic and digital approaches to instrument design in tangible sonic artefacts for musical expression — building controllers, interfaces and instruments and then composing/performing with them. Hosted by the Tangible Interaction Design department (tamlab); Anton Bruckner Privatuniversität is the cooperation partner and its composition students may take Lutherie courses as electives.
_rec.entryRequirements: CONFIRMED, verbatim: "To study at Postdigital Lutherie you need a valid bachelor (or equivalent) degree to qualify for the admission to this master programme." No field restriction, no German requirement. For online registration you must provide a copy of your degree, a motivation letter, your CV and a portfolio of your works.
_rec.portfolioSpec: "a portfolio of your works" — that is the entire published specification. No number of works, no duration, no file format, no size limit is stated on either the English or German admission page. UNVERIFIED at that level of detail; contact Univ.-Prof. Dr. Martin Kaltenbrunner (martin.kaltenbrunner@kunstuni-linz.at), who runs the registration procedure.
_rec.auditionSpec: An entrance examination in the form of an interview ("Vorstellungsgespräch") built around the submitted portfolio, plus "Materials needed for the interview". Whether attendance in Linz is required is NOT stated (UNVERIFIED); the exam being scheduled for a single fixed day (29 June 2026 for the 26/27 intake) implies on-site attendance. No musical performance audition is mentioned.
_rec.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED for the 2027/28 cycle — the page only ever shows the currently open window.
_rec.deadline: Published on the official page for the 26/27 intake: "The application window for the next academic year 26/27 is now open until June 19, 2026. The entrance exams will take place on June 29, 2026." PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Note this is a JUNE deadline, far later than the usual Oct–Feb window, so the 2027/28 dates will likely not appear until spring 2027.
_rec.tuitionIntl: CONFIRMED, verbatim: "For EU-citizens the programme is generally free of charge, non-EU-citizens currently have to pay a fee of 726,72 € per semester." (Plus the standard ÖH fee, which the page does not itemise.)
_rec.scholarship: CONFIRMED that "Students can apply to university fee reduction funds" (Studienbeitragsermäßigung). No amounts, eligibility criteria or named external scholarship are published — UNVERIFIED. No stipend of any kind is mentioned.
_rec.fundingLevel: Partial (very low fee; fee-reduction funds may apply)
_rec.facilities: tamlab (Tangible Interaction Design laboratory) at the Media Institute; cooperation with Anton Bruckner Privatuniversität's composition/computer-music department and its electronic-music production and presentation spaces. Linz hosts Ars Electronica and Kunstuni Linz work is regularly presented there. Specific studio inventory not published (UNVERIFIED).
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: Yes — best-in-batch on this point, confirmed verbatim in both language versions: only "a valid bachelor (or equivalent) degree" is required. No music degree, no conservatory training, no German. The subject matter (building instruments, code, interfaces, interaction design) directly rewards a software-engineering background.
_rec.fitNotes: The most realistically enterable, genuinely hands-on, English-taught, near-free option in this batch for a CS/SE graduate with no conservatory record: any bachelor qualifies, no German, €726.72 a semester, and the work itself is building instruments and performing with them. Two caveats: the portfolio specification is not published at all, so he must email Kaltenbrunner early to find out what is actually expected; and it is instrument-design and performance research, not a DJ/producer or mixing-and-mastering course. He must also watch the unusual June deadline rather than assuming an Oct–Feb window.
_rec.verificationNotes: Both the English master-programme page and the English and German admission pages were fetched and read in full. Confirmed verbatim: English-language four-semester master; "a valid bachelor (or equivalent) degree"; "German skills are not required"; non-EU fee €726.72 per semester; fee-reduction funds; required documents = degree copy, motivation letter, CV, portfolio; application window for 26/27 open until 19 June 2026 with entrance exams 29 June 2026. Could NOT be verified anywhere on the official site: total ECTS, the formal degree abbreviation, the portfolio specification in any detail, and whether the interview is on-site or remote. sourceUrl switched from the master-programme page to the admission page because that is where the load-bearing facts (entry requirement, fee, language, documents) are actually published.

_rec.program: Elektronika a komunikace / Electronics and Communications (EK), navazující magisterský program — specializace Audiovizuální technika a zpracování signálů / Audiovisual Technology and Signal Processing
_rec.institution: České vysoké učení technické v Praze (ČVUT) / Czech Technical University in Prague, Fakulta elektrotechnická (FEL / FEE)
_rec.publicPrivate: PUBLIC — CONFIRMED. Veřejná vysoká škola under Act No. 111/1998 Sb.; admission conditions issued as a dean's decree under that Act and the CTU Statute.
_rec.language: TWO PARALLEL TRACKS — NOW FULLY CONFIRMED, not merely inferred. The Czech-taught track (free) and the English-taught track (fee-paying) both exist, and 'Electronics and Communications' appears by name on FEL's official list of study programmes conducted in English. Critically, the English programme site en.ek.fel.cvut.cz lists all SEVEN specializations of the English master's and Audiovisual Technology and Signal Processing IS among them (the other six: Electronics, Photonics, Technology of the Internet of Things, Communication Networks and Internet, Mobile Communications, Radio Systems). The previous record's caveat 'confirm before applying which track carries the specialization' can be closed: it is available in English.
_rec.languageRequirement: CORRECTED — THERE IS A PUBLISHED BAND, contrary to the previous record's claim that 'no named IELTS/TOEFL band is set, the committee judges it'. FEL's official admission-procedure page names acceptable proof of English proficiency as TOEFL iBT 70 / IELTS 6 / TOEIC 800. He should plan for IELTS Academic 6.0 as a firm target, not treat the requirement as discretionary. For the Czech track: Czech, with the entrance examination in Czech.
_rec.qualification: Ing. (inženýr) — real, state-recognised second-cycle engineering degree. CONFIRMED.
_rec.accreditationStatus: Nationally accredited public university programme (NAÚ). Supports a Czech long-term residence permit for study. CONFIRMED.
_rec.durationEcts: 120 ECTS minimum; standard 2 years / 4 semesters, full-time. Study plan 'Elektronika a komunikace — Audiovizuální technika a zpracování signálů'. CONFIRMED.
_rec.focus: Engineering of audiovisual signals — acoustics, sound and image technology, signal processing — organised around the human perceiver. NOT a creative sound-design or music-production degree. CONFIRMED.
_rec.whatYouStudy: Sensing, processing and reproduction of audiovisual signals; practical acoustic design and measurement; image and sound technology; modern methods of processing, compression and reconstruction of image, sound and other signals; explicit orientation toward 'člověk jako příjemce audiovizuální informace' (the human as recipient of audiovisual information). Graduates go into television and radio operations, AV and acoustics design, automotive, and biomedical applications. English-language description: 'Get theoretical background and practical skills in acquisition, processing and reproduction of audiovisual signals. Audio, image, video…'
_rec.entryRequirements: A completed bachelor's degree, evidenced before enrolment. For the English track the entrance examination is an ONLINE INTERVIEW plus an optional committee-set test. Required documents: transcript of results, English certificate (if not a native speaker), and a MOTIVATION LETTER; documents not in Czech, Slovak or English need certified translation. Nostrification of the foreign qualification must be completed by end of October of the first semester — i.e. AFTER arrival, which materially lowers the barrier at application time. Programme guarantor for the specialization: prof. Petr Páta (pata@fel.cvut.cz); programme responsible: prof. Stanislav Zvánovec.
_rec.portfolioSpec: NONE. No portfolio, no creative dossier, no artistic assessment. Applicants are merely 'recommended' to submit evidence of significant achievements in electrical engineering, informatics, mathematics or physics — which a software-engineering graduate supplies directly from his degree and projects. CONFIRMED.
_rec.auditionSpec: None. No audition, no musical assessment of any kind. CONFIRMED.
_rec.equipmentRequired: None.
_rec.facilities: FEL acoustics and audiovisual-technology laboratories at ČVUT Prague; measurement and signal-processing infrastructure rather than creative studios.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: YES — EMPHATICALLY, and confirmed. This is an electrical-engineering faculty programme that actively prefers applicants from electronics, informatics, mathematics or physics. A BSc in Software Engineering is the expected feeder profile. Of the six programmes reviewed, this is the only one where his existing degree is an asset rather than a liability.
_rec.englishTest: CORRECTED. TOEFL iBT 70 / IELTS 6 / TOEIC 800, named on FEL's official admission-procedure page. The previous record's 'no fixed band' framing was wrong and would have led him to under-prepare. IELTS 6.0 is well within reach for someone at working-English level, so this is a soft gate, but it is a real one.
_rec.tuitionEU: 0 CZK for the Czech-taught track (all nationalities). For the English-taught track EU citizens pay the same fee as everyone else.
_rec.tuitionNonEU: CZECH-TAUGHT TRACK: 0 CZK for a Tunisian national — tuition-free status attaches to the language of instruction, not citizenship. ENGLISH-TAUGHT TRACK: CORRECTED FROM 'UNPUBLISHED / TREAT AS UNCONFIRMED' TO CONFIRMED. FEL's official tuition-fees page states master's programmes cost 132 000 CZK per academic year (66 000 CZK per semester), ~5,280 EUR/year, ~10,560 EUR over the two-year degree. The faculty reserves the right to adjust each semester, so re-check for 2027/2028, but the figure is now on the record from the primary source rather than a secondary summary.
_rec.otherFees: Application fee 950 CZK per programme AND per specialization — two specializations cost 1,900 CZK. Payment must be made the same day the application is filed; the application enters the procedure only once the fee is paid. Prague living costs ~20,000-28,000 CZK/month, the highest of the six.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: Czech track: ~500,000-670,000 CZK (~20,000-27,000 EUR) over two years, all living costs. English track: add 264,000 CZK tuition (~10,560 EUR), so ~30,000-37,500 EUR total.
_rec.scholarships: The faculty states high-performing international students may be eligible for scholarships, with no amounts or eligibility rules published. UNVERIFIED — ask the FEL international office whether any entry scholarship is open to a first-year non-EU master's student.
_rec.intakes: Main intake for the following academic year, plus an extraordinary second round (mimořádný termín) that FEL has run in consecutive years — a genuine second chance, but requiring a brand-new application even if one was already filed that year.
_rec.applicationOpens: Autumn preceding the academic year; the dean's decree for the 2026/2027 cycle was issued 19 November 2025.
_rec.deadline: CORRECTED. The previous record gave 31 March as the English-track deadline. FEL's official admission-procedure page states that for the 2026/2027 academic year the deadline for submitting applications is 13 AUGUST 2026. The 31 March date appears to relate to the Czech-taught round (with entrance examination 5 June 2026). PRIOR CYCLE — for a SEPTEMBER 2027 start, diarise a Czech-track deadline around 31 March 2027 and an English-track deadline around mid-August 2027, and confirm both against the dean's decree when it is issued in November 2026.
_rec.visaEligible: Yes — accredited public university, full-time Ing. programme, supports a Czech long-term residence permit for study. Note the nostrification requirement lands after arrival (by end of October of semester one), so he must gather diploma, transcripts and legalisations BEFORE leaving Tunisia — the faculty explicitly warns applicants to obtain all documents before travelling.
_rec.recommendation: TOP PICK, AND THE RE-CHECK STRENGTHENED IT. Three of the four open questions in the previous record are now closed from primary sources: (1) the English-taught track definitively carries the Audiovisual Technology and Signal Processing specialization — it is one of seven listed on the official English programme site, and Electronics and Communications appears by name on FEL's list of programmes conducted in English; (2) the English-track fee is 132 000 CZK per year / 66 000 CZK per semester, published on the faculty's own tuition page, roughly 10,560 EUR for the whole degree; (3) the English requirement is TOEFL iBT 70 / IELTS 6 / TOEIC 800, not an unbounded committee judgement — so he must actually sit a test, but a 6.0 is comfortably reachable. One correction against him: the English-track deadline is mid-August, not 31 March, which is a different diary entry than previously recorded. Everything that made this the best fit still holds: no portfolio, no audition, no music degree, no conservatory training, an online interview plus a motivation letter, and his BSc Software Engineering as the preferred feeder. It is not a DJ or music-production degree — it is audiovisual signal engineering — but it is credible, affordable, visa-supporting, and puts him inside a Prague audio ecosystem where the production career can be built alongside. Three actions: (1) sit IELTS Academic targeting 6.5 for headroom; (2) e-mail pata@fel.cvut.cz to confirm the specialization runs in English for 2027/2028 and ask about entry scholarships; (3) start Czech from zero anyway, because the Czech track costs nothing.

Programme / scheme: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master DIGICREA — Digital Creativity, Art & Science (SOUND-MUSIC specialization path)

_rec.program: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master DIGICREA — Digital Creativity, Art & Science (SOUND-MUSIC specialization path)
_rec.university: Consortium coordinated by Université Jean Monnet Saint-Étienne (France), with Universidade Católica Portuguesa Porto (Portugal) and University of Silesia Katowice/Cieszyn (Poland)
_rec.degree: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master (EMJM) — multiple degrees from the three consortium universities
_rec.durationEcts: 2 years / 4 semesters, ending with an internship. Total ECTS not stated on the official pages read (EMJM standard is 120) — CONFIRMED duration, ECTS figure UNVERIFIED.
_rec.focus: Electronic Music / Music Production + Sound Design + digital creation. A dedicated SOUND-MUSIC specialization path exists, distinct from the IMAGE path; candidates apply to one only.
_rec.institutionType: Public university consortium, Erasmus Mundus Joint Master co-funded by the EU
_rec.language: English — the entire programme is taught in English. Certified English test required: minimum B2, C1 recommended (IELTS 6, TOEFL iBT 90+, TOEFL ITP 550, TOEIC 650+; or a university letter confirming a 100% English-taught degree).
_rec.whatYouStudy: Audiovisual new media, emerging technologies in the film industry, music, graphic design, artificial intelligence, virtual/extended reality and their applications. Two specialization paths (SOUND-MUSIC and IMAGE); the Selection Board assesses 'predispositions for professions related to the production of audio-visual and musical forms, including the production of Extended Reality films'. Mobility Saint-Étienne to Porto to Katowice, then an internship with public and private partners. The Saint-Étienne semester shares teaching with the UJM CCNT/RIM programme, which provides a music studio, video studio and multimedia prototyping studio. Detailed module-by-module list is not published — UNVERIFIED.
_rec.entryRequirements: CONFIRMED: 'A Bachelor's degree of at least 180 ECTS is the minimum requirement to enrol', with NO field restriction stated anywhere on the official pages. Candidates holding at least 150 ECTS at application may apply with a sworn statement that 180 ECTS will be completed before the programme starts. Documents: Europass CV in English; ID/passport; certified copies (with certified English translations) of higher-education and high-school diplomas and complete transcripts showing courses, grades, ECTS and final marks; at least two letters of recommendation in English on official letterhead with referee contacts; a 'Science qualification and experience in New Technology' self-assessment form covering level in mathematics, digital signal processing and computer science, and skills in JavaScript, Python or C, HTML, real-time graphics programming, geometry, trigonometry and algebra; certified English test at B2 minimum (C1 recommended); signed application notice. Applications go through the UJM eCandidat portal, explicitly NOT through Études en France.
_rec.portfolioSpec: CONFIRMED and exact: an Artistic or Professional Portfolio presenting productions related to the chosen specialization path. 'All projects included in the portfolio must not be more than 5 years old.' Submit EXACTLY 3 to 5 works or projects (video/audio/images) with metadata — title, short description, public link, and the applicant's role — numbered 1 to 5. For Sound-Music applicants this may be a composition project (orchestral or electronic), a sound design project, a sound concept project, a music piece cycle, a demo, etc. The PDF is capped at 5 MB, so media is supplied via online links. ALSO required in place of a cover letter: a VIDEO PRESENTATION of maximum 2 minutes covering, in order, current situation, motivation for applying, understanding of the programme, why the candidate can succeed, and ideas for applied research and professional development; the link is supplied in a PDF in the 'Motivation letter' field and must stay accessible to the selection board through mid-April.
_rec.auditionSpec: No live audition and no on-site test. Stage I is document review only. Stage II, for shortlisted applicants only, is an ONLINE 15-minute interview (2026 cycle: 24-30 March 2026) assessing personality characteristics, way of thinking, personal life experience and character attributes. Candidates may additionally be asked to join a videoconference to verify English level. No travel is required at any point in the selection.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: YES — the strongest and clearest case among all six programmes. The only academic requirement published is 'A Bachelor's degree of at least 180 ECTS', with no field restriction. The application actively rewards a software background: a compulsory form asks candidates to self-assess their level in mathematics, digital signal processing and computer science, and specifically in JavaScript, Python or C, HTML, real-time graphics programming, geometry, trigonometric functions and algebra. A software-engineering graduate with a music portfolio is close to the ideal applicant profile.
_rec.applicationOpens: 2027 CYCLE, CONFIRMED ON THE OFFICIAL PAGE: 'The call for applications for the next DIGICREA cohort 2027-2029 is expected to open in November 2026. Further information regarding this procedure will be available in the autumn. Please note that some requirements will differ from those of the 2026 selection process.'
_rec.deadline: 2027-2029 deadline NOT YET PUBLISHED — expected around mid-February 2027, to be confirmed from November 2026. PRIOR CYCLE reference (confirmed on the official page): the 2026-2028 call opened 14 November 2025 and closed 16 February 2026, with Stage II online interviews 24-30 March 2026.
_rec.tuitionIntl: ZERO. Confirmed verbatim on the official financial-aid page: 'Students (scholarship holders and non-scholarship holders) are not charged any tuition fees.' Selected self-funded applicants must supply a 'Guarantee of full financial support' with a budget simulation before enrolment, and document income for the visa.
_rec.fundingLevel: Full — for EMJM scholarship holders this is a genuinely fully funded option, the only one among the six.
_rec.scholarship: CONFIRMED: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master (EMJM) scholarship — €1,400 per month for a total duration of 24 months, maximum €33,600 per student, covering travel, visa, installation and subsistence, paid to the student. A limited number are awarded per cohort. The scholarship application is included within the programme application itself, so there is no separate form. Non-scholarship holders may add Erasmus+ KA131/KA171 mobility funds. Additional support exists for students with long-term physical, mental, intellectual or sensory impairments. Tunisian nationality is no barrier — EMJM scholarships are explicitly open to non-EU applicants.
_rec.stipend: €1,400/month for 24 months (€33,600 total) plus zero tuition, for scholarship holders.
_rec.facilities: Three-country mobility with a digital-creation environment at each site. At Saint-Étienne the shared CCNT/RIM teaching gives access to a music studio, video studio, multimedia prototyping studio, sensors, interfaces and sound capture/diffusion equipment. Professionals involved in the shared Saint-Étienne teaching include a sound designer at Ubisoft, a developer at Ableton (Berlin) and Cycling'74, the sound engineer running the studios at Le FIL Saint-Étienne, and researchers from INRIA and GRAME Lyon. Porto and Katowice facility inventories UNVERIFIED.
_rec.fitNotes: The standout recommendation and the only programme here that clears every one of his constraints at once: zero tuition, €1,400/month for two years, taught in English (so IELTS/TOEFL rather than a French DALF C1), a bachelor in ANY field accepted, a Sound-Music specialization, an application form that explicitly credits his programming skills, and a fully remote selection (one 15-minute online interview). The 2027-2029 call is expected to open November 2026 — precisely his window. Two concrete tasks now: build a portfolio of exactly 3-5 numbered works with public links and metadata (a composition, a sound-design project, a demo, a music cycle), and book an English test at B2 minimum, C1 preferred. Caveats: the curriculum is broad digital creativity — AI, XR, graphic design — rather than a dedicated club-music production course, and EMJM scholarships are highly competitive with only a limited number per cohort.
_rec.verificationNotes: Confirmed directly on the official DIGICREA site across three pages: /en/join-digicrea.html, /en/join-digicrea/how-to-apply.html and /en/join-digicrea/financial-aid.html. Confirmed: programme exists and is master level; three-country mobility; English-only instruction; the 180-ECTS bachelor requirement with no field restriction; the exact 3-to-5-work portfolio rule with the 5-year recency limit and 5 MB PDF cap; the 2-minute video presentation replacing the cover letter; the science/technology self-assessment form naming JavaScript, Python/C, HTML; English test thresholds; the two-stage selection with an online 15-minute interview only; zero tuition verbatim; the €1,400/month, 24-month, €33,600 EMJM scholarship; eCandidat as the platform and the explicit exclusion of Études en France; and the November 2026 expected opening of the 2027-2029 call. NOT confirmed: total ECTS figure (not published), the module-by-module curriculum, the number of scholarships per cohort ('a limited number'), and the exact 2027 deadline (not yet set).

_rec.program: DIGICREA — Erasmus Mundus Joint Master "Digital Creativity, Art & Science" (Sound-Music specialisation)
_rec.university: Consortium: Université Jean Monnet Saint-Étienne (FR, coordinator) + Universidade Católica Portuguesa – School of Arts, Porto (PT) + University of Silesia in Katowice (PL)
_rec.degree: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master's degree (multiple/joint award), 2nd cycle
_rec.focus: Music Production · Sound Design · Electronic Music · Immersive/XR Audio · Film/Game Sound
_rec.durationEcts: 2 years / 120 ECTS
_rec.language: English (100%); language courses in French/Portuguese/Polish included in the fee)
_rec.institutionType: Public university (FR) + private Catholic university school of arts (PT) + public university (PL)
_rec.whatYouStudy: Two entry specialisations — Sound-Music, or Image-New Media — inside a shared curriculum at the intersection of art, technology and science: music and sound design, interactive arts, film production, video game development, extended reality (XR), artificial intelligence in the arts, audiovisual new media. Hands-on studio and lab work with industry collaborations and interdisciplinary team projects across the three campuses.
_rec.entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree of at least 180 ECTS (candidates holding 150 ECTS at application may be admitted with a sworn statement undertaking to complete 180 ECTS). English B2 minimum, C1 recommended — evidence accepted: IELTS 6, TOEFL iBT 90+, TOEIC 650+, a degree taught 100% in English, or in exceptional cases a teacher attestation/sworn statement. Two letters of recommendation.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: Yes — no bachelor field is mandated. The stated candidate profile is an "artist/creator in the Sound-Music or Image-New media field WITH scientific knowledge and skills in maths and computer science", and applicants must show "predispositions for professions related to the production of audio-visual and musical forms". A software-engineering BSc is an asset here rather than a handicap; the missing half is documented creative sound work.
_rec.portfolioSpec: Compulsory. "Exactly 3 to 5 specific works or projects" (video/audio/images), each with metadata: title, short description, public link, and the applicant's role. All works must be no more than 5 years old. For the Sound-Music specialisation the accepted work types are compositions, sound design, music pieces and demos. Candidates whose portfolio does not match the guidelines are discarded.
_rec.auditionSpec: No live audition, no on-site test. Shortlisted candidates sit an ONLINE 15-minute interview assessing personality, thinking patterns and character.
_rec.tuitionIntl: ZERO. "Students (scholarship holders and non-scholarship holders) are not charged any tuition fees." (Ignore the EUR 17,000 non-EU figure that appears on the site's tuition page — that text belongs to the university's other EMJM, DYCLAM+; the DIGICREA financial-aid page states no tuition is charged.)

The university's 'Proof of Language Skills' PDF (linked from the central admission page) lists Interface Cultures under: 'The admission boards of the following artistic Master's programmes confirm the required language skills (ENGLISH) as part of the entrance exam.' English is the programme language; German is never required at any point of this degree.
_rec.languageRequirement: MAJOR CORRECTION — NO IELTS/TOEFL IS REQUIRED, AT ANY STAGE. Two official statements settle this. (1) The 'Dates entrance examination 2026' PDF: 'Language certificates for international applicants are not required for the entrance exam.' (2) The 'Proof of Language Skills' PDF: for Interface Cultures (and Postdigital Lutherie) 'the admission boards confirm the required language skills (English) as part of the entrance exam' — i.e. the panel judges his English in the interview and no certificate is filed. Contrast this with every other Kunstuni Linz master, all of which are listed in that PDF as needing a German B1 or English B2 CERTIFICATE. Interface Cultures is a named exception. The previous record marked this UNVERIFIED; it is now verified and it is the single strongest thing about this programme for him, because he has not sat IELTS or TOEFL.
_rec.entryRequirements: 'To study at Interface Cultures you need a valid bachelor (or equivalent) degree.' The official dates PDF states the enrolment prerequisite for all master's programmes as: 'Master's Degree: a Bachelor's degree or another equivalent certificate' — no subject restriction whatsoever. Plus the departmental entrance exam (portfolio submission + interview). Foreign degrees may need legalisation (see the university's 'Legalization of Foreign Documents in Higher Education' PDF) — a Tunisian BSc will need this, and it takes weeks, so start early. No music degree, no conservatory training, no art degree required.
_rec.portfolioSpec: Digital portfolio of own works + letter of motivation + CV + copy of degree, uploaded during online registration at calls.kunstuni-linz.at. The official dates PDF: 'The portfolio must be submitted in digital form. You can find further information on work samples, written examinations and interviews listed by study programme on our homepage and when you are signing up for the exam.' Exact file/format limits are published only inside the live call — UNVERIFIED until a call opens; ask interfacecultures@kunstuni-linz.at.
_rec.auditionSpec: No musical audition. A departmental entrance exam consisting of portfolio review and an admission interview (English), held in the department. The sibling programmes run ~30-minute interviews including a 10-minute presentation of selected work samples; international applicants may request Webex participation instead of travelling. CONFIRM Webex availability for Interface Cultures in writing — it removes the visa-to-attend-the-exam problem entirely and is worth more to him than any other single concession.
_rec.equipmentRequired: None stated. Department provides shared kit.
_rec.facilities: Two dedicated computer rooms, a production workshop, a rapid-prototyping lab (3D printers, soldering stations, laser cutters), and shared equipment including MIDI controllers, cameras, speakers, projectors and VR headsets. No published professional studio, control room or spatial-audio rig. UNCHANGED and still the main substantive weakness for an audio-focused applicant.
_rec.intakes: Winter semester (September/October) start. But note there are TWO entrance-exam rounds feeding it (below).
_rec.applicationOpens: MAJOR CORRECTION — there are TWO opening dates per year, not one. Per the official 'Dates entrance examination 2026' PDF (document dated 15.07.2026): summer round opens 18 March; autumn round opens 01 August. For a September 2027 start expect roughly 18 March 2027 and 01 August 2027.
_rec.deadline: MAJOR CORRECTION — the previous record said 'spring deadline only, UNVERIFIED'. Both rounds are now verified from the official PDF. SUMMER ROUND: online registration + portfolio 18 March – 09 June 2026, entrance exam 30 June – 01 July 2026. AUTUMN ROUND: online registration + portfolio 01 – 25 August 2026, entrance exam 15 September 2026. Both feed academic year 2026/27. PLANNING CONSEQUENCE FOR HIM: for a September 2027 start his two shots are approximately 18 March – 09 June 2027 (exam late June/early July) and 01 – 25 August 2027 (exam mid-September). Neither falls in the October–February window he has assumed — but the August round is a genuine second chance in the same cycle, which almost no directory records. Also worth stating plainly: the autumn 2026 round (registration 01–25 August 2026, exam 15 September 2026) is OPEN AS OF TODAY, 7 August 2026. He has no portfolio, so this is not actionable — but it proves the pattern and he should watch that same page in August 2027.
_rec.tuitionEU: EUR 363.36 per semester statutory rate; EU/EEA and Austrian nationals exempt during the standard duration plus a two-semester grace period.
_rec.tuitionNonEU: EUR 726.72 PER SEMESTER — CONFIRMED on the university's own tuition-fee page ('Euro 726.72 per semester' for international students) and repeated verbatim on the sibling Postdigital Lutherie admission page ('non-EU-citizens currently have to pay a fee of 726,72 € per semester'). This is the rate he pays as a Tunisian national. EUR 1,453.44 per year; EUR 2,906.88 for the whole 4-semester degree. Among the cheapest real master's degrees in Western Europe. Payment must be complete within the admission period — partial payment is not accepted and non-payment means no admission or de-matriculation.
_rec.otherFees: CORRECTION — ÖH student union fee (incl. liability insurance) is EUR 26.20 PER SEMESTER for winter semester 2026/27, not the EUR 24.70 previously recorded. The figure is indexed annually; confirm at enrolment. ADDITION the previous record missed entirely: Austrian student self-insurance (health) runs about EUR 65 per month for students not covered by a parent's policy — roughly EUR 780/year, EUR 1,560 over the degree. This is a bigger line than tuition and it is compulsory in practice for a residence permit.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: Institutional cost over 2 years: tuition EUR 2,906.88 + ÖH EUR 104.80 = EUR 3,011.68. Add health insurance ~EUR 1,560. Realistic institutional + insurance total ~EUR 4,570 for the whole degree. Living costs in Linz are the dominant expense and are not published by the university. For the residence permit he must additionally prove sufficient means to the Magistrat der Stadt Linz or BH Linz-Land (annual ASVG-linked figure — confirm with the Austrian embassy in Tunis / OeAD).
_rec.scholarships: CORRECTION — the previous record said 'none'. There is one real, winnable instrument: the ÖH Kunstuniversität Linz TUITION FEE GRANT (Zuschuss zum Studienbeitrag), administered by the student union's University Representation. It is a pot of just under EUR 15,000 per semester distributed by a jury (chair of the University Representation, economic advisor, social department advisor) as a REFUND of tuition already paid. It is explicitly open to 'regular degree students (Austrian or foreign nationals)' — so a Tunisian master's student qualifies. Announced each semester via calls.kunstuni-linz.at (e.g. 'Tuition Fee Grant SS24'); contact oeh.sozial@kunstuni-linz.at. It will not fund living costs, but it can plausibly zero out the EUR 726.72. SEPARATELY: the university's own 'scholarships' page is entirely OUTGOING mobility funding for Austrians going abroad — nothing there applies to an incoming Tunisian, and the tuition-fee page states the university 'generally does not offer any scholarships'. External route remains OeAD/grants.at; the Ernst Mach Grant is oriented to short research stays, not full masters — still UNVERIFIED as a full-degree route.
_rec.visaEligible: Yes — CONFIRMED, with the exact procedure published. The university's 'Information for international applicants' PDF sets out the visa-required path: (1) apply at the Austrian embassy/consulate for a visa to PARTICIPATE IN THE ADMISSION EXAMINATION; (2) return to Tunisia by the visa expiry; (3) on passing, request the residence permit – student through the Austrian representation, using the confirmation of passing issued by studien.office@kunstuni-linz.at; (4) permit issued by the district authority (Magistrat der Stadt Linz for Linz city). So he may need a visa TWICE — once for the exam, once to study — unless the interview is granted by Webex. Ask for Webex.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: YES — explicitly and without qualification. The official requirement is 'a valid bachelor (or equivalent) degree' / 'a Bachelor's degree or another equivalent certificate'. No subject restriction, no music degree, no art degree, no conservatory training, no audition. A BSc Software Engineering with a strong interactive/sound portfolio is a coherent and even attractive application here.
_rec.recommendation: THE BEST-FITTING AND MOST ATTAINABLE PROGRAMME IN THIS SET — and it is stronger than the previous record concluded, because the language question is now settled in his favour. Confirmed advantages: English-taught with the language judged at interview and NO certificate ever required (he never has to sit IELTS or TOEFL for this one); EUR 726.72/semester with a real ÖH fee-refund fund on top; any bachelor accepted; no audition; a portfolio gate a software engineer can genuinely build in a year; sound art named by the department itself; the Ars Electronica connection. Confirmed limits: it is media art, not music production — it will not train him as a DJ or a record producer, and there is no published pro studio or spatial-audio rig. THREE CORRECTIONS TO HIS PLANNING. (1) There are TWO application rounds a year (≈18 Mar–09 Jun and 01–25 Aug), not one, and neither is in his assumed Oct–Feb window. (2) No English certificate is needed — he can stop worrying about IELTS for this application. (3) Start the Tunisian degree legalisation now; it is slower than the portfolio. ACTIONS: email interfacecultures@kunstuni-linz.at and ask (a) for the exact portfolio spec, (b) whether the admission interview can be held via Webex — this would save him an entire embassy visa run for the exam, and (c) the ECTS figure. ALSO FLAG, because it may be the better programme: the same university runs POSTDIGITAL LUTHERIE (MA) in the Tangible Interaction Design department (Prof. Martin Kaltenbrunner, tamlab). Its official admission page states: 'you need a valid bachelor (or equivalent) degree'; 'German skills are not required to join the programme. Our faculty can support German, English and Spanish speaking students'; same EUR 726.72/semester; same two rounds (18 Mar–19 Jun and 01 Aug–01 Sep in 2026). Postdigital lutherie is the design and building of new digital musical instruments — measurably closer to his stated goal than media art is. He should apply to BOTH in the same cycle; the marginal cost is one extra portfolio submission.

_rec.program: Zeitbasierte Medien / Timebased Media — Master Programme (MA)
_rec.institution: Universität für künstlerische und industrielle Gestaltung Linz (Kunstuniversität Linz / University of Arts Linz)
_rec.institutionType: Public federal art university (Kunstuniversität) under the Austrian Universitätsgesetz 2002
_rec.publicPrivate: PUBLIC — CONFIRMED. Same federal university, same UG 2002 statutory fee schedule, same BMBWF funding. Not a private provider.
_rec.accreditationStatus: CONFIRMED. Ordentliches Masterstudium under UG 2002 awarding a Master of Arts. Supports the §64 NAG student residence permit via the procedure published in the university's 'Information for international applicants' PDF.
_rec.qualification: Master of Arts (MA), 4 semesters. A genuine second-cycle degree.
_rec.focus: Time-based media: video practice and theory, film theory, SOUND, media installation and staging, interactive systems, design with digital media, innovative programming. Sound is a named component — the reason this programme is on the list.
_rec.whatYouStudy: Interdisciplinary work across time-based media — audiovisual culture, moving image, sound, installation, interactive systems and creative coding; professional handling of works and products of audiovisual culture.
_rec.durationEcts: 4 semesters. ECTS not published — UNVERIFIED (Austrian norm 120). Ask gerlinde.schmierer@kunstuni-linz.at.
_rec.language: GERMAN AND ENGLISH. The official registration/admission page states the programme accommodates both, and that admission interviews can be held in English for international applicants on request. Bilingual in practice, not English-only. The language-certificate rule below confirms the programme expects a student to work in one or the other.
_rec.languageRequirement: CORRECTED AND NOW PRECISE — and it is materially worse for him than for Interface Cultures. The official 'Proof of Language Skills' PDF places Timebased Media (MA) in the group requiring 'a German language certificate at level B1 OR an English language certificate at level B2'. Critically: 'The ENGLISH language certificate needs to be submitted AT THE TIME OF ENROLMENT. Otherwise, students need to provide a German language certificate before they can receive the enrolment confirmation for their third semester.' So: no certificate is needed for the entrance exam itself (the dates PDF confirms 'language certificates for international applicants are not required for the entrance exam'), but he MUST hand over an English B2 certificate — i.e. an IELTS/TOEFL or equivalent — when he enrols, or else reach certified German B1 within a year. He has taken neither test. Unlike Interface Cultures, this programme gives him no exemption. Budget for IELTS.
_rec.entryRequirements: 'A completed bachelor degree programme in a study area with interdisciplinary focuses' — the page names time-based/interactive media, media design, film, video, sound, or comparable credentials from accredited institutions. Plus the departmental entrance exam. RISK UNCHANGED AND CONFIRMED: unlike Interface Cultures this programme names related disciplines rather than accepting any bachelor. A Software Engineering BSc rides on the 'comparable' clause and on the portfolio. Get it confirmed in writing before investing. Note also that the central dates PDF states the generic master's prerequisite as simply 'a Bachelor's degree or another equivalent certificate' — so the departmental wording is the binding constraint, not the university's.
_rec.portfolioSpec: Four-step procedure, all published officially: (1) online registration through the university portal; (2) upload of portfolio AND a short letter of motivation explaining personal goals and fit; (3) admission interview with the Selection Committee, approx. 30 minutes, requiring a ten-minute presentation of selected work samples; (4) result by email and PIN. The committee assesses aptitude and how the work aligns with the programme's academic profile. Exact format/size limits not published — UNVERIFIED.
_rec.auditionSpec: No musical audition. A 30-minute selection interview with a 10-minute presentation of work samples. IMPORTANT AND CONFIRMED: 'Interviews occur in-person but international applicants may request Webex participation by notifying gerlinde.schmierer@kunstuni-linz.at.' This removes the need for a separate Austrian visa merely to attend the exam — a concrete, decisive advantage over every Swiss option in this set. Request it in writing at registration.
_rec.equipmentRequired: None stated.
_rec.facilities: Still not published on the programme pages — UNVERIFIED. The department covers video, film, sound, media installation and interactive systems, so post-production facilities exist, but there is no published equipment inventory (studios, monitoring, spatial audio). Ask gerlinde.schmierer@kunstuni-linz.at for a facilities list before applying — for an audio-focused applicant this is the decisive unknown.
_rec.intakes: Winter semester (September/October) start, fed by two entrance-exam rounds.
_rec.applicationOpens: CORRECTED — two openings per year: mid-December and mid-March. For 2026/27 the official dates PDF gives 15 December 2025 (winter round) and 18 March 2026 (summer round). Expect roughly mid-December 2026 and mid-March 2027 for a September 2027 start.
_rec.deadline: MAJOR CORRECTION — the previous record recorded only the spring round and concluded the deadline falls outside his planning window. That is wrong. The official 'Dates entrance examination 2026' PDF (dated 15.07.2026) lists TWO rounds for Timebased Media (MA): WINTER ROUND — online registration and portfolio 15 December 2025 – 18 January 2026, exam 04 February 2026. SUMMER ROUND — online registration and portfolio 18 March – 07 June 2026, exam 30 June – 01 July 2026. There is NO autumn round for this programme (unlike Interface Cultures). PLANNING CONSEQUENCE: the winter round — roughly mid-December 2026 to mid-January 2027, exam early February 2027 — falls squarely INSIDE his October 2026–February 2027 window. This is one of only two programmes in this set that does. He can apply in the winter round and, if unsuccessful, apply again in the summer round of the same cycle.
_rec.tuitionEU: EUR 363.36 per semester statutory rate; EU/EEA nationals exempt for the standard duration plus two semesters.
_rec.tuitionNonEU: EUR 726.72 PER SEMESTER — CONFIRMED on the university's tuition-fee page. EUR 1,453.44/year; EUR 2,906.88 for the full degree. Payment in full within the admission period; partial payment not accepted.
_rec.otherFees: CORRECTION — ÖH fee incl. insurance is EUR 26.20 per semester for WS 2026/27, not EUR 24.70. Indexed annually. ADDITION: Austrian student health self-insurance ~EUR 65/month (~EUR 1,560 over the degree) for students not covered by a parent's policy.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: Institutional: EUR 2,906.88 tuition + EUR 104.80 ÖH = EUR 3,011.68 over 2 years. Plus ~EUR 1,560 health insurance. Plus IELTS/TOEFL exam cost (needed here, unlike Interface Cultures). Plus living costs in Linz and the means-of-subsistence proof for the residence permit.
_rec.scholarships: CORRECTION — same as Interface Cultures: the ÖH Kunstuniversität Linz tuition-fee grant fund (~EUR 15,000/semester pot, refunds tuition already paid, explicitly open to foreign nationals) is a real partial route. Apply via calls.kunstuni-linz.at each semester; contact oeh.sozial@kunstuni-linz.at. No programme-level scholarship; the university's published 'scholarships' page is outgoing-mobility funding for Austrians only and is irrelevant to him. External: OeAD/grants.at, UNVERIFIED for a full master's.
_rec.visaEligible: Yes — §64 NAG standard route. AND the Webex interview option means he may not need a separate visa to attend the entrance exam, only the study permit. That is a genuine cost and timeline saving.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: PARTIALLY — CONFIRMED UNCHANGED. No music degree is needed anywhere, but the named prior fields are media/film/video/sound rather than 'any bachelor'. A CS/software background must be carried by the 'comparable' clause plus the portfolio. Ask the department in writing before applying.
_rec.recommendation: APPLY TO IT ALONGSIDE INTERFACE CULTURES — and the case is now stronger than the previous record allowed, for one reason it got wrong. There is a WINTER round (registration ≈15 December – 18 January, exam early February) as well as the spring round, so this is one of only two programmes in this set whose deadline lands inside his October–February planning window. Advantages: sound is an explicitly named subject; German is never required at entry; the fee is the same EUR 726.72/semester; no audition; the interview can be taken by Webex from Tunis. Disadvantages against Interface Cultures: the bachelor-field requirement is narrower and he must argue 'comparable'; teaching is bilingual rather than English-only; and he WOULD need an English B2 certificate (IELTS/TOEFL) at enrolment, which Interface Cultures waives entirely. No facilities inventory is published — a serious unknown for someone whose goal is production. ACTIONS, all free and all decision-changing: write to gerlinde.schmierer@kunstuni-linz.at asking (a) does a BSc Software Engineering count as 'comparable' for admission, (b) what audio facilities does the department actually have, (c) confirm Webex interview availability, and (d) which English certificates satisfy the B2 requirement. Then sit IELTS in good time — for this programme, unlike Interface Cultures, he cannot avoid it.

Artistic courses, quoted: 'techniques d'écriture, composition sur support, solfège de l'objet sonore, spatialisation, analyse perceptive'. _rec.fitNotes: Better documented than before, and cheaper to fund than previously thought, but the strategic verdict is unchanged. _rec.whatYouStudy: The programme combines theoretical research with mastery of advanced electronic and digital technologies for musical and artistic production. Students choose one option: Réalisateur en Informatique Musicale (RIM) or Arts numériques. Teaching is shared between the Arts plastiques and Musicologie departments — described by the university as unique in France — with contributions from many internationally recognised professionals. Max/MSP appears in module descriptions. Dedicated equipment and production spaces are provided across both years: computers, sensors, interfaces, image-capture, sound-capture and diffusion tools, plus a 'studio musical', a 'studio de prise de vue' and a 'studio de maquettage de dispositifs multimédia'. Placements in both M1 and M2. Named RIM career outcomes include work in music production centres, recording studios, theatre, dance, video games and sound design; the wider list includes designer sonore, professeur de MAO, développeur en informatique musicale, and roles at IRCAM, GRM and Centres Nationaux de Création Musicale.
_rec.entryRequirements: The official university page confirms the entry level is M1 (start of the programme) but does NOT publish the admission criteria — the livret states only 'CONDITIONS D'ADMISSION — Se référer aux portails monmaster ou ecandidat.' The older RIM-specific documentation (for the M2 route) states entry for holders of a 'Master I en musique, en arts numériques, ou équivalents', or any Master 1 with a demonstrated strong level in musical or digital-arts practice, and expects 'une culture scientifique et une expérience en informatique musicale et/ou en programmation dans le champ des arts numériques'; professionals may enter via VAE. Cohort reported at a maximum of 20 students — UNVERIFIED on the current official page. Programme directors: Laurent Pottier (RIM, laurent.pottier@univ-st-etienne.fr) and Vincent Ciciliato (Arts numériques). Faculty ALL: 04 77 42 13 05.
_rec.portfolioSpec: NOT PUBLISHED for M1 entry. For M1 via monmaster the required documents will appear in the mention's 'critères d'examen des candidatures' when the 2027 campaign opens — UNVERIFIED until then. For the M2 RIM route the documented requirement is a dossier from the secretariat or the university site submitted via eCandidat, plus an 'audio commentary' exercise for RIM candidates (an analysis of a musical work) demonstrating artistic/musical competence. He should email laurent.pottier@univ-st-etienne.fr directly to ask what an M1 applicant must submit.
_rec.auditionSpec: No instrumental audition. For the M2 RIM route: an interview with a jury of professionals assessing motivation and career project, plus the audio-commentary exercise. For M1 entry via monmaster the selection method is UNVERIFIED. The only dates ever published for the RIM exam route are from a 2018 cycle (application 31 May, admission exams 8 June) — PRIOR CYCLE, long superseded, do not rely on these.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: CHECK — leaning favourable but not proven for M1. Substantively the profile sought is scientific: the RIM documentation asks for 'une culture scientifique et une expérience en informatique musicale et/ou en programmation dans le champ des arts numériques', and accepts 'des étudiants issus d'autres formations ... pouvant justifier d'un bon niveau en pratique musicale et/ou artistique numérique'. So a computer-science background is welcome in principle. What is NOT published anywhere official is the M1 admission criterion — the university page confirms M1 is an entry point but defers entirely to monmaster. He must confirm with the programme director whether a Tunisian BSc in software engineering with a self-built music portfolio is an acceptable M1 dossier.
_rec.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. M1 applications go through monmaster.gouv.fr on the national calendar, which typically opens in late February; M2 applications go through UJM eCandidat. No 2027 dates are published. Monitor monmaster.gouv.fr from January 2027.
_rec.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. No current deadline is published for this programme. The national monmaster M1 window for the 2026-2027 cycle ran roughly late February to late March 2026; the 2027-2028 window will follow the national calendar published in winter 2026-2027. The only programme-specific dates ever found are from a 2018 cycle and must not be used.
_rec.tuitionIntl: CORRECTED — the earlier claim of a near-automatic reduction to about €255 is no longer safe. UJM publishes the non-EU differentiated master fee for 2026-2027 as €3,950/yr. UJM's conseil d'administration decided on 8 September 2025 to apply an automatic partial exemption from differentiated fees for international-mobility students enrolled in a UJM national master's diploma; however the €255 reduced figure on that page is explicitly tied to students already enrolled at UJM in 2023-2024 continuing in the same programme, not to new entrants. Crucially, décret n° 2026-385 of 19 May 2026 abolished blanket institutional exemptions and caps discretionary exemptions at 30% of affected students in 2026-2027, 25% in 2027-2028 and 20% from 2028 — so a September 2027 entrant faces a 25% cap. Plan for €3,950/yr plus CVEC (~€105) and treat any reduction as a bonus. Confirm the 2027-2028 UJM policy in spring 2027.
_rec.fundingLevel: Partial at best, and now uncertain — no programme stipend, and the fee exemption that previously looked near-automatic is capped and discretionary after décret 2026-385.
_rec.scholarship: No programme-specific scholarship found. Two realistic routes: (1) the EMJM DIGICREA at the SAME university, whose €1,400/month scholarship is the funded alternative — apply to both; (2) France Excellence Eiffel, which is nominated BY the institution, pays €1,181/month at master level and carries an age limit of 25 for master candidates. Eiffel internal institutional deadlines for the 2026-2027 cycle fell in October-December 2025 with the Campus France national deadline in early January 2026, so for a September 2027 start he must contact UJM about Eiffel nomination by roughly October 2026. Campus France Tunisie and French Embassy bourses are the other vehicles. UNVERIFIED whether UJM nominates for Eiffel in the Arts mention.
_rec.facilities: CONFIRMED on the official page: a dedicated music studio, a video/filming studio and a multimedia prototyping studio, plus computers, sensors, interfaces and capture/diffusion tools available across both years. Teaching staff reported to include Pierre Colomies (sound designer, Ubisoft Montpellier), Emmanuel Jourdan (Ableton Berlin and Cycling'74), Christophe Lebreton (LISILOG), Stéphane Letz (GRAME Lyon), Romain Michon (INRIA), Jérémy Lhuillier (head of studios at Le FIL Saint-Étienne), Michele Tadini (CNSMD Lyon) and Michel Pascal (CNRR Nice) — staff list PARTIALLY VERIFIED, drawn from programme documentation rather than the main university page. Regional partners GRAME and AADN Lyon. Opens onto doctoral study.
_rec.fitNotes: Content-wise this is the best match in the whole batch for a programmer who wants to make electronic music: Max/MSP, music computing, sound design for games and live performance, an Ableton developer on the teaching staff, a real music studio, and Ubisoft/GRAME/INRIA connections. The good news from this verification round is that M1 is confirmed as an entry point, so the earlier worry that RIM was M2-only is resolved at programme level. Three live caveats: the M1 admission criteria are simply not published, so he must email Laurent Pottier before committing; instruction is in French, so he needs a DALF/TCF C1-level certificate; and the fee position has worsened — budget €3,950/yr rather than €255. Practical strategy: apply here AND to DIGICREA at the same university in the same season, since a DIGICREA place brings zero tuition plus €33,600.
_rec.verificationNotes: Confirmed on the official UJM programme page: the programme exists at master level, the exact parcours and two options (RIM / Arts numériques), 2-year duration, Saint-Étienne, French as language of instruction, entry level M1 (this CORRECTS the earlier ambiguity that RIM might be M2-only), the three dedicated studios quoted verbatim, the RIM career outcomes, and the two programme directors with contact emails. Separately confirmed via a UJM search that the mention is offered at both M1 and M2. Fees verified on UJM's own 'Droits d'inscription différenciés' page: €3,950 for master 2026-2027, with the €255 figure applying to students already enrolled in 2023-2024. Décret n° 2026-385 of 19 May 2026 verified via Légifrance/Sénat sources: caps exemptions at 30% (2026-27), 25% (2027-28), 20% from 2028, and ends blanket institutional exemptions. NOT confirmed: total ECTS, the 20-student cohort cap, M1 admission criteria and required documents, whether a portfolio or audio commentary is required at M1, the 2027 application dates, the English-taught shared DIGICREA courses (livret only), and the detailed staff list.

_rec.whatYouStudy: Three years covering physical acoustics, sound technologies and practices, and the aesthetics of artistic projects, training students for 'des postes de régie, d'ingénierie ou de création, seul ou en encadrement d'équipe', becoming 'l'interlocuteur privilégié dans son domaine qui guide techniquement et artistiquement la mise en scène'. A Master-level mémoire is written — the prerequisites ask for 'Qualités rédactionnelles (en vue de la rédaction d'un mémoire de niveau Master)'. Cross-disciplinary work with the other nine ENSATT parcours (Jeu, Administration du spectacle vivant, Atelier costume, Conception costume, Conception lumière, Direction technique, Écriture dramatique, Scénographie, Mise en scène) on shared productions. A 'Grille pédagogique 2026-27' is downloadable. NOTE: the programme page carries 'Attention : page de formation en cours de mise à jour' — the detailed module list is UNVERIFIED.
_rec.entryRequirements: CONFIRMED from the official fiche concours. Age: minimum 18 at 1 September of the entry year, 'sans dérogation possible' and, per the concours page, 'sans limite d'âge maximum'. Diplomas: 'Etre titulaires du baccalauréat ou d'une équivalence' AND 'Justifier d'au moins 2 années d'études supérieures et être détenteurs de 120 crédits ECTS … délivrés dans le cadre d'une formation reconnue par l'Etat'. Foreign nationals outside the francophone list must supply their most recent diploma translated into French by a sworn translator (or a plurilingual version) plus DALF C1 or equivalent. 'Aucune demande de dérogation ne sera possible.' Connaissances souhaitées: 'Mathématiques, Physique : niveau minimum requis BAC + 1 scientifique' — published syllabus covers integral calculus, linear ODEs of 1st and 2nd order, complex numbers and De Moivre, log/exp/power functions, Taylor expansions, derivatives, binary arithmetic and 'Notion de programmation algorithmique'; physics covers electricity and electromagnetism (Ohm, Kirchhoff, superposition, Thévenin/Norton, capacitors, Laplace, Faraday, Lenz, impedance/admittance), mechanics, damped and forced oscillators, resonance, bandwidth, Q factor, and travelling/standing waves with interference. Also: writing ability; broad general, literary, contemporary-art (photo, plastic arts, cinema, music) and theatre culture; ability to work collectively; 'Toute expérience vécue en milieu professionnel, au sens large, est souhaitée'. Three recommended books: Daniel Deshays 'Pour une écriture du son'; Larrue & Mervant-Roux 'Le son du théâtre XIXe-XXIe siècle'; Yann Paranthoën 'Propos d'un tailleur de sons'. A candidature-review commission decides who is authorised to compete at all.
_rec.portfolioSpec: CONFIRMED format, but the SUBJECT CHANGES EACH YEAR — the 2027 subject is not yet published. Admissibilité 1 = 'Dossier de recherche : projet de réalisation sonore sur un thème donné'. The 2026 brief was: 'Vous réaliserez, à partir de sons que vous aurez enregistrés vous-même, une courte séquence sans musique ni parole ni texte dont le sujet sera (au choix) : Le portrait sonore d'un espace naturel que vous avez visité (mer, forêt, lac, montagne...) OU Le portrait sonore d'une promenade nocturne que vous avez effectuée' — 'Cette courte séquence devra rester compréhensible par l'auditeur·ice.' Deliverables (stable across years): (1) 'Un document sonore, ne dépassant pas 3 minutes, au format WAV ou AIFF (format compressé refusé). La réalisation sera structurée par la prise de son, le montage et le mixage effectués avec les moyens dont dispose le/la candidat(e), même rudimentaires'; (2) 'Un texte au format PDF justifiant la démarche de réflexion, de conception et de réalisation ne dépassant pas 6 pages dactylographiées de format A4'. Both uploaded via francetransfert.numerique.gouv.fr to concours@ensatt.fr, files named CONCOURS_NOM_INITIALE_NUMERO (e.g. SON_DUPONT_P_55298157). Only dossiers from candidates authorised to compete are examined.
_rec.auditionSpec: CONFIRMED. No music audition. Admissibilité 2, ON SITE at ENSATT Lyon: 'Une épreuve écrite de physique (durée 2h00 ; coefficient 1)' and 'Une épreuve écrite d'analyse de textes et/ou de documents audiovisuels (durée 1h30 ; coefficient 1)'. Admission: 'Un entretien avec le jury portant notamment sur le CV, les motivations du candidat ou de la candidate et les épreuves d'admissibilité (durée : 20 minutes environ)'. 'Nombre de places maximum : 6.'
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: YES — CONFIRMED and unusually favourable. No music, audio or artistic diploma is required: only the baccalauréat plus 2 years of higher education totalling 120 ECTS in a State-recognised formation. The desired knowledge is explicitly scientific at Bac+1 level in maths and physics, and the published maths syllabus even lists 'Arithmétique binaire. Notion de programmation algorithmique.' A software-engineering BSc over-satisfies both the credit requirement and the maths/physics expectation. The genuine filters are the self-recorded 3-minute sound portrait, the theatre/contemporary-art culture expected, the DALF C1, and 6 places.

Entry needs only 120 ECTS plus Bac+1 scientific maths and physics — which his degree covers outright, down to the algorithmic-programming line in the syllabus — fees are €605 a year, the test dates for the September 2027 intake are already published, and the portfolio brief is explicitly forgiving about equipment ('même rudimentaires'), so he can produce it on a laptop. Content mismatch remains: he would emerge an excellent theatre sound designer and live-sound engineer, with electronic-music production as a side benefit rather than the core — and the 3-year, prep-year-first structure means graduating in 2030.

M.Sc. (Universität Bremen): a SINGLE video of no more than 5 minutes demonstrating the breadth of his digital-media work. _rec.recommendation: This record survived verification with ZERO corrections — every figure, date and requirement checked out exactly, which is not true of any other entry here. It is the best-documented and most accessible option of the six for him: English-taught with no German required at all, a 150-ECTS entry bar his BSc clears comfortably, software engineering explicitly named as an acceptable background, EUR 431.40 a semester and nothing more, no audition, and an M.Sc. route whose entire portfolio requirement is a 5-minute video. Three action items, in order: (1) request a medium-of-instruction letter from SMU MedTech immediately and send it to the HfK International Office asking in writing whether it waives the IELTS 7 requirement — this single email could remove his largest obstacle; (2) if it does not, book a diagnostic IELTS now, because Band 7 from 'working English' is a genuine year of work; (3) start building the 5-minute video around sound and music-technology projects so that his portfolio year, his application and his career goal all point the same direction. Apply to both the M.Sc. and M.A. routes if permitted — the M.Sc. video is easier to produce than 10-20 finished works. _rec.accreditationStatus: NOT OFFICIAL — NOT NVAO-ACCREDITED. Verified on the official fees page: the programme 'is registered as short vocational education in the Netherlands' (CRKBO). CRKBO is a VAT-exemption and quality register for short vocational training — it is NOT higher-education accreditation, is NOT NVAO, and gives the diploma no legal status as a Dutch degree and no ECTS. The institution is 'niet-bekostigd' (private/unfunded) and explicitly 'not eligible for NL undergraduate student loans'. No accreditation statement of any kind appears on the course, fees or FAQ pages. In EHEA terms this diploma is unrecognised: it will not admit him to a PhD, will not transfer credit anywhere, and cannot be used for professional recognition.

_rec.visaEligible: NO — EXPLICITLY, IN WRITING, AND THIS IS DECISIVE. The entry-requirements page repeats that non-EU residents must secure their own visa as the institute cannot assist. Abbey Road Institute Amsterdam is NOT an IND recognised sponsor and cannot host a student residence permit — and in the Netherlands only a recognised sponsor can. The FAQ's suggested workarounds are Working Holiday visas for select nationalities and the DAFT visa for US citizens; TUNISIA QUALIFIES FOR NEITHER. For a Tunisian national with no independent Dutch residence route, family connection or separate university registration, this programme is simply unreachable — no amount of money or portfolio strength changes that.
_rec.reputationSignals: POSITIVE: the Abbey Road name is the strongest brand in the industry, with a genuine institutional link to Abbey Road Studios London and Universal Music; located inside Q-Factory, a real working music hub rather than an office block; teaching by industry practitioners with guest lectures from award-winning professionals; unusually generous six-day-a-week studio access; and a real portfolio-based selection process, meaning cohorts are self-selecting and serious. RED FLAGS: (a) NOT NVAO-accredited and not a degree — near-degree money for a private certificate; (b) cannot sponsor a visa, and this is buried in an FAQ rather than stated on the fees or course pages where an international applicant would see it before paying €200; (c) no named teaching staff, no named alumni and no graduate-employment statistics published anywhere; (d) no accreditation statement at all on the course or fees pages; (e) the only 'funding' offered is a tax deduction the institute itself concedes does not apply to the unemployed or newly arrived; (f) the fee pages have a history of going stale (a €16,400 figure from a 2022 update circulated long after it lapsed). No formal published complaints or regulatory actions were found.
_rec.recommendation: OUTSTANDING SCHOOL, WRONG COUNTRY, AND NOT A MASTER — DO NOT APPLY. On pure craft this is the best hands-on music production and sound engineering training in this entire Dutch slice: real studios six days a week, Abbey Road pedigree, industry teaching, a serious portfolio-selected cohort. Three things kill it for him, and the first is fatal on its own. (1) IT CANNOT GET HIM A DUTCH RESIDENCE PERMIT — stated in writing by the institute, and the workarounds it suggests are open to Working Holiday and US DAFT nationals, not Tunisians. (2) It is NOT a master or any accredited degree — no NVAO, no ECTS, no PhD route, no credit transfer. (3) At €18,860–€20,160 tuition plus roughly €16,000 living costs it is among the most expensive options here for the least formal recognition — €33,000–€39,000 for an unaccredited diploma. He also does not currently hold the mandatory 4–8 track portfolio. MY ADVICE: rule Amsterdam out now and spend no application fee on it. If the Abbey Road brand genuinely appeals, look at Abbey Road Institute campuses in countries where a private school CAN sponsor a student visa — but go in understanding he would be buying training, not a qualification, and check that campus's accreditation separately, since it does not transfer across the franchise. THE ONE THING TO TAKE FROM THIS ENTRY REGARDLESS: adopt its portfolio spec — 4–8 finished tracks, each demonstrating a different role (performer, producer, engineer, writer), with his role documented per track — as his personal build target for September 2027 applications anywhere.
