_rec.program: Digital Interactive Arts (Arte digitale interactive), MA
_rec.institution: Universitatea Babeș-Bolyai din Cluj-Napoca (UBB), Facultatea de Teatru și Film — Departamentul de Cinematografie și Media
_rec.publicPrivate: PUBLIC — CONFIRMED. Romania's largest state university, ARACIS-accredited. Verified directly in the UBB Senate Regulation on fees for 2026-2027, which is structured as a Senate decision (abrogating Hotărârea Senatului nr. 13/17.02.2025 at art. 16) — conclusive evidence of state governance.
_rec.institutionType: Comprehensive state university; Faculty of Theatre and Film, Department of Cinematography and Media
_rec.qualification: Diplomă de master — genuine state-recognised second-cycle degree (ciclul II), accredited under the Bologna Process per the official programme page. Supports a non-EU student residence permit via the Ministry of Education Letter of Acceptance.
_rec.accreditationStatus: ARACIS-accredited state university; the programme page states accreditation by the Romanian Ministry of Education under the Bologna Process. Listed among the English-taught master's programmes of the Cinematography and Media department.
_rec.focus: Digital interactive arts / new media. Sound is a single elective, not the spine of the degree.
_rec.whatYouStudy: CONFIRMED AND EXPANDED with the full four-semester curriculum. Semester I: Interactive Digital Performance, Production Management, Creative Performing Arts Project, plus electives in Visual Culture, Performance Theory or Practice as Research. Semester II: Creative Industries, Curatorial Models in Digital Media, Creative Visual Arts Project, plus electives in Augmented Reality or Visual Programming. Semester III: New Media Documentary, Creative Transmedia Project, Management and Marketing for Independent Artists, plus electives in Spectatorship Studies or Visual Storytelling. Semester IV: Academic Ethics, Directed Reading and Dissertation Writing, Digital Technologies in Art, plus electives in Sound Design or Interactive Media. CRITICAL: 'Sound Design for Digital Media' is an elective in SEMESTER IV ONLY — the final semester — and it competes with 'Interactive Media' for the same elective slot. So across a two-year degree he would take at most ONE sound course, in his last six months. The previous entry called sound 'one elective'; that is right, but it understated how late and how marginal it is. Note also 'Visual Programming' (Sem II elective) and 'Augmented Reality' — those play to his coding background more than the sound course does.
_rec.durationEcts: 4 semesters (2 years), full-time. Total ECTS still NOT stated on the official programme page — UNVERIFIED. A Romanian two-year master's is normally 120 ECTS and UBB's fee regulation treats it as a standard masterat, but get this in writing from the faculty.
_rec.language: ENGLISH — CONFIRMED on the official programme page, with the admission interview also 'conducted in English'. IMPORTANT CAVEAT DISCOVERED: the faculty's own tuition page lists Digital Interactive Arts under its Romanian-language programme listing. This is most likely an artefact of the Romanian version of the website rather than a second Romanian-taught cohort, but because the whole case for this programme rests on it being English-taught, he must confirm the teaching language in writing before applying.
_rec.languageRequirement: English. The specific certificate and band remain UNVERIFIED — no English test requirement is stated anywhere on the programme page or in the admission criteria, and UBB's central non-EU degree-student page was unreachable (HTTP 404) at the time of checking. Because he has not taken IELTS or TOEFL, this is his single most urgent question. CORRECTED CONTACT: the programme page names Assistant Professor Cristina Pop-Tiron (cristina.pop-tiron@ubbcluj.ro) as the contact — the previous entry gave constantin.parvulescu@ubbcluj.ro and Prof. Rodica Mocan, which are not the contacts published on the current page. Faculty secretariat: +40 264 590 066 / +40 264 405 357. Confirmed advantage: no Romanian requirement and no preparatory Romanian year, since Romanian rules exempt students on foreign-language programmes.
_rec.entryRequirements: CORRECTED AND IMPROVED — the previous entry said 'no field restriction published', which understated the case. The official page states the programme 'addresses graduate students in visual arts, architecture, music, theater, and film AND GRADUATES FROM OTHER FIELDS interested in a theoretical and practical interdisciplinary approach to new digital technologies in visual, performing, and cinematic arts.' So non-arts graduates are EXPLICITLY invited by name, not merely un-excluded. His BSc Software Engineering is squarely within the published eligibility. Non-EU applicants apply through UBB's Centrul de Cooperări Internaționale with a Ministry of Education Letter of Acceptance.
_rec.auditionSpec: CONFIRMED AND EXPANDED. An ONLINE interview conducted in English — note 'online', which means no travel cost for the entrance exam, a real advantage over UNATC's Romanian-taught programmes. Assessment covers: ability to articulate the concept and relevance of the proposed project; domain knowledge; command of terminology; and general knowledge of cinema and media studies. That last criterion is new and worth flagging — he will be assessed on general cinema and media studies knowledge, an area where a software engineering graduate has no formal grounding and should read deliberately during his portfolio year.
_rec.portfolioSpec: MANDATORY, TWO PARTS — CONFIRMED: (1) an individual artistic project, submitted in writing, demonstrating interest in interactive technologies, and (2) a portfolio of artistic works, either previous work or work related to the proposed project. The application is complete only on confirmed receipt of both. The project may be PROPOSED rather than completed — the interview tests whether he can argue its relevance. For a software engineer this remains among the most reachable portfolio requirements available: a generative music system, a reactive audio-visual installation, an audio plugin or a game-audio prototype all qualify and all build on skills he already has.
_rec.equipmentRequired: Not published — UNVERIFIED. Assume a personal laptop capable of running Max/MSP, TouchDesigner or equivalent.
_rec.facilities: Not published — UNVERIFIED, no inventory available. Direct this question to Cristina Pop-Tiron: what studio, lab and multi-channel audio facilities are actually available to master's students, and is the Sound Design elective taught with hardware or only in software?
_rec.tuitionEU: Romanian/EU fee-paying and budget places per UBB's domestic schedule. Specific figure for this programme UNVERIFIED — see ubbcluj.ro/ro/taxe. Payment terms confirmed on the faculty page: four equal instalments (October, December, March, May), 10% discount for full payment by 15 October, late-payment penalty 0.04% per day.
_rec.tuitionNonEU: €950 PER MONTH — CONFIRMED VERBATIM. I extracted the full text of the UBB Senate fee regulation and located Anexa nr. 4 ('Taxe de şcolarizare în valută ale cetăţenilor care studiază pe cont propriu în România, proveniți din state care nu sunt membre ale Uniunii Europene...'). Row 11 lists the Faculty of Theatre and Film split across two domains: 'domeniul teatru și artele spectacolului' at €750/month and 'domeniul cinematografie şi media' at €950/month, for masterat, învățământ cu frecvență. Digital Interactive Arts sits in the Department of Cinematography and Media, so €950/month is the rate he pays. Art. 15.2(a) confirms fees are payable over 9 months where the curriculum has no distinct practice period, or 10 months where it does. At 9 months that is €8,550/year and €17,100 over two years; at 10 months, €9,500/year and €19,000. The previous entry's figures were correct — but he should confirm in writing whether this curriculum triggers the 10-month rule, a €950/year difference, and separately confirm the domain classification, worth €1,800/year.
_rec.otherFees: €50 non-refundable admission dossier processing fee for non-EU applicants — CONFIRMED VERBATIM at art. 15.1 of the Senate regulation: 'Pentru procesarea dosarului de admitere se va achita o taxă de 50 Euro, indiferent de nivelul de studiu sau forma de învățământ'. Art. 15.2(c) confirms tuition EXCLUDES accommodation and meals, and art. 15.4 confirms any other personal costs including housing, food and transport are the student's own. A separate dissertation defence fee applies per Anexa nr. 6 (amount UNVERIFIED). Add document legalisation, translation, Letter of Acceptance costs and Cluj-Napoca living costs.
_rec.scholarships: The Romanian Government/MFA route (scholarships.studyinromania.gov.ro) is established under Government Decision no. 288/1993 for non-EU citizens and requires a minimum study-years average of 7/10 or 'Good' — CONFIRMED. But the critical catch stands and I could NOT resolve it: the MFA scheme's published rule is that bachelor's and master's beneficiaries study only in Romanian, with only doctoral holders permitted a foreign language, which would exclude an English-taught master's from MFA funding. The scholarship portal's public pages do not state the language rule explicitly, so this must be settled by direct enquiry. This single question decides whether the programme is a €17,100 self-pay or a funded option. ARICE may operate differently — verify separately. NOTE THE ASYMMETRY: the very feature that makes this programme accessible to him (English) may be what disqualifies it from the main Romanian scholarship, whereas UNATC's Romanian-taught programmes are scholarship-eligible but linguistically closed to him.
_rec.intakes: September
_rec.applicationOpens: Application 13-17 July 2026; exam 24 July 2026; final results 30 July 2026 (2026-27 cycle) — CONFIRMED. PRIOR CYCLE. Non-EU applicants must start months earlier for the Letter of Acceptance.
_rec.deadline: 17 July 2026 for the 2026-27 cycle — CONFIRMED. For a September 2027 start expect a mid-July 2027 window, with the Ministry Letter of Acceptance process beginning several months earlier. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new dates.
_rec.visaEligible: Yes. UBB admits non-EU students on the 'cont propriu valutar' basis through its Centrul de Cooperări Internaționale, and Anexa nr. 4 of the Senate regulation exists precisely to price that category — institutional proof the route is live. The Ministry of Education Letter of Acceptance supports the Romanian long-stay study visa and student residence permit. Full-time (învățământ cu frecvență) status is confirmed, which is what the permit requires.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: YES, EXPLICITLY AND BY NAME — this is stronger than the previous entry claimed. The official page names 'graduates from other fields' as an intended audience alongside arts graduates. No music degree, no conservatoire training and no instrumental audition are required. Selection turns on an interactive-technology artistic project, which a software engineering graduate is unusually well placed to produce. Caveat: the interview also assesses general cinema and media studies knowledge, which he must read up on.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: About €17,100 in tuition over two years (€950 × 9 months × 2), or about €19,000 if the 10-month practice rule applies, plus the €50 application fee, plus a dissertation defence fee, plus Cluj-Napoca living costs (UNVERIFIED, no official figure), plus IELTS/TOEFL costs. No preparatory language year needed, saving a full year of time and money relative to every Romanian-taught option.
_rec.recommendation: CONFIRMED ACCURATE ON FEES AND ELIGIBILITY, BUT ITS HEADLINE CLAIM IS FALSE AND ITS RANKING MUST CHANGE. Everything financial checks out verbatim: €950/month for the cinematografie și media domain, 9-10 months a year, €50 dossier fee, all confirmed in Anexa nr. 4 and art. 15 of the UBB Senate regulation. Eligibility is better than previously described — the page explicitly invites 'graduates from other fields', so his BSc is named-in rather than merely not excluded. CORRECTION 1, and it is the important one: the previous entry asserted this is 'the ONLY English-taught programme with meaningful sound content found anywhere in Hungary, Romania or Bulgaria'. That is wrong. UNATC Bucharest runs at least five English-taught master's programmes — Design for New Media, Visual Effects, Audiovisual Preservation and Programming, Interactive Technologies for Performing and Media Arts, and Art of Game Design — all listed in its Senate fee decision at 13,750 lei per year, roughly €2,750, with budget places available. ITPMA in particular is a 120-ECTS English-taught MA that trains students in 'digitally controlling sound, light, image and code for the arts', explicitly welcomes science and engineering graduates, and accepts a 1500-2000 word essay in place of a portfolio. It costs roughly one third of this programme and has MORE sound content, not less. CORRECTION 2: the contact is Cristina Pop-Tiron, not the names previously given. CORRECTION 3: the Sound Design elective falls in semester IV and competes with Interactive Media for the same slot, so he may take at most one sound course, at the very end. Rating B rather than A: it is a legitimate, well-matched, visa-supporting degree with an online English entrance interview and no language-year penalty, but at €17,100 it is expensive for a programme where sound is a single final-semester elective, and its scholarship eligibility is unresolved. Actions in order: (1) apply to UNATC ITPMA as the primary Romanian target and treat this as the parallel application; (2) ask studyinromania.gov.ro in writing whether an English-taught master's can be MFA-funded; (3) ask Cristina Pop-Tiron what English certificate is required, whether the fee domain is cinematografie și media (€950) or teatru (€750), and whether the curriculum triggers 9 or 10 months of fees; (4) spend the portfolio year building ONE strong interactive audio project with proper documentation, which serves both applications.

_rec.visaEligible: NO — and this is confirmed in Point Blank's own Ibiza terms and conditions, which state: 'pointblank Ibiza welcomes students from all over the world. If you are applying from a non-EU country, you may require a student visitor's visa which entitles you to study in Spain. CRITICAL RISK: the same clause continues 'Where an international student has not been successful in securing a visa, the deposit (referred to in Clause 3 below) will not be returnable, though the balance of the course fees will be refunded.' So a Tunisian national who is refused a Schengen visa LOSES the £100 or £200 deposit. A one or two-week course cannot support a Spanish student residence permit under any circumstances.
_rec.focus: DJing on Pioneer DJ equipment and electronic music production in Ableton Live, with opportunities to play out at Ibiza venues. The most directly DJ-career-relevant training found anywhere in this slice — but it is training, not education at any level.
_rec.whatYouStudy: VERIFIED from the course pages. Level 1 (beginners, supported by Pioneer DJ): production fundamentals — making beats with drums, basslines and chords; recording audio into Ableton Live; editing with effects such as compression and reverb; mixing your tracks; plus DJ skills — tempo and cueing, beatmatching, EQing and effects, creative mixing, looping and set preparation. Level 2 is 'designed for those of you who have already mastered the basics (or who have graduated from the Ibiza DJ/Producer Course - Level 1 or similar)' and covers beat matching, looping, harmonic mixing, effects, plus sound design, sidechaining, synthesis, warping, slicing, mixing and mastering. 26 hours of tuition per week, comprising classroom time plus the DJ experiences playing out at venues. Timetable Monday to Friday roughly 10:00-15:00 including a lunch hour (listed as TBC).
_rec.durationEcts: 1 week or 2 weeks. NO ECTS. Five distinct products verified: 1 Week DJ/Producer Level 1, 1 Week DJ/Producer Level 2, 2 Week DJ/Producer Level 1, 2 Week DJ/Producer Level 2, and a standalone 1 Week DJ Skills course.

The verified published price is £1,145 for every one-week course (DJ/Producer Level 1, DJ/Producer Level 2 and DJ Skills), and £1,695 for both two-week courses. Prices as published for the 2026 season; 2027 pricing is not yet posted, so treat these as indicative. _rec.otherFees: CORRECTED — the deposit is NOT £200 for both. Verified: one-week courses take a £100 registration fee plus a £1,045 balance; two-week courses take a £200 registration fee plus a £1,495 balance. THE DEPOSIT IS NON-REFUNDABLE IN ALL CIRCUMSTANCES, including visa refusal. Not included and not published: flights from Tunis, accommodation (partner-hotel discounts are offered but the rates are not published), Ibiza living costs in peak summer, travel to the venues (students 'are asked to make their own way to the venues'), and a Schengen short-stay visa application fee for a Tunisian national. No insurance or materials fee is charged.
_rec.equipmentRequired: None mandatory — Pioneer DJ industry-standard equipment and Ableton Live are provided at the academy. Students do receive substantial software discounts: 50% off Native Instruments Komplete, Ableton Live and Roland Cloud, and 40% off Serato DJ. _rec.totalCostEstimate: Two weeks: £1,695 tuition (or roughly £1,356 with a 20% early-bird code), plus flights Tunis-Ibiza, plus peak-summer Ibiza accommodation which can easily exceed the tuition, plus a Schengen visa fee and the documentation burden that comes with it. Realistically £3,000-£5,000 all-in for two weeks. Very high cost per contact hour, but the only credential-free route into the Ibiza scene on this list.
_rec.paymentPlans: CORRECTED — there is NO payment plan. The Ibiza terms and conditions state explicitly: 'Payment by instalments is not possible for pointblank Ibiza Can Blau music courses.' The two-part structure (registration fee then balance) is a booking deposit, not an instalment plan: full payment including the non-refundable deposit must be received at least 14 days before the course starts. Cancellation with less than 14 days' notice leaves the full fee payable, and dropping out gives no refund of any kind. The only genuine saving is the recurring 20% early-bird discount code.
_rec.scholarships: NONE. No scholarship, bursary or financial aid of any kind is published for the Ibiza short courses.
_rec.facilities: A fully-equipped academy just outside Ibiza Town at Instituto de Educación Secundaria Isidoro Macabich, Calle de sa Blanca Dona s/n, 07800 Eivissa (the FAQ also refers to it as the Ibiza Blau / Can Blau music school). Pioneer DJ-sponsored studios with industry-leading kit and Ableton Live. Tutors are working Ibiza DJ/producers (Javier Garcia 'Grazze', Veve Milah, vocalist Blanka Nova). A free media pack is included for every student on these courses: 10 professional press shots and 2 Instagram reels. Industry partner discounts and event access are provided but confirmed only during the course.
_rec.reputationSignals: Point Blank is a genuinely well-regarded electronic music school with real standing in DJ and production education and authentic Ibiza industry access; alumni include Nicole Moudaber, and the school cites Goldie, Leona Lewis and Pete Tong among its associations. The free media pack (10 press shots plus 2 Instagram reels) and the software discounts are concrete, unusual deliverables. RED FLAGS for this search, all verified: it is a one or two-week short course, not education at any level; it carries no Spanish accreditation, no ECTS and no named certificate; it cannot support a student residence permit; the deposit is forfeited even if his visa is refused; and the performance slots are NOT guaranteed despite how the marketing reads — the course page says only that there is 'potential for you to perform', and the FAQ adds that set times and locations are 'subject to venue availability and the instructor' and that 'due to venue size not every student will be able to play at the same venue on the same night'.
_rec.recommendation: EXPLICITLY NOT A MASTER — one or two weeks, no ECTS, no certificate named, no Spanish accreditation, and it cannot bring him to Spain on a student permit. Three corrections he must not miss: the one-week price is £1,145 not £1,195; the deposit is £100 for one week and £200 for two, and it is NON-REFUNDABLE EVEN IF HIS VISA IS REFUSED; and the performance slots are advertised as potential opportunities subject to venue availability, not the guaranteed bookings the marketing implies. That said, my candid verdict stands: as a roughly £1,700 two-week investment (nearer £1,350 on the recurring 20% early-bird code) in real Ibiza contacts, a free professional media pack of 10 press shots and 2 Instagram reels, and 50% off Ableton Live, it would do more for his stated ambition of becoming a working DJ than several of the five-figure 'másteres' elsewhere on this list. Treat it as career marketing bought with a Schengen tourist-style visa, taken in a summer BEFORE the September 2027 intake, and never as a qualification or a route to residency. CONDITIONAL strictly on that framing — if he is tempted to substitute it for an accredited programme, the answer is AVOID.

_rec.focus: Computational and immersive audio; Electronic Music technology; sound synthesis, signal processing, music information retrieval and music AI — research/engineering-led, not studio production
_rec.durationEcts: VERIFIED: 60 ECTS — 40 credits of compulsory and optional subjects plus a 20-credit master's thesis (the official Catalan register breaks this into 25 mandatory + 15 optional + 20 thesis). Face-to-face, full-time, one year by default; an official PART-TIME route spreads the 60 ECTS over two years. Depending on prior education you may be required to take up to 15 (full-time) or up to 50 (part-time) complementary undergraduate credits, extending the master to two years. _rec.language: English (verified on the official Overview page). All complementary undergraduate courses are also taught in English.
_rec.whatYouStudy: VERIFIED: the whole sound-communication chain — creation and generation of sound, transmission, perception. Grounding in "the most advanced technologies for the analysis, synthesis, transformation, and production of sound and music" plus the technologies and processes supporting sound and musical creation. Draws on music (composition, performance, musicology), physics/acoustics, engineering (signal processing, AI, human-computer interaction, electronics) and psychology (psychoacoustics). The programme explicitly "focuses on the more technical aspects of this field". Research focus mirrors the MTG: audio signal processing, music information retrieval, musical interfaces, computational musicology. Coordinator: Xavier Serra. Workload is openly stated as roughly 50 hours/week; mornings are deliberately kept free for study and NOT to make the master compatible with parallel work.
_rec.entryRequirements: VERIFIED on UPF's official admission-requirements page under this exact master: official bachelor's or master's degree from the EHEA or an equivalent foreign degree giving access to postgraduate study in the issuing country — and, verbatim, "S'accepten titulacions de qualsevol àmbit acadèmic" (degrees from ANY academic field are accepted); academic transcript with grade average; CV in English; motivation letter in English of 400–600 words; at least ONE academic recommendation letter (requested through the online application, institutional email addresses only — no gmail/yahoo/hotmail); accredited English at B2 level; passport/ID. "Complementàriament ... la comissió de selecció pot concertar una entrevista amb el candidat" — the committee may additionally arrange an interview. The SMC FAQ adds that the most important criterion is "excellence in the academic CV as related to the topics of the master", then the motivation letter, and that "if you do not have a Computer Science degree, you should be able to demonstrate an equivalent background" in maths, programming, signal processing and/or machine learning. Documents not in Catalan, Spanish, English, French, Italian or Portuguese need a sworn translation — his French-language documents are directly acceptable.
_rec.portfolioSpec: CONFIRMED: no portfolio required. Admission is CV + transcript + 400–600-word motivation letter + one academic reference + English B2 + passport, with a possible interview. The FAQ notes that if he has no formal music education, "the motivation letter is a good place to explain your non-formal musical training" — so his music case is made in prose, not in a submitted body of work.
_rec.auditionSpec: None. No audition and no on-site test. The only possible live element is a discretionary selection-committee interview, normally by video for international candidates.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: Yes, unambiguously — the strongest verified "yes" in this batch. UPF's official requirements page states "S'accepten titulacions de qualsevol àmbit acadèmic" (degrees from any academic field are accepted), and the programme's own FAQ says "The ideal candidate has an undergraduate degree in Computer Science." His BSc Software Engineering is literally the preferred profile. No music degree is required at any point.
_rec.tuitionIntl: VERIFIED on UPF's official page under this master: "Estudiants UE: 1.302 € / Estudiants no UE: 5.749,8 €". A Tunisian national pays €5,749.80 for the 60 ECTS. A separate non-refundable pre-registration fee applies (reported around €30 by third parties; not confirmed officially).
_rec.scholarship: None found for a non-EU Tunisian. The SMC scholarships page simply redirects to UPF's general master's grants list, on which every item is a Spanish/Catalan state or regional grant with residency conditions (AGAUR general grant, EQUITAT, Basque Government, UPF community hardship aid), a Santander programme tied to enrolment at a Spanish university, or nationality-restricted — Fundación Carolina, the most visible option, is for IBERO-AMERICAN graduates only and therefore excludes Tunisia. What the MTG does offer, after enrolment, is paid research assistantships on specific projects plus partner-company internships (see the SMC internships page) — a partial offset, not entry funding.
_rec.stipend: None at entry. Post-enrolment MTG research assistantships and partner-company internships exist; amounts are not published.

For a September 2027 start he should plan a January–March 2027 submission once the 2027–2028 dates appear. Only complete applications validated by the administrator are considered.
_rec.facilities: UPF's Music Technology Group is among Europe's most cited sound-and-music research groups (origin of Freesound and the Essentia audio-analysis library). Verified graduate destinations are R&D roles or PhDs: BMAT, Native Instruments, Sony CSL, Dolby, Pandora, Telefónica, Google, Apple, Adobe, Spotify; PhDs at IRCAM, QMUL, Amsterdam, Utrecht, NYU, City London, Stanford. _rec.publicPrivate: PRIVATE — CONFIRMED, and now from an independent official source, not just the school's own claim. (obecně prospěšná společnost). Not a veřejná vysoká škola. The previous record's reasoning was right and its conclusion stands.
_rec.language: CORRECTED — the previous record's 'Czech, UNVERIFIED whether any English-medium delivery exists' is WRONG. FAMO runs a full parallel English-medium division, the International Film School (IFS), and its own page states the programmes are 'taught exclusively in the English language'. IFS offers Certificate Film Course (1 sem), Diploma Film Course (2 sem), Bachelor of Arts (6 sem) and Master of Arts (4 sem), with Sound design named as an MA specialization. So there are two real routes: Czech-taught at 79,000 CZK/year, or English-taught at a completely different price (see tuitionNonEU).
_rec.languageRequirement: CORRECTED — both tracks now verified, and they differ sharply. CZECH TRACK: the official přijímací řízení page states Czech language proficiency is MANDATORY to commence study; interpreters are permitted only during the admission interview, not for the degree itself. No certificate level is published, but this is a hard practical block for someone starting from zero Czech. ENGLISH TRACK (IFS): English at B2, and critically NO IELTS OR TOEFL — proficiency is verified through an online conversation with a native speaker. That is a genuinely significant finding for this candidate, who has not sat any English test and has no time budgeted for one.
_rec.qualification: Czech track: MgA., navazující magisterské studium, programme code N0211P310001, standard duration 2 years. English track: awarded as 'Master of Arts Degree'; FAMO and the Study in Czechia portal both present the English BA/MA as accredited variants of the same Multimediální produkce programme. The MŠMT/NAÚ register (regvssp.msmt.cz) is a JavaScript application that could not be machine-queried, so the register ENTRY ITSELF remains unopened — but the programme code, the mirrored register data on vysokeskoly.com, and the listing on the government Study in Czechia portal all corroborate genuine national accreditation of the Czech-language programme. What is NOT independently confirmed is that the ENGLISH-language variant carries the same accreditation and awards the same MgA. title rather than an in-house 'Master of Arts'. Get that in writing before paying anything.
_rec.accreditationStatus: PARTIALLY RESOLVED. The Czech-taught N0211P310001 is corroborated as a nationally accredited navazující magisterský programme by three independent sources. The English-taught IFS MA is claimed by the school to be accredited and EU-recognised, but neither the IFS homepage nor the IFS about-page carries any accreditation statement at all — the claim appears only in third-party directory listings and marketing copy. Given the price difference (see below), the single most important question to answer in writing before any payment is: does the English-taught MA appear in the MŠMT register as a language variant of N0211P310001, and does it confer MgA.? If it does not, a Tunisian national would be paying 30,000 EUR for a non-state-recognised private certificate that may not support a residence permit.
_rec.durationEcts: 2 years / 4 semesters, full-time, both tracks. 120 ECTS is the Czech norm for navazující magisterské studium; the specific ECTS count is not published on either the Czech or English pages.
_rec.focus: Film-school multimedia production with a dedicated sound line. Ateliér zvuku trains 'zvukaře ve filmové, televizní, rozhlasové a divadelní tvorbě' — sound engineers for film, television, radio and theatre. Note carefully what that is NOT: it is post-production and location sound for screen and stage, not music production, not electronic music, not DJing.
_rec.whatYouStudy: CORRECTED on the key open question. The previous record flagged as UNVERIFIED whether a sound specialization continues into the master's. It DOES. The FAMO studium page lists eight ateliérs applying to both the bachelor and the follow-up master's, including Ateliér zvuku, and the IFS master's page independently names 'Sound design' among the MA specializations alongside Screenwriting and Directing, Cinematography, Production and Animation. So master-level sound is real at this school. The remaining mismatch is one of content, not existence: this is screen-and-stage sound engineering, whereas the candidate's stated goal is international DJ and music producer. Nothing in either track's published specialization list covers music production, electronic music composition, or club/dance music.
_rec.entryRequirements: CORRECTED FROM 'UNVERIFIED'. Czech track: completed bachelor's degree (thesis and diploma required, or supplied at enrolment if the defence is pending); general conditions under § 48 of the Higher Education Act; interview before an admission commission which assesses submitted works and tests cultural, artistic and technical awareness. Foreign applicants face IDENTICAL admission conditions to Czechs but must obtain either general nostrification (valid nationwide) or FAMO's own internal nostrification of the prior degree — Tunisia is NOT on the exemption list (only Germany, Slovakia, Slovenia, Poland, Hungary are exempt). Maximum 35 students admitted across ALL specializations combined. English track (IFS): completed application form, CV, motivational letter, bachelor degree certificate, valid passport, portfolio, plus the B2 English conversation. Nostrification also required.
_rec.portfolioSpec: CORRECTED FROM 'UNVERIFIED'. Czech track: the bachelor's thesis from prior study PLUS a portfolio of works matching the chosen specialization; the commission 'individuálně posuzuje možnosti uchazečů a profesní předpoklady' — it assesses each candidate's capabilities and professional prerequisites individually, which is a genuinely low and flexible bar compared with FAMU or a conservatory. English track: master's applicants must submit portfolio samples (mandatory at MA level; optional at BA level). For a candidate with no portfolio yet, the year he has before applying is exactly the right amount of time — but it must contain sound work, not just music tracks, if he wants this school.
_rec.auditionSpec: No performance audition. Czech track: an interview before the admission commission on the day of the přijímací řízení, conducted over the submitted works. English track: an online conversation with a native English speaker (which doubles as the language check) rather than a formal audition. Both are conversational rather than performance-based — materially easier for a non-conservatory applicant than any music-academy entrance exam.
_rec.equipmentRequired: None required for admission. IFS states the tuition fee covers tuition plus basic equipment for each practical exercise and specialized software — so no separate hardware purchase is implied. Teaching uses Pro Tools and multi-channel recording setups.
_rec.facilities: Sound studio with professional audio equipment including Pro Tools and multi-channel recording; small film school with hands-on production access; teaching staff drawn from working industry professionals. IFS claims its teaching staff outnumbers its international students. Small scale means more individual studio time and far less institutional weight than FAMU.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: YES — and this is now well-supported rather than inferred. No music degree, no conservatory training and no film degree is required by either track. The Czech track's own wording is that the commission assesses candidates individually on capabilities and professional prerequisites; the English track asks only for a bachelor's degree in anything, plus a portfolio. A BSc Software Engineering graduate is admissible on paper to both. This is one of the genuinely open doors in the whole search.
_rec.englishTest: NONE — no IELTS and no TOEFL, for either track. The English track verifies B2 through an online conversation with a native speaker. For a candidate who has not taken and does not want to pay for a standardised test, this removes a real obstacle. It is the single strongest point in this school's favour for him.
_rec.tuitionEU: Czech-taught track: 79,000 CZK per academic year (~3,200 EUR), identical for Czech and EU students, payable before the programme starts. English-taught IFS track: 7,500 EUR per SEMESTER at master's level — the same rate for EU and non-EU applicants, since IFS prices by programme, not nationality.
_rec.tuitionNonEU: THE BIGGEST CORRECTION IN THIS RECORD. The previous entry stated a Tunisian would pay 79,000 CZK/year (~3,200 EUR) because FAMO 'publishes a SINGLE rate with no separate non-EU tariff'. That is true only of the CZECH-TAUGHT track, which he realistically cannot enter without Czech. The track actually open to him is the English-taught IFS MA, and its published rate is 7,500 EUR PER SEMESTER — i.e. 15,000 EUR per year, 30,000 EUR for the two-year master's. That is roughly FIVE TIMES the figure previously recorded, and it is not a non-EU surcharge — it is simply the price of the English-medium programme, which the earlier research missed entirely. (The IFS Bachelor and the film courses are 6,500 EUR/semester; only the MA is 7,500.)
_rec.otherFees: CORRECTED FROM 'UNVERIFIED'. Czech track: non-refundable administrative fee of 1,000 CZK, paid to account 190 134 906 / 0300 (ČSOB Písek) with the applicant's ID as variable symbol. English track: no application fee published, BUT a deposit of 50% of the first semester's tuition — approximately 3,750 EUR for the MA — must be paid BEFORE formal acceptance, explicitly to 'establish the sincerity of the application'. Nostrification of the Tunisian BSc is required and carries its own cost and delay. Písek living costs are low, roughly 12,000-16,000 CZK/month.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: CZECH TRACK (not realistically open to him): ~158,000 CZK tuition over two years (~6,400 EUR) plus ~290,000-380,000 CZK living (~12,000-15,500 EUR) — about 18,000-22,000 EUR total. ENGLISH TRACK (the one he could actually enter): 30,000 EUR tuition plus ~12,000-15,500 EUR living — about 42,000-45,500 EUR total for the degree, before nostrification and visa costs. The previous record's headline of 'roughly 18,000-22,000 EUR' understated his real exposure by more than half.
_rec.scholarships: None identified for either track. Private Czech HEIs rarely fund non-EU degree students, and Czech government scholarship schemes are generally tied to public institutions. Assume full self-pay. The 50% pre-acceptance deposit on the English track means he would be committing ~3,750 EUR of his own money before he has an acceptance in hand, let alone a visa.
_rec.intakes: CORRECTED FROM 'UNVERIFIED'. Annual September intake. The Czech track runs TWO admission rounds per cycle; the English track has a single annual deadline.
_rec.applicationOpens: Applications open well ahead of each round. FAMO explicitly warns on its own admissions page: 'Neposílejte přihlášky a povinné práce poslední den, kdy je deadline!' — do not send applications and required works on the deadline day; send them several weeks early. For a September 2027 start he should have materials ready by early 2027.
_rec.deadline: CORRECTED FROM 'UNVERIFIED'. Published dates for the 2026/27 cycle, which map directly onto his 2027/28 target one year later. CZECH TRACK: two rounds — exam 14 May 2026 with applications due 8 May 2026, and exam 3 September 2026 with applications due 7 August 2026. ENGLISH TRACK (IFS): 30 April 2026. Expect the equivalent 2027 dates, i.e. an IFS deadline around 30 April 2027 and Czech-track rounds in May and August/September 2027. Note the IFS April deadline is COMFORTABLE for a September 2027 start and fits his stated Oct 2026 - Feb 2027 preparation window with room to spare.
_rec.visaEligible: Czech track: YES if N0211P310001 is confirmed in the MŠMT register — study at an accredited private Czech HEI supports a long-term residence permit for study purposes. English track: PROBABLY, but this is precisely where the unresolved accreditation question bites. If the English MA is an accredited language variant of N0211P310001, it supports the permit; if it is an in-house 'Master of Arts' outside the register, it may not, and he would have paid a 3,750 EUR deposit and potentially far more for a qualification that does not underpin his residence. Resolve this in writing BEFORE the deposit. Also note the sequencing risk the previous record correctly identified and which is now worse: the deposit falls due before acceptance, which is before any visa decision.
_rec.recommendation: The previous record treated this as a cheap Plan C fallback at ~3,200 EUR/year. That framing collapses once the English track is priced correctly. The route he can actually walk — English-taught, no IELTS, non-music bachelor accepted — costs 7,500 EUR per semester, 30,000 EUR for the degree, roughly 42,000-45,500 EUR all-in. The route that costs 3,200 EUR/year requires Czech language proficiency as a precondition of commencing study, which he cannot reach from zero by September 2027 while also building a portfolio. So the cheap option and the accessible option are not the same option, and the earlier entry conflated them. On top of the price, three things push this to AVOID for HIM specifically. First, fit: Ateliér zvuku and the IFS Sound design line train sound engineers for film, television, radio and theatre — screen and stage post-production. His goal is international DJ and music producer. Neither track's published specialization list contains music production, electronic music, or composition. He would pay 30,000 EUR to learn a genuinely skilled trade that is adjacent to, not aimed at, what he wants. Second, accreditation asymmetry: the Czech programme's national accreditation is well corroborated, but neither the IFS homepage nor its about-page makes any accreditation statement whatsoever, and the English MA's register status and degree title (MgA. or an in-house 'Master of Arts') are unconfirmed. Paying master-level money for a private award whose state recognition is unverified is exactly the trap to refuse. Third, money at risk before certainty: a 50% first-semester deposit, about 3,750 EUR, is demanded before formal acceptance and therefore long before a visa decision. That said, record the genuine positives honestly, because they are unusual and may matter if better options fail: no IELTS or TOEFL at all, a conversational rather than performance-based entrance, explicit willingness to assess non-traditional candidates individually, a confirmed master-level sound specialization, a portfolio requirement he has a full year to satisfy, and an April deadline that fits his timeline comfortably. If he ever reconsiders, he must first get in writing (1) the English MA's entry in the MŠMT register and the exact degree title, (2) confirmation the deposit is refundable on visa refusal, and (3) a syllabus showing how much music-production content, if any, the sound line contains. Until then this is a 30,000 EUR answer to a question he has not asked.

Semesters 2-3 specialise into Ingénierie et conception sonore: Physical Acoustics (6+3 ECTS), Perception and Cognition (6+3), Signal Processing (3+6), Informatics (3+3), Research and Professional Context (3+3), Sonic and Musical Listening Practices (3), and Collective Projects and Field Schools (6+3 per semester). Semester 4 is a compulsory 5-month internship (24 ECTS) plus the final collective project restitution (6 ECTS). Teaching runs in 9-week blocks followed by 3 weeks of field schools, workshops and seminars; attendance is mandatory and learning is team-based. Internships may be hosted in the PRISM laboratory if places are available.

_rec.tuitionNonEU: CORRECTED — 3 941 € per year, NOT 3 879 €. THIS IS THE RATE HE WOULD PAY. Quoted verbatim from Enjmin's own official tariff sheet (Tarifs 2025-2026): 'Vous êtes un étudiant ou une étudiante extra-communautaire … Le montant des frais d'inscription que vous avez à payer est de 3 941 €.' ALSO CORRECTED: the previous entry said 'no institutional exemption'. That overstates it — the annex records that three EPN (ESGT, INSEAC, EPN5) volunteered exemptions and ENJMIN was not among them, BUT the same document then asks the governing board to approve a scheme covering up to 10% of FI enrolments per programme, on the basis of national fees for students under a partnership convention and 50% of the differentiated fee for candidature libre non-EU students, with 'chaque EPN concernée' running its own academic/social selection. _rec.totalCostEstimate: 3 941 € + 105 € CVEC = 4 046 €/year at full rate, or roughly 2 075 €/year if he wins the 50% EPN exemption. Plus ENIC-NARIC comparability fee, plus Angoulême living costs (a genuinely cheap French town — materially cheaper than Lyon, Paris or Strasbourg).
_rec.scholarships: None programme-specific. Two real levers: (1) the Cnam/EPN 10% differentiated-fee exemption scheme described above — ask Enjmin; (2) national French routes (Eiffel, Campus France Tunisie, French Embassy Tunis) which must be pursued in parallel from autumn 2026.
_rec.visaEligible: YES — CONFIRMED. Diplôme national de master at a public establishment. Études en France is used afterwards, once admitted, to obtain the visa.
_rec.recommendation: Still the single best thematic fit in this batch: game audio sits exactly on the seam between a software-engineering BSc and a career in sound, and the official page genuinely accepts any bac+3 background with no music degree. It is a real accredited state master (RNCP 38202) that fully supports a student residence permit, and the language gate is French B2 — a certificate he can realistically get, unlike IELTS which is not even asked for here. Three corrections to the previous entry: the non-EU fee is 3 941 €, not 3 879 €; the EU rate is 254 €; and CVEC is 105 €, both published on Enjmin's own tariff sheet. Also, an institutional exemption of up to 50% may be reachable through the Cnam's EPN scheme — worth an email, because it would halve the cost. CONDITIONAL rather than WORTH IT for one reason only: the gate is a creative dossier plus written and oral exams at a very small, very competitive national school, and he has no portfolio today. His entire 2026 has to go into producing game-audio work aimed at the cahier des charges that drops in mid-December. Second caution: this trains game sound designers, not DJs or record producers — the club/production ambition has to run alongside it. Practical sequencing: file the ENIC-NARIC attestation de comparabilité by September 2026 (four-month turnaround), sit a DELF/TCF B2 by November 2026, then answer the December brief.

_rec.program: M2 ATIAM — Acoustique, Traitement du signal, Informatique, Appliqués à la Musique
_rec.university: Sorbonne Université (Faculté des Sciences et Ingénierie), in collaboration with IRCAM and Télécom Paris
_rec.degree: Master 2 (parcours of a Sorbonne Université Sciences et Technologies master; ATIAM is the second year only)
_rec.durationEcts: One year (M2): semester 1 = 30 ECTS (5 modules of 6 ECTS), semester 2 = a 5-6 month research internship in a company or laboratory in France or abroad.
_rec.focus: Technical — musical acoustics, sound signal processing, computer music. NOT a production or craft degree.
_rec.institutionType: Public university consortium with a national research institute (IRCAM) and a grande école (Télécom Paris)
_rec.language: French predominantly — 'Un bon niveau de français est conseillé ... car les cours sont en majorité dispensés en français'; 'un bon niveau d'anglais' also required.
_rec.whatYouStudy: 'Fournir les connaissances scientifiques et la culture musicale nécessaires pour entreprendre une recherche dans les domaines de l'acoustique musicale, du traitement du signal sonore et de l'informatique musicale.' Five 6-ECTS taught modules then a 5-6 month research internship. Career destinations are public and private research and engineering, teaching, and the music-software and pro-audio industries.
_rec.entryRequirements: M2 ENTRY ONLY — a first year of master already completed is required. Informatics track: 'niveau de maîtrise ou master M1 en informatique ou mathématiques, école d'ingénieur avec spécialité informatique'. Acoustics track: 'niveau master 1 en physique/acoustique, école d'ingénieur avec spécialité physique/acoustique/traitement du signal'. Candidates must show 'un niveau similaire à celui atteint à l'issue d'une première année de master' in one or two of acoustics, signal processing and computer science, plus 'motivation et leur intérêt pour la musique' and 'un bon niveau d'anglais'. Non-EU candidates following the CEF/Campus France procedure must also observe Campus France deadlines, which differ from the university's.
_rec.portfolioSpec: No artistic portfolio. Application is an academic dossier submitted to Sorbonne Université (Faculté des Sciences et Ingénierie), with the motivation letter explicitly stating that ATIAM is the desired parcours. UNVERIFIED whether musical work may be attached.
_rec.auditionSpec: 'Un entretien de motivation' for pre-selected candidates, held at IRCAM. No audition, no practical sound test.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: YES on field — a computer-science or mathematics background is the intended profile ('M1 en informatique ou mathématiques, école d'ingénieur avec spécialité informatique'), and no music degree is required, only 'un intérêt pour la musique'. But NO on level: this is an M2, so a fresh Bac+3 cannot enter directly. He would need to complete an M1 (in computer science, acoustics or signal processing) first.
_rec.applicationOpens: 2026-2027 cycle: applications open 26 March 2026 (per the ATIAM candidatures page). For a 2027-2028 entry, expect a comparable spring 2027 window — PRIOR CYCLE, confirm.
_rec.deadline: 2026-2027 cycle: applications 26 March - 11 June 2026; interviews at IRCAM (date TBA); results 'courant juillet'; enrolment July-October 2026; start early September 2026. For a September 2027 entry these dates are PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Non-EU candidates must additionally respect the Campus France calendar, which is earlier.
_rec.tuitionIntl: UNVERIFIED — not stated on the ATIAM candidatures page. Sorbonne Université is a public university; the national non-EU differentiated master rate (~€3,950/yr for 2026-2027) may apply unless exempted.
_rec.scholarship: None programme-specific found on the pages read. The internship semester is normally paid (French gratification de stage) — UNVERIFIED amount.
_rec.stipend: UNVERIFIED; the 5-6 month internship in a company or laboratory is typically remunerated in France but no figure was published.
_rec.facilities: IRCAM — Europe's leading music research institute (STMS lab, Max/MSP lineage, spatialisation and analysis-synthesis research) — plus Sorbonne Université's Institut Jean Le Rond d'Alembert acoustics team and Télécom Paris signal processing. Internships placed in labs and companies in France and abroad. Named alumni/staff not read — UNVERIFIED.
_rec.fitNotes: Flagged as requested: this is the TECHNICAL/RESEARCH route, not a production or craft master — it trains audio DSP engineers and music-software researchers, and its graduates go into R&D and the audio industry, not into DJ booths. It is also M2-only, so unreachable directly from his BSc; he would need an M1 first (which a French computer-science M1 could provide). Relevant to him mainly as a strategic second step if he wants to build plugins, audio software or research credentials alongside a music career, or as the technical complement to a creative master. Not a September 2027 target.

_rec.institution: Université Lumière Lyon 2, UFR Lettres, sciences du langage et arts (LESLA), Campus Rachais
_rec.institutionType: Public university (EPSCP)
_rec.publicPrivate: PUBLIC — CONFIRMED. State university; its official pages publish the ministerially-set national rate (255 €) and the state differentiated non-EU rate (3 950 €), plus CVEC — public-sector mechanisms.
_rec.qualification: CONFIRMED — Diplôme national de master, mention Musicologie, parcours MAAAV. RNCP N°39199, registered with France Compétences (stated on the official M2 page). Real second-cycle state degree supporting a student residence permit.

_rec.englishTest: None required.
_rec.durationEcts: CONFIRMED — M1 60 ECTS + M2 60 ECTS (S3 30 ECTS, S4 30 ECTS), 2 years total. M1 includes a compulsory internship of at least 12 weeks full-time in semester 2, in film, animation, video game or multimedia production; M2 semester 4 is a compulsory internship (minimum 12 weeks full-time) plus report and defence. In-person only, Campus Rachais, Lyon.
_rec.focus: Composing and producing music for the moving image — cinema (animation, live action, documentary), video games, advertising, television and multimedia.
_rec.whatYouStudy: CONFIRMED from the official M2 page, semester 3 (30 ECTS): musical composition and orchestration applied to image, electronic music and synthesis, advanced mixing, English, cinematic culture and research methodology, history of film sound, and intellectual property law. Semester 4 (30 ECTS) is the compulsory internship plus report and defence. Core competences: image analysis, orchestration technique, and command of digital audio workstations.
_rec.entryRequirements: CONFIRMED — M1 entry by competitive selection, 16 places ('une promotion de 16 étudiants compositeurs'), open to holders of a licence in ANY field, or via VAPP with at least 5 years of professional activity in music. Critically, the official M1 page states the target profile as 'Etre déjà compositeur au moment du recrutement' — already a composer at the time of recruitment — with command of music notation, orchestration and DAW tools. M2 entry CONFIRMED as requiring completion of M1 MAAAV ('avoir effectué un master 1 MAAAV'), so there is no lateral entry at M2.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: Formally YES, substantively NO. A licence in any discipline is accepted, which on paper admits his BSc Software Engineering. But the official page requires the applicant to already be a composer commanding music notation and orchestration. The open-discipline rule exists to admit self-taught composers, not career changers with no music.
_rec.portfolioSpec: A composition portfolio is the selection instrument: three recent personal compositions in varied styles written to three short films (3–5 minutes maximum each) — three audio files (wav or mp3) synchronised to the films, plus three corresponding scores in PDF. NOTE this specification comes from the programme's dedicated site maaav.fr rather than the univ-lyon2.fr catalogue pages; confirm the exact 2027 brief with the scolarité.
_rec.auditionSpec: Selection is by concours on the composition portfolio. Whether an interview follows is not stated on the official pages.
_rec.equipmentRequired: CONFIRMED on the official M1 page and MORE DEMANDING than previously reported: a powerful computer (MacBook Pro, iMac or high-spec PC) with at least 1 TB SSD storage; professional DAW software (Logic Pro X, Reaper or Cubase); quality headphones; and an audio interface with microphone inputs. This is a published mandatory technical prerequisite and a real cost line of roughly 2 000–3 000 € on top of tuition.
_rec.facilities: Campus Rachais, Lyon. Students work on their own DAW rigs (see equipment requirement). Studio inventory not published.
_rec.intakes: September (annual), 16 places.
_rec.applicationOpens: Not dated on the official pages. Route: the official M1 page states applications are made exclusively through Mon Master (monmaster.gouv.fr); the M2 page uses eCandidat and explicitly notes that Campus France procedures are required for non-EU students in designated countries. As a Tunisian national resident in Tunisia he goes through Études en France / Campus France Tunisie rather than Mon Master — confirm with the scolarité before the campaign opens.
_rec.deadline: Not published. Contact lesla.m1maaav@univ-lyon2.fr and Campus France Tunisie.
_rec.tuitionEU: CONFIRMED — 255 € at master level, academic year 2026-2027, from Lyon 2's official droits d'inscription page.
_rec.tuitionNonEU: CONFIRMED — 3 950 € at master level for non-EU students, academic year 2026-2027, from Lyon 2's official droits d'inscription page. THIS IS THE RATE HE WOULD PAY. Also CONFIRMED: Lyon 2's own page states its transitional exemption regime 'prend fin dès la rentrée 2026/2027' and that prior automatic exemptions no longer carry over — limited exemptions remain only in 'des cas très spécifiques'. A new non-EU entrant in 2027 should assume the full 3 950 €. Fees are annual and non-refundable after 15 November.
_rec.otherFees: CVEC 105 € for 2026-2027, payable in addition. Plus the mandatory home-studio rig described under equipmentRequired.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: ~4 055 €/year (3 950 € + 105 € CVEC) plus Lyon living costs, plus a one-off ~2 000–3 000 € for the mandatory computer, DAW licence, interface and headphones.
_rec.scholarships: Nothing programme-specific. The transitional exemption has ended for 2026/2027 onward, so the practical levers are Eiffel and Campus France Tunisie.
_rec.visaEligible: YES — public university, diplôme national de master, RNCP 39199.
_rec.recommendation: All the previous entry's key claims are confirmed, and two things are now firmer: M2 entry is explicitly reserved for students who completed M1 MAAAV, so there is no lateral entry, and the mandatory equipment list is more specific than reported (1 TB+ SSD, Logic Pro X / Reaper / Cubase, audio interface with mic inputs, quality headphones) — a real 2 000–3 000 € cost on top of tuition. The AVOID is about eligibility, not legitimacy: this is a properly accredited public master (RNCP 39199) that supports a residence permit. But the gate closes it for him. Sixteen places a year, decided on three original compositions scored to three short films with PDF scores, and an official page stating the candidate must ALREADY be a composer commanding music notation and orchestration. He cannot write orchestral scores and has one year, not five. The unusual open-discipline rule (a licence in any field) makes it look reachable for a software engineer, and the M2 content — electronic music, synthesis, advanced mixing, composition for image — reads beautifully against his goals, which is exactly why it needs the explicit warning. Report it so he knows it exists; do not queue it for 2027. If film and game scoring genuinely attracts him, this is a 2029-2030 target reachable only after sustained composition study. The Enjmin sound-design route and the two engineering routes are the ones that fit the profile he actually has.

_rec.focus: Film Sound + Sound Design + Recording, practice-based and very production-heavy. This is cinema and audiovisual sound, not music production.
_rec.institutionType: Public university film school — école interne of Université Toulouse - Jean Jaurès, described as the first and only national film school located outside Paris
_rec.language: French throughout
_rec.whatYouStudy: Roughly 15 compulsory exercises across the two years — sound pieces, documentaries and fiction works, each with defined pedagogical constraints — plus a personal film at the end of M1 and of M2 with no restriction on genre or duration, each accompanied by a methodological dissertation. Taught content covers acoustic principles, analogue and digital audio technology, sound recording, editing, mixing and diffusion. CONFIRMED M2 Son exercises specifically: location sound recording (phonography), documentary sound creation, sound post-production, a written audio-technology dissertation, sound design for a visual sequence, collaborative work with the Image and Réalisation M2 students on the 'Filmer le Travail' project, and a final thesis with an accompanying audio or audiovisual product defended before a professional jury.
_rec.entryRequirements: IMPORTANT STRUCTURAL CORRECTION. ENSAV does not run a 'parcours Son' from M1. It runs a Master 1 Cinéma & Audiovisuel Parcours Généraliste (alongside M1 Production, REX and XR), and Son is one of seven M2 specialisations (Son, Image, Réalisation, Production, REX, Architecture Décor/VFX, XR). M1 Généraliste entry: 'Licence Création Audiovisuelle ou d'une formation bac+3 équivalente dans les domaines des arts, des arts du spectacle, de l'architecture, du design, des arts plastiques, DE L'INFORMATIQUE ou des beaux-arts', i.e. Bac+3 / 180 ECTS. M2 Son entry: Bac+4 / 240 ECTS, and the ENSAV page states that entrants must have 'already been previously trained in sound basics during the generalist years of Licence and Master 1' at ENSAV. Selection is on dossier, and after the file review 'un entretien peut être programmé avec le candidat'. Dossiers are emailed directly to ensav@univ-tlse2.fr — the Son route is handled by ENSAV itself, not via Mon Master (the Production parcours does use Mon Master). Extra-European applicants are also routed through Études en France. Contact: Djazaira Berkouk, ensav@univ-tlse2.fr, 05 61 50 44 46; ENSAV, 56 rue du Taur, 31000 Toulouse, 05 61 50 35 07.
_rec.portfolioSpec: Not published. The application is a downloadable ENSAV dossier form emailed back to the school. For the Production parcours the dossier requires a one-page mémoire project; the equivalent creative requirement for the generalist M1 and for M2 Son — number of works, length, format — is NOT specified on any public page. UNVERIFIED. He must request the current dossier from ensav@univ-tlse2.fr.
_rec.auditionSpec: No live audition and no written concours found. Selection is on dossier, with a possible interview after the file review ('un entretien peut être programmé'). Whether the interview is remote or on-site in Toulouse is UNVERIFIED.

No music degree, no audition and no music-theory test. BUT — and this is the correction — that acceptance gets him into the GENERALIST M1, not into Son. M2 Son requires Bac+4 and presumes sound training already acquired during ENSAV's own Licence and M1 years, so reaching the Son specialisation means completing the generalist M1 first and then competing internally.

_rec.facilities: ENSAV is a public national film school with seven M2 specialisations co-located, so sound students work inside real crews with image, directing, production, VFX and XR students. The M2 Son year emphasises analogue and digital audio technology, acoustic principles and professional audio systems, and includes a cross-specialisation collaborative project. No itemised equipment or console inventory is published — UNVERIFIED.
_rec.fitNotes: Verification changed the verdict here. The admissions wording is still the most CS-friendly in France — 'de l'informatique' is a named accepted licence — and the route into the M1 Généraliste is genuinely open to him, dossier plus possible interview, no audition. But Son is not an M1 parcours: it is one of seven M2 specialisations, and ENSAV states that M2 Son entrants are expected to have already acquired sound basics during the school's own Licence and M1 years. So the realistic path is two-step and uncertain: get into the generalist M1, absorb the sound fundamentals there, then compete for one of the M2 Son places. Layered on top: it is cinema sound rather than music production, so it trains a boom operator or re-recording mixer, not a DJ or producer; it is French-language throughout (fine for him, though a C1 certificate will still be asked for); the dossier contents are not public so he must write to ENSAV; and the fee is now €3,950/yr rather than near-free. Good school, wrong craft for his stated goal, and a bottleneck between entry and specialisation.
_rec.verificationNotes: Confirmed on the official Université de Toulouse formations page: the Master Cinéma et audiovisuel parcours Son exists at master level in Toulouse, Bac+5, French, roughly 15 compulsory exercises over two years plus a personal film and methodological dissertation in each year, curriculum covering acoustic principles, audio technology, recording, editing, mixing and diffusion, and — verbatim — computer science among the accepted bac+3 backgrounds. Also confirmed there: M1 applications route via Mon Master or Études en France for extra-Europeans, but 'les inscriptions au Master doivent être effectuées directement sur le site de l'ENSAV'. MAJOR CORRECTION established from ensav.fr: there is no M1 Son — ENSAV offers a Master 1 Cinéma & Audiovisuel Parcours Généraliste plus M1 Production, REX and XR, and Son is one of seven M2 specialisations; the M2 Son page requires Bac+4 and states entrants must already have been trained in sound basics during ENSAV's generalist Licence and Master 1 years. Deadlines confirmed from ensav.fr/inscription: M1 closed for 2026-2027 with a 10 May 2026 dossier deadline, M2 REX 31 August 2026, DURCA 13 September 2026. NOT confirmed: total ECTS, dossier and portfolio contents for either M1 or M2 Son, interview format and location, UT2J's specific differentiated-fee exemption policy, and the equipment inventory.

_rec.auditionSpec: No audition. An interview ('entretien') follows the dossier review for BOTH M1 and M2 entry — this is a mandatory part of selection, not an optional add-on. Format (remote or on-site in Brest) and language of the interview are UNVERIFIED; assume French.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: CHECK — leaning yes on subject matter, unproven on procedure. The stated requirement is an L3 in Sciences Pour l'Ingénieur with the Image & Son specialisation 'ou équivalent'. A software-engineering BSc is scientifically adjacent and the master's own spine is signal processing, electroacoustics and audio informatics, so the content fit is real. But the programme is explicitly designed as a continuation of UBO's own L3 Image & Son, and nowhere does the page publish wording accepting a general non-specialised science degree, let alone a foreign one. With only 18 places and internal candidates in the pipeline, a direct M1 entry from a Tunisian CS degree needs a case-by-case ruling. He must email the programme to test eligibility BEFORE the monmaster window opens. Note: no music degree is required — the obstacle is the missing image-and-sound specialisation, not a missing music background.

UBO's own notice states plainly that until the new decree it applied a partial exemption to ALL non-EU students it hosted, and that this is 'désormais plus possible'. Following décret n° 2026-385 of 19 May 2026, exemptions are granted only on individual circumstances and may cover a maximum of 30% of affected students in 2026-2027, falling to 25% in 2027-2028 — his intake year. Budget €3,950/yr plus CVEC (~€105). Contact for eligibility: mobilite.internationale@univ-brest.fr.
_rec.fundingLevel: None to partial, and materially worse than previously assumed — the blanket partial exemption UBO used to give every non-EU student has been abolished.
_rec.scholarship: None programme-specific. External routes only: France Excellence Eiffel (institution-nominated, €1,181/month, master age cap 25, institutional internal deadlines around October-December preceding the Campus France national deadline in early January), Campus France Tunisie and French Embassy bourses, and a French government scholarship (BGF) which also brings full exemption from differentiated fees.
_rec.facilities: Studio practice in recording, mixing and mastering; spatial audio work across stereo, object-based and binaural formats; electroacoustics, microphones and loudspeakers taught as dedicated modules; a cohort capped at 18 so per-student studio access is high; M1 internship of at least 4 weeks and M2 internship of at least 4 months. Console and room inventory UNVERIFIED — no equipment list is published.
_rec.fitNotes: Technically the closest French public master here to a real sound-engineer training, and verification improved the picture on content: the S8-S9 split confirms an explicit Sound/Music track whose practical project can be musical recordings with mixing and mastering, not just film sound. With 18 students per year, studio time should be genuinely available. Three frictions, one of them new. First, entry: the programme is built as a continuation of its own L3 Image & Son, so a direct M1 entry from a Tunisian CS degree needs a case-by-case ruling — send an eligibility email well before February 2027. Second, money: the blanket partial exemption is gone, so this is now a €3,950/yr proposition rather than the near-free option previously assumed. Third, place: Brest is a long way from any electronic-music scene, which matters for someone whose goal is to become a working DJ. If they accept him, the curriculum-to-goal alignment is among the best in this batch; the risk is that they simply do not.
_rec.verificationNotes: Confirmed on the official UBO formations page: the programme exists at master level; Brest; French; 2 years, 4 semesters, 120 ECTS at 60 per year; the 18-student-per-cohort cap quoted verbatim; M1 entry from L3 SPI parcours Image & Son 'ou équivalent' via monmaster with dossier plus interview; M2 entry via UBO eCandidat with dossier plus interview; the full sound module list (electroacoustics and room acoustics, microphones and loudspeakers, audio signal processing, sonic perception, studio recording/mixing/mastering, spatialized sound in stereo/object-based/binaural); the S8-S9 choice between a Sound/Music and a Cinema track; the practical project alternative of musical recordings with mixing and mastering; internship minimums of 4 weeks in M1 and 4 months in M2; and the ABSENCE of any portfolio requirement. _rec.program: International Master of Science in Acoustics
_rec.institution: École Centrale de Lyon, in partnership with INSA Lyon and ENTPE, supported by the CeLyA acoustics laboratory cluster (eight Lyon research laboratories)
_rec.institutionType: Three public grandes écoles d'ingénieurs (state engineering schools) delivering a joint national master
_rec.publicPrivate: PUBLIC — CONFIRMED. Centrale Lyon, INSA Lyon and ENTPE are state engineering schools under ministerial supervision; Centrale Lyon's official master fees page applies the state national rate (255 €), free tuition for French government scholarship holders, and the state differentiated non-EU rate — all public-sector mechanisms.
_rec.qualification: CONFIRMED — 'National Master's degree accredited by the French State', stated in those words on the official Centrale Lyon page, delivered jointly by Centrale Lyon, INSA Lyon and ENTPE. Real second-cycle state degree supporting a student residence permit. RNCP number not displayed.
_rec.accreditationStatus: State-accredited national master's degree (explicit on the Centrale Lyon page). Specific RNCP registration not displayed online.
_rec.language: English — CONFIRMED. Centrale Lyon's official page states the programme is delivered entirely in English. The programme's own site adds that supplementary English and/or French language courses are provided so that students can follow M2 material in either language. Scientific teaching is in English.
_rec.languageRequirement: CONFIRMED — English B2 for both M1 and M2 entry (official Centrale Lyon page). The application page requires an English certificate as a mandatory document.
_rec.englishTest: REQUIRED — CONFIRMED. TOEFL iBT, TOEIC, IELTS or Cambridge English. Two waivers exist on the official application page: a signed declaration of native-English-speaker status, or proof of at least three years of education delivered in English. Neither applies to him (his BSc at SMU MedTech would only qualify if he can evidence three years taught in English — worth checking his transcripts, it could save him the test). Minimum scores are not published; ask the programme office. This is the ONE certificate in this batch he does not yet hold.
_rec.durationEcts: CONFIRMED — 2 years, 4 semesters. 500 hours in M1 and 240 hours in M2 (740 hours of in-person instruction), plus a 4–12 week internship in M1 and a 22–26 week thesis placement in M2. Total ECTS not stated online; a French DNM is 120 ECTS by definition, of which 27 ECTS are M2 optional specialisation courses.
_rec.focus: Scientific and engineering acoustics. The M2 'sound perception' specialisation is the branch closest to audio and psychoacoustics.
_rec.whatYouStudy: M1: fundamentals of mechanics, continuum physics, data and signal processing, plus introductory acoustics. M2 specialisations (confirmed on the official programme site): aeroacoustics, building acoustics, vehicle acoustics, sound perception, ultrasounds, vibro-acoustics, fluid-structure interactions. Theory, numerical and experimental work, laboratory projects, and more than one semester of research training as an intern in a laboratory or in industry, in France or abroad.
_rec.entryRequirements: CONFIRMED — M1: a bachelor's degree (or equivalent) in a science or engineering field, minimum 180 ECTS from a three-year programme, plus English B2. Direct M2 entry is possible for holders of a master's in mechanics, physics or mechanical engineering. Selection is on dossier. Required documents (official application page): CV, motivation letter, passport/ID copy, ID photo, reference letter(s), transcripts, copy of the last degree awarded, English language certificate.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: YES — it is a physics/engineering master and expects no music background whatsoever. His BSc Software Engineering is a plausible 'science or engineering' degree, but acoustics assumes more physics and mechanics than a pure software curriculum delivers; the admissions committee judges relatedness on dossier. He should email the programme office with his transcript before investing in the application.
_rec.portfolioSpec: None. No creative portfolio requested — selection is purely academic dossier. Decisive for a candidate with no portfolio.
_rec.auditionSpec: No audition.
_rec.equipmentRequired: None published.
_rec.facilities: CONFIRMED — backed by the CeLyA (Centre Lyonnais d'Acoustique) cluster spanning eight Lyon research laboratories, with laboratory-based projects and research internships.
_rec.intakes: September (annual).
_rec.applicationOpens: Not published as a fixed date. The 2026 cycle ran with committee responses by 30 April 2026, and a third session for European applicants only closing 30 April 2026 — i.e. the non-EU window closes earlier than the European one. For a September 2027 entry he should treat autumn 2026 as the real start because Études en France binds first.
_rec.deadline: CORRECTED/CLARIFIED — the previous entry reported an unconfirmed 30/04/2026 deadline with a 29/05/2026 committee reply. Centrale Lyon's official 'Applying for a master's degree' page confirms 30 April 2026 as the 2026-cycle date for committee responses, and flags that the third/complementary session is open to EUROPEAN applicants only — so a Tunisian national must make the earlier session. PRIOR CYCLE — confirm the 2027 dates. IMPORTANT NEW FINDING: that same official page states the International Master in Acoustics M1 applies through MonMaster (monmaster.gouv.fr), NOT the school's own candidature portal, while separately stating that non-EU international students must apply via Études en France AND submit on candidature.ec-lyon.fr. These two instructions conflict for his case. He must write to the programme office and to Campus France Tunis to establish which portal governs a Tunisian M1 applicant before the campaign opens.
_rec.tuitionEU: CORRECTED — 255 € + CVEC for non-scholarship students from the enlarged EU, academic year 2026-2027; free for French government scholarship holders. Source: Centrale Lyon's official master fees page (the previous entry left this unverified).
_rec.tuitionNonEU: CORRECTED — 3 950 € + CVEC for 2026-2027, NOT 3 770 €. THIS IS THE RATE HE WOULD PAY. Source: Centrale Lyon's official 'Frais d'inscription – Masters' page for 2026-2027. The 3 770 € figure on the programme's own application page (master-acoustics.ec-lyon.fr) is stale and reflects the older national reference amount. The school's fees page notes some students qualify for waived differentiated fees by profile and points to Campus France to check eligibility — no automatic exemption for a Tunisian self-funded applicant.
_rec.otherFees: CVEC payable in addition — Centrale Lyon's page cites 103 € (2024-2025 rate); the current national CVEC for 2026-2027 is 105 €, as published by UPHF. Budget 105 €.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: ~4 055 €/year (3 950 € + 105 € CVEC) plus Lyon living costs. Lyon is France's second most expensive student city — this is the highest total cost of living in the batch alongside Strasbourg. No official living-cost estimate published.
_rec.scholarships: Nothing programme-specific published. Two levers: the differentiated-fee waiver by profile mentioned on the Centrale Lyon fees page (check eligibility via Campus France), and the Eiffel scholarship — note Eiffel candidates are nominated BY the institution, so he would need Centrale Lyon to put him forward, meaning contact by autumn 2026 at the latest.
_rec.visaEligible: YES — public establishments, French state-accredited national master; the official pages instruct non-EU applicants to run Études en France in parallel for visa purposes.
_rec.recommendation: Two figures in the previous entry were wrong and both matter: the non-EU fee is 3 950 €, not 3 770 € (Centrale Lyon's own 2026-2027 fees page supersedes the stale number on the programme site), and the EU rate is 255 €. A new procedural problem also surfaced: Centrale Lyon's official application page says the International Master in Acoustics M1 goes through MonMaster, while also saying non-EU students must use Études en France plus candidature.ec-lyon.fr — the two are inconsistent for a Tunisian applicant, and the complementary late session is restricted to European applicants, so he cannot rely on a spring catch-up. On the merits it remains highly admissible: no portfolio, no audition, no music degree, no French-language gate, and an entry rule written for science graduates, with 'sound perception' and signal processing as a legitimate on-ramp to audio DSP and immersive audio. CONDITIONAL on three things. (1) He must book IELTS or TOEFL — unless he can evidence three years of instruction in English at SMU MedTech, which is the one waiver on the official page that could plausibly apply to him and is worth checking immediately. (2) His curriculum is software, not mechanics or physics; email the programme office with his transcript in autumn 2026 before spending money on the application. (3) It is acoustics engineering, not music production — the DJ/producer ambition runs in parallel, not through this degree. Cost is the full non-EU rate in France's second most expensive student city, so this is also the most expensive of the three viable options.
