_rec.focus: Film/Game Sound; Sound Design; Immersive Audio (Dolby Atmos); production sound
_rec.whatYouStudy: CONFIRMED: production of the audio layers of film and television. Year 1 concentrates on original sound recording on set; year 2 on post-production. Content includes location recording, sound design, mixing in a DAW, cinema film mixing and Dolby Atmos, working with Foley artists, film-music recording and mixing, and dialogue editing. Optional specialisations in media design and sound for games. Entirely project-based — students work on the academy's own film productions.
_rec.entryRequirements: General/subject-specific Hochschulreife (with a talent clause, the 'Begabtenpassus' under §10 of the exam regulations, for applicants without Abitur — an extended interview substitutes). For the Diplomaufbaustudiengänge specifically, an 'entsprechende Vorqualifikation, etwa mindestens ein Vordiplom oder Bachelor' is required, submitted as an officially certified copy. Applicants must bring working knowledge of studio audio technology, microphones and DAW operation. B2 German per the academy's general standard.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: CHECK — most likely YES, but with one conflicting signal. The programme-overview table requires only 'entsprechende Vorqualifikation, etwa mindestens ein Vordiplom oder Bachelor' with NO subject restriction, and no music degree is anywhere demanded — a BSc Software Engineering satisfies that on its face. However, the general application page summarises Diplomaufbaustudium entry as requiring a 'completed degree in a related field', which introduces a relatedness test that is not defined for Filmton. A software-engineering degree is plausibly 'related' to audio technology, but he must get this confirmed in writing before applying. The decisive filter in practice is the Pro Tools practical exam, not the bachelor subject.
_rec.portfolioSpec: PARTIAL. Own projects/work samples are uploaded via the online portal, and applicants must clearly identify their individual contribution to each. Published technical limits (example spec, varies by department): video up to 1 GB, MP4 container, H.264 codec, data rate 15 MB/s, typically 5–7 minutes maximum. The exact number and duration of AUDIO samples required for Filmton/Sounddesign is not published — UNVERIFIED. Also submit certified copies of the Hochschulreife and of any Vordiplom/Diplom/Bachelor/Master.
_rec.auditionSpec: YES — pre-selection on the file, then an on-site Aufnahmeprüfung conducted IN PRO TOOLS. Confirmed: 'Die Aufnahmeprüfung für Filmton/Sounddesign wird mit dem Programm Pro Tools durchgeführt. Bewerber*innen sollten daher Grundkenntnisse in den Disziplinen Aufnahme, Sounddesign, Mischung und Bouncing mitbringen.' There is NO instrumental audition and no music-theory paper — the gate is a DAW competence test. This is by far the most learnable audition of the six programmes here.
_rec.applicationOpens: The online portal opened 7 January in the current (2026) cycle. Expect a comparable early-January opening for the 2027 cycle — confirm.
_rec.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: 15 February, annually and without a year published on the programme page. The 2026 cycle ran with a portal opening on 7 January 2026 and the standard 15 February deadline (other departments had later dates: Motion Design 15 May 2026, Werbefilm Producing lateral entry 7 April 2026). For a 2027 start plan on 15 February 2027 and confirm when posted.
_rec.tuitionIntl: CORRECTED AND MORE EXPENSIVE THAN RECORDED: the €1,500 is PER SEMESTER, not a one-off. The academy's fee schedule is €0/semester for a first degree, €650/semester for a second degree or Projektstudium, and €1,500/semester for non-EU citizens, plus a €131.50 semester contribution for everyone. As a Tunisian national over 5 semesters that is roughly €7,500 in fees plus ~€658 in contributions — about €8,150 total, before living costs. The Diplomaufbaustudiengänge are exempt from the second-degree fee, but NOT from the non-EU fee.
_rec.fundingLevel: Partial at best — in practice closer to self-pay on fees (~€8,150 over 5 semesters) with no institutional funding found.
_rec.scholarship: None found at the academy. External only: DAAD Study Scholarships (Film/Fine Art strand), Deutschlandstipendium. DAAD/Tunisia eligibility NOT re-verified in this pass. Note that DAAD art/film scholarships generally target accredited degree programmes, so the non-master status of this Diplom should be checked against DAAD's eligibility rules before counting on it.
_rec.facilities: PARTIALLY VERIFIED via the curriculum: cinema film mixing and Dolby Atmos, Foley collaboration, film-music recording and mixing, on-set production-sound equipment, and DAW-based post-production suites are all taught, which confirms the corresponding facilities exist. Detailed room and console specifications UNVERIFIED. The academy is one of Europe's most production-active film schools with heavy German TV/film placement.
_rec.fitNotes: The most realistically ENTERABLE film-sound route in Germany for someone without a music degree — the gate is a Pro Tools practical test he can genuinely train for, not a conservatory audition or a theory paper, and no music bachelor is demanded. But verification worsened two things: the fee is €1,500 PER SEMESTER (~€8,150 total, no funding found), and the award is an institutional Diplom rather than an accredited master's. And it makes film and game sound designers, not DJs or producers. Only worth an application if he decides he genuinely wants a screen-audio career alongside producing, and only after confirming both the degree recognition and whether his SE bachelor counts as 'related'.
_rec.verificationNotes: Confirmed on official Filmakademie pages: the programme exists as a Diplomaufbaustudium in Filmton/Sounddesign awarding the Diplom der Filmakademie; 4 semesters + 1 diploma semester; German with English in Projektstudium; the curriculum including Dolby Atmos, Foley, dialogue editing and optional games-sound specialisation; the 15 February deadline (no year); the Pro Tools-based Aufnahmeprüfung with the required prior knowledge of recording, sound design, mixing and bouncing; the video work-sample technical spec (1 GB, MP4, H.264, 15 MB/s); the Hochschulreife requirement with the Begabtenpassus talent clause; B2 German as the academy standard; and the fee schedule. KEY CORRECTIONS: the non-EU fee is €1,500 PER SEMESTER plus €131.50 semester contribution (previously ambiguous), and the Diplom is officially described only as 'comparable to professional qualifying degrees' of state art universities rather than as an accredited master. NOT confirmed: ECTS, the audio work-sample count and duration, the 2027 portal opening date, whether a software-engineering BSc satisfies the 'related field' phrasing, and DAAD eligibility for a non-accredited Diplom.

_rec.whatYouStudy: Verified from the official call and the programme regulation. Two specialisations: SONIC ARTS (electroacoustic creation) and AUDIO TECHNOLOGIES (applied production). Stated aim: specialisation in the interdisciplinary area emerging from the intersection of electronic sound technology, sound art and music production, covering recording, processing and reproduction of sound in art and production. Structure: two semesters of taught modules combined with supervised practical/research work, then a third semester devoted entirely to the master's thesis. Article 7 of the regulation requires that AT LEAST 50% OF THE TOTAL TEACHING WORK consists of applied creative projects rather than theory — an unusually explicit practice guarantee.
_rec.entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree holders from relevant fields. The published list explicitly includes Music Studies, Music Science & Art, Audio & Visual Arts, Audiovisual Technologies, Film; AND on the technology side Music Technology & Acoustics, Physics, IT, Electronics, Electrical Engineering, Audio Technology and Engineering; AND Cultural Management, Cultural Technology & Communication, Mass Media. _rec.portfolioSpec: A portfolio is RECOMMENDED BUT NOT MANDATORY. No number of works, duration or format is prescribed. _rec.auditionSpec: No live audition. Candidates whose files are complete and meet the criteria proceed to an INTERVIEW before an evaluation committee, held either in person in Corfu OR ONLINE — remote-friendly. _rec.whatYouStudy: CONFIRMED programme description: one-to-one lessons with a composition teacher developing one's own compositions and analysing 20th- and 21st-century pieces; performance of orchestral and vocal final diploma pieces; composition-related special courses freely chosen by interest; master courses from visiting professors and artists; and explicitly "Possibility to deepen studies in the field of electronic music." _rec.entryRequirements: Bachelor diploma or higher. CONFIRMED verbatim: "Applicants must submit a preliminary credit recognition request directly to the Liszt Academy to determine whether the applicant's BA diploma can be accepted to apply for the programme, unless they have finished their BA studies at the Liszt Academy in the same field. Deadline: 31 March." Acceptable BA diplomas are defined in Annex 8 of the Academic Regulations for Students. An official Hungarian translation of the BA diploma is required by 31 March, made from the original document (not a copy); English translations are accepted during the application window only. Language certificate: TOEFL iBT min. 60, IELTS Academic min. 5.0, or Cambridge min. 154 — no other certificates accepted. A motivation letter is required. Applications route through the Stipendium Hungaricum portal or, for self-financed study, separately by 31 March.
_rec.portfolioSpec: MAJOR CORRECTION — this is far less classical than previously recorded. For the ELECTROACOUSTIC COMPOSITION specialisation, verbatim: "Presentation of a fixed electroacoustic music piece and another piece applying live electronics with an acoustic instrument", and "The pieces submitted together must not exceed 25-30 minutes." Style exercises for electroacoustic are: "1 short etude in the style of any significant 20th-century musique concrète composer" and "1 short etude in the style of significant 20th-century synthesis technique composer". THERE IS NO BACH FUGUE AND NO CLASSICAL SONATA REQUIREMENT for this specialisation — the fugue, the Viennese Classical sonata movement and the 20th-century etude apply ONLY to Classical and Applied Composition. Separately, the Stipendium Hungaricum course record states generically that applicants "are to upload sheet music of three of their own compositions (and recordings if possible)" and are first pre-screened on that portfolio — reconcile this generic wording with the specialisation-specific spec directly with the Academy.
_rec.auditionSpec: In person in Budapest, per the Academy's Stipendium Hungaricum page, verbatim: "All applicants are required to appear at the entrance examinations in person in Budapest, Hungary. The live entrance examinations cannot be substituted in any way", and on the SH course record: "Live streaming, video streaming, DVDs, CDs, or any other recordings are not accepted as a substitute." Exams take place late June / early July; candidates who clear the portfolio pre-screening are told their date during May. Components FOR ELECTROACOUSTIC specifically: formal analysis, written and oral, of a 20th-century instrumental work and an electroacoustic work; orchestration assessed as "MIDI sequencer orchestrating a chamber music piece for MIDI instruments or sampler" (not symphony-orchestra orchestration, which is the Classical track); score reading replaced by "Analysis of a contemporary graphic music notation"; a mandatory written test on the basics of electronic music (history from Varèse through Stockhausen, Xenakis, Chowning; sound parameters; waveform/spectrum/sonogram; sound types; tunings; sampling rate, Nyquist, bit depth; additive, subtractive, FM and granular synthesis); an oral practical computer task — mounting in ProTools or another DAW, algorithmic music in MAX/MSP or Pd, or sound synthesis in MAX/MSP, CSound, Pd or SuperCollider; and a personal interview on artistic beliefs, goals and general musical literacy. NOTE A CONTRADICTION: the admission-requirements page carries the heading "For applicants for the online entrance examination:", implying an online route exists, while the SH pages insist on in-person only. Resolve with international.office@lisztacademy.hu.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: Check — no longer a flat 'no', but genuinely uncertain and gated. Nothing formally bars a non-music BA, and the electroacoustic exam does NOT test classical composition craft. The binding gate is the mandatory preliminary credit recognition request, which decides "whether the applicant's BA diploma can be accepted to apply for the programme" against Annex 8 of the Academic Regulations — a software-engineering BSc may simply fail that check, and it is decided before the exam. The exam itself still assumes he can produce two credible electroacoustic works including one with live electronics and an acoustic instrument, write two style etudes, analyse 20th-century scores and graphic notation, and pass an electronic-music theory test. This is buildable in a year of hard work in a way a Bach fugue is not. Submit the credit recognition request early and treat its outcome as the go/no-go.

This is the only fully-funded, English-taught, Tunisia-eligible route in the slice, and the electroacoustic entrance exam turns out to be about electroacoustic craft, not classical conservatory training — no fugue, no sonata, no orchestral score reading, and the orchestration test is MIDI sequencing. Marketing prose: managing a music-production project through every phase, from creative idea to arrangement with real and virtual instruments, recording, mixing and mastering. The actual credit-weighted plan is: COMPOSIZIONE MUSICALE ELETTROACUSTICA I and II — 22 CFA each, by far the largest component; TECNOLOGIE E TECNICHE DELLA RIPRESA E DELLA REGISTRAZIONE 1 and II (6 CFA each) — the Music Producer specialisation strand, in which "ciascuno specializzando produrra' sotto la guida del docente due brani", taking two tracks from songwriting and pre-production (key, bpm, groove, feel, style) through arrangement with real and virtual instruments, rehearsals, recording and overdubbing in both a home and a commercial studio, microphone choice and placement, monitoring, executive production, mix and mastering, for himself and for third parties; TECNICHE COMPOSITIVE POP ROCK I and II (10 CFA each); ANALISI COMPOSITIVA (8) and FORME, SISTEMI E LINGUAGGI MUSICALI (8); STORIA DELLE TECNOLOGIE ELETTROACUSTICHE (8); DIRITTO D'AUTORE E ROYALTIES (5) covering copyright, royalties, licence, publishing, production and performance contracts; 6 CFA of free electives usable across any department; 9 CFA thesis and final work. Course page: "Diploma accademico triennale di primo livello già conseguito o da conseguirsi entro la sessione di Febbraio (iscrizione con riserva)". Official international-students page: "Accademici di II Livello: possono richiedere l'ammissione Cittadini UE o NON-UE in possesso del Diploma di Triennio universitario o accademico (o equivalente), ottenuto in Italia o nel proprio Paese di provenienza. È inoltre necessario dimostrare di avere un minimo di 15 anni di scolarizzazione." Degree must be submitted as a scanned original plus certified translation plus DOV (Dichiarazione di Valore) from the Italian embassy/consulate, or alternatively a CIMEA Diplome certificate. Attendance minimum 80% of classes; a part-time route exists. Erasmus+ mobility up to 12 months within the biennio. Non-EU applicants must ALSO run the parallel Universitaly pre-enrolment through the Italian diplomatic mission in Tunisia, which normally closes in July with no extensions; Saint Louis advises starting it no later than January/February.

And the official international-students page gives the applicable brief verbatim: "Composizione/Musica Elettronica/Musica Applicata: Prepara un link contenente il Portfolio (video, audio, spartiti) dei tuoi lavori più indicativi e recenti." That third element is a supervised FIVE-HOUR production test: build a track in two different versions, any style, from a supplied vocal. CRUCIAL for him: the international-students page states that for international candidates the admission tests "potranno essere sostenute online tra Gennaio e Giugno, in date da concordare individualmente" — online, individually scheduled, January to June; only if he chooses to sit them in person is there a single June session. Its own international-students page acknowledges only that non-EU students need a visa: 'If you are NOT a EU citizen, there are a few more requirements you have to consider in order to come study in the Netherlands, like obtaining a visa.' It then points applicants at generic government resources and at third-party agencies rather than offering any sponsorship. It makes NO claim to be an IND recognised sponsor, and as an unaccredited private provider it cannot be one — Dutch student residence permits require both a recognised-sponsor institution and accredited full-time higher education. So the school markets an international-students page, discusses housing and registration and health insurance for incoming foreigners, and then routes the one question that determines whether they can legally come at all to an outside agency. He could not obtain a student residence permit through this school.
_rec.reputationSignals: RED FLAGS DOMINATE, and re-checking did not improve the picture: no educational accreditation of any kind, not even CRKBO which its serious Dutch private competitors hold; NO PUBLISHED PRICE anywhere, for a one-year programme; no published syllabus, no teaching hours, no intake dates, no facility inventory, no equipment list; no named instructors, no alumni, no graduate outcomes; an audition required for the Advanced course with zero published specification; and an international-students page that markets to non-EU applicants while redirecting the visa question to a third-party agency. The 'Ableton and Steinberg certified diploma' is a vendor badge presented in the visual language of an educational credential, which invites exactly the wrong inference. POSITIVE, in fairness: the vendor certifications are real partner schemes and do indicate the trainers are approved by those manufacturers; the school runs a genuine studio; it maintains an English-language international page; and it is located in Rotterdam, a real music city. No published complaints were found — but there is also strikingly little published information of any kind.
_rec.recommendation: AVOID. This is the thinnest proposition in the slice. Verification this cycle added only two facts — that the Full Course runs one year, and that it leads to an Ableton/Steinberg VENDOR certificate — and both make the picture worse rather than better: he would be committing a full year, at an undisclosed price, to a course whose only credential is a software-manufacturer badge. Set against that: no accreditation, no price, no syllabus, no dates, no named staff, no visa. And note the asymmetry that matters most — it advertises to exactly his profile (non-EU international student) while being structurally incapable of sponsoring him and quietly handing the visa problem to an outside agency. Anything that does that deserves scepticism as a matter of principle. There is nothing available here that he cannot get better, cheaper, more transparently and with published pricing from DJ School Amsterdam, which quotes EUR 2,499 openly, teaches one-to-one in English, and can be done inside a tourist visa. Do not engage.

_rec.reputationSignals: Positive: genuine international brand with campuses in London, Los Angeles, San Francisco, Barcelona and Lisbon; official Ableton Certified Training Center; a well-structured 6-level curriculum with a fit-for-release EP as the deliverable; one-to-one mentoring; class sizes capped at eight; probable English-medium delivery; and prices that — contrary to the draft — ARE published. _rec.recommendation: AVOID — IT IS STRICTLY DOMINATED BY PRODJ ON EVERY VERIFIED MEASURE. Now that the real prices are established, the comparison is no longer close. Garnish Lisbon: €4,100–€4,600 for 120 hours, no Portuguese accreditation of any kind, no studio hours disclosed, no equipment list, no published dates, no visa. ProDJ: €2,955 for 200 hours PLUS 40 studio hours PLUS 20 LAB hours, in English, with real DGERT certification, a published equipment inventory and published start dates. He would pay roughly €1,500 MORE for 80 FEWER hours from the ONLY provider in this slice holding no Portuguese recognition whatsoever. Garnish's genuine advantages — capped class of eight, one-to-one mentoring, the EP deliverable, the Ableton brand — are real but nowhere near worth a 55% premium for 40% less contact time and strictly less institutional standing. Separately and emphatically: DO NOT ENTERTAIN THE BA (Hons) PATHWAY. Roughly €34,500 for a Level 6 top-up whose validating university Garnish declines to name, entered with 'no formal education required' and a phone interview, delivered mostly online, is the highest-risk item anywhere in this report and would be a catastrophic use of a budget-sensitive applicant's money. If for some reason he still wants Garnish, the minimum discipline is a written quotation naming the total, the registration fee, the instalment surcharge, the exact start dates, the delivery language, and — for the BA — the actual name of the awarding university. _rec.accreditationStatus: NOT OFFICIAL — AND WEAKER THAN EVERY OTHER PORTUGUESE ENTRY IN THIS BATCH. Garnish Lisbon holds NO Portuguese educational recognition: not A3ES-accredited, not DGES-registered, and — unlike ProDJ and EMMA — not even DGERT-certified as a vocational training provider. It is an unregulated commercial school in the Portuguese system. Its 'Ableton Certified Training Center' status is a software vendor's partner programme, awarded by Ableton the company, and carries no educational or governmental weight anywhere. Its certificates are its own paper. On the BA (Hons): it is a UK Level 6 top-up 'validated by one of our UK University partners' — the partner is NEVER NAMED on the page, which is disqualifying on its own. Even if genuine, it would be a UK award, not a Portuguese one, carrying no A3ES/DGES status and no Portuguese residence rights. Nothing Garnish offers in Lisbon is a mestrado, a pós-graduação, or a recognised Portuguese qualification of any kind.

In fact prices are published across several Lisbon pages and were verified directly: Electronic Music Producer Program (Ableton, 120h) €3,999 in person / €2,679 online; 360° Academy €12,999 + €500 registration (€200 if 14 days early); 36-hour Electronic Music Production course €1,299 + €100 registration / €803 online; private tuition €90/hr with 3-hour minimum AND a previously unreported 24-hour package at €1,560 (€65/hr); iMac rental supplement €75. Structurally he also fails on the merits: a DGERT vocational certificate from a non-higher-education academy is not a recognised visa-sponsoring category, and 10 months falls short of the 12-month threshold for a D4 study residence visa. HE CANNOT MOVE TO PORTUGAL ON THIS.
_rec.reputationSignals: Positive and genuinely relevant: DGERT certification is real and verifiable, and ProDJ's claim to be the only DGERT-certified DJ/production academy in Portugal appears sound; instructors hold CCP pedagogical credentials; two physical campuses; a published, credible equipment inventory (Moog, Roland, Adam, Focal, Pioneer, Technics); 40 included studio hours; confirmed English-language delivery; fixed March/September intakes rather than chaotic rolling starts; and a syllabus squarely aimed at electronic music and DJing — which is what he actually wants. Negative: age-14 minimum and zero selection; the 'Master Producer' name invites precisely the confusion this report exists to prevent; a separate €45 charge to issue the diploma; an enrolment fee that varies by payment method and is quoted INCONSISTENTLY across ProDJ's own pages (€420 here, €520 on the Producer I page) — a small but real sign of loose administration; a 10-month payment plan that raises the total by up to €710 without this being flagged; a headline IRS tax-deduction benefit that is worthless to a non-resident; and no independent graduate-outcome data, no named alumni, no placement statistics.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: €2,955 all-in paying upfront or on the 4-instalment plan (tuition €2,490 + enrolment €420 + diploma €45). Up to roughly €3,665 on the 10-month plan. Living costs dominate and are unfunded: Lisbon or Porto at roughly €900–€1,300/month for 10 months adds €9,000–€13,000, giving a realistic all-in of €12,000–€16,600 — with no visa, no scholarship and no legal study status attached to any of it.
_rec.recommendation: CLOSEST TO WHAT HE WANTS TO DO, FURTHEST FROM WHAT HE NEEDS INSTITUTIONALLY — and it verifies better than the draft assumed. Three things improved on verification: delivery in ENGLISH is confirmed by ProDJ itself, the equipment inventory is real and respectable (Moog, Roland, Adam, Focal, Pioneer, Technics), and the 4-instalment plan costs no more than paying upfront. On content, price and language this is the strongest hands-on electronic-music training in Portugal for the money: €2,955 for 200 hours plus 40 studio hours plus 20 LAB hours, in English, with no entry barrier and no IELTS. But three things are unchanged and decisive: it is NOT a master's despite its name, it confers NO academic credit, and it CANNOT get him a residence permit — ProDJ's own page requires him to arrive already holding a valid visa. Paying €12,000+ including living costs to sit in Lisbon on a tourist footing with no legal study status is not a plan. THE RATIONAL SEQUENCE IS THE INVERSE: use an accredited master's (UCP Porto, Lusófona, or a funded ReSound place) to obtain the D4 visa and residence permit, then, once legally resident, add ProDJ's Master Producer as a €2,955 evening top-up in English while his status is secure. Never the other way round. One practical instruction: before paying anything, make ProDJ confirm in writing the enrolment fee (their own pages say €420 and €520), whether a DAW licence is included, and the exact total.
_rec.accreditationStatus: NOT OFFICIAL HIGHER EDUCATION — and it is important he understands what DGERT is and is not. ProDJ is certified by DGERT (Direção-Geral do Emprego e das Relações de Trabalho), which sits under the LABOUR ministry and regulates VOCATIONAL TRAINING PROVIDERS. It is a legitimate quality mark for professional training and it is not a scam — but it is NOT an educational accreditation. Specifically: this is NOT accredited by A3ES (Agência de Avaliação e Acreditação do Ensino Superior) and is NOT registered with DGES (Direção-Geral do Ensino Superior), the two bodies that make a Portuguese qualification a recognised higher-education degree. Consequences: no grau académico, no ECTS, no place in the EHEA/Bologna framework, no automatic recognition abroad, no route onward to a PhD, and no standing in a visa assessment. It is not a 'mestrado' and it is not even a 'pós-graduação' — it is below both. It is a vocational training certificate, correctly labelled, from a properly certified vocational provider.
_rec.verificationNotes: Official course page fetched and verified in full. CONFIRMED unchanged: €2,490 tuition, €420 enrolment, €45 diploma fee, 200 hours over 10 months, age-14 minimum, 40 studio hours + 20 LAB hours, DGERT certification, CCP-credentialled instructors. CORRECTED OR NEWLY ESTABLISHED: (1) English-language delivery CONFIRMED by ProDJ's international students page — the draft had this UNVERIFIED, and it is the single most consequential upgrade; (2) the 4-instalment plan totals €2,490, identical to upfront — the draft wrongly implied all instalment routes cost more; only the 10-month plan does; (3) full hour breakdown established as 140h in-person + 40h studio + 20h LAB; (4) DAWs are Ableton Live, FL Studio AND Logic Pro, not Ableton alone; (5) a real equipment inventory is published (Moog, Roland, Adam, Focal, Pioneer, Technics, MacBook Air/Mac Mini) — the draft marked facilities UNVERIFIED; (6) intakes are TWO fixed windows (March/September), not fully rolling, with exact 2026–2027 start dates published through March 2027 and September 2027 NOT yet published; (7) NEW FINDING — the advertised '30% IRS tax deduction' is worthless to a non-resident non-taxpayer and must not be counted as a saving; (8) the visa position is now confirmed from ProDJ's own wording, which requires the student to ALREADY hold a valid passport or visa — ProDJ sponsors nothing. STILL UNVERIFIED: whether a DAW licence is included, insurance/materials fees, and the reason the enrolment fee is quoted as €420 here but €520 on the Producer I page. The English-language master-producer page (prodj.pt/en/academy/master-producer-course/) returned a bot-verification interstitial and could not be cross-read.

_rec.otherFees: CORRECTED from 'not published'. Published figures: administrative fee 1,000 RSD payable with the enrolment documents; on enrolment all students must pay a 20% deposit (akontacija) — EUR 900 for this programme — plus a further 20% as the first instalment, no later than 1 October; enrolling after 1 September requires 40% of the tuition up front; the remaining balance runs as 11 monthly instalments of EUR 327.27 with no interest. DISCOUNT: candidates who enrol preliminarily and pay the 20% deposit by 31 March receive a 10% tuition discount, valid for the first year of studies only, and discounts cannot be combined. Nostrification/recognition of his Tunisian diploma is required and is charged separately by the recognising body. Health-insurance cost for foreign students — UNVERIFIED.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: EUR 4,500 tuition for the one-year 60-ECTS master, or about EUR 4,050 with the 31 March early-payment discount, plus ~1,000 RSD administrative fee and separate diploma-recognition costs, before living costs in Belgrade, visa and health insurance. If his degree is 180 ECTS he must first fund a fourth bachelor year at Metropolitan, which on the published bachelor table runs EUR 2,990–3,990 depending on programme — pushing the realistic total past EUR 7,000–8,500. Against the state Academy of Arts Novi Sad at EUR 1,800 for a comparable one-year MAS, this is roughly 2.5x on tuition alone. It fails his 'self-pay only if genuinely cheap' test.
_rec.fundingLevel: None. A private university with no state-budget places. The only published price reductions are the 10% early-payment discount and interest-free instalments — neither is a scholarship.
_rec.scholarships: CONFIRMED: nothing a Tunisian master applicant can win. Re-checked the official Stipendije page. What exists: (1) competition-based full four-year bachelor scholarships for Serbian secondary-school pupils; (2) internal merit scholarships for existing Metropolitan undergraduates in years 2–4, six per year, one per faculty per year level, with fourth-years able to continue tuition-free into a master; (3) a dual-education package created with A+Crowd of Toronto offering free study, EUR 100/month and a guaranteed job, aimed at school-leavers entering IT, management or design. None is open to an incoming foreign master applicant in music production. Anything else would have to be negotiated directly with upis@metropolitan.ac.rs.
_rec.visaEligible: Yes in principle, and the case is stronger than the previous record suggested. The programme is a nationally registered accredited MAS (NAT register entry 53, 03.06.2025) at a licensed university, and — importantly for a residence permit — it is accredited for TRADITIONAL IN-PERSON delivery only, with no distance-learning variant, so it is not an online degree that immigration authorities would refuse. That is the class of enrolment that supports a Serbian temporary residence permit for education. A Tunisian needs a long-stay visa D before travel. The university still publishes nothing about visa support or an international-student office — UNVERIFIED at that level; confirm with the Serbian Ministry of Interior (MUP) and the Serbian embassy accredited to Tunisia before paying anything, and ask the university who handles foreign-student enrolment. Serbia is outside the EU/Schengen.
_rec.intakes: Rolling. The official admission page states master enrolment 'može se izvršiti bez ograničenja tokom čitave godine'. The Serbian academic year starts in October and the payment schedule is anchored to 1 October, so an October 2027 start is the natural target.
_rec.applicationOpens: Rolling, online via the university's application portal. After the online application the candidate receives procedural instructions and submits scanned diploma and transcript; the file then goes to the faculty commission, which issues individual admission conditions and any differential exams. Practical planning date: pay the 20% deposit by 31 March 2027 to secure the 10% discount for a 2027/28 start.
_rec.deadline: No published application deadline — rolling admission. The binding dates are financial and immigration ones, not academic: 20% deposit plus 20% first instalment by 1 October; 40% up front if enrolling after 1 September; 31 March for the 10% early-payment discount; and, dominating all of these, the visa D and residence-permit timeline plus the diploma-nostrification timeline, which he should start at least six months ahead.
_rec.recommendation: This record needed substantial correction and the programme comes out of it looking better on paper and worse in practice than the previous assessment implied. Three corrections he must hear. FIRST, the previous warning that the price is unknown and probably higher for a non-EU national is WRONG: Metropolitan's own admission rules state that foreign nationals enrol under the same conditions and the same tuition-financing conditions as Serbian citizens, so he pays EUR 4,500 — the published figure, not a mystery. SECOND, the claim that admission requirements are unpublished is also WRONG: they are published in detail, and they are more accommodating than anything at Novi Sad — 240 ECTS required but with an explicit route for a 180-ECTS three-year graduate to complete a fourth Metropolitan bachelor year first; non-cognate first degrees expressly admitted via commission-set differential exams; no entrance exam; no portfolio; rolling admission; full document list published. THIRD, the accreditation is now nailed down: NAT register, accredited 3 June 2025, approved intake 20, in-person Serbian delivery. So it is a real, state-recognised, visa-supporting second-cycle degree — the AVOID verdict reserved for master-priced non-degrees does not apply. What actually blocks him is language and money, not admissions. The programme is accredited for Serbian-language in-person delivery only — the register carries no English-language flag, unlike Metropolitan's own IT and business masters — so an Arabic/French/English speaker cannot follow it in September 2027. And EUR 4,500 (EUR 4,050 with the March discount), or EUR 7,000+ if he must buy a fourth bachelor year first, is 2.5x the state Academy in Novi Sad for a private-university degree with no scholarship he can win. Action if he still wants it: one e-mail to upis@metropolitan.ac.rs asking (a) to confirm in writing that the EUR 4,500 rate applies to a Tunisian national given that the price table is headed for Serbian and ex-SFRY citizens, (b) whether his specific BSc counts as 240 ECTS or requires the fourth-year route, (c) how many differential exams a software-engineering graduate would be set, (d) whether any part of the programme can be followed in English, and (e) whether they issue the enrolment documents needed for a Serbian study visa D.

_rec.program: Máster en Producción Musical Discográfica e Ingeniería de Sonido — Oficial de AVID (MPD)
_rec.institution: CICE — La Escuela Profesional de Nuevas Tecnologías
_rec.institutionType: Private technology and creative-industries training school; authorised vendor-certification centre (Avid, Waves)
_rec.qualification: A CICE private professional certificate branded 'Máster', bundled with software-vendor certifications (Avid Pro Tools, Waves Level A). No university validation, no ECTS, 300 teaching hours.
_rec.accreditationStatus: NOT OFFICIAL — and the naming is actively misleading. The word 'Oficial' in the title 'Máster ... - Oficial de AVID' means OFFICIAL AVID CERTIFICATION, a software-vendor credential, NOT Spanish academic accreditation. There is no ANECA verification, no validating university, no ECTS, no EHEA status and no PhD access. Independent confirmation of its nature: the Emagister listing describes the outcome as conferring professional specialisation status 'rather than an academic degree'. It is a private certificate course. The decisive new number is the DURATION: 300 teaching hours (with roughly 600 hours of total student dedication). A genuine 60-ECTS master implies about 1,500 hours. At 300 taught hours this is one-fifth the size of the cheapest real master in this batch — it is a short course wearing the word 'máster'.
_rec.visaEligible: NO. At 300 teaching hours with 'fechas a elegir' (self-chosen scheduling), this cannot deliver the 20 contact hours per week over more than 90 days that a Spanish estancia por estudios requires — 300 hours at 20 h/week is only 15 weeks, and CICE's flexible-dates model means it is typically taken at a far lower weekly intensity. It is also offered FULLY ONLINE, and an online course carries no visa value whatsoever (Spain requires at least 50% in-person). Nothing about non-EU student visas is published anywhere by CICE. Treat as a definitive no.
_rec.focus: Record production and sound engineering: sound capture, processors, mixing architecture, mastering and genre-specific mixing, wrapped around vendor certification. Studio-engineering oriented, NOT DJ or electronic-music oriented.
_rec.whatYouStudy: Ten modules, VERIFIED: (1) Sound and Capture; (2) Processors and Production Phases; (3) Capture History and Advanced Techniques; (4) Analysis Keys for Productions; (5) Introduction to Mixing and Mastering; (6) Mixer History and Studio Performance Optimisation; (7) Mixing Architecture; (8) Dynamic Control and 3D Depth Mixing; (9) Official Waves Level A Certification; (10) Mixing According to Musical Styles. Note what is ABSENT: no synthesis, no sound design, no composition, no live performance, no DJ technique, no music business.
_rec.durationEcts: 300 teaching hours, with approximately 600 hours of total student dedication. No ECTS published. NEWLY VERIFIED — the input recorded duration as entirely unknown.
_rec.language: Spanish, with 'elementary English competency' listed as an entry requirement.
_rec.intakes: 'Fechas a elegir' (dates chosen by the student) — a flexible, rolling model rather than a cohort intake. The Emagister listing currently shows enrolment CLOSED for the in-person Madrid option. Available both in-person in Madrid and fully online.
_rec.entryRequirements: Published prerequisites are technical, not academic, and VERIFIED: 'Conocimientos de Sistema Operativo Mac, nivel usuario'; 'Conocimientos de Protools u otra plataforma similar, nivel usuario'; and basic English proficiency. No degree requirement of any kind is stated.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: YES — trivially. No academic or music prerequisite exists at all; the bar is Mac OS and Pro Tools user-level familiarity, which a software-engineering graduate clears immediately. But read this the right way: a programme with NO degree requirement whatsoever is not a postgraduate qualification in any meaningful sense, whatever it is called.
_rec.portfolioSpec: None.
_rec.auditionSpec: None.
_rec.englishTest: No IELTS. 'Elementary English competency' is a stated entry requirement (for vendor documentation), but instruction is in Spanish.
_rec.applicationOpens: Rolling / 'fechas a elegir'. In-person Madrid enrolment currently shown as closed.
_rec.deadline: No published deadline. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new dates; the Lectiva listing still shows a May 2018 start date, which is how stale some of this school's published data is.
_rec.tuitionPerYear: €4,233 including IVA, per the Emagister listing, which notes this reflects a 17% discount already applied — so an undiscounted list price near €5,100 is implied, which reconciles the two conflicting figures previously on file. CICE's own website returned HTTP 403 and could not be checked. Treat as best-available but not officially confirmed.
_rec.tuitionTotal: €4,233 (IVA included, after a 17% discount) for the 300-hour programme. Undiscounted list price appears to be around €5,100. No separate non-EU rate is published. UNVERIFIED against CICE directly.
_rec.otherFees: CONFLICTING EVIDENCE, resolve before paying. The Emagister listing states the certifications are included, naming both the 'Certificación Oficial de Waves Level A' and official AVID certification as part of the programme. A separate source indicated the price includes Waves Level A but NOT the Avid Pro Tools certifications. Since those vendor exams are the programme's entire selling point, this ambiguity is material — insist on a written statement naming every exam included and every exam billed separately, with amounts. Application, enrolment and materials fees UNVERIFIED.
_rec.equipmentRequired: Mac OS proficiency is an entry requirement, strongly implying a Mac is expected (€1,300+). Pro Tools familiarity is expected on entry, implying a licence he must already hold. Neither cost is published or included.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: Roughly €4,233 for the course itself, plus a Mac and a Pro Tools subscription, plus possibly unbundled certification exam fees. As a route to Spain the figure is moot — it cannot support a visa, so Madrid living costs do not arise. As a skills purchase for someone already resident: €4,200–€6,000 all in.
_rec.paymentPlans: UNVERIFIED — none published. The 17% discount embedded in the advertised price suggests promotional pricing is routine and therefore negotiable.
_rec.scholarships: UNVERIFIED — none published, and nothing for non-EU applicants.
_rec.facilities: Madrid, Calle Maldonado 48, 28006. CICE is a genuinely authorised training centre for a range of vendor certifications including Avid and Waves — that part of the offer is real. Studio inventory UNVERIFIED.
_rec.reputationSignals: POSITIVE: long-established Madrid technology-training school; genuine authorised-certification status with Avid and Waves; forum discussion of its sound programmes is broadly positive on value for money and teaching staff. RED FLAGS, and they are serious: the 'Oficial de AVID' naming reads as academic accreditation and is not; the programme is only 300 taught hours yet is marketed as a 'máster'; published prices are stale and inconsistent across aggregators (one listing still advertises a May 2018 start); the school's own website is not publicly reachable for verification; certification exam inclusion is ambiguous; and an online delivery option is sold under the same 'máster' name with zero visa or campus value.
_rec.recommendation: AVOID as anything to do with his move to Spain. This is a 300-hour vendor-certification bootcamp with the word 'máster' attached and the word 'Oficial' borrowed from Avid's marketing rather than from ANECA. It cannot support a student visa — 300 hours cannot produce 20 contact hours a week over 90+ days, and it is sold online as readily as in person. It is also aimed at the wrong craft: pure studio engineering, with no synthesis, no sound design, no composition, no live performance and no DJ content anywhere in the ten modules. For a software engineer who wants Pro Tools and Waves credentials cheaply it has genuine, narrow utility — but that is a €4,000 skills purchase for someone already living in Madrid, not a postgraduate route into Europe for a Tunisian graduate. If he ever does pursue it, insist first on a current written price stating exactly which certification exams are included, because the advertised figure already carries a 17% discount and the exam bundling is contradicted between sources.

CICE's own site (cice.es) returned HTTP 403 and could not be verified directly — this is the main gap. DECISIVE NEW FINDING: duration is 300 teaching hours (~600 hours total student dedication), previously recorded as entirely unverified. That single figure resolves the programme's character — it is roughly one-fifth the size of a 60-ECTS master and makes visa eligibility impossible, upgrading the assessment from 'unverified/doubtful' to a firm NO. A BSc Software Engineering therefore enters through the discretionary route: "Applicants with other backgrounds will be assessed individually by the Study Board of Media Technology." His case is strong on the substance - he will comfortably clear the Programming (min 10 ECTS) competency and can likely argue media technologies and/or UX design from his coursework - but it is an individual assessment, not an entitlement. He should email mediatek-studvejlcph@create.aau.dk with his transcript in autumn 2026 for a pre-assessment.

_rec.program: Medialogy (Copenhagen) — MSc, with specialisation in Sound and Music Computing (CORRECTION: NOT closed — it survives as a specialisation, not a standalone degree)
_rec.university: Aalborg University (AAU), Copenhagen campus
_rec.degree: MSc (cand.scient. in Medialogy). Sound and Music Computing is an officially published specialisation chosen after the 1st semester — the diploma is Medialogy, the specialisation is the track.
_rec.durationEcts: 2 years / 120 ECTS (4 semesters). Confirmed on the official page: "Specialiseringen i Sound and Music Computing på Aalborg Universitet består af fire semestre (120 ECTS-point)".
_rec.focus: Sound Design + Immersive Audio + Electronic/interactive audio (sonic interaction design, spatial audio for VR/AR, machine learning for sound). This is the CS-to-audio bridge — engineering and interaction-design framing, not music-conservatory craft.
_rec.institutionType: Public university (problem-based learning / group project model)
_rec.language: English. Confirmed: the Medialogy Copenhagen page lists "Engelsk" as Sprog, and the specialisation page states "2-årig specialisering / Engelsk". (The AAU website itself is Danish; teaching is English.)
_rec.tuitionIntl: 57,850 DKK / EUR 7,745 PER SEMESTER for non-EU/EEA students, listed explicitly as "Medialogy (Copenhagen)" in the official 2026 tuition table. That is roughly EUR 30,980 / 231,400 DKK for the full 2-year degree. Plus a non-refundable application fee of EUR 150 (1,150 DKK) for non-EU/EEA applicants, which covers up to 3 AAU applications and is refunded if he enrols.
_rec.fundingLevel: Full (competitive, scarce) or None. There is no partial tier.
_rec.scholarship: Danish Government Scholarships administered by AAU. Official wording: "Each September intake, Aalborg University grants a limited number of scholarships to individually selected applicants from non-EU/EEA countries based on strategic considerations and academic qualifications... All non-EU applicants are automatically considered when applying to a master's programme. Therefore, it is not possible to apply for a scholarship separately." A Tunisian national is eligible. BUT: "approximately 15 each year" for the ENTIRE university, and AAU explicitly warns "We do not advise you to rely solely on receiving a scholarship".
_rec.stipend: A scholarship = full tuition-fee waiver PLUS a monthly living stipend. 2026 rate: 11,225 DKK / EUR 1,503 per month, paid for four semesters. Possibly taxable. Decision communicated by early July at the latest; if he has already paid tuition it is refunded.
_rec.entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree. Three bachelors are pre-approved as directly qualifying: BSc Medialogy (Aalborg or Copenhagen) and BSc Engineering (Electronic Engineering / Electronic Systems Engineering) at AAU. Everyone else is individually assessed against explicit ECTS thresholds: "Minimum 10 ECTS i Programming", "Minimum 10 ECTS i technical knowledge behind media technologies", "Minimum 10 ECTS i methods within Interaction Design/User Experience Design". CRITICAL WARNING, quoted: "Bemærk, at det ikke er muligt at supplere fag for at opfylde adgangskravene" — it is NOT possible to take top-up courses to meet the entry requirements. Also: no pre-assessment is offered ("Der foretages ikke forhåndsvurderinger"). English at Danish B-level required, evidenced by upper-secondary certificate or an accepted English test. The programme is capacity-capped (adgangsbegrænset): Medialogy Copenhagen offered 33 places in 2025, and qualified applicants are ranked by (1) bachelor grades, (2) a max 1-page English statement of relevance/motivation and knowledge of the programme — where he may indicate he wants the Sound and Music Computing specialisation, and (3) documented relevant activity such as work experience in IT, media production, programming, sound or film.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: Yes — emphatically. This is an engineering/media-technology master and no music qualification is asked for anywhere. The risk runs the other way: his BSc Software Engineering will clear the 10 ECTS Programming bar easily, but he must be able to point to 10 ECTS of media-technology content AND 10 ECTS of Interaction Design / UX methods in his SMU MedTech transcript, and he cannot make up a shortfall afterwards. He should map his transcript against those three lines before anything else.
_rec.portfolioSpec: No creative portfolio required. The only written submission is the ranking-criterion statement: an English text of maximum 1 page covering relevance to his future career goals, his reasons for applying, and his knowledge of the programme — plus documentation of relevant activities/work experience. Uploads: bachelor diploma and full transcript (or transcript to date if not yet graduated), and English B-level documentation.
_rec.auditionSpec: None. No audition, no interview, no on-site test. Selection is entirely on documents and grade ranking.
_rec.applicationOpens: The application portal (Ansøgningsportalen) opens "medio december" — mid-December — for the following September intake. For a September 2027 start that means roughly mid-December 2026. This is a published standing rule, not a one-off date.
_rec.deadline: 1 March at 23:59 for a September start — published as a standing annual rule on AAU's official 'Ansøgning og frister' page ("Du skal søge senest den 1. marts kl. 23.59, hvis du vil optages til september"), with decisions by 10 June at the latest and any leftover places advertised mid-June on a first-come-first-served basis. So for September 2027: apply by 1 March 2027. Re-confirm in late 2026, but this is a stable rule rather than a lapsed cycle date. He may apply to a maximum of 3 AAU masters per intake.
_rec.whatYouStudy: Semester 1: project 'Adaptive Media Systems' plus 'Machine Learning for Media Experiences', choosing two electives from Sound and Music Perception and Cognition (recommended for this specialisation), Real-Time Computer Graphics, Mobile and Wearable Computing, Narratives in Interactive Systems. Semester 2: project 'Immersive Sonic Experiences' plus the course 'Sonic Interaction Design', with two electives from Multi-Sensory Interaction and Media Cognition, Signal Processing for Interactive Systems, Embodied Interaction, Spatial User Interfaces, Game Research and Development. Semester 3: a company internship, DADIU Game Production (the Danish national game-production programme), a regular project, or a semester abroad. Semester 4: thesis only. Everything is problem-based group project work. Honest framing for him: this is audio ENGINEERING and interaction design — spatial audio, VR/AR sound, AI for sound, new interfaces for musical expression — not beat-making, mixing records or DJ craft.
_rec.facilities: The Multi-sensory Experience Lab is attached to the programme and is named on the official page in a student testimonial as offering "ekstraordinære faciliteter" for spatial audio in VR. Named employer/industry pipeline on the official page: Bang & Olufsen, T-Rex Engineering, IO Interactive, Carl Martin, Dicentia. Semester 3 can be spent inside DADIU, the Danish national game-production consortium.
_rec.fitNotes: The previous entry's claim that this programme is dead is WRONG and must be corrected before he sees it. The old standalone smc.aau.dk / 'Sound and Music Computing' master URL does redirect into AAU's 'programmes without admission' area, which is what caused the false negative — but the content has moved: it is now a live 2-year, 120-ECTS, English-taught specialisation inside the MSc Medialogy at the Copenhagen campus, and it is open for application. This remains the single most natural destination in this whole slice for a computer-science graduate who wants to work in sound. Two real obstacles: (1) the hard ECTS gate — 10 ECTS each of programming, media technology and interaction design/UX, with no possibility of topping up, and no pre-assessment, so he is guessing until he submits; (2) money — EUR 7,745 per semester, about EUR 31,000 all in, with the only escape being one of roughly 15 government scholarships awarded across the whole university, which do at least pay tuition in full plus about EUR 1,500 a month. It will not, on its own, make him a DJ or a record producer; it will make him someone who can build audio technology and design interactive sound.
_rec.verificationNotes: sourceUrl CORRECTED. Verified directly on the live official AAU pages: the specialisation page (curriculum, 120 ECTS, English, entry ECTS thresholds, ranking criteria, 33 places), the parent Medialogy Copenhagen page (Copenhagen, English, 2 years, September start), AAU's official master admission-and-deadlines page (1 March deadline, portal opens mid-December, decision by 10 June), and AAU's official English 'Finance and fees' page (Medialogy Copenhagen listed at 57,850 DKK / EUR 7,745 per semester for 2026; EUR 150 application fee; Danish Government Scholarship terms and the 11,225 DKK monthly stipend rate). Not verified: whether the 33-place cap is unchanged for 2027, and whether his specific SMU MedTech transcript satisfies the media-technology and interaction-design ECTS lines — AAU refuses pre-assessment, so this can only be resolved by applying or by emailing the study board.

SECOND ROUND: a single public oral interview IN PARIS, max 30 min, coefficient 4, between Mon 15 and Fri 26 June 2026, covering culture, tastes, experience and projects, the earlier tests, and the note de synthèse / motivation letter / portfolio. Core studies: computer music, recording studio, acoustics and psychoacoustics, sound synthesis. Electives are drawn from multimedia, music performance, engineering and computer science — which is exactly where his software engineering background becomes an asset rather than a liability. Teaching staff span music performance and composition, art, multimedia, business, electronic engineering and computer programming, with integration discussed in computer-music classes and industry seminars. So 6.5 with no band below 6.0 is the PROBABLE requirement and the safe planning assumption, but it is NOT verified for Cork, and there is a real possibility this CS-and-engineering-adjacent programme falls under Level 1 at 6.0/5.5. MTU's own page adds: 'Please note some programmes have a higher requirement in English Language. You should contact the International Office for further details.' It is an unambiguously accredited NFQ Level 9, 90-ECTS master's from an Irish public university, it costs €13,500 (less than half Queen's and cheaper than the UK options even after their scholarships), it is taught in English, it explicitly offers RPL to applicants without a relevant honours degree, its electives are drawn from engineering and computer science so his BSc is an asset, and it supports an Irish student permission plus post-study stay-back. _rec.qualification: VERIFIED. "Diploma Accademico di II livello in Sound Design, titolo riconosciuto dal Ministero dell'Universita e della Ricerca (MUR)". This is the OFFICIAL second-cycle Italian award (120 CFA, laurea magistrale equivalent). It is NOT a 'Master universitario di I/II livello' and NOT a private certificate. Saint Louis itself operates BOTH kinds of award, so read the label carefully: at this school the 'Biennio di II livello' is the HIGHER qualification and the 'Master di I livello' is the lower one.
_rec.institutionType: Private specialist music academy (Saint Louis Music Center srl), MUR-authorised AFAM institution. Founded 1976, ~1,800 students/year. Main campus via Baccina 47 Rome, plus via Urbana 49/a, via Boschetto 102/106, via Cimarra 19/b; second site in Milan (viale L. Bodio 37).
_rec.accreditationStatus: OFFICIAL - fully verified with decree numbers. The institution page states: "Il Saint Louis College of Music e la prima istituzione privata autorizzata dal Ministero dell'Universita e della Ricerca a rilasciare Diplomi Accademici di I e II livello, equipollenti alle lauree triennali e magistrali e con lo stesso valore dei Diplomi di Conservatorio", and "L'autorizzazione ministeriale, formalizzata con i decreti n. 144 del 1 agosto 2012 e n. 246 del 28 marzo 2013". Additional signals: AEC (Association Europeenne des Conservatoires) member since 2012; ISO 9001; accredited with Regione Lazio as a vocational training body; MIUR recognition path from 2005. In practice: EHEA-valid, valid for AFAM III-level/doctoral entry, valid for Universitaly pre-enrolment and a type-D study visa.
_rec.focus: Sound design and audio post-production for cinema, TV series, gaming, animation, media and advertising; plus audio restoration/remastering and forensic audio.
_rec.durationEcts: 2 years. Year 2 = Restauro II 6, Sound Design II 20, Campionamento e post produzione audio 8, Wwise II 8, Ripresa e registrazione II 12, Materie elettive 3 (the final thesis credits are not itemised in the published table). Nominal AFAM total 120 CFA. Fortnightly lessons concentrated in two consecutive days - compatible with part-time work.

The foreign degree must be submitted as a scanned original plus certified translation plus a Dichiarazione di Valore from the Italian Embassy/Consulate, OR a CIMEA Diplome statement.
_rec.auditionSpec: MAJOR CORRECTION - this is the single most important finding for this candidate. Sound Design sits in the TECNICO DEL SUONO department (DCSL61), and the international admissions page states explicitly: "Per il Corso di Tecnico del Suono non e prevista pre-selezione ma un colloquio attitudinale." There is NO portfolio pre-selection and NO performance video. The official piano di studi gives the full admission exam as: "1) Colloquio attitudinale. 2) Test scritto a risposte multiple incentrato sui seguenti argomenti: Fondamenti di audio digitale, Pro Tools, Riprese microfoniche, Protocollo MIDI." That is a studiable technical exam, not an artistic audition.

The portfolio route ("Prepara un link contenente il Portfolio (video, audio, spartiti) dei tuoi lavori piu indicativi e recenti") applies to the Composizione / Musica Elettronica / Musica Applicata family, NOT to Tecnico del Suono. This corrects the earlier draft, which wrongly attached the portfolio requirement to Sound Design.
_rec.englishTest: No IELTS or TOEFL requirement is published anywhere - not on the course page, not on the international students page, and not in the official International Students Guide PDF. Language ability (English or Italian) is assessed in the colloquio attitudinale. Confirm in writing with the international office, but on the published evidence he does NOT need IELTS for this programme.
_rec.whatYouStudy: Sound Design I/II (recording, construction and manipulation of sound effects for film, TV series, games and media; Pro Tools and post-production plug-in workflow); Audio Interattivo non Lineare with Audiokinetic Wwise I/II (sound implementation, events, spatialisation, non-linear mixing, game-engine integration); Campionamento e post produzione audio (custom sample-library building, instruments, modulators, envelopes, mapping); Tecnologie e tecniche del Restauro Audio I/II (digitisation of historic media, remastering, forensic audio); Tecnologie e tecniche della ripresa e della registrazione audio I/II; Storia del Sound Design e della post produzione audio; 9 CFA of free-choice electives across any department. Original projects developed with the Composizione and Musica Applicata alle immagini departments and with RUFA and Vigamus (Rome video-game museum).
_rec.facilities: Rome recording studios across four operational sites; Pro Tools-centred workflow; Saint Louis in-house record labels that release the best student work to international streaming platforms; Erasmus+ partner since 2012; AEC network; separate Dolby Atmos, Pro Tools 101/110 certification, Djing, Electronic Music Producer and 'Techno 360' short courses purchasable alongside; UniPlaces and StuRent accommodation conventions; dedicated International Office (Marzia Bagli) plus a buddy system and International Orientation Day.
_rec.tuitionPerYear: VERIFIED EXACTLY on the official Iscrizione page, INTERNATIONAL rate (defined as "uno studente di nazionalita EU (non italiana) o NON-EU residente all'Estero al momento dell'iscrizione"), column ACCADEMICO II LIVELLO: Very Early Bird 7.230,00 EUR; Early Bird 7.650,00 EUR; Regular Upfront 7.900,00 EUR; Regular 3 installments 8.500,00 EUR. The separate ISEE income-banded table is headed "SOLO STUDENTI ITALIANI" - a Tunisian applicant CANNOT use it.
_rec.tuitionTotal: Two years at the international rate: 14,460 EUR (Very Early Bird both years) to 17,000 EUR (Regular 3 instalments both years). These are the currently published rates (a.a. 2026/27 cycle). PRIOR CYCLE for a September 2027 start - expect a modest increase and re-confirm.
_rec.otherFees: VERIFIED on the Iscrizione page: quota annuale di iscrizione 240,00 EUR if paid by 30 May, 290,00 EUR thereafter (explicitly non-refundable - "il Pagamento della Tassa d'Iscrizione (240/290 EUR) non e rimborsabile"); one-off second-level diploma exam fee 500,00 EUR; annual out-of-course (fuori corso) fee 380,00 EUR; annual regional Diritto allo studio tax 140,00 EUR paid to Regione Lazio via LazioDisco. CORRECTION: the 250 EUR acconto appears on the international page only in the PRE-ACCADEMICI step list, not in the ACCADEMICI step list - treat it as UNVERIFIED for the biennio. The admission process itself is free. NON-EU-SPECIFIC COSTS from the official International Students Guide, previously missing entirely: health insurance 122 EUR for the entry visa and 125 EUR total for the residence permit; optional voluntary SSN registration (Tessera Sanitaria) 700 EUR per year; permesso di soggiorno approx. 116-121 EUR (16 EUR marca da bollo + 30 EUR postal kit + 70-75 EUR permit fee), renewable annually.
_rec.equipmentRequired: Explicit warning on the fee page: "Per i Bienni in Sound Design e Mix & Mastering, eventuali Corsi di Pro Tools aggiuntivi saranno calcolati a parte, in aggiunta ai presenti costi" - additional Pro Tools courses are billed on top and the amount is NOT published (UNVERIFIED; get it in writing before committing). No laptop or DAW licence requirement is itemised anywhere - UNVERIFIED; budget realistically for a capable laptop plus a Pro Tools subscription.
_rec.paymentPlans: VERIFIED. Very Early Bird = 15% off the annual fee, requires completing admission AND paying in a single instalment by 30 April. Early Bird = 10% off, requires completing admission by 15 June, payable in 2 instalments (June + September). Regular Upfront = single payment by 5 September. Regular 3 rate = 5 September / 5 December / 5 March. An extra 8% discount exists for wind instruments (not applicable). Bank financing via Banca Sella and the Intesa Sanpaolo 'per Merito' student loan are offered but both require an Italian income holder - not realistic for him.
_rec.scholarships: CORRECTED from UNVERIFIED - real amounts are published. (1) Borse di studio Saint Louis: partial fee exemptions worth 500-2,500 EUR per year, reserved to I- and II-level academic students; conditions are ISEE below 22,000 EUR AND, for entrants who did not come through the Saint Louis pre-accademico, an admission-test average of at least 26/30. Applications 2-31 July each year. RISK: ISEE is an Italian income indicator and the school explicitly restricts the ISEE fee table to Italian students - he would need an ISEE parificato; confirm eligibility with the international office before counting on it. (2) LazioDisco regional scholarships: "un contributo da 1.900 euro fino a 5.000 euro per ciascun anno di corso, oltre a una serie di servizi aggiuntivi" - this is the single biggest lever available to him, applied for separately at laziodisco.it, and it stacks with the Saint Louis exemption. (3) Borse di collaborazione: 1,095 EUR each for up to 150 hours/year of work for the school; the application form asks for "copia del permesso di soggiorno (se straniero)", confirming international students are eligible, and lists 'Tutor per studenti internazionali' as a role. (4) Premio Giorgia Mileto (40-100% of the annual fee, 2,000-4,500 EUR) is NOT available here - it is restricted to instrument and voice courses in the Jazz and Popular Music departments. (5) The La Sapienza convention (15%/5%) does not apply.
_rec.visaEligible: Yes - verified. As a MUR-authorised AFAM institution Saint Louis hosts non-EU students through the standard dual procedure: official pre-enrolment through the Italian Embassy/Consulate on the Universitaly portal for a type-D multi-year study visa, run in parallel with the school's own admission process. "La lettera di accettazione, necessaria all'ottenimento del Visto per motivi di studio, viene di norma inviata al termine dell'intero processo." The school warns visa procedures "possono essere anche molto lunghe" and advises starting in January/February for a September arrival; pre-enrolments normally close in July with no extension. Non-EU students must hold Italian-valid health insurance before arrival and convert the visa into a permesso di soggiorno, renewed annually. Useful fallback: the pre-accademico courses are ALSO visa-valid - "L'iscrizione ai corsi pre-accademici per gli studenti extraeuropei e valida ai fini dell'ottenimento del Visto, in quanto corsi di preparazione (Foundation Courses)".
_rec.totalCostEstimate: First-year outlay, international Regular Upfront: 7,900 tuition + 290 enrolment (or 240 if by 30 May) + 140 regional tax + approx. 122-125 visa/permit insurance + approx. 116-121 permesso di soggiorno = approx. 8,570-8,580 EUR, before laptop/software, any extra Pro Tools course, and Rome living costs. Best case with Very Early Bird: approx. 7,850-7,900 EUR. Two-year tuition and fees including both years' enrolment and regional tax and the 500 EUR diploma exam fee: approx. 15,600 EUR (Very Early Bird) to 18,300 EUR (Regular 3 instalments), plus roughly 250-500 EUR of annual visa/permit/insurance admin and Rome living costs (not published by the school; realistically 900-1,200 EUR/month).
_rec.reputationSignals: Strongest possible signal for a private Italian music school: first private institution authorised by MUR to issue academic diplomas, by named decrees (144/2012 and 246/2013). AEC member since 2012, ISO 9001, Erasmus+ participant, Regione Lazio accredited, 1,800 students/year, in-house record labels with streaming distribution, partnerships with RUFA and Vigamus. Masterclass history includes Kees Tazelaar and Diemo Schwarz on the electronic side. No published complaints found. Red flags for this candidate: teaching is partly in Italian; the school is a music conservatory culturally, and the fee page is written around Italian ISEE bands with internationals paying a flat, higher, non-means-tested rate.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: YES, and this is the least gated of the four bienni. The formal requirement quotes only a three-year university or academic degree plus 15 years of schooling, with no mention of a music degree. Critically, because Sound Design is a Tecnico del Suono course there is no portfolio pre-selection and no performance requirement - only "un colloquio attitudinale" plus a multiple-choice test on digital audio fundamentals, Pro Tools, microphone technique and MIDI. A software engineer can prepare for that in a year. The safety net is also stated: "Gli studenti la cui preparazione in entrata NON sia RITENUTA IDONEA all'ingresso diretto ai Corsi di livello Accademico, potranno accedere ai Corsi di livello pre-accademico di livello piu adeguato", and pre-accademico enrolment is itself visa-valid.
_rec.recommendation: The most WINNABLE official Italian degree in scope, and the entry route he should actually target alongside Music Production. It gives a genuine MUR Diploma Accademico di II livello (laurea magistrale equivalent) for roughly 8.5k EUR a year all-in, and - the key correction to the earlier assessment - it does NOT require a portfolio or an audition. Admission is an interview plus a written technical exam on digital audio, Pro Tools, mic technique and MIDI, all of which a disciplined software engineer can study for during 2026-27. The Wwise and game-audio content also converts his coding background into an asset. Honest caveat: the subject is film/TV/game post-production, not club music - it will make him employable in audio, but it is not a DJ course. Practical plan: register interest now, apply between 3 February and 30 April 2027 to capture the 15% Very Early Bird rate, start the Universitaly/Embassy visa track no later than January 2027, and separately apply to LazioDisco for the 1,900-5,000 EUR regional scholarship. Get the extra Pro Tools course price in writing first.

Two-year tuition and fees including the diploma exam: approx. 15,600-18,300 EUR, plus a Max licence and any sensor hardware, plus Rome living costs of roughly 900-1,200 EUR/month.
_rec.reputationSignals: The most technically serious electronic-music offer among the Italian private institutions reviewed - the study plan names real tools and real repertoire (Max8, Kyma, Pure Data, SuperCollider, Processing, Arduino, C++/JUCE, Nono, Manoury, Di Scipio, Stroppa, Tudor) rather than marketing abstractions, and the faculty are named with their subjects. Backed by MUR authorisation and AEC membership. The corresponding risk is that this is a rigorous art-music course with an intellectually demanding entrance exam.

BUT the entrance exam requires him to present and analyse his own acousmatic or real-time-electronics composition AND to analyse the compositional methods of a canonical electroacoustic work from a set list. That is a music-literacy barrier a software engineer with no conservatory training cannot clear in a few months.
_rec.recommendation: The best intellectual fit and the worst admission odds - treat it as a stretch target, not the primary application. It converts his coding skill into a coursework advantage like nothing else in this batch, and it is an official MUR degree at about a third of NABA's price. But the earlier draft understated the gate badly: he would have to arrive able to present his own acousmatic or instrument-plus-live-electronics piece, discuss the compositional method of Stockhausen's Kontakte or Parmegiani's De Natura Sonorum, and pass a Max8 or Pure Data test. That is 18 months of deliberate study, in Italian-inflected art-music vocabulary. It is also worth saying plainly: this is installation and concert-hall electroacoustic music, not club or dance-floor work. If his goal is genuinely to DJ and release dance records, Music Production or Sound Design serve him better and admit him more easily; keep Live Electronics as a second-choice application only if he falls in love with the material during 2026.

The fee page states explicitly: "Per i Bienni in Sound Design e Mix & Mastering, eventuali Corsi di Pro Tools aggiuntivi saranno calcolati a parte, in aggiunta ai presenti costi." The amount is NOT published (UNVERIFIED) and the Pro Tools 210M/310M certification costs are not itemised either - the school separately sells a 'ProTools, certificazione 101 e 110' short course, which suggests certification is billed as an add-on. Get a written quote before enrolling. Laptop/DAW licences also not itemised.

_rec.totalCostEstimate: First-year outlay Regular Upfront approx. 8,570-8,580 EUR including enrolment, regional tax, visa insurance and permesso - PLUS an unquantified Pro Tools course/certification top-up, which is the reason this course's true cost is the least predictable of the four. Two-year tuition and fees including the diploma exam: approx. 15,600-18,300 EUR before that top-up, plus Rome living costs.
_rec.reputationSignals: Avid Pro Tools 210M/310M certification embedded; real commercial releases through the school's own labels; concrete graduate outcomes as studio engineer and broadcast/radio-TV sound technician; named working-engineer faculty. Backed by MUR authorisation and AEC membership. The unpriced Pro Tools add-on is the only commercial red flag.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: Yes, and this is the least music-dependent of the four. Formal entry needs only a three-year degree plus 15 years of schooling; there is no pre-selection, no portfolio and no performance - just an interview, a technical MCQ on digital audio, Pro Tools, mic technique and MIDI, and a practical mix of a supplied multitrack. A technically minded non-musician who practises mixing for a year has a genuine route in.
_rec.recommendation: The safest admission and the wrong ambition - take it only as a deliberate career hedge. Everything about the gate suits him: no portfolio, no audition, a studiable written exam and a practical mix test on material the school hands him. And it produces a real MUR degree plus Pro Tools 210M/310M certification, which is directly employable. But it trains the engineer who serves other people's records, not the artist who makes his own - if the goal is to DJ and release music, Music Production is the same money for a far closer fit, and Sound Design is equally winnable with more distinctive skills. Only pick Mix & Mastering if he consciously wants a studio-technician day job to fund the DJ ambition. Before committing, get the price of the extra Pro Tools courses and the 210M/310M certifications in writing - it is the only figure in this batch the school refuses to publish.
