_rec.institution: Saint Louis College of Music, Rome (Saint Louis Music Center srl — 'scuola autorizzata dal MUR')
_rec.qualification: OFFICIAL for the biennio route — Diploma Accademico di II livello, 120 CFA, under MUR authorisation; the school styles itself 'scuola autorizzata dal MUR' and its own English page calls this programme a 'Master Diploma' / 'Two-Year Postgraduate Program'. SEPARATE AND LESSER: Saint Louis also runs 'Master di I livello' one-year programmes which are post-degree certificates and are NOT equivalent to a laurea magistrale. He must enrol on the BIENNIO, not a Master di I livello.
_rec.institutionType: Private specialist music school authorised within the AFAM/MUR framework; member of the AEC (European Association of Conservatoires); public institutional relationship with Sapienza Università di Roma
_rec.focus: THE CLOSEST SUBJECT MATCH IN THIS BATCH BY A WIDE MARGIN — but read the fine print. The biennio is Sound Design AND AUDIO POST-PRODUCTION, aimed at cinema, TV series, video games, animation, media, advertising, sound branding, audio restoration and audio forensics. It is NOT an electronic-music-production or DJ degree. A sibling biennio exists in Mix & Mastering. Saint Louis also runs 'Sonic Arts' and Composition/Electronic/Applied Music strands at second level; the existence of separate second-level bienni specifically in 'Music Production' and 'Live Electronics' is UNVERIFIED and must be checked directly.
_rec.durationEcts: 2 years, 120 CFA (Diploma Accademico di II livello). VERIFIED CONTACT HOURS: 'Approximately 300 hours of classes per year', with classes 'mostly held on a fortnightly basis', mandatory attendance of at least 80%. A part-time route exists and may extend the course beyond 3 years. 300 h/year is roughly 10 hours a week — LOW, and he must check that it satisfies the Italian study-visa full-time expectation before relying on it.
_rec.language: Italian is the safe assumption, but the enrolment form asks 'Language of Attendance — in what language would you like to attend classes?', and the international admission process describes an aptitude interview 'also aimed at testing English (or Italian) language proficiency'. An English attendance route therefore appears to exist. CONFIRM IN WRITING for this specific biennio — the answer changes the whole feasibility of a September 2027 start.
_rec.whatYouStudy: VERIFIED module list. Sound Design — techniques and concepts of sound design and audio post-production, recording, construction and manipulation of sound effects for film, TV series, video games and media, Pro Tools with a detailed focus on the audio post-production and sound-design workflow, plus other sound-manipulation software and plug-ins. Wwise Nonlinear Interactive Audio — audio nonlinearity in interactive video-game sound design using Audiokinetic Wwise. Audio Sampling and Post Production — Kontakt and its engine, modulators, envelopes, zones, groups, mapping, and building a custom sample library. Sound Branding — analysis, composition, implementation, mix and mastering of a sound brand. Technologies and Techniques of Audio Restoration — restoration and audio forensics from film to tape to digital, in specialised laboratories. Mix e Mastering — mix and mastering sessions finalising multimedia products. Students are also involved in projects with the Saint Louis Composition and Music Applied to Images departments and with the film/animation departments of RUFA, Vigamus and others. Career outcomes: Sound Designer, Sound Restorer, audio post-production sound engineer, Sound Designer for gaming.
_rec.facilities: Rome campus with recording and production facilities and 'specialized laboratories' for restoration; Bibliomediateca and library; Erasmus+ since 2012; career service; formal relationship with Sapienza. Note the school's own caveat that for the Sound Design and Mix & Mastering bienni, 'eventuali Corsi di Pro Tools aggiuntivi saranno calcolati a parte' — additional Pro Tools courses are billed separately. Detailed studio inventory UNVERIFIED.
_rec.entryRequirements: VERIFIED and quoted. 'Level II Academics: EU or NON-EU Citizens holding a Three-year University or Academic Diploma (or equivalent), obtained in Italy or in their home country, may apply for admission. Proof of a minimum of 15 years of schooling is also required.' The degree must be submitted as a scanned original with certified translation and a Declaration of Value (DOV) from the Italian Embassy or Consulate, or alternatively a CIMEA Diplome certificate. A Tunisian BSc after 13 years of school plus a 3-year degree gives 16 years — but he must count this precisely against his own transcripts, because falling short of 15 diverts him to Pre-Academic courses.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: THIS IS THE REAL BARRIER, AND IT IS WORSE THAN PREVIOUSLY RECORDED. The programme page states: 'Bachelor of Sound Technician graduates gain access by right to one of the two-year degrees listed above. Graduates in other disciplines who have prior experience in phonics may enter upon entrance examination.' He is a graduate in another discipline WITHOUT prior experience in phonics (audio engineering). On the published wording he does not currently meet the alternative route. Compounding this, the international page warns: 'Students whose incoming preparation is NOT CONSIDERED SUITABLE for direct entry into Academic Level Courses will be eligible for more appropriate Pre-Academic Level Courses' — i.e. he risks being offered a pre-academic year instead of the biennio. GET A WRITTEN RULING FROM THE SEGRETERIA DIDATTICA BEFORE INVESTING IN THIS PATH, and use the year to 2027 to build demonstrable audio work.
_rec.portfolioSpec: VERIFIED and favourable. The pre-selection route differs by department. For Jazz/Pop/Songwriting/Classical the candidate must record four songs performed, at least three in a group of at least a trio — that would be impossible for him. BUT for 'Composition/Electronic/Applied Music' the requirement is: 'Prepare a link containing Portfolio (video, audio, sheet music) of your most indicative and recent works.' A self-built production portfolio is therefore admissible on the correct track. For the Sound Technician course there is no pre-selection at all, only an aptitude interview. He must confirm which pre-selection route the Sound Design biennio follows.
_rec.auditionSpec: No performance audition on the portfolio track. After pre-selection there are ADMISSION TESTS — the course page says they run 'over two consecutive days'; the international page says they can be taken online between January and June on individually agreed dates, or in a single in-person session in June. Results feed a merit ranking (graduatoria). Test contents are published in the Course Catalog.
_rec.englishTest: IELTS is NOT the binding requirement and is not mentioned. Language proficiency is assessed in the aptitude interview, in 'English (or Italian)'. If the biennio is delivered in Italian he will need real Italian; if an English route exists, English suffices. CONFIRM WHICH — this is the highest-value single question to put to the Segreteria.
_rec.tuitionPerYear: *** THE MOST IMPORTANT CORRECTION IN THIS BATCH. THE ~€2,800/YEAR FIGURE IS WRONG BY A FACTOR OF ABOUT THREE. *** Saint Louis publishes a SEPARATE, HIGHER, NON-ISEE-BASED price list for international students, defined as 'uno studente di nazionalità EU (non italiana) o NON-EU residente all'Estero al momento dell'iscrizione' — which is exactly him. VERIFIED international rates, ACCADEMICO II LIVELLO: VERY EARLY BIRD €7,230 (15% off the annual fee, for students who complete admission AND pay in a single payment by 30 April); EARLY BIRD €7,650 (10% off, admission completed by 15 June, payable in 2 instalments in June and September); REGULAR UPFRONT €7,900 (admission after 15 June and/or single payment by 5 September); REGULAR 3 INSTALMENTS €8,500 (September, December, March). The ISEE-banded table (€4,890-€8,150 for II livello) applies 'SOLO per studenti italiani' — he cannot access it. An extra 8% discount exists for wind instruments, irrelevant here.
_rec.tuitionTotal: €14,460 over two years at the Very Early Bird rate, rising to €17,000 at the Regular 3-instalment rate. Add the compulsory annual and one-off charges below and the two-year fee total is roughly €15,700-€18,400, before any additional Pro Tools courses.
_rec.otherFees: VERIFIED and itemised. Quota annuale di iscrizione: €240.00 if paid by 30 May, €290.00 thereafter (the international page states €240-€290 depending on the month of enrolment). Down payment on enrolment: €250, later deducted from the annual fee. Tassa annuale Diritto allo studio: €140.00 per year, paid to Regione Lazio through LazioDisco, for every year of first- and second-level academic courses including any years fuori corso. One-off second-level diploma examination fee: €500.00. Students fuori corso: €380.00 a year. And the specific warning for his programme: 'Per i Bienni in Sound Design e Mix & Mastering, eventuali Corsi di Pro Tools aggiuntivi saranno calcolati a parte, in aggiunta ai presenti costi.' The €240/€290 registration fee is non-refundable even though the admission process itself is free.
_rec.equipmentRequired: Not published as a mandatory list, but the curriculum is built on Pro Tools, Wwise and Kontakt, and additional Pro Tools courses are chargeable extras. Budget a capable machine plus licences; UNVERIFIED as a formal requirement.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: Fees: roughly €7,900-€9,200 in year one (tuition band + €240/€290 registration + €140 regional tax, with the €250 deposit absorbed) and €7,900-€9,300 in year two (including the €500 diploma exam fee), so about €15,700-€18,400 over two years, plus any extra Pro Tools modules. Rome living costs of €11,000-€14,000 a year take the realistic two-year all-in to €38,000-€47,000. Still the cheapest genuinely relevant official second-level route found — but three times the previously recorded figure.
_rec.scholarships: (1) SAINT LOUIS INTERNAL SCHOLARSHIPS — partial exemptions from the fees, worth €500 to €2,500 per year of the course for full-time attendance, restricted to first- and second-level academic courses. FIRST-YEAR criteria are two, jointly: an ISEE below €22,000 AND merit. For a student who has NOT come through Saint Louis pre-academic courses, the merit test is 'la media delle prove di ammissione deve essere pari o superiore a 26/30', with a 1-point penalty on the average for each subject carried as a debit. Application window 2-31 JULY each year. SECOND-YEAR renewal: ISEE still below €22,000, plus at least 50 CFA with a weighted average of 26/30 or higher by the September session. Not available for years fuori corso. AS A NON-EU APPLICANT HE WOULD NEED AN ISEE PARIFICATO built from consular-legalised Tunisian tax and property documents to prove the €22,000 test — the same exercise described in the IED entry, and it must be started months ahead. (2) *** PREMIO GIORGIA MILETO — CORRECTION: HE ALMOST CERTAINLY CANNOT WIN THIS. *** It is worth 40% to 100% of the annual fee, €2,000-€4,500 per awardee, but it is awarded 'tramite audizioni aperte a tutti i corsi di STRUMENTO E CANTO del Dipartimento di Jazz e di Popular Music', held as a LIVE CONCERT in a Rome venue with the candidate backed by a professional resident band; to reach the audition he must submit audio/video of two pieces played IN A GROUP (duo, trio, quartet). It is a performer's award, open to 'musicisti, cantanti e songwriter'. A sound-design student who does not perform is outside its scope. Do not budget for it. (3) BORSE DI COLLABORAZIONE — annual competition for student collaboration grants across all departments; amounts UNVERIFIED. (4) LAZIODISCO / DiSCo LAZIO REGIONAL SCHOLARSHIP — awarded through a separate regional call on income and merit. Non-EU students are eligible and, under Art. 13(3) d.p.c.m. 9/04/2001 (quoted verbatim in the IED entry), are automatically classified 'fuori sede', the highest-value bracket. Saint Louis confirms compatibility: 'Gli esoneri parziali dal versamento delle quote sono compatibili con le borse di studio LazioDisco, è possibile conseguire entrambi' — so a Saint Louis internal exemption AND a LazioDisco award CAN be stacked. This is the only genuine stacking opportunity found anywhere in this batch. LazioDisco amounts for Saint Louis students UNVERIFIED. (5) Convenzione with Sapienza and other partnership discounts — details UNVERIFIED. (6) FINANCING via Banca Sella and Intesa Sanpaolo 'per Merito': the Banca Sella application requires an Italian tessera sanitaria/codice fiscale and, above €7,000, an Italian income document from the borrower — effectively closed to him before he is resident.
_rec.paymentPlans: VERIFIED, and the payment formula IS the discount structure. Very Early Bird: single payment by 30 April, 15% off, €7,230. Early Bird: admission completed by 15 June, 10% off, TWO instalments in June and September, €7,650. Regular Upfront: single payment by 5 September, €7,900. Regular 3 instalments: September, December, March, €8,500. Choosing instalments over Very Early Bird costs him €1,270 a year, €2,540 over the degree. Banca Sella financing is arranged through the Segreteria Didattica but requires an Italian-resident borrower with income. Note the school's own instruction that students awaiting a scholarship ranking should wait for the outcome before starting a financing application.
_rec.accreditationStatus: OFFICIAL for the biennio — Diploma Accademico di II livello, MUR-authorised, 120 CFA, equivalent to a laurea magistrale for public competitions and for doctoral/specialisation admission in artistic and musical fields. AEC member. Institutional relationship with Sapienza. But note the internal distinction: the Bienni are second-level academic diplomas; the 'Master di I livello' offerings (Music Business & Management, Consulente Musicale per Cinema e TV, Direzione d'Orchestra) are one-year post-degree certificates and are NOT equivalent. Choose the biennio.
_rec.visaEligible: YES in principle, with a documented process. The school explicitly admits NON-EU citizens to second-level academic courses, runs an international students office, and states: 'The acceptance letter, which is required to obtain a Student Visa, is usually sent after the entire process is completed.' Non-EU students 'must simultaneously follow a dual enrollment procedure', with official pre-enrolment through the Italian diplomatic representations (UniversItaly), and the school points applicants to studiare-in-italia.it, noting that updates to enrolment procedures are usually published in May for the following academic year. ONE CAVEAT TO RESOLVE: at approximately 300 taught hours a year on a fortnightly timetable, he should confirm with both the school and the Italian consulate that the programme is treated as full-time study for visa purposes.
_rec.applicationOpens: VERIFIED. Applications for admission to academic courses, complete with pre-selection links, are accepted each year from 1 JANUARY and no later than 30 APRIL. Late applications are considered individually at the discretion of management, subject to places. Admission tests: online between January and June on individually agreed dates, or a single in-person session in June; the course page also mentions June and September sessions. Scholarship applications: 2-31 July annually.
_rec.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new dates for 2027 entry, but the pattern is stable and the dates are early. For a SEPTEMBER/OCTOBER 2027 START he should expect: applications 1 January - 30 APRIL 2027; Very Early Bird payment deadline 30 APRIL 2027 (15% off); Early Bird admission completed by 15 JUNE 2027 (10% off); registration fee €240 by 30 May 2027; internal scholarship application 2-31 JULY 2027; regular upfront payment by 5 September 2027. The binding constraint is 30 April 2027 — which means the portfolio, the DOV/CIMEA and the language evidence must all be ready by roughly March 2027.
_rec.reputationSignals: Long-established Rome music school founded 1976, MUR-authorised, AEC member, public institutional relationship with Sapienza Università di Roma, Erasmus+ participant since 2012, cross-institution projects with RUFA and Vigamus, a jazz and popular-music identity far closer to his world than any design academy, and named international guests (Paolo Fresu, Fabrizio Bosso, Gianluca Petrella and others) in its ensemble programme. RED FLAGS: the website is behind an aggressive bot challenge and several pages return nothing to ordinary fetching, which is why the fee error persisted; international fees are a separate and much higher schedule than the Italian ISEE table; the published admission rule requires 'prior experience in phonics' for graduates of other disciplines; contact hours are only about 300 a year; extra Pro Tools modules are chargeable; and applicants judged unsuitable are diverted to Pre-Academic courses.
_rec.recommendation: This remains the best SUBJECT fit in Italy for him and the cheapest genuinely accredited second-level route in this batch — a real Diploma Accademico di II livello in Sound Design and Audio Post-Production, taught on Pro Tools, Wwise and Kontakt, from a MUR-authorised music school with an AEC membership and a Sapienza relationship. But three corrections change the plan. FIRST, THE PRICE: it is not €2,800 a year. As an international student he pays €7,230 to €8,500 a year depending purely on how early he commits, plus €240-€290 registration, €140 regional tax a year, a €500 diploma exam fee and chargeable extra Pro Tools modules — about €15,700-€18,400 over two years. The €1,270-a-year gap between Very Early Bird and Regular instalments is the single easiest saving available to him anywhere in this batch: commit and pay by 30 April. SECOND, ADMISSION IS NOT ASSURED: the published rule gives access by right only to Sound Technician graduates, and admits 'graduates in other disciplines who have prior experience in phonics' by entrance examination. He has none. He must (a) get a written ruling from the Segreteria Didattica now, and (b) spend the year to April 2027 producing demonstrable audio work so that the 'prior experience' claim is real — the good news is that the Composition/Electronic/Applied Music pre-selection route accepts exactly that, 'a Portfolio (video, audio, sheet music) of your most indicative and recent works', with no group-performance requirement. THIRD, KNOW WHAT HE IS BUYING: this is sound design for film, TV, games and restoration, not electronic music production or DJing. If his goal is genuinely to become an international DJ/producer, this teaches him the professional audio craft underneath that ambition but not the ambition itself. Practical sequence: written ruling on eligibility and on teaching language first; then Italian to B2 if the answer is Italian; DOV or CIMEA started by autumn 2026; ISEE parificato paperwork started in spring 2027 for the 2-31 July scholarship window; application filed by 30 April 2027 to capture the 15%; and LazioDisco pursued in parallel, since the school confirms in writing that its own exemptions and LazioDisco awards can be held together.
_rec.verificationNotes: The Saint Louis site sits behind a SiteGround bot challenge that returns empty content to normal fetching — the enrolment, scholarship, programme and international pages had to be retrieved through a rendering proxy, and this is almost certainly why the fee figure was wrong. MAJOR CORRECTION: the ~€2,800/year figure is WRONG. The verbatim international table gives ACCADEMICO II LIVELLO at €7,230 (Very Early Bird) / €7,650 (Early Bird) / €7,900 (Regular Upfront) / €8,500 (Regular 3 instalments); the €4,890-€8,150 ISEE-banded table is explicitly headed 'SOLO STUDENTI ITALIANI'. OTHER CORRECTIONS: (1) international fees are NOT ISEE-based — the ISEE-based model applies only to Italians, so the previous framing of an ISEE-linked fee for a non-EU student is wrong, though an ISEE parificato is still needed for the internal scholarship; (2) full fee schedule now itemised — €240/€290 annual registration, €250 deposit, €140/yr LazioDisco regional tax, €500 second-level diploma exam, €380/yr fuori corso, and chargeable extra Pro Tools courses specifically for the Sound Design and Mix & Mastering bienni; (3) THE PREMIO GIORGIA MILETO IS A PERFORMER'S AWARD assigned by live audition for instrument and voice courses in the Jazz and Popular Music departments, requiring group-performance recordings — the previous description of it as directly available to a popular-music student overstates his access; treat it as unavailable; (4) internal scholarship first-year merit criterion is now precise: admission-test average of 26/30 or higher for students not from Saint Louis pre-academic courses, with ISEE below €22,000, worth €500-€2,500; renewal to year 2 is 50 CFA at 26/30 (not the 26/30-at-50-CFA-plus-different-thresholds mix previously recorded); (5) NEW AND IMPORTANT: Saint Louis states in writing that its internal exemptions ARE compatible with LazioDisco awards and both can be held — the only verified stacking opportunity in this batch; (6) admission wording verified — Sound Technician graduates enter by right, 'graduates in other disciplines who have prior experience in phonics may enter upon entrance examination', which is a genuine barrier for him; (7) applications run 1 January - 30 April; scholarship applications 2-31 July; acceptance letter for the visa issued after the whole process; (8) contact hours verified at approximately 300 per year on a mostly fortnightly timetable with 80% mandatory attendance — low, and a point to check for visa full-time status; (9) 15-years-of-schooling rule and DOV/CIMEA requirement confirmed verbatim; (10) the biennio is sound design and audio POST-PRODUCTION for cinema/TV/games/restoration — the existence of separate second-level bienni in 'Music Production' and 'Live Electronics' could not be confirmed and should be treated as UNVERIFIED.

_rec.program: ReSound — Erasmus Mundus Joint Master of Arts in Sound Design for Media Arts
_rec.institution: Consortium: IADT Dún Laoghaire (Ireland) + Universidade Lusófona (Portugal, private) + Lithuanian Academy of Music and Theatre (Lithuania), within the FilmEU alliance
_rec.city: Lisbon (one semester); Dublin and Vilnius for the others
_rec.country: Portugal (one of three countries; the Portuguese partner is the private Universidade Lusófona)
_rec.qualification: ERASMUS MUNDUS JOINT MASTER (EMJM) — 120 ECTS joint/multiple master's degree awarded by the consortium partners. A full, official 2nd-cycle degree, not a certificate.
_rec.accreditationStatus: OFFICIAL, and the highest-quality accreditation signal in this entire batch. Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters are selected and funded directly by the European Commission, and each partner's award is nationally accredited — Lusófona under A3ES (verified separately in this batch: R/A-Cr 34/2018/AL01 for its sister mestrado, and the institution is an accredited Portuguese university), IADT under Irish QQI, LMTA under Lithuanian accreditation. EMJM designation is itself an external quality endorsement that no purely private school can buy. There is no plausible scenario in which this qualification turns out to be worthless paper — which is precisely the risk that dominates the rest of this search.
_rec.focus: Sound as an artistic, cultural and technological force across media arts, immersive environments, performance and the audiovisual industries. The most internationally-facing sound master's touching Portugal.
_rec.whatYouStudy: Four semesters with compulsory structured mobility across the three partner institutions, closing with a master's thesis/project. The Lisbon semester draws on Lusófona's Dolby Atmos/3D audio room, professional multitrack studios and acoustic laboratories. DETAILED PER-SEMESTER MODULE LISTS COULD NOT BE VERIFIED — the public pages describe the programme as 'a two-year, four-semester journey' with Erasmus+ mobility but do not publish a module-by-module curriculum, and the semester-to-institution mapping is NOT stated on the pages I could read. This is a real gap for a €15,000 (or scholarship-competitive) decision: he must request the full programme handbook and the semester/institution mapping from the consortium before applying.
_rec.durationEcts: 2 years / 4 semesters / 120 ECTS, full-time, in-person, with compulsory mobility across three countries.
_rec.language: ENGLISH. VERIFIED via the published IELTS requirement. This is the decisive difference from every other accredited option in this batch — it is the ONLY one he can study in a language he already has, and it removes the twelve-month Portuguese problem entirely.
_rec.entryRequirements: VERIFIED VERBATIM: 'Applicants with degrees in other fields may also be considered if they possess relevant prior experience in areas such as sound, music, film, or media studies.' Baseline expectation is a bachelor's in sound, music, film or media studies. Application pack: academic transcripts, portfolio, two recommendation letters, proof of English proficiency. Maximum 24 places per year — VERIFIED: 'A maximum of 24 places are offered at ReSound each year.'
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: CONDITIONALLY YES — AND THIS EXACT CLAUSE IS THE WHOLE BALLGAME FOR HIM. Verified wording: 'Applicants with degrees in other fields may also be considered if they possess relevant prior experience in areas such as sound, music, film, or media studies.' His Software Engineering BSc is unambiguously 'a degree in another field', so admission turns entirely on evidencing 'relevant prior experience' in sound, music, film or media. He currently has NONE — no music degree, no conservatory training, no professional audio work. Note the clause says 'may also be considered', not 'will be accepted': it is a discretionary door, not a right. Between now and a likely late-January 2027 deadline he must manufacture genuine evidence — released tracks, credited sound work on short films or games, live sets, a substantial audio-software project. Without it this is a rejection, and no amount of essay-writing substitutes.
_rec.portfolioSpec: VERIFIED AND UNUSUALLY PRECISE — the clearest spec in this entire batch, which is a gift because it removes all guesswork. Quoted: 'Please supply no more than 3 examples', each with 'a short reflective paragraph on each piece explicitly stating your role in the work'. Acceptable formats: 'a single hyperlink to a portfolio website or a compilation audio or video file'. Reviewers assess realistically 10–15 minutes of material per application. The discipline this demands is the point: three strong finished pieces totalling 10–15 minutes, not a dump of everything he has ever made. He should build to exactly this spec and use it as the target for the whole next twelve months.
_rec.auditionSpec: No audition or performance test is published. Selection rests on documents, portfolio and references. Whether an interview stage exists is UNVERIFIED.
_rec.englishTest: YES — VERIFIED, AND THIS IS HIS MOST URGENT ACTION ITEM. IELTS 6.0 minimum with 'no component less than 6.0' — every band, not just the overall. Verified equivalents: TOEFL iBT 79, Duolingo 110, Cambridge B2. Certificates must be 'taken within the last two years'. He has NOT taken IELTS. Working backwards from a probable late-January 2027 deadline, he should book and sit it in autumn 2026 — now — leaving room for one retake if a single band comes in at 5.5. Worth checking separately whether his SMU MedTech BSc was English-taught and qualifies for a prior-study waiver, which would save both the fee and the sitting; the ReSound page lists alternative qualifications but I could not verify the exact waiver wording, so do not rely on it — book the test.
_rec.tuitionPerYear: €7,500 per year for self-funded students, charged as two instalments of €7,500 rather than four — VERIFIED. NON-EU PRICING IS IDENTICAL TO EU PRICING: no differentiation is stated anywhere, which is unusual and strongly in his favour. Most international programmes penalise a Tunisian passport here; this one does not.
_rec.tuitionTotal: €15,000 total for the four-semester programme (self-funded) — VERIFIED on the official consortium application page as '15,000 Euro' split into two payments of '7,500 EUR'. CONFLICT FLAG STANDS: Universidade Lusófona's own ReSound page quotes an average of roughly €2,250 per month for 30-ECTS semestral units (about €9,000 per semester), which does not reconcile with the consortium's €15,000 total. Treat resound-ma.eu as authoritative — it is the consortium's own page and the figure is unambiguous — but get the discrepancy resolved in writing before paying anything, because a €36,000 reading of the Lusófona page is not a rounding error.
_rec.otherFees: No application fee is mentioned on the application page — VERIFIED absence, though absence of mention is weaker than an explicit statement of zero. Travel, accommodation and living costs are explicitly excluded from tuition and estimated by the consortium at €600–€1,000 per month. HIDDEN COST HE MUST BUDGET FOR: three-country mobility means THREE separate immigration processes (Ireland — outside Schengen and with its own IRP regime — plus Portugal and Lithuania) and two inter-country relocations. Realistically €1,500–€3,000 across the two years in permit fees, flights and deposits. This is nowhere published — UNVERIFIED as a figure, but it is certain to exist and it disproportionately burdens a Tunisian passport holder.
_rec.equipmentRequired: Not published — UNVERIFIED. A capable laptop and reference headphones are a practical necessity for a mobility-based sound programme where he will be working away from any one studio for much of the time.
_rec.paymentPlans: Self-funded tuition is split into two payments of €7,500, at semester 1 and semester 3 — VERIFIED. Note this is a harsher cash-flow shape than it first appears: €7,500 due before he starts. No instalment plan, early-bird or alumni discount is published — UNVERIFIED.
_rec.scholarships: THE BEST FUNDING AVAILABLE ANYWHERE IN THIS SEARCH, AND HE IS ELIGIBLE AS A NON-EU NATIONAL. VERIFIED: Erasmus Mundus scholarship holders 'pay no tuition fees' and receive a stipend of '1,400 EUR per month'. Over 24 months that is roughly €33,600 in stipend plus €15,000 in waived tuition — around €48,600 of value, and it converts his entire plan from a €30,000+ outlay into a net-positive one. Awarded on merit. The number of scholarships is a limited share of the maximum 24 annual places, so it is genuinely competitive; EMJM calls typically reserve a substantial quota for Partner Country (non-EU) applicants, which is his category, though I could not verify the specific quota for this consortium — UNVERIFIED. This single line item is the most consequential fact in the entire Portuguese slice.
_rec.intakes: One intake per year, September. VERIFIED.
_rec.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. The 2026 intake round opened in autumn 2025. Expect the round for a September 2027 start to open around October–November 2026 — i.e. within about two to three months of now. HE SHOULD BE CHECKING resound-ma.eu WEEKLY FROM OCTOBER 2026. This is the nearest live deadline in his entire plan.
_rec.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. VERIFIED CURRENT STATUS: the consortium site states 'Applications for ReSound 2026 have now closed' and no 2027 dates are yet published. The last published deadline was extended to 27 January 2026 for 2026 entry, so expect a comparable late-January 2027 deadline for September 2027 entry. Erasmus Mundus scholarship deadlines are hard and are not extended for late portfolios or missing IELTS certificates.
_rec.facilities: Lisbon semester: Lusófona's professional multitrack studios, acoustic laboratories, cinema post-production and 3D Dolby Atmos room. Dublin: IADT's media production facilities. Vilnius: LMTA. Plus the FilmEU alliance network across Europe. Per-institution facility inventories are not published in detail — UNVERIFIED.
_rec.visaEligible: YES, with an important asterisk. Erasmus Mundus students receive structured institutional support for visas at each partner, and a €1,400/month stipend comfortably satisfies proof-of-means tests everywhere — for a Tunisian applicant, proof of means is usually the hardest part of a study-visa file, and the scholarship eliminates it. The asterisk: three separate immigration processes in two years is administratively heavy on a Tunisian passport, and IRELAND IS OUTSIDE SCHENGEN, so the Irish IRP process is entirely separate from the Portuguese and Lithuanian residence permits. Self-funded (non-scholarship) entry is materially riskier here, because he would have to evidence means three times over.
_rec.reputationSignals: European Commission selection and funding; FilmEU European University alliance membership; three national accreditations; capped at 24 students a year, so genuinely small cohorts and real staff contact; explicit English-medium delivery. This is the most prestigious sound qualification reachable through a private Portuguese institution. No red flags found. Two honest structural caveats: only ONE of four semesters is actually in Portugal, so if his goal is to establish himself in the Lisbon scene specifically, this scatters him across three countries at exactly the age when building a local network matters; and the absence of a published module list is a transparency gap he should close before committing.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: WITH an Erasmus Mundus scholarship: €0 tuition and a net-positive €1,400/month, i.e. the plan pays for itself. WITHOUT a scholarship: €15,000 tuition + roughly €14,400–€24,000 living over 24 months + €1,500–€3,000 relocation and permits — a realistic all-in €31,000–€42,000 over two years, front-loaded with €7,500 due before he starts.
_rec.recommendation: APPLY. THIS IS HIS SINGLE HIGHEST-VALUE SHOT IN THE PORTUGUESE SLICE, AND THE ONLY ONE TAUGHT IN ENGLISH THAT CAN BE FULLY FUNDED. The arithmetic is decisive for a budget-sensitive self-payer: a scholarship converts a €30,000-plus plan into a funded one with a €1,400 monthly stipend, worth roughly €48,600. Nothing else in this search comes close. But be blunt with him about the odds and the work. Twenty-four places, worldwide competition, and an admission clause requiring 'relevant prior experience' he does not have. His concrete twelve-month plan, in priority order: (1) book IELTS NOW and clear 6.0 in EVERY band — a single 5.5 disqualifies him — or verify an English-medium waiver for his BSc; (2) build exactly three portfolio pieces totalling 10–15 minutes, ideally one released track, one piece of sound-to-picture, and one audio-software or interactive piece that turns his engineering background into a differentiator rather than the liability the admissions clause implies; (3) secure two recommenders now, while his SMU lecturers still remember him; (4) watch resound-ma.eu from October 2026 for the call. If he does only ONE thing from this entire Portugal report, it should be this application — with UCP Porto and the Lusófona mestrado as the paid, Portuguese-language fallbacks. He should treat self-funding this at €15,000 as a poor third option: without the scholarship, the Lusófona mestrado teaches similar content for roughly half the tuition.
_rec.verificationNotes: Consortium application page fetched and confirmed verbatim: the 'degrees in other fields' clause; the portfolio spec (max 3 examples, reflective paragraph per piece stating role, single hyperlink or compilation file acceptable, 10–15 minutes); IELTS 6.0 with no component below 6.0, TOEFL iBT 79 / Duolingo 110 / Cambridge B2 equivalents, certificates within the last two years; maximum 24 places; €15,000 total split into two €7,500 instalments with no EU/non-EU differentiation; €1,400/month stipend with tuition waived for scholarship holders; no application fee mentioned. The consortium homepage confirmed 'Applications for ReSound 2026 have now closed' and that no 2027 dates are yet published. REMAINS UNVERIFIED: the per-semester module list (not published), the semester-to-institution mapping (not stated on the pages read), the Erasmus Mundus project number, the non-EU scholarship quota, whether an interview stage exists, equipment requirements, and the €15,000 vs Lusófona's ~€2,250/month conflict, which is real and must be resolved in writing.

_rec.program: Sound Design for Live, Studio and Interactive Media
_rec.institution: ETIC – Escola de Tecnologias, Inovação e Criação (private school, Lisbon; Pearson BTEC Accredited Centre since 2016; DGERT-certified training provider)
_rec.qualification: CORRECTED AND SHARPENED. The award is a "BTEC Higher National Diploma, Level 5, carrying a total of 240 CATS credits" — ETIC's own wording. The page also calls it a "Pearson BTEC Level 5 Professional Certification (240 CATS)". It is an HND: NOT a mestrado, NOT a pós-graduação, NOT a Portuguese degree, and NOT a bachelor's. ETIC states plainly on its own page: "Certification follows the British education system; ETIC is not a higher education institution." NEW FINDING: the optional 3rd year is a separate award — "ETIC / SOLENT UNIVERSITY RECOGNITION / 120 CATS", taking the total to 360 CATS, i.e. a UK bachelor's-level top-up recognised by Solent University (Southampton). So the 2-year route ends BELOW bachelor's; only the 3-year route reaches bachelor-equivalent — still nowhere near a master.
_rec.institutionType: Private art/technology school in Portugal delivering a UK awarding-body qualification (Pearson/Edexcel), with a Solent University top-up route in the optional third year
_rec.focus: Sound design for live performance, studio, broadcast, games/VR/AR and installation art. IMPORTANT CORRECTION OF EMPHASIS: this is media, live-event and installation sound design — it is NOT music production, not electronic music, and not DJing.
_rec.whatYouStudy: CORRECTED — the module content was previously UNVERIFIED and is now confirmed in detail from the official page, and it is not what a producer/DJ needs. Verified units: sound design for film, documentary and animation; adaptive audio systems for video games, virtual reality (VR) and augmented reality (AR); sound design for installations, exhibitions and public spaces; technical installation and operation of Public Address (P.A.) systems including tuning and calibration; Lighting Control fundamentals covering the DMX system, cabling, projectors and digital lighting consoles; Broadcast and LUFS Standards (sound engineering for TV and radio, loudness measurement and regulatory volume standards); Sound for Arts, Theatre and QLab (setup, automation and playback control for live performance); Sound Systems for Museums and Installations (multi-channel and distributed audio design); and Sonic Interactivity and Prototyping using sensors and Arduino/Raspberry Pi. Stated career outcome: "Sound Designer specialising in recording and post-production for video games, film, theatre, advertising and sound installations." Schedule: Mon-Friday 14:00-18:00, in person, project-based, max 16 students. Erasmus+ international internships available on completion, subject to performance.
_rec.durationEcts: "Duration: 2 years + 1 (optional). Level: 5" — ETIC's own wording. 240 CATS after year 2 (BTEC HND, Level 5); a further 120 CATS with Solent University recognition in the optional year 3, totalling 360 CATS. CATS is a UK credit unit, NOT ECTS; 240 CATS is nominally 120 ECTS but the LEVEL is what matters, and Level 5 is below bachelor's.
_rec.language: English — VERIFIED. This is genuinely an international programme delivered in English, a real advantage over every Italian- and Spanish-language option in this slice, and ETIC's international page confirms Sound Design is among the certifications available in English.
_rec.accreditationStatus: NOT a Portuguese degree — VERIFIED IN ETIC'S OWN WORDS. It is NOT accredited by A3ES or DGES, is NOT a mestrado, and is NOT a pós-graduação in the Portuguese academic sense. It is a UK Pearson BTEC Higher National Diploma at Level 5, assigned its level "by Ofqual (Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation) under the Regulated Qualifications Framework (RQF), which forms part of the UK qualifications system", delivered in Portugal by a DGERT-certified vocational provider. ETIC states: "ETIC is not a higher education institution." It describes the programmes as "internationally recognised, enabling direct entry into the labour market as well as progression to further studies" — "progression to further studies" is the operative admission: an HND Level 5 is a stepping stone TOWARD a bachelor's, which is exactly what the optional Solent third year completes. For someone who already holds a BSc, the two-year award is a step DOWN and the three-year award is at best lateral.
_rec.visaEligible: CORRECTED — Yes, ETIC explicitly supports it, though not as a higher-education permit. ETIC's international page states that non-EU students need "a student visa and residence permit ... for the full duration of studies", obtained from a Portuguese embassy or consulate before travel and then processed with AIMA on arrival, and confirms that ETIC issues the enrolment document: "a confirmation letter is issued to prove the student is enrolled at the school, which can subsequently be submitted to AIMA for visa application purposes." It warns to "apply well in advance, as processing can take several months" and provides a dedicated channel (international@etic.pt, +351 213 942 140). This is a materially better position than most private providers in this batch — but note the legal basis is a study/training residence permit at a non-higher-education establishment, not the university student route, so it does not carry the same downstream rights. Get the specific permit article confirmed in writing.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: Yes, comfortably. VERIFIED: no degree, no music background and no formal prior qualification is required. Entry is by motivation letter, an OPTIONAL portfolio and an interview. His BSc sits far above the entry bar — which is precisely the problem.
_rec.entryRequirements: VERIFIED verbatim: a motivation letter outlining professional goals; a "portfolio or showreel" listed as OPTIONAL; attendance at an interview; and a "recommended english entry level: B1". Places are limited: "Enrolment in a specific timetable is limited to the number of available places" and "the opening of each course, class or timetable is subject to a minimum number of enrolments."
_rec.portfolioSpec: Portfolio or showreel is OPTIONAL — VERIFIED. This remains genuinely notable: with no portfolio yet built, this is one of the very few audio programmes across the four countries he could apply to today without producing a single finished track.
_rec.auditionSpec: Interview only. No audition, no test, no entrance exam. VERIFIED.

_rec.paymentPlans: VERIFIED and genuinely fair by the standards of this batch. Standard route: 24 monthly instalments of €485 with no surcharge. Prompt payment: 2 x €5,529 with a 5% discount built in. Non-tax-resident route (his): €3,492 up front then 23 x €354.26. Additional discounts published: PROMPT PAYMENT 5%, ALUMNI 6%, PARTNERS "according to defined protocol". Bank financing is offered via Caixa Geral de Depósitos, Santander, Banco CTT and BPI — all of which require Portuguese residency and income, so realistically inaccessible to him before arrival.

ETIC's site carries an "Erasmus+ Scholarships" menu item and offers Erasmus+ international internship mobility after completion subject to performance, but that is a placement scheme, not a fee reduction. _rec.facilities: VERIFIED and better documented than previously recorded: computer labs with individual Apple iMac workstations and headphones; Pro Tools, Logic Pro and Ableton Live; mixing consoles; professional microphones from Neumann, Sennheiser and AKG; studio monitors. Classes capped at 16 students, in person, Mon-Fri 14:00-18:00. Erasmus+ internship access on completion.
_rec.reputationSignals: ETIC is a long-established, DGERT-certified Portuguese creative school and a Pearson BTEC Accredited Centre since 2016, meaning the qualification carries external UK quality assurance under Ofqual's RQF. The Solent University recognition on the optional third year is a real, named UK university progression route. Small classes (max 16), transparent published pricing with genuinely fair instalments, explicit and detailed non-EU visa guidance with a dedicated international office, and no consumer complaints or red flags found. The decisive negatives are level and subject: it is not higher education, not a degree, not a master — and its content is media/live/installation sound design, not music production. Worth restating plainly: Portugal has essentially NO international private chain campus offering master-level music production or sound design — SAE, Abbey Road, Berklee, Point Blank and dBs all have zero presence there — so this is the strongest chain-adjacent option the country offers, and it still is not close.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: CORRECTED. Tuition €11,640 over two years (or €11,058 prompt-paid) PLUS €900 non-refundable application fees = €12,540 total to ETIC on the instalment route, or €11,958 prompt-paid. His first-year outlay as a non-tax-resident is front-loaded: €700 application + €3,492 first instalment = €4,192 due immediately, then €354.26/month. Add Lisbon living costs — the cheapest of the four capitals in this slice but now expensive for housing, realistically €900-€1,200/month. All-in over two years, tuition plus modest living: roughly €34,000-€41,000. ETIC publishes no living-cost estimate (UNVERIFIED).

_rec.recommendation: Cheap, English-taught, visa-supported and genuinely accessible — and still the wrong course, for two independent reasons. First, LEVEL: the two-year award is a BTEC Higher National Diploma at Level 5, which is BELOW bachelor's. ETIC says outright it is not a higher education institution. Paying €12,540 and two years to obtain a sub-bachelor vocational diploma when he already holds a BSc is a downgrade, not a postgraduate step. The newly-verified optional third year (Solent University recognition, +120 CATS, 360 total) only brings him back up to bachelor-equivalent — still not a master, and now three years and considerably more money. Second, and previously unverified, CONTENT: the module list is now confirmed and it is media, live-event and installation sound design — film and documentary post, game/VR/AR adaptive audio, P.A. rigging and calibration, DMX lighting control, broadcast LUFS compliance, QLab theatre playback, museum multichannel systems, Arduino sensor prototyping. There is no music production, no electronic music, no DJing, and the stated career outcome is "Sound Designer specialising in recording and post-production for video games, film, theatre, advertising and sound installations". That is a different profession from the one he wants. Correct the money on the record: tuition is €11,640 not €11,200, the schedule is 24 x €485 not 10 x €560, there IS a non-refundable application fee of €700 in year one plus €200 in year two, and as a non-tax-resident he must pay €3,492 up front rather than a first monthly instalment — so his day-one cash requirement is €4,192, not €560. What still makes it worth keeping on the page: it is the only entry in this batch with a published price, English delivery, NO IELTS requirement (B1 recommended only), an OPTIONAL portfolio, and explicit written non-EU visa support including an AIMA enrolment letter. If his real constraint turns out to be that he cannot reach IELTS 7.5 or cannot build a portfolio in time for a 2027 master's, this is the fallback that would still take him — but he should choose ETIC's music production certification rather than this sound design one, because this one does not teach what he wants to do. And the honest structural finding stands: Portugal has no international private chain master's in this field at all, so if Portugal matters to him the search must move to private Portuguese universities such as Universidade Católica Portuguesa's Som e Imagem mestrado.

THREE MATERIAL MONEY CORRECTIONS: (1) tuition is €5,820/year undiscounted, i.e. 24 instalments of €485 = €11,640 total, or 2 x €5,529 = €11,058 with the 5% prompt-payment discount — the previously stated €5,600/year, 10 x €560, €11,200 total was wrong on all three counts; (2) a non-refundable APPLICATION fee of €700 (year 1) and €200 (year 2) exists and had been recorded as absent; (3) a distinct schedule applies to "CITIZENS WITHOUT TAX RESIDENCE IN PORTUGAL" — €3,492 first instalment plus 23 x €354.26 — which is the schedule this candidate would face, front-loading €3,492 instead of €485. The fee table is dated 2025 and states prices may change before enrolment. QUALIFICATION SHARPENED: the award is a "BTEC Higher National Diploma, Level 5, 240 CATS", Ofqual-regulated under the RQF; NEW FINDING from the certification-structure image is that the optional third year carries "SOLENT UNIVERSITY RECOGNITION, 120 CATS", giving 360 CATS and a UK bachelor's-level top-up — previously unknown. VISA CORRECTED from UNVERIFIED to supported: ETIC's international page confirms it issues an enrolment confirmation letter for AIMA visa purposes and runs a dedicated international office. _rec.accreditationStatus: OFFICIAL. In practice: valid across the EHEA, valid for PhD entry, unambiguous for the student visa, and recognised by employers as a real engineering master. Caveat worth knowing: this is a NEW programme launching in the 2026/27 course, so there are no graduate-outcome data and no alumni network yet.
_rec.visaEligible: Yes — the safest possible category. An official Spanish Máster Universitario at a recognised private university satisfies art. 52.1.a RLOEx directly. One item to confirm: the programme page states the schedule is 'weekday afternoons with some online sessions', so he should verify with admissions that the weekly teaching load meets the 20-hours-per-week guideline in the Spanish immigration management criteria and that at least 50% of the programme is delivered in person. For an official 60-ECTS full-time master this is normally straightforward, but the phrase 'some online sessions' means it is worth one email.
_rec.focus: Acoustics engineering, audio signal processing, vibration control, noise control, and applied artificial intelligence in acoustics. This is ENGINEERING, not music production.

_rec.accreditationStatus: OFFICIAL — and this is the decisive distinction in this entire batch. This is a Máster Universitario of Universitat Ramon Llull, a private but fully official Spanish university whose degrees are ANECA/AQU-verified. It is valid across the EHEA, gives access to a Spanish doctorate, and carries full official professional standing. It is the direct counterexample to every título propio and private certificate in this batch: same private sector, completely different legal standing. _rec.visaEligible: YES — and now backed by documentary evidence rather than inference. An official Máster Universitario at a recognised Spanish university is the cleanest possible basis for a Spanish student visa and subsequent residence permit. VERIFIED CORROBORATION: La Salle's admissions terms contain an explicit visa-denial clause — 'Visa denial: the reservation of the place will be reimbursed, except for €300 for administrative expenses. The presentation of supporting documentation is required.' A school only writes that clause if it routinely admits non-EU students who apply for visas. The admissions process also explicitly requires a PASSPORT 'for international students'. This is as safe as it gets.
_rec.focus: Acoustics, audio engineering, audio signal processing and vibrations — an ENGINEERING master, not a creative music-production one. Covers noise and vibration control, environmental acoustics, sound quality enhancement and audio system optimisation.
_rec.whatYouStudy: 60 ECTS across 10 modules of 5 ECTS plus a 10-ECTS thesis. Verified module examples: 'Métodos numéricos para bajas frecuencias: FEM y BEM' (5 ECTS), 'Métodos numéricos para altas frecuencias' (5 ECTS), and 'Temas avanzados en acústica, audio y vibraciones' (5 ECTS). This is finite-element and boundary-element numerical modelling, applied physics and signal processing — mathematically demanding engineering work. Taught partly at the IASLab (Interactive Laboratory of Arts and Sciences). Classes are held on weekday afternoons with some online sessions.
_rec.durationEcts: 10 months, 60 ECTS. In-person, weekday afternoons, with some online sessions. 30 places available.
_rec.language: ENGLISH — now VERIFIED, resolving the previous uncertainty. The programme is taught entirely in English. _rec.reputationSignals: Universitat Ramon Llull is one of Spain's most respected private universities, and La Salle Barcelona has a long track record in audiovisual and telecommunications engineering, including an established Grado en Ingeniería Audiovisual. The official Máster Universitario status is the key signal and is what separates this from everything else in the batch. Institutional maturity is evident in the admissions terms — statutory withdrawal rights, a formal visa-denial refund clause, Flywire international payments, published price lists, and a 30+ scheme scholarship programme. NEW RED FLAG, and he should weigh it: this is a BRAND-NEW PROGRAMME launching in the 2026-27 academic year — La Salle announced it alongside two new AI masters. He would be in the first or second cohort ever, which means no graduate outcomes data, no alumni network, no track record, and the usual first-run teething problems. SECOND RED FLAG: he may not meet the published entry requirements at all (see entryRequirements). Neither is a quality concern about the institution; both are real risks for him specifically.
_rec.recommendation: This remains the ONLY programme in the private-sector Spanish audio landscape that would give him an official, ANECA-standing, EHEA-valid, PhD-eligible master's degree with a clean student-visa path — and verification has made it considerably more concrete and, in one respect, more doubtful. THE GOOD NEWS: the price is now known and is more reasonable than feared at €11,940, only modestly above ENTI's indicative €7,570 for a qualification in a completely different legal class; it is taught entirely in ENGLISH, so his lack of Spanish is not a barrier here as it is everywhere else in this batch; real scholarships of 20–50% exist and are plausibly within reach if his GPA converts to 8.0 or above, which could bring tuition to €7,000–€9,500; and the formal visa-denial refund clause is documentary proof they routinely handle non-EU students. THE BAD NEWS, and he must not skip it: Software Engineering is NOT on the published list of accepted bachelor's degrees. La Salle names Mechanical, Telecommunications Systems, Industrial Technology, Audiovisual Systems, Physics, Aerospace, Mathematics and Civil Engineering 'or equivalent'. The previous assessment that his degree makes him a natural fit was too confident — he would be arguing his way in under an equivalence clause, against a syllabus heavy in FEM/BEM numerical methods and applied physics that a software engineering curriculum does not typically prepare him for. He should email Sardor Abdullaev or Iona Lafont with his transcript BEFORE investing any hope here, and ask three questions: does a BSc in Software Engineering qualify, what English evidence and minimum score do they require, and what scholarship would his converted GPA attract. Note too that this is a brand-new programme with no graduates yet. MY CANDID VERDICT IS UNCHANGED IN SUBSTANCE: this is the safest qualification and the worst match for his stated dream. It is acoustics and audio ENGINEERING — noise control, environmental acoustics, numerical modelling — and it will not, by itself, make him an international DJ. It is worth serious consideration only if he decides he wants an official credential and a legal foothold in Europe first and a music career second. That is a legitimate strategy and deserves to be put to him explicitly — but he should now also know he might not be eligible for it.

_rec.portfolioSpec: MAJOR CORRECTION — the previous record described this only as 'a written project description' and called the full spec unpublished. It IS published, and it is far more demanding. TEST 1 (digital, uploaded after the application deadline on emailed instructions) requires THREE work samples: (1) a recording with him in a LEADING role; (2) a recording where he COLLABORATES WITH OTHER MUSICIANS OR ARTISTS; (3) documentation of collaborative artistic work such as a concert or installation. Audio must be MP3, max 50 MB, max 8 minutes; video MP4, max 100 MB per file; credits identifying all participants and a description of work processes are required. Plus a text of maximum 700 words presenting himself, his background and interests, and what motivates him to apply. Test 1 is assessed pass/fail.
_rec.auditionSpec: MAJOR CORRECTION AND THE DECISIVE FINDING ON THIS PROGRAMME. The previous record left the entrance examination as 'three components, detail UNVERIFIED'. The detail is published and it is a performing-musician audition held ON CAMPUS IN STOCKHOLM. TEST 2 — Musical performance ability: from an assignment given on the day, and TOGETHER WITH TWO MUSICIANS PROVIDED BY KMH, he must prepare and perform a short piece of music THAT INCLUDES IMPROVISATION. Structure: 30 minutes solo preparation, 15 minutes rehearsal with the two musicians, a performance of maximum 5 minutes, then oral reflection; about 60 minutes total, scored 0–6 on musical interpretation and artistic reflection. TEST 3 — Artistic reflection and musical expression: an on-campus interview of about 20 minutes discussing the Test 1 works, his creative process and his motivation, scored 0–6. Two consequences the previous record missed entirely: (a) he would have to perform live improvised music with professional musicians, which no amount of DAW portfolio work substitutes for; (b) Tests 2 and 3 are in person in Stockholm, so he must travel from Tunisia — and enter Schengen on a short-stay visa — BEFORE any admission decision exists.

After checking the official syllabus and the published entrance-test specification, it is BETTER THAN CLAIMED ON LANGUAGE AND MUCH WORSE THAN CLAIMED ON ADMISSIBILITY, and the second point governs. Resolved in his favour: the language of instruction is ENGLISH, stated verbatim in the KAIM1 syllabus — the previous record's biggest open question, now closed, and he should not waste the email asking it. Also confirmed: no music bachelor required, sound art and music in computer games are named parts of the remit, SEK 264,000/yr, SEK 900 application fee, roughly three full-tuition scholarships institution-wide (plus FAS+ insurance) decided only after May admission. Resolved against him, decisively: the entrance examination is not the written project description the previous record described. Test 1 demands three recorded works including one where he leads and one where he collaborates with other musicians or artists. Test 2 is an ON-CAMPUS live performance in Stockholm where he must prepare and perform improvised music with two musicians KMH assigns him, scored 0–6. Test 3 is a 20-minute on-campus interview. That is a performing-musician audition, and it is the sole basis of selection. A man with no conservatory training, no ensemble experience and no portfolio cannot pass it in one year of bedroom production, and he would have to fund travel and a Schengen visa to Stockholm to fail it. Add that KMH still has not published whether autumn 2027 is even an admission year. VERDICT: do not build his 2027 plan on this. Revisit AIM only if he ever acquires genuine live-improvisation ability, in which case it becomes a strong target because the degree itself is a real, English-taught, state-accredited master that does not require a music bachelor.

MECHANISM THAT MATTERS: a 50% TA or GSR appointment in the UC system carries full FEE REMISSION (tuition and most campus fees) plus a salary, and for international students the Nonresident Supplemental Tuition is also waived for GSRs/TAs in many cases — this is a genuine full-funding mechanism, but at M.S. level it is NOT guaranteed at admission and must be hunted for term by term. _rec.fitNotes: STILL NOT A MASTER'S — but the correct verdict is now sharper than "unaccredited marketing". It is a real, NCFE-accredited, Home-Office-overseen, Level 5 vocational qualification, and Abbey Road Institute London genuinely holds a Student Visa sponsorship licence: "Abbey Road Institute London holds a Student Visa sponsorship licence. This means that we are now able to accept a limited number of international students who require a Student visa to study on the UK." So a Tunisian national CAN legally come and study here, unlike the Amsterdam campus. The problem is value, not legitimacy. He would pay £23,950 in full up front, with no work rights, to earn a Level 5 award — one level BELOW the BSc he already holds, and worth nothing towards a master's, a Level 7 recognition in Europe, or doctoral progression. The teaching and the Abbey Road access are probably excellent, and the portfolio bar ("we do not expect to receive high-quality productions") is realistically within reach for him. But as a step after a completed bachelor's, paying nearly £24k to move DOWN the qualification framework is hard to justify, especially with zero funding. RATED C for that reason, not because it is fake. If he wants the Abbey Road name cheaply, the 4-day Song Production Masterclass (10-13 Oct 2026, one day at Abbey Road Studios, three at Angel Studios, with Sylvia Massy) is the sane version of this.

_rec.whatYouStudy: CORRECTED SCOPE (quoted from the official page). Aim: "to explore, discover and comprehend the emerging digital technology and its aural impact in society; to find and exploit the possibilities it opens to acoustic communication, sonic interaction and new interfaces for musical expression". Named areas: "sound and music computing, sound art and auditory culture, sonic interaction design, artificial intelligence applied to sound design and music, game audio and acoustic branding". Tools and skills explicitly listed: "creative coding, physical computing, digital fabrication, sonic interaction design, extended reality, generative composition methods and other emerging technologies" — note how directly a software-engineering BSc maps onto creative coding and physical computing. Teaching is "project-oriented, combining practice with theory, hands-on with minds-on", with "intensive workshops" and "tutored studio work". Every student writes a Personal Study Plan (PSP); year 1 is programme/major core, year 2 is electives, minors and the thesis. Research anchor: the Sound and Physical Interaction research group (SOPI). CONFIRMED CROSS-REGISTRATION: "Majority of our students take courses from the Sibelius Academy Department of Music Technology, and these studies can be included to the MA degree." Closest internal partners: Aalto Department of Signal Processing and Acoustics and the Master's Programme in Information Networks.
_rec.entryRequirements: Programme page eligibility line: "Relevant Bachelor's degree". Aalto general eligibility: a bachelor's degree equivalent to 180 ECTS / three years full-time, giving eligibility for master's study in the awarding country, from an institution recognised in its national education system. He may apply before graduating provided the degree is awarded by the equivalent of 31 July 2027 (2026-cycle wording: 31 July 2026). ENGLISH TEST IS REQUIRED — Tunisia is NOT on Aalto's exemption list, so he must sit one of: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 with Writing 6.0; TOEFL iBT (tests from 21 Jan 2026 onward) total 4.5 with all four subtests 4.0, or, for pre-21-Jan-2026 tests, total 92 with Writing 22; PTE Academic overall 68 with Writing 61; Cambridge C1 Advanced grade A/B/C; Cambridge C2 Proficiency grade A/B/C or Level C1. Scores are valid two years from the test date and must be uploaded by the document deadline (2026 cycle: 9 January 2026, 15:00 UTC+2). APPLICATION FEE: EUR 100 for non-EU/EEA/Swiss citizens. One application form; a maximum of TWO study options may be ranked on it.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: YES — and unusually explicitly so for this applicant. The only stated degree condition is "Relevant Bachelor's degree"; there is no music-degree, music-theory or conservatory requirement anywhere on the page. Decisively, the published evaluation criteria for Artistic and/or design practice state: "Demonstrations of artistic and/or design work related to sound, e.g. artistic or commercial projects, publications, performance/exhibition documentations or other works of art and/or design in the audible domain. Proven musical competence of any kind (e.g. violin playing, DJ'ing etc) is a plus." DJing is named, in Aalto's own words, as a positive. The programme also states it "brings together a multicultural group of students with very versatile skills and backgrounds", and the toolset it teaches (creative coding, physical computing, generative composition) presupposes technical entrants. Selection is portfolio-, motivation- and interview-driven. Aalto does not publish an enumerated list of "relevant" fields — that single point remains unverified; confirm with arts-admissions@aalto.fi.
_rec.portfolioSpec: EXACT published spec: "The portfolio is presented and discussed during the application interview. The form and format of the portfolio is free; however, the portfolio should be online so that it can be accessed via Internet with a common web browser (Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox or Safari). The access to the portfolio might be password protected on the responsibility of the applicant. The portfolio may consist of individual art/design works, documentation of exhibitions and/or performances etc. The portfolio must showcase the applicant's previous academic, professional and/or scientific activity in a diverse and comprehensive manner. The applicant should be able to present the portfolio in 10 minutes." Maximum file size 1.0 GB; file named Portfolio-lastname-firstname.pdf; document language English. NOTE THE ODD HYBRID: Aalto asks for an online, browser-accessible portfolio AND names a PDF file — in practice submit a PDF that carries links out to hosted audio/video. NO fixed number of works, no per-track duration and no audio format are specified. Also required: motivation letter, max 4,000 characters, single PDF, English, explaining "why they wish to apply to the degree programme in question, what their particular areas of interest in this field are, and what their objectives and hopes are regarding the studies at the School of Arts, Design and Architecture"; and a CV (single PDF, English) with personal data, education, work experience, exhibitions, publications, awards and grants, study trips and positions of trust. "Lack of this application document will adversely affect the evaluation of the application."
_rec.auditionSpec: NO live audition and NO on-site test. Two-phase selection, both remote-capable. Phase I scores Suitability/Motivation letter plus Other areas of competence (CV); "the scoring and/or ranking of the first phase doesn't affect the final, 2nd phase scoring." Only the highest-ranked are invited onward, with at least 7 days' notice. Phase II: "applicants complete one or more assignments within the given time. The assignment(s) can be written or audible and is (are) based on the provided material and/or given topic. The assignment(s) is (are) submitted in electronic form as text file(s) with possible supporting graphs and images and/or as audio file(s)." Plus "a 30-minute interview" (Aalto states interviews "may be conducted remotely"), in which the portfolio is presented and discussed. Important caution published by the programme: "the application process aims at a balanced group of different kinds of students... even exceptional skills and talent in one field don't automatically guarantee that the applicant would be selected. Furthermore, the more there are applicants with a similar profile, the harder the competition is."

CORRECTIONS MADE TO THE INPUT RECORD: (1) The parent programme is the Master's Programme in ART AND MEDIA, not "New Media" — Sound in New Media is one of its majors alongside New Media, Photography, Visual Communication Design, Game Design and Development, Visual Cultures Curating and Contemporary Art, and Visual Arts Education. (2) The scholarship is the Aalto University Excellence Scholarship and now covers the FULL tuition fee, not "either 50% or 100%". (3) The deadline is NOT a prior-cycle date — 7 Dec 2026 to 5 Jan 2027 is published for autumn 2027. (4) An EUR 100 application fee for non-EU applicants was missing. (5) English test scores and the fact that Tunisia carries no exemption were missing; exact thresholds now recorded. (6) The programme description was skewed toward "concept design to live performance" wording that does not appear on the current page; replaced with the page's actual language. (7) The Sibelius Academy cross-registration claim is CONFIRMED on the official page. (8) Campus is Otaniemi, Espoo. (9) The evaluation criteria explicitly naming DJ'ing as a plus were absent from the record and are the single most decision-relevant sentence for him. _rec.fitNotes: The strongest Nordic option on the list by a wide margin, and the only one where the official evaluation criteria literally say "Proven musical competence of any kind (e.g. violin playing, DJ'ing etc) is a plus". No music degree, no instrument audition, no on-site test, no theory exam — a remote 30-minute interview plus a written-or-audio assignment. His software-engineering BSc is an asset rather than a liability here: the major teaches creative coding, physical computing and generative composition, and it sits next to Signal Processing and Acoustics. He can also pull Sibelius Academy Music Technology courses into the degree, which is the practical bridge from sound design toward music production. TWO REAL CAVEATS, which is why this is B and not A. First, money: EUR 20,000 per year, EUR 40,000 over the degree, with the only route to affordability being a competitive Excellence Scholarship that the programme is free to award to nobody — his admission and his funding stand or fall on the same application. Second, content drift: this is sound design, sonic interaction and sound art for media, installation and games, not club-music production or record mixing; the DJ/producer ambition is served obliquely. Practical plan: sit IELTS by spring 2027 at the latest (target 7.0 to leave headroom over the 6.5/6.0 floor), spend the next twelve months building a portfolio that pairs finished electronic tracks and DJ work with at least one technical/interactive sound project that shows the coding side, and note he can rank TWO study options on one form — pair this with a second Aalto or Finnish option rather than wasting the slot.

_rec.focus: Art-music composition (contemporary classical), with an electronic-composition and sound-art application stream and a sound-technology course in the core
_rec.whatYouStudy: "The international MA program in composition enables the student to develop his/her artistic and theoretical activity in a stimulating creative and critical environment, with access to the staff's wide professional experience and theoretical knowledge and supported by an inspiring learning community." Structure, per the official page: one-to-one private lessons with a composition tutor plus collective composition classes; "the subject of composition is by far the largest item in the syllabus, generating almost half the credits in the first three terms"; first two terms also carry "a course in sound technology, either electronic or instrumental, a course on artistic research, a course on music analysis and an introduction to some recent issues [in] music composition", plus electives. Weekly seminars analyse notable compositions and discuss students' research. The school "collaborates with professional musicians who give workshops where students' works are heard and discussed". Master's project options: (a) 20-credit composition + 10-credit paper, (b) 10-credit composition + 20-credit paper, or (c) a 26-credit practical project + a 4-credit reflection. CONFIRMED on the official page (previously flagged as aggregator-sourced): "Students are offered the opportunity to have their final project performed by the Caput Ensemble at a graduation concert." No PhD in music yet, though one is in development.
_rec.entryRequirements: NOW PUBLISHED AND CONFIRMED (previously logged as UNVERIFIED). General: "a bachelor's degree or equivalent university education that supports the applicant's ability to meet the [demands] of the MA Program", with certified academic transcripts. Programme-specific: "Applicants will have completed a BA degree in composition or the related fields of music theory or the arts. Non musical academic degrees are not excluded, especially on graduate and doctoral levels. Applicants who do not have a BA degree in composition can be recommended to the program provided they demonstrate a comparable knowledge, experience and technical ability in the field of musical composition." Language: "Students must be proficient in spoken and written English in the academic context. In case the admission committee has doubts regarding the applicant's competence, he/she may be required to submit evidence of English proficiency" — so no blanket IELTS/TOEFL requirement, but a test can be demanded. Documents: certified degree certificate(s) and transcript(s) (PDF); ONE reference, max one page, submitted directly by the referee via an emailed link (waived for former LHÍ students); letter of motivation in English (PDF); CV in English (PDF); portfolio. Non-refundable application fee ISK 5,000, payable per application; the application is not valid until both submitted and paid.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: TECHNICALLY YES, PRACTICALLY DEMANDING. Quoted: "Non musical academic degrees are not excluded, especially on graduate and doctoral levels." But the same paragraph sets the real bar: an applicant without a BA in composition must "demonstrate a comparable knowledge, experience and technical ability in the field of musical composition" — i.e. the door is open only if the portfolio performs at conservatory-graduate level. With no music degree, no conservatory training and no professional audio experience, he would be asked to evidence exactly what he does not yet have. The sibling MMus in New Audiences and Innovative Practice (NAIP), described on the department page as suitable for musicians from diverse backgrounds with "innovative and interdisciplinary approaches to creating and communicating music", is the more permissive door — but it carries the identical Department of Music tuition, which is the real blocker.
_rec.portfolioSpec: NOW PUBLISHED AND CONFIRMED (previously UNVERIFIED). Item 5, "Portfolio of works (PDF/URL)", compulsory: "Portfolio of 5 scores with or without audio files are required for applications in instrumental composition. Applicants in electronic composition and sound art must submit 5 works. Applicants for interdisciplinary studies (composing for film, theater etc.) must submit 5 original works." So his route would be the electronic-composition/sound-art stream: FIVE works, no notation obligation on that stream. No per-work duration, no audio format and no total runtime cap are specified. Submitted as PDF or URL.
_rec.auditionSpec: NO live audition and no on-site entrance test published. "An admission committee assesses applications on the grounds of assessment of the subject material, the applicant's motivation and aim with the study at the Iceland University of the Arts and the interview(s) with the applicant." Interview(s) form part of selection; the mode is not stated, so confirm whether they are held remotely. Additional risk on the official page: "If the number of applicants meeting the admission requirements for the study program falls below the minimum threshold, the program will not be offered for the upcoming academic year."
_rec.tuitionIntl: BLOCKING FINDING — the amount is now published and it is very large. From LHÍ's tuition-fee page, for the academic year 2026-2027, non-EEA students pay per academic year: Department of Music ISK 5,500,000 (also Performing Arts and Film ISK 5,500,000; Architecture, Fine Art, Design and Arts Education ISK 4,500,000). ISK 5,500,000 is roughly EUR 37,000-38,000 per year at mid-2026 rates, i.e. on the order of EUR 75,000 for the two-year MA — indicative conversion, verify at the time. LHÍ states the fees "reflect the actual cost of the studies and the amount may change between academic years", are charged in ISK by bank transfer, are non-refundable, and "must be paid in full before enrolment or continuation of studies can be confirmed. Failure to pay on time or in full may result in the loss of the study place." The ISK 100,000 annual registration fee does NOT rescue him: it applies to "students with citizenship within the EEA, the Faroe Islands, Greenland and Switzerland as well as all students regardless of nationality who started studying at LHÍ in the fall of 2025 or earlier." Only two exemptions exist, neither of which he meets: holding an Icelandic permanent residence permit (or one that can lead to it), or studying at LHÍ via an international university cooperation project, cooperation programme or university network. Separate application fee ISK 5,000, non-refundable, per application, not deducted from any other fee.
