STILL UNVERIFIED: whether the interview can be conducted remotely; whether non-EEA students also owe the ISK 100,000 registration fee on top of tuition; whether the ISK 5,500,000 figure will be revised for 2027-2028 (LHÍ warns it "may change between academic years"); and the full admission detail for the sibling NAIP MMus.
_rec.fitNotes: DOWNGRADED TO C — this is now a confirmed financial dead end, not merely an unverified one. LHÍ has published the number the earlier record could not find: from autumn 2026 a non-EEA student in the Department of Music pays ISK 5,500,000 per academic year, roughly EUR 37,000-38,000, about EUR 75,000 across the MA, with tuition due in full before enrolment can be confirmed, no refunds, and the institution stating flat out that it offers no scholarships for tuition or living costs — in Iceland, one of Europe's most expensive countries. The only two exemptions are Icelandic residency and inbound exchange/network mobility; neither is available to him as a direct-entry Tunisian applicant. Set the money aside and the fit is still weak: it is a contemporary art-music composition MA built around private composition tutorials, score-based work and a Caput Ensemble graduation concert, with electronics as one course and one application stream. The published entry rule is honest about the bar — a non-composition bachelor is "not excluded" but must "demonstrate a comparable knowledge, experience and technical ability in the field of musical composition", which is precisely the evidence he cannot produce this cycle. There is one genuine positive to bank: the electronic-composition and sound-art portfolio route asks for five works with no notation requirement, which is a spec he could realistically meet in a year — the same five-work package would serve the Aalto portfolio. Recommendation: do not apply. If Iceland matters for non-academic reasons, email lhi@lhi.is and registration@lhi.is to check whether the NAIP MMus route or any Erasmus/network mobility arrangement could bring him in under the cooperation-programme exemption, since that is the only published mechanism that removes the fee.

(1) 'Create Your Future' AY 2026/27 — 4 awards at 50% of tuition, open to all applicants, renewable on grades, deadline was 7 June 2026 — BUT it applies to MUSIC BUSINESS ONLY, not Audio Production. _rec.auditionSpec: No audition and no interview — confirmed absent from the entry-requirements page. Selection is on portfolio, motivation letter, CV and academic/music documentation.
_rec.englishTest: CONFIRMED VERBATIM: 'Demonstrated competence in English (for non-English speaking countries)'. IELTS is NOT named and NO score is specified anywhere on the entry-requirements page. Notably lenient versus Berklee (7.5) or SAE degrees (IELTS 6.0).
_rec.intakes: One full-time intake per year, October. CONFIRMED: next intake starts 5 October 2026, capped cohort. For a 2027 full-time start, PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date — expect early October 2027.
_rec.applicationOpens: Rolling — applications open well ahead of the October start.
_rec.deadline: CORRECTED — a deadline IS published, contrary to the previous 'no published deadline' note. Applications for the October 2026 intake close 5 SEPTEMBER 2026, exactly one month before the start date. The equivalent 2027 deadline should therefore fall in early September 2027: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date, but plan on roughly one month before start rather than assuming open-ended rolling admission.
_rec.tuitionPerYear: VERIFIED EXACTLY. No EU/non-EU distinction — the same fees apply to all applicants. One-year full-time: €18,860 upfront (Plan C), €19,380 in 3 term instalments of €6,460 (Plan B, 16 weeks per term), or €20,160 in 12 monthly instalments of €1,680 (Plan A).
_rec.tuitionTotal: €18,860 (upfront) to €20,160 (monthly), plus the €200 application fee. Monthly payment costs €1,300 more than upfront.
_rec.otherFees: €200 application fee — confirmed, and confirmed refundable if the applicant does not complete the admission process. No materials, exam, insurance or equipment fees published — UNVERIFIED whether any exist.
_rec.equipmentRequired: UNVERIFIED — the course page specifies no laptop or personal-equipment requirement and notes access to 'industry-standard equipment and studios' on site. Given the portfolio requirement, he would need his own production setup before applying regardless.
_rec.paymentPlans: Three, all published exactly: Plan A €200 + €20,160 (12 × €1,680); Plan B €200 + €19,380 (3 × €6,460); Plan C €200 + €18,860 upfront. No early-bird, alumni or referral discounts published — UNVERIFIED.
_rec.scholarships: None published — UNVERIFIED. The only financial relief mentioned is a Dutch income-tax deduction on study costs, which the institute itself qualifies heavily: it does not apply to those receiving government benefits or not yet employed, depends on tax bracket and income earned, and the rules changed in 2022 — the institute disclaims liability and refers applicants to the Belastingdienst. Worthless to someone who will not be a Dutch taxpayer. No student loans, no study finance.
_rec.facilities: Abbey Road Institute Amsterdam campus with industry-standard equipment and studios; detailed inventory not published — UNVERIFIED. The brand connection to Abbey Road Studios is the principal draw.
_rec.reputationSignals: The Abbey Road name is the strongest studio brand in the world and carries genuine weight with engineers and producers. The institute is a legitimate registered Dutch entity (ARI Education NL B.V., CRKBO-approved) with fully transparent pricing, a clear professional admissions specification, published deadlines and small capped cohorts. Honest counterweights: no academic accreditation whatsoever, an explicit written inability to help non-EU students with visas, and a €19,000–€20,000 price for a one-year non-degree diploma. No published complaints or red flags found.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: €19,060–€20,360 for the year (tuition plus the €200 application fee), before living costs. Amsterdam housing is expensive and scarce and the institute publishes no living-cost estimate (UNVERIFIED). Realistic all-in for one year: comfortably over €35,000.

_rec.verificationNotes: Three pages opened and verified. CORRECTION: a firm application deadline IS published — 5 September 2026 for the 5 October 2026 start, one month before commencement. The previous 'no published deadline — rolling until the cohort fills' was wrong and would have caused him to miss a cut-off. NEW DETAIL: 48 tuition weeks; timetable Monday–Thursday 10:00–14:00 plus Friday workshops; the tax deduction carries explicit institute-published caveats (does not apply to the unemployed or benefit recipients, rules changed 2022, verify with Belastingdienst). CONFIRMED EXACTLY AS RECORDED: all three payment plans (€18,860 / €19,380 as 3 × €6,460 / €20,160 as 12 × €1,680), the €200 refundable application fee, the CRKBO short-vocational-education status, the 'not eligible for NL undergraduate student loans' statement, the visa statement word-for-word, the 4–8 production portfolio spec word-for-word, the flexible music-qualification wording word-for-word, and the absence of any named IELTS score.
_rec.valueVerdict: AVOID. Decisive reason: the institute states in writing it 'cannot assist non-EU residents with their VISA application', so a Tunisian applicant cannot get there — and separately, €19,000–€20,000 for a one-year non-accredited diploma is master-level money for a certificate with no academic standing.
_rec.recommendation: Blocked for him — but the portfolio specification is the single most valuable thing to come out of this entire research batch. Take the entry spec and treat it as his 12-month build target: 4 to 8 finished productions in MP3 or WAV, deliberately spanning DIFFERENT roles (performer, producer, engineer, writer), each accompanied by a written description of exactly what he contributed. That is concrete, achievable from where he stands today, and it is close to a universal currency — it would materially strengthen a Berklee Valencia application and almost any other portfolio-gated route. Build to that spec and apply elsewhere. On the programme itself, three reasons to rule it out: the visa wall is explicit and in writing; €19,000–€20,000 buys a non-accredited diploma with no credits and no academic standing; and it is a studio-engineering course rather than a DJ or electronic-music one, so it is off-target for his stated goal even setting the other problems aside. One correction he must not miss: applications DO close, one month before the start date, so this is not the open-ended rolling admission previously assumed. Finally, note the pattern — both Dutch private providers in this slice are visa-dead for identical reasons, which means the Netherlands as a whole should drop down his country list unless he finds an NVAO-accredited, bekostigd institution.

_rec.recommendation: This is the best-matched programme in this batch and the only one that is simultaneously a real accredited master's degree, taught in English, aimed squarely at producers and DJs, and backed by a documented, functioning non-EU student-visa pathway. The curriculum literally contains Electronic Music Production and Performance and DJing electives, and the school names DJs among its graduate outcomes — that is his stated goal in the school's own words. His software-engineering background is a genuine asset here, not a liability: Max/MSP, interactive media and hardware/software design are core content, and Berklee explicitly lists 'software and/or hardware designers' as an outcome. Four hard realities. FIRST, money: roughly $67k–71k all-in for one year, billed in USD, plus an unpublished mandatory insurance cost. SECOND, the scholarship picture is weaker than commonly reported — the €125,000 figure is reserved for Valencian students and he cannot touch it; his realistic levers are the General Scholarship and the Diversity Scholarship (up to 50%), the latter requiring a deliberate 3-minute video or 500-word essay by 1 February, sent to a separate email address from the main application. THIRD, IELTS 7.5 from a standing start is a serious 12-month study target and should be booked as a diagnostic in 2026. FOURTH, the award is a US Master of Music, not a Spanish official master — excellent internationally and perfectly adequate for a production career, but it would need homologación if he ever wanted Spanish PhD entry or public-sector recognition. For a DJ/producer career that last point barely matters. VERDICT: worth the money ONLY if he lands 40–50%+ in scholarship AND spends the next twelve months building three finished tracks strong enough to carry the portfolio. At full sticker price this is poor value against simply building a catalogue independently. Concrete plan: sit IELTS by early 2027, produce the three portfolio tracks through 2026, and apply Early Action (1 Nov 2026) with the Diversity Scholarship submission prepared in parallel.

No assistantship system waives full tuition. The FAFSA route ("April 1 priority deadline... for federal funds and CalArts grants") is closed to non-US citizens for federal aid. Targeted awards such as the Herb Alpert School of Music Scholarship for MFA students require a separate application — amounts UNVERIFIED, but they are partial tuition awards, not full rides. CalArts openly prefers maths/CS/engineering applicants, accepts code and hardware schematics as portfolio items, holds no audition, and will let one portfolio item be a speculative instrument design. If he could pay, this is where a software engineer becomes an electronic-music artist. But at ~USD 78k/yr with only partial merit scholarships and no assistantship route, it is unaffordable without Fulbright — which has closed for the 2027 intake. Apply only if a full external sponsor materialises.

For Opera of the Future / Responsive Environments the de facto expectation is documented built work (instruments, software, installations, demo videos, code repositories), which a software engineer can assemble without any musical training. However, if you have solid professional industry experience rather than academic achievement, this may be acceptable for entry to study at this level through a process called Accreditation of Prior Experiential Learning (APEL).' Also confirmed: 'We welcome international applications with equivalent qualifications of our entry requirements' with country-specific equivalence pages. And USW operates a published Contextual Admissions Policy: it 'supports students who have the potential to succeed and who may have faced barriers that make it more difficult to access university', meaning a lower offer may be made based on background and individual circumstances. THE REAL CAVEAT: the 2:1 floor is a full classification higher than the Hertfordshire programmes' 2:2. That is the one place where USW is stricter than Hertfordshire. Note the format: a LINK to a website or digital portfolio, not a physical or time-limited submission — so a well-built personal site, or a curated SoundCloud/Bandcamp presence with production credits and process documentation, satisfies it. Unlike Queen's ten-minute video cap and four permitted art-music formats, there is no restriction on genre or duration, so electronic music and DJ work fit without contortion.

_rec.scholarships: MAJOR CORRECTION. The prior record said specific awards open to a Tunisian national were 'UNVERIFIED' and told him to ask the international office. That is now resolved, and the answer is strongly in his favour. USW's official international scholarships pages confirm: (1) CHANCELLOR'S INTERNATIONAL DEVELOPMENT SCHOLARSHIP of £2,500 for students from eligible regions — and the official eligible-countries page lists TUNISIA EXPLICITLY BY NAME under Africa, alongside Algeria, Egypt, Libya and Morocco. It is available for postgraduate courses and it replaces the standard scholarship rather than stacking with it. (2) INTERNATIONAL OFFICE SCHOLARSHIPS of up to £2,000 for postgraduates who are self-funding — superseded for him by the larger Chancellor's award. (3) EARLY CAS SCHOLARSHIP of an additional £500 on top of an existing USW scholarship for students who are CAS-ready by 31 MAY for a September intake — the page gives a worked example confirming a £2,500 Chancellor's award becomes £3,000 with the early CAS bonus. MECHANISM CONFIRMED VERBATIM: 'You will be automatically considered for one of these awards when we receive your application. You do not need to make a separate application and confirmation of the scholarship will be included in your offer letter.' CONDITIONS: he must be self-funding (students sponsored by their government or a company are NOT eligible), must pay the minimum deposit stipulated in the offer letter by the date on the Acceptance Form, and scholarships do not apply to English language courses or placement years. NET EFFECT: roughly £3,000 off, taking effective tuition to about £14,900, guaranteed and automatic rather than competitive. Chevening and GREAT remain the routes to full funding, but note the sponsorship exclusion — a full government scholarship would displace the USW award rather than add to it.

The BBC National Orchestra and Chorus of Wales placement does imply access to broadcast-grade orchestral recording contexts, which is a real and unusual asset.

_rec.valueVerdict: WORTH IT. It is an accredited Level 7 MSc from a Welsh public university, explicitly open to a non-music engineering graduate ('an appropriate area', plus APEL and contextual admissions), it has the lowest English requirement of the six with a possible waiver if his BSc was English-medium, it publishes the only concrete portfolio specification he can actually build toward, and it carries a confirmed automatic £2,500–£3,000 scholarship for which Tunisia is named by name — bringing effective tuition to about £14,900, the lowest of the four UK options. The caveats are real but manageable: a 2:1 floor rather than a 2:2, an undocumented facilities inventory, and roughly £15,000 still to self-fund.
_rec.recommendation: CONFIRMED AS THE STRONGEST UK PICK, and UPGRADED on the most important axis. THE MAJOR CORRECTION: the prior record listed fundingLevel as 'Check' and said awards open to a Tunisian were UNVERIFIED. They are now verified and they are good. USW's Chancellor's International Development Scholarship of £2,500 names TUNISIA EXPLICITLY on its official eligible-countries list, is awarded AUTOMATICALLY with no separate application, and is confirmed in the offer letter. On top of that, an Early CAS Scholarship adds £500 if he is CAS-ready by 31 May — USW's own worked example confirms £2,500 becomes £3,000. Effective tuition therefore falls from £17,900 to about £14,900, guaranteed rather than competitive. That is a better funding position than Hertfordshire's (whose comparable awards demand a £5,000 tuition deposit cleared months in advance) and it is the difference between 'check with the office' and 'money he can bank on'. Two conditions matter: he must be SELF-FUNDING (government- or company-sponsored students are excluded, so a Chevening award would displace this rather than add to it), and he must pay the deposit stipulated in the offer letter by the date on the Acceptance Form. EVERYTHING ELSE CONFIRMS EXACTLY: £17,900 international 2026/27 with a within-course fee-hold commitment, IELTS 6.0 with 5.5 in each component (the lowest bar of the six) with a possible waiver if he studied through the medium of English, the 2:1 in 'an appropriate area' with APEL and contextual admissions, the verbatim digital-portfolio requirement (website or digital portfolio, first section of the personal statement or section 12 of the form), September 2027 full-time and part-time apply links already live, and the BBC National Orchestra and Chorus of Wales placement. THE ONE HONEST CAVEAT that keeps this at B rather than A: the 2:1 floor is a full classification stricter than Hertfordshire's 2:2, and the studio facilities are undocumented on the page where Hertfordshire's are exhaustively listed — he should request a facilities list before committing. HIS TWELVE-MONTH PLAN FOR THIS APPLICATION: build the website/digital portfolio USW explicitly asks for, since it is the only published spec in this set and it accommodates electronic music and DJ work without contortion; email admissions to ask whether his English-medium BSc waives IELTS, and if not sit it targeting 6.0 with no band under 5.5; apply early in the 2027 cycle and aim to be CAS-ready by 31 May 2027 to capture the extra £500. Rank this second overall behind MTU Cork, and first among the UK options.

Compulsory modules with ECTS: Technologie audio (12), Projets de production / 'Book' (24), Projet de recherche (22), Prise de son classique (9), Prise de son jazz et musiques actuelles (9), Mixage musiques actuelles (9), Mixage musique acoustique (9), Travaux pratiques FSMSI, Communication et gestion de projet (4), Stage FSMSI (20), plus law/regulation and live-performance safety modules. Applicants must have a very good knowledge of music theory, a sound musical culture, a knowledge of composition (harmony and/or counterpoint) and musical analysis.' French: candidates admitted to the 2nd cycle who are not nationals of francophone countries must present CEFR B1 before 30 June preceding first enrolment and B2 before 10 December following first enrolment.
_rec.portfolioSpec: Eligibility stage: 'Review of each candidate's project portfolio, CV and covering letter. Candidates will be required to submit 3 personal musical, sound or audiovisual projects demonstrating a degree of originality or creativity, or simply showing a certain level of technical mastery. The projects are free and may take any form: score, recorded music, model, sound recording, sound fiction, soundtrack for images, film music, sound design, video creation, audiovisual music clip, short film, video sequence of filmed music, etc.' Each project must carry an explanatory note on artistic aims, choices, constraints, locations and tools used plus an assessment of the result, stating what the candidate personally implemented — 'This note must be concise and may not under no circumstances exceed 3 pages.' Projects uploaded to the registration platform by midnight on 24 May 2026.
_rec.auditionSpec: Jury pre-selection of applications 4 May 2026; eligibility selection 1 June 2026. Admission tests, all on site: oral test in musical training (16 June 2026); oral test in sciences (17 June 2026); critical listening test on recordings OR comparative analysis test on films/videos/film-repertoire extracts (17 June 2026); interviews in French with the jury on the submitted personal projects and professional experience (18-19 June 2026). Roughly 8 places per year at FSMS level (per Onisep) — UNVERIFIED against the school's own page.

_rec.language: French (a compulsory 'Anglais, le langage comme matière, matériau et matériel' module in UE3)
_rec.whatYouStudy: Semesters 7 and 9 modules: 'Création sonore appliquée', 'Workshop applicatif', 'Production, diffusion et perception du son, appliquées au design sonore', 'Informatique sonore et technique son', 'Workshop arduino', 'Méthodologie créative en design sonore', 'Atelier Radio', 'Éléments scientifiques', 'Concepts de design et cognition auditive appliqués au design sonore', 'Histoire et théorie du sonore', 'Ateliers de recherche et création (ARC)', 'Anthropocène : usage et mésusage du monde', histoire des arts, pratique professionnelle, pré-mémoire then mémoire. Semester 8 is international exchange or a company placement. Semester 10 = mémoire and plastic-work defence before a jury of professionals. The year opens with a two-week 'workshop applicatif' answering a real brief from an industrial or institutional partner, in mixed teams with ENSCI design students — past clients: Décathlon, SETRAM/Le Mans Métropole tram sonification, Groupe PSA (gestural and sound interfaces), SNCF Direction Innovation, Maison de la Radio / Radio France, RATP, GHT Psychiatrie Sainte-Anne. Students also run '24 heures' of radio on the school station Radio-on and produce work for Le Mans Sonore, the city's international sound biennial.

Accepted profiles: 'Le.la candidat.e peut être diplômé.e d'une filière artistique ou d'électroacoustique des universités (ou être inscrit.e en licence au moment du concours - titre RNCP niveau II -) ; d'une école d'art ou de design équivalent au niveau licence (DNA ou équivalents étrangers) ; d'une école d'enseignement musical spécialisé équivalent au niveau licence (DNSPM ou équivalents étrangers), d'un DEM de composition ou électroacoustique d'un établissement musical spécialisé agréé par l'État, à condition de posséder en plus une licence scientifique ou en sciences humaines.' Selection criteria: 'La motivation, l'ouverture d'esprit, la faculté d'adaptation à des contextes spécifiques, le potentiel à travailler en équipe'. About ten places ('accessible à une dizaine de jeunes diplômé.e.s').

_rec.institutionType: Public university

_rec.durationEcts: 3 semesters full-time or 6 semesters part-time / 90 ECTS — VERIFIED from the current call. Semester 1: Digital Audio Processing 7.5, Audio Application Programming 7.5, General Acoustics 7.5, Sound Synthesis 7.5 = 30 ECTS. Semester 2: Special Topics in Acoustics 7.5, Applied Machine Learning for Sound and Music 7.5, Sound and Movement 7.5, Optoacoustics 7.5 = 30 ECTS. Semester 3: thesis 30 ECTS. Part-time students take the eight courses across four semesters with up to a year for the thesis. Attendance is compulsory and in person, with a maximum of three absences per course: "Το Π.Μ.Σ. υλοποιείται με τη διά ζώσης εκπαιδευτική διαδικασία. Η παρακολούθηση όλων των μαθημάτων είναι υποχρεωτική."

What is verifiable cuts both ways: the courses are listed and timetabled in Greek and taught by Greek faculty in Rethymno, which points to Greek delivery; but the ONLY language certificate the call demands is "Πιστοποιητικό γνώσης της Αγγλικής γλώσσας επιπέδου τουλάχιστον Β2" — an English certificate at B2 or above — and no Greek-language requirement appears anywhere. He must email the department to establish the actual language of delivery before applying. This is the single decisive unknown.
_rec.focus: Recording and audio engineering, sound synthesis and sound design, digital audio processing, machine learning for sound and music, acoustics and optoacoustics, motion-based interaction
_rec.whatYouStudy: Verified from the official call and the department pages. The programme "explores sound in its multiple dimensions: as a wave, as a signal, and as a carrier of information", combining applied knowledge with current research in digital audio processing, sound synthesis, acoustics and audiovisual technologies, artificial intelligence, and motion tracking for musical applications. The eight compulsory courses: DIGITAL AUDIO PROCESSING — PCM, sampling-rate conversion, spectral analysis, digital filters, noise minimisation, audio coding and decoding; AUDIO APPLICATION PROGRAMMING — building audio and music applications for capture, recording, spectral analysis and signal extraction in Python or C with specialised APIs; GENERAL ACOUSTICS; SOUND SYNTHESIS — advanced synthesis and modulation techniques, computer implementation and their application to contemporary music creation; SPECIAL TOPICS IN ACOUSTICS — musical, structural and psycho-acoustics, electroacoustics, computational acoustics; APPLIED MACHINE LEARNING FOR SOUND AND MUSIC — inferring music content information and sound-scene and event detection for intelligent applications; SOUND AND MOVEMENT — embodied music cognition, multimodality in audio interaction, correlating audio and motion data, and building interactive sound systems in which motion drives sound; OPTOACOUSTICS — optical detection of sound, light-generated sound sources, micro- and nano-acoustics. The thesis may be carried out in one of the collaborating laboratories in Greece or abroad. Weekly timetable for the current year runs Monday and Wednesday afternoons and evenings, 14:15–22:00.
_rec.entryRequirements: NOW VERIFIED from the 2026-27 call, and better for him than previously recorded. Admitted, after selection, are graduates of: Faculties of Natural Sciences; POLYTECHNIC (ENGINEERING) SCHOOLS; TEI Engineering; Sound Technology and Musical Instruments T.E. and Traditional and Folk Music T.E.; Music Studies (and Ethnomusicology), Audio and Visual Arts, Journalism and Media; and Cultural Technology and Communication. "Επιπλέον στο ΠΜΣ γίνονται δεκτοί απόφοιτοι τμημάτων που είναι αντίστοιχα των παραπάνω και ανήκουν σε ομοταγή ιδρύματα της αλλοδαπής" — graduates of corresponding departments at equivalent foreign institutions are also admitted, and "Για άλλες περιπτώσεις υποψηφίων και για τη συνάφεια των ειδικοτήτων θα αποφασίζει κατά περίπτωση η Συνέλευση του Τμήματος". Required documents: two-sided copy of ID or PASSPORT; CV; degree copy and other qualifications, or a completion certificate; full undergraduate transcript; an English language certificate at level B2 or above; copies of publications and/or evidence of professional experience if any; TWO recommendation letters (or a statement of the reasons if they cannot be supplied, e.g. time constraints); and a short report of no more than one typed page on his scientific and professional interests with a clear statement of why he wants to take the programme.

_rec.auditionSpec: No audition and no written entrance examination. "Η διαδικασία επιλογής υποψηφίων περιλαμβάνει, μεταξύ άλλων, και προσωπική συνέντευξη, η οποία μπορεί, αν συντρέχουν λόγοι, να γίνει εξ' αποστάσεως" — the selection process includes a personal interview which may, where warranted, be held remotely. Evaluation takes place after the application deadline on a date depending on the number of candidates. Maximum intake 15 students per year.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: Yes, and this is now confirmed rather than inferred. Graduates of Polytechnic (engineering) schools and Faculties of Natural Sciences head the eligible list, and corresponding foreign departments are expressly included. No special pleading and no music background needed.

_rec.facilities: Department of Music Technology and Acoustics, operating since September 1999, within the School of Music and Optoacoustic Technologies established in Rethymno in 2019 — described as the only academic programme in Greece dedicated to sound and music technologies combined with the science of acoustics. Named teaching staff include Assoc. Prof. Chrysoula Alexandraki (programme director, Digital Audio Processing), Assoc. Prof. Maximos Kaliakatsos-Papakostas (Audio Application Programming, also department chair), Asst. Prof. Nikos Stefanakis (General Acoustics), Nikolas Valsamakis (Sound Synthesis) and Asst. Prof. Panagiota-Styliani Paschalidou. The thesis may be done in a collaborating laboratory in Greece or abroad. A doctoral programme covers the same fields. HMU student welfare provides a free-meals card and a student residence. UNVERIFIED: studio and console inventory.
_rec.fitNotes: The strongest pure-funding case in the slice, and verification improved it on several fronts the prior record had marked as unknown: engineering graduates head the eligible-degree list, there is no portfolio and no audition, the interview can be held remotely, two recommendation letters and a one-page statement are the only written work required, and the sole language certificate demanded is ENGLISH at B2 — Greek is never mentioned as a requirement. Tuition is zero, Rethymno is cheap, and subsidised meals and housing exist. His software background maps directly onto Audio Application Programming, Applied Machine Learning for Sound and Music, and Sound and Movement. Three real obstacles. FIRST, the language of instruction is not published and the courses are timetabled in Greek — he must email the department (chrisoula@hmu.gr, maximoskp@hmu.gr, or the secretariat at ngoniota@hmu.gr) and get a straight answer before committing. SECOND, applications are submitted through morpheus.hmu.gr using TaxisNet credentials, which are Greek tax-authority login codes a Tunisian applicant does not have — he must ask the secretariat for the alternative route for foreign applicants, and should do so early. THIRD, only 15 places, attendance is compulsory and in person with a maximum of three absences per course, and the content is DSP, acoustics and machine learning rather than production or DJing — this would make him an audio engineer or audio-software specialist, not a producer. Worth pursuing as the free, funded, engineering-friendly option, but the language and TaxisNet questions must be settled first.

_rec.scholarships: THIS ENTRY EXISTS BECAUSE IED'S DSU BANDO IS THE CLEAREST PUBLISHED PROOF THAT A NON-EU STUDENT AT AN ITALIAN PRIVATE ACADEMY CAN WIN REGIONAL STATE AID. Key provisions of the Bando DSU 2025/26 (BAN 8203 rev 06, 4 September 2025), total fund €354,392.15 from MUR and Regione Lombardia: ELIGIBILITY expressly includes 'i cittadini di Stati non appartenenti all'Unione Europea' alongside Italians and EU citizens, for students admitted or enrolled on a Diploma Accademico di Primo or Secondo Livello at Milan, Rome, Turin, Cagliari or Florence. INCOME TEST: ISEE Universitario must not exceed €26,516.70 AND ISPE must not exceed €57,645.03 — both jointly. MERIT for a 1st-year II livello student: simply be regularly enrolled by 31 October and hold the first-level title by 31 January; confirmation of the full benefit then requires 40 credits by 10 August. AMOUNTS (including €140 regional-tax reimbursement and €818 meal allowance): in sede €3,383 / €2,950 / €2,114 by income band 1/2/3; pendolari €4,754 / €4,134 / €3,254; FUORI SEDE €8,134 / €7,073 / €5,776. THE DECISIVE DETAIL: under Art. 13(3) DPCM 9/4/2001, NON-EU FOREIGN STUDENTS ARE AUTOMATICALLY CLASSIFIED 'FUORI SEDE' regardless of where they live in Italy (unless their family lives in Italy), provided the accommodation is paid for — so a Tunisian student is placed in the HIGHEST bracket, €5,776 to €8,134 per year. NON-EU DOCUMENTATION: an 'ISEEU-ISPEU parificato' is required, built from foreign family-composition certificate, income declarations from the official tax agency of the country of residence (employer documents are NOT accepted, self-certification is NOT accepted), property and movable-asset statements, all translated into Italian by a recognised translator and legalised; Tunisia is NOT on the exemption or Apostille list published in the bando, so full consular legalisation applies. A floor applies: non-EU students' declared income cannot be counted below €7,002.97/year (the visa subsistence minimum). Free ISEEU assistance is via CAAF CGIL Lombardia under an IED agreement. DEADLINES 2025/26: applications 9 September to 7 November 2025; rent contract for fuori sede status by 10 December 2025. EXCLUSIONS THAT MATTER: anyone already holding an equal or higher qualification is excluded (a BSc does not block a II livello application); anyone receiving another income/merit-based grant for the same year is excluded; FOUNDATION course students are excluded; and the bando covers ONLY Diploma Accademico I/II livello — IED's one-year 'Master' courses are NOT covered. IED separately runs a commercial scholarship competition: 114 scholarships/tutorships covering 50% of tuition for Master of Arts and Master programmes 2025/26 across Italian campuses and Accademia di Como, rising to 127 for 2026/27 across Italy and Spain, open to local and international students including non-EU, covering partial tuition only and NOT living costs or enrolment fees.
_rec.paymentPlans: UNVERIFIED — not published in the DSU bando. Note that DSU is not a fee waiver: 'Le tasse di iscrizione e di contributo accademico dovranno comunque essere interamente versate' — fees must be paid in full and the scholarship arrives afterwards, in instalments.

Lombardia 33/2004 and DPCM 9/4/2001 for right-to-study purposes). NOT OFFICIAL in the same sense for IED's one-year 'Master' courses, which are private post-degree certificates and are excluded from DSU. Also note IED's dedicated SOUND DESIGN programme is a FIRST-level diploma (BA equivalent), not a master.
_rec.visaEligible: Yes for the Diploma Accademico route — the bando references 'permesso di soggiorno' for extra-EU students as a routine document, and the visa subsistence figure of €7,002.97 is built into the income rules, confirming this is a standard non-EU pathway.

_rec.deadline: DSU application deadline 7 November 2025; rent contract for fuori sede status by 10 December 2025 — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new dates.
_rec.reputationSignals: IED is a major international private design chain with campuses across Italy, Spain and Brazil, operating inside the AFAM system, with a substantial published DSU fund (€354,392.15 for 2025/26) and a formal CAAF agreement to help foreign students obtain the ISEE parificato. RED FLAGS for this candidate: no second-level sound-design or music-production programme (Sound Design is BA-level only), tuition not published, and the DSU documentation burden for a Tunisian is heavy — consular-legalised tax documents from the Tunisian revenue authority, translated into Italian.
_rec.recommendation: IED itself does not offer what he wants at master level — its Sound Design programme is an undergraduate diploma. Include IED in his research NOT as a destination but as the clearest published evidence of how the Italian DSU route works for a non-EU student: he can win €5,776–€8,134 a year at an Italian PRIVATE academy because non-EU students are automatically classed 'fuori sede'. Use that same mechanism at NABA, RUFA or Saint Louis instead. Practical warning: start collecting the Tunisian tax and property certificates, translations and legalisations at least four months before the September/November DSU window — self-certification is refused outright and employer letters are not accepted.

TECNOLOGIE E TECNICHE DELLA RIPRESA E DELLA REGISTRAZIONE AUDIO I–II (12 each). STORIA DEL SOUND DESIGN E DELLA POST PRODUZIONE AUDIO. _rec.institution: Netherlands private higher-education sector (systematic check across NVAO/CROHO-registered private institutions and all named specialist audio providers)
_rec.qualification: NONE EXISTS. After searching in both English and Dutch ('master muziekproductie', 'opleiding sound design particulier', 'niet-bekostigde opleiding', 'master sound design Nederland particuliere hogeschool NVAO'), I found NO privately-run, NVAO-accredited master's degree in sound design, music production, audio engineering, music technology, immersive audio or electronic music performance anywhere in the Netherlands.
_rec.accreditationStatus: DEFINITIVE STRUCTURAL FINDING. In the Netherlands the audio/music education market splits cleanly in two, with nothing in between. (1) ACCREDITED = PUBLIC. Every NVAO-accredited master in this field belongs to a government-funded ('bekostigd') public institution: HKU Utrecht (Master of Music pathway Music Design; Sound Design and Audio Design at bachelor level), Conservatorium van Amsterdam / AHK (Master Immersive Audio — NVAO-assessed; plus the AEMA associate degree for electronic musicians, English-taught), Codarts Rotterdam, and the Institute of Sonology at the Royal Conservatoire in The Hague. These are all excluded from this brief as public. (2) PRIVATE = UNACCREDITED. Every private audio provider in the country (SAE, Abbey Road Institute, Sound Education, Pro Audio Education, DDMA, Master The Mix, AV Sound Education, DJ School Amsterdam, Music Production Academy) holds at most CRKBO and/or NRTO registration. CRKBO is a short-vocational-education register that governs VAT exemption; NRTO is a private-training trade association quality mark. NEITHER IS AN ACCREDITATION AND NEITHER CONFERS DEGREE STATUS. The sole exception — SAE's MA/MSc — is a UK University of Hertfordshire award delivered fully online, with no Dutch status and no campus component. Meanwhile private institutions that DO hold NVAO accreditation (Tio, Wittenborg, Nyenrode) operate exclusively in business and hospitality.

_rec.scholarships: SECTOR-WIDE FINDING: NOT ONE private Dutch audio provider publishes any scholarship, bursary, fee waiver or discount available to a non-EU or Tunisian applicant. The only financial mechanisms found were (a) upfront-payment savings of €1,300–€5,670 versus instalment plans, (b) alumni/staff discounts of 25% at SAE UK, (c) 35–50% student software discounts at Sound Education and AV Sound Education, and (d) a Dutch study-cost INCOME TAX deduction promoted by Abbey Road Institute and Pro Audio Education, which requires Dutch taxable income and by Abbey Road's own admission 'doesn't apply to those receiving governmental benefits or who aren't yet employed'. That last one is effectively worthless to an incoming international student and should be discounted entirely when comparing prices. Dutch DUO student finance is unavailable at every private provider without exception.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: For orientation: private Dutch audio tuition ranges from €699 (SAE one-month DJ Certificate) to €37,580 (SAE BA Audio Production Standard, monthly plan). The mid-market one-year full-time option is Abbey Road Institute at €18,860–€20,160. Amsterdam living costs add roughly €14,000–€18,000 per year on top.
_rec.visaEligible: THE DECISIVE FINDING FOR THIS CANDIDATE — NO. Only an IND recognised sponsor can apply for a Dutch student residence permit on a student's behalf, and the IND study register covers higher professional/university education, senior secondary vocational education (ROCs) and IB schools. NOT ONE private specialist audio provider in the Netherlands is a recognised sponsor. Both of the two credible English-language schools say so themselves, in writing: SAE Institute Netherlands states 'SAE is a private Institute, its students are not eligible for a Visa, nor a student loan via DUO' and 'The registration at SAE Institute cannot grant you a Student Visa in the Netherlands'; Abbey Road Institute Amsterdam states 'Currently, we are not able to assist non-EU residents with their visa application to study in the Netherlands' and 'Since Abbey Road Institute Amsterdam is a private Institute, students are not eligible for a VISA or a student loan', adding that applicants may only attend if they already have 'a personal means of obtaining a VISA, for example, a family connection or registration at a university'. CONCLUSION: a Tunisian national CANNOT legally relocate to the Netherlands to study at any private audio school. Verify current status yourself at https://ind.nl/en/public-register-recognised-sponsors/public-register-study (updated monthly).
_rec.reputationSignals: The Dutch private audio market is small, expensive and structurally unable to serve non-EU students. The two brands worth respecting on teaching quality — SAE Institute Amsterdam and Abbey Road Institute Amsterdam — both disclose their inability to sponsor visas only in fine print (an entry-requirements sub-page and an FAQ respectively) while running international-facing marketing. That is the sector's central red flag. A second recurring red flag is nomenclature: Pro Audio Education titles its diploma 'Master Geluidstechniek' for what it concedes is MBO+/HBO- level work, and 'Master The Mix Academy' will surface in any search for a music-production master. Neither is a master's degree. A third is opacity: three providers (Master The Mix, AV Sound Education, Music Production Academy) publish no prices at all.
_rec.recommendation: BOTTOM LINE FOR THE NETHERLANDS: DO NOT BUILD THE SEPTEMBER 2027 PLAN AROUND A DUTCH PRIVATE SCHOOL. There is no private NVAO-accredited master in this field in the country, and no private audio provider can sponsor his residence permit — so the two things he needs (an accredited master + a visa) are simply not purchasable from the Dutch private sector at any price. He should concentrate his accredited-master applications on the Spain/Portugal/Italy slices, or reconsider Dutch PUBLIC institutions, which are outside this brief but are the only Dutch route that actually works: the Conservatorium van Amsterdam's Master Immersive Audio (NVAO-assessed) and its English-taught AEMA associate degree for electronic musicians — where, notably, 'when you enroll in an Associate Degree course, you can apply for a visa' — and HKU's Master of Music pathway Music Design. TWO THINGS HE CAN USEFULLY DO IN THE NETHERLANDS ANYWAY, both on an ordinary Schengen tourist visa and neither requiring accreditation: (1) DJ School Amsterdam's Producer Professional Course, ~€2,499 for 20 one-to-one English-language sessions plus 10 studio hours, compressible into two weeks — a direct, efficient way to build the portfolio he lacks; (2) SAE Amsterdam's one-month DJ Certificate at €699–€1,099 (confirm whether the €500 registration fee applies), ideally timed around Amsterdam Dance Event in October for scene contacts. Both are training, not qualifications — but a 4–8 track portfolio built to Abbey Road's published standard is precisely what every accredited master he applies to will ask for, and he does not have one yet. That is the highest-value use of the Netherlands for him.

Point Blank as a UK institution is a member of Independent Higher Education and was granted its own degree-awarding powers by the UK Office for Students in 2026 — a real quality signal for the organisation, but it governs UK degrees, not a two-week summer course in Ibiza. Do not conflate the two. The correct way to think about this line item is 'professional training and portfolio-building', never 'qualification'.

The Ibiza venue partnerships (Café Mambo, Destino Pacha, Ibiza Rocks, Blue Marlin) are real and are the differentiator. No red flags found. But judged against what he actually said he wants, this is the most useful and by far the cheapest thing in this batch. He has no portfolio, no IELTS, no music credential and no industry network, and every accredited master will eventually ask him for at least the first of those. Two weeks in Ibiza at roughly 26 contact hours per week, with real DJ sets at Café Mambo and Destino Pacha, a free Ableton Live Suite licence and ten professional press shots plus two Instagram reels, produces precisely the raw material a portfolio-less applicant is missing — and it produces it in a fortnight, on a short-stay Schengen visa, with no IELTS and no portfolio to get in. Book with the 20% early-bird code, read the price directly from the website since it is not machine-readable, and budget separately and honestly for August accommodation in Ibiza. The verdict is CONDITIONAL only because it must never be mistaken for a qualification — as a career investment for a would-be DJ, it is the best value here.

_rec.whatYouStudy: Across the first two semesters: two complementary Specialism modules (20 credits each) covering recent developments in the chosen pathway plus technical, research and communication skills; a Practice module devoted entirely to developing individual creative practice with one-to-one tuition; a Seminar module for contextual, aesthetic and theoretical study via group tutorials and practice-based workshops. Additional modules in Music Technology and Society and a Research Project (which may include a work placement). Third semester: Final Project (60 credits), a sustained period of self-directed practice-based work. Assessment is 100% coursework on every module — no exams — and can take the form of practical/design work, portfolio submission, performance, workshop activity, lecture recital, presentation or essay. Staff research spans composition, performance, broadcasting, contemporary music, sound design studies, film music, creative technologies and disability arts practice; Music at Ulster placed joint 2nd in the UK for Research Impact in REF2014.

The faculty does not publish an itemised list on the programme page; request the current podmínky pro přijetí. What is clear is that the expected materials are theatre, film and new-media creative work — a domain in which this candidate has no output at all, and which a year of building a music-production portfolio would not address.
_rec.auditionSpec: No performance audition in the conventional sense. Round one is decided on submitted materials with the applicant absent; round two is a discussion over those materials, held in March-April, conducted in Czech. The invitation specifies the exact date.
_rec.equipmentRequired: Not published; nothing is indicated as required for admission.
_rec.facilities: JAMU Theatre Faculty multimedia and stage-technology facilities in Brno. Whether dedicated audio post-production facilities are available to this programme is not published — but this is moot given the programme is not an audio programme.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: Formally yes — this is a theatre and new-media programme, so no conservatory music training is implied and no music degree is demanded. But that formal openness is worthless here. Admission turns on a portfolio of theatre/film/new-media creative work assessed in a Czech-language talent procedure, and a software-engineering graduate with no theatre or new-media practice would be a very weak applicant even before the C1 Czech certificate blocks the application outright.
_rec.englishTest: None — Czech-taught programme, so no IELTS or TOEFL. This is not an advantage: the Czech C1 requirement is far harder than any English test he would otherwise sit.
_rec.tuitionEU: 0 CZK. Czech-language study at a public university is tuition-free.
_rec.tuitionNonEU: 0 CZK for a Tunisian national. The Czech tuition-free rule attaches to the language of instruction, not to nationality, and this programme is Czech-only, so no foreign-language surcharge can arise. Correct as previously recorded — and it is the one genuinely attractive feature of this entry, which makes the C1 barrier all the more decisive.
_rec.otherFees: CORRECTED FROM 'UNVERIFIED'. The admission procedure fee is 1,050 CZK, non-refundable, paid through JAMU's Commercial Centre; international applicants may pay in foreign currency at equivalent value after exchange fees. Without payment the application is not included in the procedure. Brno living costs run roughly 16,000-22,000 CZK/month.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: Tuition 0. Living costs roughly 380,000-530,000 CZK (~15,500-21,500 EUR) over two years, plus the 1,050 CZK application fee and the cost of obtaining a C1 Czech certificate — which for someone starting from zero would itself mean a year or more of intensive full-time language study, very likely a paid preparatory year in the Czech Republic before the degree even begins.
_rec.scholarships: Not published for entrants. Czech public academies offer merit and accommodation scholarships to already-enrolled students but rarely fund non-EU entrants. Tuition being zero, the relevant funding gap is living costs, which he would need to self-fund or cover through a separate scholarship scheme.
_rec.intakes: Annual, September start.
_rec.applicationOpens: The faculty publishes a step-by-step admission guide (Postup krok za krokem) with the cycle's dates; applications are submitted through the IS JAMU system.
_rec.deadline: CORRECTED FROM 'UNVERIFIED'. Navazující magisterské applications are due 31 MARCH — the published 2026/27 cycle date is 31 March 2027, which is in fact the deadline for a September 2027 start and therefore lands squarely on his target intake. (Note the faculty runs different deadlines by level and specialization: 30 November for some bachelor specializations, 28 February for others including the BcA. in Audiovizuální tvorba a divadlo, and 31 March for master's specializations.) The timing suits him; nothing else about the programme does.
_rec.visaEligible: Yes in principle — accredited public arts academy, full-time MgA., supports a Czech long-term residence permit for study. Academic in practice, since he cannot meet the C1 Czech entry condition.
_rec.recommendation: The previous record recommended not pursuing this, and that conclusion is confirmed — but the reasoning was incomplete, and the newly verified facts make the case far more emphatic. The earlier entry treated the Czech language requirement as unknown and worth asking about; it is in fact published, certificated and set at C1 CEFR, the highest tier at the faculty, applied specifically to Audiovizuální tvorba a divadlo and demonstrable only through a Charles University or Masaryk University examination or a Czech secondary-school leaving exam. For a Tunisian applicant with no Czech at all in August 2026 and a 31 March 2027 deadline, that is not a hurdle to plan around — it is a closed door. Even setting language aside, the programme fails on content: it is a theatre and new-media creation degree in which sound design is not a named specialization, admission is decided on a portfolio of theatre/film/new-media work he does not have and would not produce while building a music-production portfolio, and both admission rounds are conducted in Czech. Zero tuition at a genuine public arts academy is real value, and the 31 March deadline fits his September 2027 target perfectly — which is exactly why this needs to be marked clearly rather than left looking attractive on price. Do not apply. The entry's lasting worth is the negative finding, now doubly confirmed: JAMU's Theatre Faculty is widely assumed to host a sound-design master's and it does not; JAMU's real audio degree is the joint VUT Brno Audio Engineering Ing. already in the database. Keeping this record closes that gap permanently.

_rec.auditionSpec: On-site, single-round, in Brno. Talent exam = 90% of the score, conducted as an oral interview (ústní pohovor) assessing prior study results and the bachelor graduation project, the portfolio, the written master's project concept, the written thesis-topic proposal, knowledge of current developments in the field, and language readiness. Foreign-language written test = 10%, a lexico-grammatical test at B2+ CEFR including specialist music terminology. CRUCIAL EXTRA: "V případě uchazeče, který absolvoval bakalářské studium v jiném (byť příbuzném) oboru, se úroveň jeho znalostí prověří praktickou zkouškou" — an applicant from a different field sits an additional practical exam in three parts: (a) a thematic task, a multimedia-work project on a set theme; (b) a practical task on the visual component; (c) a free task in any media with a compulsory musical component. 2026/27 exam date was 16 June 2026 (KKMT). _rec.scholarship: None found for Tunisians. JAMU publishes no international entrance scholarship for this programme.

_rec.facilities: VERIFIED on the department/programme pages: two electroacoustic music studios, a professional recording studio, a fully equipped theatre and chamber hall, interactive technologies, multichannel audio systems, a large stock of professional software and hardware, a MODULAR SYNTHESISER, and an equipped loan pool of microphones, field recorders, video cameras and sensors. Jaroslav Šťastný, MgA. Jiří Suchánek.

Verified against four official sources: the programme database page; the master's admission-requirements page (https://hf.jamu.cz/studijni-obor/multimedialni-tvorba-3-prijimaci-rizeni/) for entry conditions and exam weights; the bachelor page (https://hf.jamu.cz/studijni-obor/multimedialni-tvorba-2-prijimaci-rizeni/) which is where the 20–40 item portfolio spec actually lives; and the official decree PDF "Vyhláška – magisterské navazující studium pro akademický rok 2026-2027" (https://is.jamu.cz/do/jamu/doc/5451/smer_pr_hf/Vyhlaska_nav.MgA.26-27_JVS.pdf) for the deadline, exam date, 990 CZK fee, 2 places and the Czech B1 requirement. That single unknown decides whether this programme is reachable for him at all. Ask mad@hbksaar.de.
_rec.auditionSpec: CORRECTED — the previous record said 'None', which is wrong. Master applicants must pass an EIGNUNGSPRÜFUNG (aptitude examination). After the submitted materials are assessed, shortlisted candidates proceed to an oral/practical examination which is held IN PERSON at the institution in Saarbrücken. For a Tunisian applicant this is a real and expensive obstacle: it means a Schengen short-stay visa and a trip to the Saarland before any study visa exists. Ask mad@hbksaar.de whether remote examination is ever permitted for overseas candidates — do not assume it is.
_rec.portfolioSpec: CORRECTED from 'NOT PUBLISHED'. It is published, on the application information page. Media Art & Design applicants must submit a PORTFOLIO OF WORK SAMPLES together with a LETTER OF MOTIVATION and a PROJECT PROPOSAL (Projektvorhaben). Format: PDF, maximum 100 MB; larger material such as video must be supplied as external links (YouTube, Vimeo, cloud storage). Applications go through the SIM application portal. This is an artistic portfolio judged as art — a year of bedroom production tracks will not read as one unless he deliberately builds installation, audiovisual or sound-art pieces with a stated concept.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: YES — no music degree is required, and a computing background is not itself a barrier at a media-art college. The obstacles are the 240-ECTS rule, the German B2 requirement, the in-person aptitude exam, and the need for a genuinely artistic portfolio.

For a September 2027 (winter semester 2027/28) start his deadline is 31 MAY 2027 — which is LATER than the October 2026-February 2027 window he has been planning around, so this one does not clash with his other applications. _rec.tuitionNonEU: EUR 0 — CONFIRMED. Saarland levies no non-EU tuition at state institutions and HBKsaar publishes no separate international rate. As a Tunisian national he pays the same nothing an EU student pays. This is now confirmed rather than assumed.
_rec.otherFees: CORRECTED from UNVERIFIED — the semester contribution for winter semester 2026/27 is EUR 422.20 for a student enrolled only at HBKsaar, made up of Studierendenwerk Saarland EUR 121.20, accident/liability/theft insurance EUR 1.30, student body fee EUR 22.90, Deutschlandticket semester ticket EUR 226.80, and an administrative fee of EUR 50.00. More than half of it is the nationwide transport ticket, which is genuine value. Students also enrolled at another Saarland institution pay EUR 274.70.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: Tuition EUR 0. Semester contribution EUR 422.20 x 2 semesters = roughly EUR 845 for the whole 60-ECTS master, including a year of nationwide German public transport. Add Saarbrücken living costs and the blocked account (currently around EUR 12,000 for the year). Plus the unbudgeted cost of travelling to Saarbrücken for the in-person aptitude exam, and whatever the unpublished transition programme charges. On tuition alone this is one of the cheapest real master's degrees available to him anywhere.
_rec.scholarships: None published by the institution. DAAD schemes would be the route, applied for separately.
_rec.englishTest: None — German-taught, so IELTS/TOEFL is irrelevant. His unwritten English test is not the obstacle here; German B2 is.
_rec.visaEligible: YES for the M.A. itself — full-time degree at a state university of fine arts, squarely within the section 16b(1) AufenthG entitlement. Two caveats specific to this programme. First, a 60-ECTS one-year master gives a short residence window and correspondingly little time to convert into the 18-month post-study job-seeking permit. Second, any preliminary transition programme would need its own residence basis, and a preparatory course is a weaker footing than a degree — clarify with the International Office before committing.
_rec.recommendation: CONDITIONAL, rating C — the record is much better documented than before, and most of the corrections went in his favour, but the one obstacle that matters did not move. Corrected on this pass: the master exists and is NOT suspended; teaching is in German; the language bar is B2, not DSH-2, which is genuinely achievable for him; the deadlines are published (31 May for winter, 30 November for summer), so a September 2027 start means 31 May 2027; the portfolio requirement is published and specific (PDF under 100 MB, plus motivation letter and project proposal); there IS an aptitude examination, held in person in Saarbrücken, which the previous record wrongly recorded as 'none'; and the real cost is EUR 0 tuition plus EUR 422.20 a semester including the Deutschlandticket. What did not change is the 240-ECTS entry rule, which his 180-ECTS BSc fails, and the transition programme that might bridge it remains entirely unpublished despite direct checking. So this is not a thin record any more — it is a well-documented programme with one decisive unknown. The action is unchanged and cheap: one email to mad@hbksaar.de and s.rauber@hbksaar.de asking exactly two things now that the rest is settled — the terms, length, cost and residence basis of the transition programme for a 180-ECTS holder, and whether the in-person aptitude exam can be taken remotely from Tunisia. If the bridge is short and carries a visa, this becomes a serious B. If not, it is closed. Separately, be clear-eyed that even on success this is a media-ART degree with sound as one medium among many — it serves an installation and audiovisual practice, not a career as a DJ and record producer. _rec.whatYouStudy: Project-driven master integrating performative, compositional and algorithmic forms of contemporary art. The student's own project sits at the centre and is re-conceptualised across two years on the basis of critical, multi-perspectival peer feedback. Two focus areas (Studienschwerpunkte), and the application is made to ONE of them: Epistemic Media (art as a method of enquiry — acoustic research, documentary film, algorithmic composition) and Transmedia Forms (performance, sound art, installation, digital media). CONFIRMED on the official page, including that 'Musical practice is not bound to musical instruments'.

_rec.acceptsNonMusic: Yes — explicitly, and this remains the clearest published welcome to a non-music graduate of any German programme in this batch. Official page: 'Musical practice is not bound to musical instruments; it encompasses many approaches to art and research. Accordingly, the master's program is open to students from all disciplinary backgrounds.' A software-engineering BSc qualifies on paper, and his coding ability is directly relevant to the algorithmic strand (the programme is co-led by Prof. Julian Rohrhuber, known for live-coding/SuperCollider work).
_rec.portfolioSpec: NOW EXACT (from the official German Anforderungen page). Three documents, uploaded with the aptitude-test registration in the online portal: (1) 'ein Portfolio mit bereits realisierten Projekten' from the chosen focus area (Transmediale Formen or Epistemische Medien) — no number, duration or format limit is published; (2) a motivation letter expressing the applicant's interest in that specific focus area; (3) 'eine ausführliche Beschreibung eines Projektvorhabens mit detailliertem Zeitplan sowie konkreten Ideen zur Mitarbeit von Mitstudierenden in diesem Projekt' — a detailed project proposal WITH a detailed timetable AND concrete ideas for how fellow students would contribute to the project. _rec.auditionSpec: No audition, no on-site test, and — importantly — the assessment is REMOTE: 'Das Projekt muss anschließend der Auswahlkommission in einer Online-Präsentation vorgestellt werden. Darauf folgt ein Online-Bewerbungsgespräch mit der Kommission. Die Präsentation und das Gespräch dauern zusammen maximal 60 Minuten.' An online presentation of the project to the selection panel followed by an online interview, together max 60 minutes. No travel to Germany is needed to apply.
_rec.applicationOpens: About one month before the deadline: 'Die Bewerbungslinks werden in jedem Jahr etwa einen Monat vor dem jeweiligen Bewerbungsschluss freigeschaltet' — so roughly late September each year, via muvac.

Courses start at the beginning of April. CONSEQUENCE FOR HIM: a September 2027 start is impossible. The reachable options are apply by 31 October 2026 for an April 2027 start, or 31 October 2027 for April 2028.

_rec.scholarship: DAAD Study Scholarships – Master Studies (artists/music or all-disciplines route); Tunisia is DAAD-eligible. RSH lists 'Stipendien' internally but no named scheme open to an incoming non-EU student was confirmed — UNVERIFIED.

_rec.facilities: Institut für Musik und Medien studios and collaborative project spaces; the IMM also runs a 'BASISLAGER' project space. No console, studio or immersive-room inventory is published for this programme — UNVERIFIED.
_rec.fitNotes: By far the easiest German conservatory door for him to open: open to all disciplinary backgrounds in the school's own words, no audition, no on-site test, assessment by a 60-minute online presentation and interview, and no tuition. His coding background is a genuine asset for the algorithmic strand. Three real caveats. First, German B2 is required — though the Kollegstudierender route lets him produce the certificate during year one, which is the softest German requirement of any RSH programme. Second, the intake is April only, so this cannot serve a September 2027 target; the nearest realistic entry is April 2027 (apply 31 October 2026 — that is roughly three months from now) or April 2028. Third and most important for his actual goal: this is artistic-research and transmedia practice, not production craft. He would graduate with a conceptual sound-art practice and a strong European network, not with mixing, mastering or dance-floor production chops. Best used as a funded, low-barrier route into a German art scene if he is genuinely drawn to experimental and algorithmic work — not as a producer's apprenticeship.

For a candidate targeting commercial and media work this framing is a better match than a composition degree — but note it is still not a club/dance-music degree.
_rec.whatYouStudy: Composition for music applied to images (the dominant credit block), electroacoustic composition and sound design, music informatics, history of electroacoustic music, and audio post-production and mixing technologies. _rec.auditionSpec: CONFIRMED, and it is the lowest published barrier of the four. A single ORAL assessment, verbatim: 'Presentazione da parte del candidato di un book contenente lavori video o audio, realizzazioni in elettronica o partiture, che saranno oggetto di discussione con la commissione.' The commission evaluates command of electronic music production and realisation across varied instrumental contexts, and prefers candidates strong across all listed areas. DECISIVE POINT, CONFIRMED: there is NO written theory paper, NO solfège or lettura cantata, NO ear-training test and NO instrumental performance requirement published. This is the only one of the four programmes with no musicianship examination at all — the single most important fact in this entire comparison for a self-taught candidate.
_rec.portfolioSpec: A 'book' of video works, audio works, electronic realisations, OR scores — CONFIRMED, and note the 'or': scores are only one of four accepted alternatives, so a purely audio/DAW portfolio is fully admissible. This is exactly what a year of self-directed work can produce. Build toward the course's own centre of gravity: three to five cues scored to picture, several original electronic pieces, and demonstrable mixing and post-production work. The commission discusses the book with him, so he must be able to talk about his own production decisions — in Italian.

The structural point does stand on general Italian rule: Rovigo applies the ISEE-band system, not a flat non-EU surcharge, so a Tunisian family income declared through an ISEE parificato/ISEEE should place him at or near the lowest band. _rec.totalCostEstimate: Cannot be stated precisely — no contributi table verified. On the standard Italian pattern with an ISEEE filed, plausibly near-zero to roughly €2,000/year in fees. _rec.scholarships: ESU Padova, the Veneto regional right-to-study agency covering Rovigo, runs income-based borse di studio that are open to non-EU students and can cover fee exemption, a maintenance grant and subsidised housing. This is the realistic funding route and it is means-tested, not merit-gated on musical achievement — which suits him. MAECI Italian government scholarships are the national alternative and are open to Tunisian nationals. UNVERIFIED whether the conservatoire offers any internal award.

_rec.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED — not published on the course page. Italian conservatoire ammissioni bandi typically appear in spring. _rec.deadline: UNVERIFIED — set by the annual Bando di ammissione. Request it from the segreteria in autumn 2026.
_rec.visaEligible: YES. A Diploma Accademico di Secondo Livello from a state conservatoire is a full second-cycle degree and supports an Italian student visa (type D) and a permesso di soggiorno per studio. As a non-EU applicant resident abroad he must pre-enrol via Universitaly and compete within the annually published non-EU contingent for the institution — that contingent, not the academic entry rule, is the real practical bottleneck and should be checked early.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: YES — CONFIRMED, and it is the clearest yes of the four. 'Diploma di laurea triennale' is named as a qualifying title in its own right, and the admission assessment is a portfolio book plus an oral discussion with no theory paper, no ear training and no instrumental test. A Software Engineering BSc plus a genuine audio/audiovisual portfolio maps onto the published requirements without any exception needing to be made for him.
_rec.recommendation: VALUE VERDICT: WORTH IT. RATING: A. — VERIFIED AND CONFIRMED; this remains the best-matched of the four and the only one with an unobstructed path. Three things line up here that line up nowhere else in this set: the entry rule explicitly accepts any three-year university degree with no music precondition; the admission is a portfolio-and-interview with NO musicianship examination whatsoever (the other two Italian options both impose sung reading, ear training and music history on him); and the cost sits inside the ISEE system, so a low Tunisian family income should translate into a low contributo rather than a flat foreign surcharge. One genuine improvement over the previous report: B2 Italian may be satisfied by an in-house test OR a certificate, so he is not forced to buy a CILS/CELI. Real conditions remain: B2 Italian is mandatory, not advisory, so Italian study must start now — his French makes this the fastest language on his list, realistically 12 months to B2 with sustained work; and the degree's centre of gravity is composition for images and applied media sound, not club music, so his DJ ambition is served only indirectly. One correction to the previous record's confidence: its fee-exemption claims for foreign candidates could not be re-verified and must not be budgeted on. Actions: contact the segreteria in autumn 2026 for the Bando di ammissione, the Regolamento tasse e contributi, and written confirmation of how B2 is assessed and whether the admission exam fee is waived for foreign candidates. Build the portfolio to the syllabus — scored-to-picture cues first, original electronic pieces second, mixing and post-production evidence third. If one place comes out of this whole search, this is it.

_rec.whatYouStudy: Official text: an interdisciplinary synthesis of technology and music, science and art. Chairs: Robert Höldrich (recording and reproduction technology, electronic music), Alois Sontacchi (acoustics and audio engineering), Franz Zotter (acoustics and audio engineering). A written admission examination at IEM in three parts: (1) Seashore hearing test over headphones, approx. 40 minutes — paired-comparison thresholds for frequency, intensity and tone duration, timbre discrimination, tone and rhythm memory (sample tests with solutions are published on Moodle); (2) second written aural test, approx. 20 minutes — melodic and rhythmic dictation, recognition of modes, time signatures, triads and instruments, plus spotting errors in a printed score; (3) written music-theory test, approx. 15 minutes — interval and scale construction, rhythm. Confirmed on the page: 'Die Zulassungsprüfung für das Wintersemester 2027/28 findet online statt' — the WS 2027/28 admission exam is ONLINE. Results normally 2 days later via KUGonline.

_rec.stipend: UNVERIFIED — no stipend found for this profile. Austrian OeAD scholarships were not checked against this programme.

_rec.whatYouStudy: CONFIRMED from the official course-contents and master-class pages. Core: economy, law, management and scientific work, plus TV, video and audio production, storytelling, video/audio/studio technology, media coding, digital imaging, information visualisation, 360-degree video, AR and VR. You then choose one of three master classes — Animation & Visual Effects, 3D Audio & Sound Design, or Film & TV. The Audio master class runs four independently designed, developed, planned, implemented and evaluated projects across four semesters: semester 1 Design Thinking, project on sound design in animation; semester 2 Prototyping & Implementation, project on Sonic Interaction; semester 3 Evaluation & Testing, project on 3D Audio & Virtual Realities; semester 4 a group project. In-depth courses: Audio System Design; Film & Location Sound & Post Production; Film & Game Sound Design; Prototyping & Implementation; Coaching & Consulting. Software focus: Pro Tools Ultimate with Dolby Atmos Production Suite, Nuendo, Reaper, Ableton Live, Max4Live, Max8, Pure Data, Unity 3D with Wwise, Python, IRCAM SPAT5, IEM Plugin Suite, Sparta VST, Zylia Studio Pro, EASE 4, Tsugi GameSynth, iZotope RX. Students can 'buy' skills they lack (e.g. programming, graphic design) from students in other master classes, paying in ECTS credits. Regular field trips to Tonmeistertagung (VDT), next_generation (ZKM), klingt gut! (HAW Hamburg), ICSA and AES Conventions.

_rec.whatYouStudy: Though formally a module of the Montaža (Editing) master, it is 'largely conceived as an independent program'. It aims to educate creative and professional practitioners who acquire sound knowledge and skills through artistic, theoretical and professional subjects, for film and television as well as for other performing, broadcast and stage arts. Courses dealing with film sound are tied to practical work, individual and team-based: sound-design students realise film, television, radio and stage works produced by ADU's other departments and collaborate with other University of Zagreb faculties. Teaching staff are working sound recordists, sound editors, music editors, re-recording mixers and sound designers. Graduates work across film, television, theatre, radio, performing arts, multimedia projects and video games.
_rec.portfolioSpec: EXACT, from the official 2026/27 entrance-exam document. Stage (A) submission, all eliminatory: (1) životopis (CV); (2) motivacijsko pismo — motivation letter, up to 2 'kartice' of text (~3,600 characters); (3) an audiovisual work for which the candidate conceived the sound picture or participated in creating it; (4) a written analysis of that submitted audiovisual work explaining the sound-picture concept AND listing the origin of the noises, music, sound effects and computer programs used in sound post-production. Positive evaluation of BOTH the audiovisual work and the written analysis is a precondition for reaching stage (B). (An older ADU booklet additionally specified DVD-video format in at least 3 copies and three copies of the analysis — check the current submission format.)
_rec.auditionSpec: Yes — on-site, three-part, out of 100 points, with a hard 80/100 pass threshold. (1) klauzurni rad (supervised in-house practical exam) up to 20 points; (2) izlaganje koncepta zvučne slike za zadani predložak — presentation of a sound-picture concept for a given template/brief, up to 30 points; (3) razgovor s povjerenstvom (interview) up to 50 points. The commission assesses knowledge of film history, film-music history and music history, and recognition of musical forms, styles and genres. Recommended reading includes Sonnenschein, 'Sound Design: The Expressive Power of Music, Voice and Sound Effects in Cinema', and Weis & Belton, 'Film Sound'.
_rec.entryRequirements: For Montaža the published prerequisite is a 'trogodišnji sveučilišni ili stručni prijediplomski studij, 180 ECTS bodova' — a three-year university OR professional undergraduate degree of 180 ECTS. Croatian-language competence is expected in speech and writing; ADU requires no certificate but 'Povjerenstva Prijamnih ispita imaju pravo eliminirati kandidata ... ako ocjene da kandidat ne poznaje hrvatski jezik u mjeri koja je potrebna za uspješno studiranje'. Non-EU nationals compete in a separate foreign-nationals quota with its own priority list.

The direct-admission ('izravni upis') shortcut is reserved for ADU's own Montaža undergraduates, so an external applicant simply takes the full entrance exam. The genuine filter is the exam's assumed knowledge of film and music history, not the bachelor subject.

_rec.reputationSignals: POSITIVE: A3ES accreditation with a specific, checkable registration and despacho; IADE is a long-established and well-regarded Lisbon design school; unusually transparent published price list with named discount categories — better fee disclosure than most schools in this whole search; a clearly quantified merit scholarship. Note also the commercial signals, which I verified rather than inferred: rolling year-round admissions with no published entry criteria, a phone-and-WhatsApp enquiry funnel, at least four overlapping discount and scholarship categories, discount columns 'subject to limited vacancies defined in the selection process' (i.e. scarcity framing on price), and mandatory direct debit to unlock either instalments or scholarships. _rec.recommendation: DO NOT PRIORITISE — RIGHT COUNTRY, RIGHT ACCREDITATION, WRONG SUBJECT. Let me be blunt, because the accreditation being genuine is exactly what makes this dangerous: a real A3ES degree, real visa eligibility and a real quantified scholarship can all be true while the programme still teaches him nothing he wants. He wants music production, mixing, sound design and electronic music. This degree teaches digital journalism, infographics, transmedia and web labs, in Portuguese, with one shared sound studio and zero audio modules. Paying around €12,000 plus two years of his life for that would be a poor use of a budget-sensitive candidate's money when the Lusófona mestrado, in the same city, teaches acoustics, capture, synthesis, sound design and studio practice for less. Three further practical cautions: the exact tuition and emolumentos figures could NOT be verified from the official PDF and must be obtained in writing; the merit scholarship threshold for him is the FOREIGN-institution bar of 16.5/20, not 15.5, and the two official sources disagree on both threshold and percentage; and every scholarship and the 11-instalment plan require a Portuguese direct debit he cannot set up before arriving. Keep it only as a distant fallback if UCP, Lusófona and ReSound all fail AND he decides he wants an accredited Portuguese degree for immigration reasons more than he wants sound training — which would be an honest choice, but he should make it with his eyes open rather than mistake this for a sound course.
