_rec.program: Mestrado em Som e Imagem — especialização em Design de Som (Sound Design)
_rec.institution: Universidade Católica Portuguesa — Escola das Artes (Porto)
_rec.qualification: MESTRADO — Portuguese 2nd-cycle degree, 120 ECTS. A real Bologna master's, NOT a pós-graduação. Awards 'Mestre em Som e Imagem'. VERIFIED: the Escola das Artes course page states the programme is 'acreditado pela A3ES' and DGES-registered, 120 ECTS, 2nd cycle.
_rec.institutionType: Private university (Universidade Católica Portuguesa — private, State-recognised, established under Concordat). Escola das Artes is its arts faculty in Porto.
_rec.accreditationStatus: OFFICIAL — AND NOW FULLY VERIFIED. This is the key upgrade from the draft. The mestrado carries DGES registration R/A-Ef 1160/2011/AL01 and A3ES accreditation process ACEF/1415/14132; the Escola das Artes course page independently confirms 'acreditado pela A3ES' and DGES registration for the 2nd cycle. The draft's claim that the A3ES reference was UNVERIFIED is now SUPERSEDED — the reference exists. Practical meaning: this is an official Portuguese 2nd-cycle degree, valid across the EHEA, valid for doctoral entry, and valid as the basis for a Portuguese D4 study residence visa. It is emphatically NOT a 'pós-graduação' and not a school-issued certificate. He should still ask admissions to email him the registo/despacho reference on letterhead before paying — standard hygiene, not a doubt about the status.
_rec.focus: Sound design for film, theatre and concerts, music production, sound art installations and game audio, taught inside a wider sound-and-image school. VERIFIED: the school runs FOUR specialisations, not three as previously recorded — Animação, Design de Som, New Media Art, and Visual Effects. He would enter the Design de Som track.
_rec.whatYouStudy: Year 1 S1 (30 ECTS): Projeto/Produção I — Exterior e Estúdio (12), Produção de Som para Videojogos (5), Produção Eletrónica (5), Artes e Tecnologias do Som (5), Investigação em Som e Imagem (3). Year 1 S2 (30 ECTS): Projeto II — Pós-Produção/Design de Som (12), Banda Sonora (5), Projeto Interdisciplinar (5), Seminário Interdisciplinar (3), Interfaces Tangíveis e Computação Física (5). Year 2: Portfólio e Showreel (3) plus Dissertação/Projeto/Estágio (27+30). Covers microphone technique, studio recording and mastering, surround mixing for cinema, live sound, game audio and sound art. Curricular internship option of minimum 24 weeks. NOTE THE PROPORTION: exactly ONE 5-ECTS unit ('Produção Eletrónica') out of 120 touches electronic music production. This is a film/game/media sound-design degree with strong studio craft — it is not an electronic-music or DJ programme, and no amount of framing changes that.
_rec.durationEcts: 2 years / 4 semesters / 120 ECTS. VERIFIED. Regime PÓS-LABORAL (evening), classes roughly 18:00–22:00 — genuinely useful, it leaves his days free to produce and build the DJ side in parallel.
_rec.language: PORTUGUESE. This remains the single biggest practical risk for him and I could NOT verify any English-taught route — the course pages do not state a language of instruction at all, which in Portuguese higher education defaults to Portuguese. Treat 'taught in Portuguese' as the working assumption and get it confirmed in writing. He does not speak Portuguese; this is the decisive constraint on the whole entry.
_rec.entryRequirements: VERIFIED verbatim from the admissions page: 'Licenciado ou equivalente legal (na área do cinema, audiovisual, fotografia, multimédia, artes plásticas, arquitetura, design, engenharias, etc.)'; OR a foreign qualification conferred following the Bologna Process by a signatory State; OR a foreign academic qualification recognised as meeting the objectives of a licenciatura; OR a professional/academic curriculum recognised by the Escola das Artes Scientific Council. Documents: degree certificate, transcript of curricular units, ID, Europass CV, artistic portfolio. Foreign documents require Hague Apostille (Tunisia is an Apostille member, so the apostille route applies rather than full diplomatic legalisation).
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: YES — EXPLICITLY, AND THIS IS VERIFIED WORD-FOR-WORD. The published eligibility list names 'engenharias' (engineering) as an accepted first-cycle field, alongside cinema, audiovisual, fotografia, multimédia, artes plásticas, arquitetura and design. This is the ONLY programme in this Portuguese batch that names engineering in its own admission wording, which makes it the strongest structural fit on paper for a BSc Software Engineering holder. Caveat: eligibility is not selection — an artistic portfolio is still mandatory for candidates external to the Escola das Artes, and there is an interview.
_rec.portfolioSpec: VERIFIED as required, but the SPEC ITSELF IS STILL UNPUBLISHED. Exact wording: 'Portfólio do trabalho artístico (deverá ser indicado um link para acesso ao portfolio)' — an artistic work portfolio supplied as a link through the application platform. The page explicitly limits the interview stage to candidates external to the Escola das Artes, and the portfolio requirement attaches to the same group. No page count, runtime, format or assessment criteria are published — UNVERIFIED. He must email candidaturas.porto@ucp.pt for the assessment criteria; with no music background, he cannot afford to guess what they want.
_rec.auditionSpec: Interview — VERIFIED as a fixed, scheduled step in every application phase, held 'exclusivamente para alunos externos à Escola das Artes', i.e. it definitely applies to him. Dated slots were published for each 2026/27 phase (e.g. 14–15 April after phase 1). No performance audition, no written test, no instrument requirement. Whether the interview can be conducted online from Tunisia is NOT published — UNVERIFIED and worth confirming early, because travelling to Porto for a 30-minute interview would be a real cost.
_rec.englishTest: No IELTS requirement is published, and none should be expected — the programme is Portuguese-medium, so IELTS is simply the wrong test here. His untaken IELTS is therefore NOT the blocker for this programme; Portuguese is. What level of Portuguese evidence is demanded is UNVERIFIED — no language-proficiency requirement appears on the admissions page. Assume one will be applied in practice and budget roughly a year of Portuguese study to a working B1/B2.
_rec.tuitionPerYear: €6,570 per year — VERIFIED. Published as €657 per month × 10 monthly instalments, 2026/27 rate. No separate non-EU rate is published anywhere on the admissions page: he pays the same as a Portuguese student.
_rec.tuitionTotal: €13,140 total tuition for the full 2-year mestrado (€657 × 10 × 2), 2026/27 rate — VERIFIED, and the page itself states the total. NON-EU NOTE: no international or non-EU surcharge is published. By Western European private-school standards this is remarkably cheap — the entire degree costs less than a single year at most Spanish or Dutch private audio schools.
_rec.otherFees: VERIFIED: Application fee (taxa de candidatura) €50, waived for UCP graduates. Enrolment fee (taxa de inscrição) €460. Both figures confirmed on the official admissions page. STILL UNVERIFIED: whether the €460 recurs in year 2 or is a one-off at first enrolment; and insurance, materials and exam fees, which are not itemised anywhere public. The full 'Regulamento de propinas, taxas e emolumentos' exists on porto.ucp.pt but is image-encoded and could not be machine-read. Ask for the current emolumentos table as a text document.
_rec.equipmentRequired: Nothing mandatory is published — UNVERIFIED. The school supplies studios and preferential 24/7 student access to specialised equipment. A personal laptop plus a DAW licence is realistically expected but is nowhere stated as a requirement. Budget €1,500–€2,500 for a capable laptop, interface, headphones and software regardless; no accredited sound programme is genuinely doable without one.
_rec.paymentPlans: VERIFIED: tuition is structured by default as 10 monthly instalments per academic year (€657/month) — no separate application or approval needed, that IS the billing model. Early-bird, alumni or referral discounts: none published — UNVERIFIED.
_rec.scholarships: Merit scholarships (bolsas de mérito) are offered by the Escola das Artes and referenced from the course page's 'Apoios e Bolsas' section; UCP Porto's general merit scholarship consists of full exemption from tuition up to a maximum of 36 ECTS per semester plus exemption from registration and enrolment fees. CRITICAL UNVERIFIED POINT: whether a non-EU FIRST-YEAR entrant can win one on entry, as opposed to after a year of graded performance at UCP — the mechanics were not published and I could not confirm them. Portuguese State social scholarships (DGES Ação Social) are not realistically open to a newly arrived non-EU student. PLANNING ASSUMPTION: full self-pay for year 1, with a merit scholarship as a possible year-2 upside only.
_rec.intakes: One intake per year, September (start of the academic year). Three application phases all feed the same September start. VERIFIED.
_rec.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. VERIFIED for 2026/27: phase 1 opened 2 February 2026. Expect the 2027/28 cycle to open late January / early February 2027. He should start watching admissions.porto.ucp.pt from January 2027.
_rec.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. VERIFIED 2026/27 phases, all three: Phase 1 — 2 Feb to 9 Apr 2026 (interviews 14–15 Apr, results 21 Apr, enrolment 27–28 Apr). Phase 2 — 30 Apr to 11 Jun 2026 (interviews 16–17 Jun, results 23 Jun, enrolment 26–29 Jun). Phase 3 — 1 Jul to 26 Aug 2026 (interviews 1–2 Sep, results 7 Sep, enrolment 9–10 Sep). FOR A SEPTEMBER 2027 START HE MUST APPLY IN PHASE 1 (roughly Feb–Apr 2027). A phase-3 result dated 7 September leaves literally zero time to obtain a Tunisian D4 visa for the same month's start — phase 3 is structurally useless to a non-EU applicant.
_rec.facilities: Motion Capture Laboratory; Surround Sound Mixing Studio; Interactive Art and Digital Fabrication Laboratory; Cinema/TV studio with chroma-key; recording studios with preferential 24/7 student access. Curricular internship of minimum 24 weeks placed with host companies. Teaching staff described as working professionals and artists alongside academic supervisors. No console models, monitoring chain or microphone inventory are published — the facility disclosure is good by Portuguese standards but not itemised.
_rec.visaEligible: YES — and this is verified at the level that matters. UCP is a State-recognised private university awarding an A3ES-accredited, DGES-registered 2nd-cycle degree lasting 2 years, which is exactly the category that supports a Portuguese D4 residence visa for study (courses longer than 12 months). Standard file from Tunis: UCP acceptance letter, proof of means, accommodation, insurance, criminal record. The institution's status is not the risk here; his timeline is.
_rec.reputationSignals: The strongest single signal in Portuguese private sound education. Positives: A3ES/DGES-recognised degree with a traceable registration reference; a dedicated Design de Som specialisation, which is rare; a research-active school with a Doutoramento em Ciência e Tecnologia das Artes sitting above it; motion-capture and surround facilities; an Erasmus Mundus programme (Digicréa) hosted in the same school; four coordinated specialisations under a named coordinator. Selective but not tiny. No published complaints, no red flags, no aggressive commercial-intake pattern. The honest caveat is scope, not quality: it is a film and media-arts sound school, not a club-music or DJ school.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: First-year outlay approx. €7,080–€7,600 (tuition €6,570 + application €50 + enrolment €460, plus unpublished insurance/materials). Full two-year tuition + fees approx. €13,650–€14,500. EXCLUDES Porto living costs (budget €800–€1,100/month, i.e. roughly €19,000–€26,000 over two years — living cost dwarfs tuition here) and excludes a laptop/DAW at €1,500–€2,500. Realistic all-in two-year figure: €35,000–€43,000.
_rec.recommendation: THE STRONGEST PORTUGUESE OPTION ON PAPER — BUT THE LANGUAGE MAKES IT CONDITIONAL, NOT AUTOMATIC. It is the only entry in this batch that is simultaneously a genuine A3ES/DGES master's degree, explicitly open to an engineering bachelor in its own published wording, visa-safe, and cheap (€13,140 for the whole degree). The accreditation question that the draft left open is now closed in its favour. Two things must be said bluntly. First, it is taught in Portuguese and he does not speak it — that is a 12-month project he must start NOW if he wants the Feb–Apr 2027 phase-1 window, and if he will not do it, this entry is unworkable and he should put everything into ReSound instead. Second, it will not make him a DJ. It will make him a competent film and game sound designer with real studio craft and one 5-ECTS brush with electronic production. If he is honest that the accredited degree is the visa-and-craft vehicle and the DJ career is built in parallel on evenings and weekends, this is excellent value. If he expects the degree itself to deliver the DJ career, he will be disappointed and out €35k.

_rec.durationEcts: VERIFIED: 120 ECTS over 2 years, delivered PÓS-LABORAL (evening/part-time schedule). Year 1 is curricular specialisation; Year 2 offers three pathways — Final Project (practical/artistic), Dissertation (research), or Internship (professional).
_rec.language: Portuguese. VERIFIED Sound Design internship partners: Worten Digitópia (Casa da Música), Loudness Studios, Indigo Música, Lourisom, SomNorte, Soundtrapp, ElitPalco, Warehouse Studios (Czech Republic), Ad-hoc Studios (Spain). _rec.facilities: VERIFIED and the best published facilities in this batch: Motion Capture laboratory; SURROUND SOUND MIXING STUDIO; Interactive Art and Digital Fabrication laboratory; Cinema/TV studio with chroma-keying; individual video editing suites; stereo and surround mixing studios; and a 400-seat cinema auditorium with surround sound. _rec.entryRequirements: VERIFIED: a licenciatura or equivalent in cinema, audiovisual, film, photography, multimedia, plastic/visual arts, architecture, design, ENGINEERING, etc.; OR a foreign higher-education degree aligned with the Bologna Process; OR a foreign degree recognised by the Escola das Artes Scientific Council; OR a 'currículo escolar, científico ou profissional' recognised by the Scientific Council as demonstrating capacity for this cycle. _rec.acceptsNonMusic: YES — AND UNUSUALLY EXPLICITLY SO. The published entry list names 'engenharia' (ENGINEERING) directly among the accepted licenciatura fields, alongside design, multimedia and architecture. His BSc Software Engineering is therefore an EXPRESSLY LISTED qualifying background, not a borderline case. This is the only programme in this batch where his exact degree subject is named in the admissions rule.
_rec.portfolioSpec: VERIFIED AND MANDATORY: 'Portfólio do trabalho artístico (deverá ser indicado um link para acesso ao portfolio)' — an artistic-work portfolio submitted as a LINK. Combined with a scheduled interview (interview dates are published for each phase). Exact content/length expectations are not published — request from admissions.
_rec.auditionSpec: Interview, scheduled as a distinct published stage in each application phase (e.g. 14–15 April for Phase 1). No musical audition.
_rec.englishTest: NOT APPLICABLE as the binding requirement — the programme is Portuguese-medium, so IELTS will not satisfy entry. No English-test requirement is published. Portuguese proficiency is the real gate. UNVERIFIED what level is demanded — ask admissions.
_rec.tuitionPerYear: VERIFIED: €657.00 per month × 10 monthly instalments per year = €6,570 per year. No differential pricing for non-EU applicants is published — he pays the same as everyone else.
_rec.tuitionTotal: VERIFIED: €13,140 for the full two-year programme (stated on the admissions page as '13.140€').
_rec.otherFees: VERIFIED: application fee €50 for external candidates (free for UCP graduates); enrolment fee €460. Annual re-enrolment of €365 was asserted in the parent brief but was NOT confirmed on the pages read — UNVERIFIED. Insurance, materials and equipment fees: not published, UNVERIFIED.

Given the promised 'continuous and preferential access' to campus studios, motion-capture lab and surround mixing rooms, personal equipment demands are likely lighter here than at the private academies, but budget for a capable laptop, headphones and a DAW licence.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: Year one: €50 application + €460 enrolment + €6,570 tuition = €7,080. NET POSITION: the only realistic UCP award for him is the Escola das Artes merit bolsa, on unpublished terms. _rec.program: Mestrado em Produção e Tecnologias do Som (Master in Sound Production and Technologies)
_rec.university: Universidade Lusófona
_rec.institutionType: Private university
_rec.focus: Music Production; Recording/Engineering; Sound Design; Immersive Audio
_rec.durationEcts: 2 years / 4 semesters / 120 ECTS; in-person, evening classes starting 18:00 on weekdays
_rec.language: Portuguese
_rec.whatYouStudy: Advanced training for sound directors, sound designers, music producers, and recording/mastering engineers. Core units cover acoustics, sound capture, synthesis, composition, mixing, studio practice, virtual auditory environments and audiovisual sound relationships, plus a 30-ECTS dissertation. Principal software taught: Avid Pro Tools, Max/MSP, Arduino.
_rec.entryRequirements: Holders of a licenciatura or equivalent; holders of a foreign first-cycle degree from a Bologna-process country; holders of a foreign degree recognised as equivalent; or candidates whose "currículo escolar, científico ou profissional" is recognised by the institution as demonstrating capacity for master's study. Selection weighting is published: 25% prior qualification, 75% interview and portfolio (100% interview where there is no degree).
_rec.portfolioSpec: Portfolio required and weighted heavily — portfolio + interview together account for 75% of the admission score. The number of works, duration and format are NOT specified on the course page; request the current regulamento de candidatura from the university.
_rec.auditionSpec: No audition. Admission interview required (heavily weighted).
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: Yes. The page describes the intake as "licenciados nas áreas da musicologia e tecnologias do som" together with professionals from audiovisual, digital arts and performance fields, and the general admission rule accepts any licenciatura plus a recognised professional/academic CV. A software-engineering BSc is admissible; the 75%-weighted portfolio is what would actually decide it.
_rec.tuitionIntl: Published 2025/26 figures are internally inconsistent on the site as read: ~€365/month for a 30-ECTS semester load (≈€7,300 across two years at 10 months/year) alongside a stated €12.18 per ECTS, plus a €450 fee. Treat the per-ECTS figure as UNVERIFIED and get a written payment plan. No separate international rate was published.
_rec.scholarship: None found for this standalone master. Note: Lusófona is the Lisbon partner in the fully funded ReSound Erasmus Mundus master listed separately — that is the funded route into the same building.
_rec.applicationOpens: 18 July (2026/27 cycle)
_rec.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Published 2026/27 master's application window: 18 July – 1 September 2026. Expect an equivalent mid-summer 2027 window for a Sept 2027 start — note this is much later than the Portuguese public universities.
_rec.facilities: Recording studios and digital labs on the Lisbon campus; Pro Tools / Max-MSP / Arduino toolchain; free parking for postgraduate students attending evening sessions. Shares infrastructure with the ReSound Erasmus Mundus consortium and the FilmEU alliance.
_rec.fitNotes: A hands-on production-and-engineering master where the portfolio counts for three quarters of the decision — good for someone whose evidence is tracks rather than transcripts. Evening classes leave the day free for work or studio time. Main obstacles: Portuguese-language teaching and no visible funding; the smarter play is to use this as the paid fallback if the ReSound scholarship (same city, same partner) does not land.

_rec.institution: Universitatea Națională de Artă Teatrală și Cinematografică „I.L. Caragiale" București (UNATC), Facultatea de Teatru
_rec.publicPrivate: PUBLIC — CONFIRMED. State university under the Romanian Ministry of Education. Verified directly in Hotărârea Senatului nr. 290/27.05.2026, Anexa 1, signed by Rector Prof.univ.dr. Liviu Lucaci and Senate President Prof.univ.dr. Doru Nițescu — a published Senate fee decision with Ministry-allocated budget places is conclusive evidence of state status.
_rec.institutionType: State film and theatre university. This programme sits in the Facultatea de TEATRU (domain: Teatru și artele spectacolului), not the Facultatea de Film.
_rec.qualification: Diplomă de master — CONFIRMED genuine second-cycle degree (ciclul II). The Senate fee decision files it under 'II. TAXE DE STUDII – CICLUL II – STUDII UNIVERSITARE DE MASTERAT'. 120 ECTS confirmed on the official admissions page. Supports a student residence permit via the Ministry Letter of Acceptance route.
_rec.accreditationStatus: CONFIRMED. ARACIS-accredited state university; programme listed on the official 2026-27 admissions portal (admitere.unatc.ro) and in the Senate fee schedule under Faculty of Theatre master's programmes.
_rec.focus: Live sound design AND lighting design for the performing arts — the two are equally weighted, not sound-led.
_rec.whatYouStudy: Lighting and sound design for stage. CORRECTED/SHARPENED: the official page describes the 3-hour written exam as two tasks involving analysis of lighting/sound design drawn from PLAYS (dramatic texts) plus graphic projection of design concepts. So the discipline is text-driven theatre design — reading a play and designing its light and sound — not studio production or electronic music.
_rec.durationEcts: CONFIRMED: 2 years, 120 ECTS, full-time (învățământ cu frecvență).
_rec.language: Romanian — CONFIRMED on the official programme page. No English track exists for this programme.
_rec.languageRequirement: CONFIRMED via UNATC's own foreign-citizen admission page: non-EU applicants must complete a Romanian preparatory language year UNLESS they hold a minimum B1 Romanian certificate or have completed 4 years of prior study in Romanian. IELTS/TOEFL are irrelevant here — his untaken English tests neither help nor hurt.
_rec.entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree (licență) plus diploma supplement, or a faculty certificate for 2026 graduates. CONFIRMED: no field restriction is published — a BSc Software Engineering satisfies the academic condition. Minimum admission mark 6.00/10 (average of the two exams), applying to both budget and fee-paying places. Non-EU applicants go through UNATC's foreign-citizen route with a Ministry of Education Letter of Acceptance.
_rec.auditionSpec: CORRECTED ORDER AND DETAIL. Exam 1 is ORAL, 15 minutes, graded 1-10: a discussion based on his portfolio of representative works. Exam 2 is WRITTEN, 3 hours, graded 1-10: two tasks requiring analysis of lighting and sound design from plays plus graphic projection of design concepts. Final grade is the average of the two; minimum 6.00. Both conducted in Romanian. The written paper requires him to draw/diagram design concepts, not just write — an additional skill barrier the previous entry missed.
_rec.portfolioSpec: MANDATORY — CONFIRMED. A personal artistic project (un proiect artistic personal) in the performing arts, sound and/or light, accompanied by a 3-5 page theoretical argument submitted in Word format. The required work is THEATRE/PERFORMANCE sound or light. Club tracks, DJ sets and studio production do not satisfy this. He would need to earn credits on actual student theatre productions.
_rec.equipmentRequired: Not published — UNVERIFIED. The written exam is theoretical/graphic; the portfolio is documentation-based. Assume he supplies his own laptop and design software.
_rec.facilities: Not published — UNVERIFIED. UNATC operates theatre venues and technical stages in Bucharest. Ask the Faculty of Theatre secretariat (secretariat@unatc.ro) for a written inventory before committing.
_rec.tuitionEU: CONFIRMED EXACTLY: 8,000 lei per academic year. Verified in Hotărârea Senatului nr. 290/27.05.2026, Anexa 1, section II.1 (Master - Facultatea de Teatru), where 'Design, lumină și sunet în artele spectacolului' is listed at 8.000 lei alongside the other Theatre master's programmes. For comparison the Film Faculty's master's programmes are 13,750 lei — the previous entry's contrast was accurate.
_rec.tuitionNonEU: STILL UNVERIFIED, AND I CONFIRM THE PREVIOUS AGENT'S CAUTION WAS CORRECT. I extracted the full text of the Senate decision: it contains no valutar, euro, or foreign-citizen rate anywhere across all six pages. The document covers licență, masterat, doctorat, postgraduate and enrolment fees in lei only. Do NOT assume 8,000 lei applies to him. For calibration, UBB Cluj's verified 2026-27 rate for the theatre domain is €750/month over 9 months (about €6,750/year). He must obtain the euro rate in writing from UNATC's International Students Office (study@unatc.ro) before budgeting.
_rec.otherFees: CORRECTED — the previous entry marked this UNVERIFIED; it is now verified. Master's admission registration fee: 400 lei, per Hotărârea Senatului nr. 290, 'TAXE DE ÎNSCRIERE ÎN ANUL UNIVERSITAR 2026-2027', item 2, covering all programmes in both faculties. Optional admission preparation courses cost 150 lei per course (15% discount if paid in full). Additional: document legalisation, translation, Letter of Acceptance costs, and Bucharest living costs (UNVERIFIED).
_rec.scholarships: Two Romanian government routes, both open to him in principle. (1) Romanian Government/MFA scholarships via scholarships.studyinromania.gov.ro — CONFIRMED requirement of a minimum study-years average of 7/10 or 'Good'; established under Government Decision no. 288/1993 for non-EU citizens. Deadline historically about 31 March with results about 15 July — PRIOR CYCLE, confirm. Critically for THIS programme the Romanian-only teaching rule is an advantage rather than an obstacle, since the programme is taught in Romanian and a preparatory Romanian year is granted to scholarship holders. (2) ARICE scholarships with the Ministry of Education, documents by email in the May-June window. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new dates. Reality check: only 3 budget-funded and 3 fee-paying places exist in total — CONFIRMED on the official page — so even a funded applicant faces a 6-seat lottery.
_rec.intakes: September (single annual intake).
_rec.applicationOpens: 4 August 2026 for the 2026-27 cycle — CONFIRMED. PRIOR CYCLE, expect early August 2027 for his target intake.
_rec.deadline: CONFIRMED AND EXPANDED: registration closes 9 September 2026; document verification 10-11 September; EXAMS 15-20 SEPTEMBER 2026; results per the exam schedule. The previous entry gave the 9 September registration deadline but omitted that he must be physically in Bucharest in mid-September for the exams. Scholarship deadlines are far earlier — about 31 March. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm all 2027 dates.
_rec.visaEligible: Yes — CONFIRMED. UNATC operates a foreign-citizen admission route; the Ministry of Education (General Directorate for International Relations and European Affairs) issues the Letter of Acceptance, and UNATC's own guidance states the visa is issued on the basis of that letter plus full payment of the tuition fee. Note that last condition: he must pay the year's tuition up front to get the visa.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: YES on paper — CONFIRMED. A licență in any field is accepted and no music or arts degree clause is published. His BSc Software Engineering is formally sufficient. The real obstacles are elsewhere: a Romanian-language 3-hour written design exam, a live performing-arts portfolio he does not have, and 6 total places.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: Domestic-rate scenario: 8,000 lei/year (about €1,600) × 2 years = about €3,200, plus 400 lei admission fee. Non-EU euro-rate scenario: UNVERIFIED, but if it tracks the regional arts norm of roughly €750/month × 9 months, budget about €6,750/year and about €13,500 over two years, plus a preparatory Romanian year if he lacks B1. Add Bucharest living costs. Fully covered if he wins a Romanian Government or ARICE scholarship.
_rec.recommendation: CONFIRMED AS REAL, BUT DOWNGRADED — AND I HAVE FOUND HIM A STRICTLY BETTER PROGRAMME AT THE SAME UNIVERSITY. Everything structural checks out: it is a genuine ARACIS-accredited 120-ECTS second-cycle master's, the domestic tuition of 8,000 lei/year is confirmed verbatim in the Senate decision, the admission fee is 400 lei, and it is eligible for Romanian government scholarships whose Romanian-only teaching rule actually suits it. But it is a poor fit for HIM and I am rating it C rather than treating it as a serious second application. Four reasons. First, it is half lighting design, examined in a 3-hour written paper in Romanian that requires analysing plays and producing graphic design projections — a skill set he has no route to in one year. Second, the portfolio must be a live performing-arts project with a 3-5 page theoretical argument; club music and studio work do not qualify. Third, there are 6 places in total. Fourth and most importantly: THE SAME UNIVERSITY RUNS 'Interactive Technologies for Performing and Media Arts', a 120-ECTS MA taught entirely in ENGLISH, which explicitly welcomes applicants from science and engineering backgrounds, whose second admission test is a practical software demonstration in Processing, Max/MSP, TouchDesigner, Unity or Blender, and which accepts a 1500-2000 word English essay IN PLACE OF a portfolio for candidates who do not yet have one. That programme is 13,750 lei/year with 3 budget and 4 fee places, needs no Romanian at all, and its non-EU admission runs 10-27 June with an ONLINE exam option. For a Tunisian software engineer with no portfolio and no Romanian, that is a categorically better application than this one. He should apply to ITPMA and treat Design lumină și sunet as, at most, a throwaway second option only if he has by then genuinely built stage-sound credits.

_rec.focus: Film sound design and post-production
_rec.whatYouStudy: Film sound as an art form: sound design, recording, editing and post-production for cinema, worked through DAW projects. The competition bibliography is the professional film-sound canon: Yewdall 'Practical Art of Motion Picture Sound', Sonnenschein 'Sound Design', Chion 'Film, A Sound Art' / 'Audio-Vision' / 'The Voice in Cinema', Murray 'Sound Design Theory and Practice', Holman 'Sound for Film and Television', Purcell 'Dialog Editing for Motion Pictures', Ament 'The Foley Grail', Viers 'The Sound Effects Bible' and 'The Location Sound Bible', Rumsey & McCormick 'Sound and Recording', Schafer 'The Soundscape', Weis & Belton 'Film Sound: Theory and Practice'. Toolchain: Avid Pro Tools, Steinberg Nuendo, Cockos Reaper, Adobe Audition, Adobe Premiere Pro, Fairlight/DaVinci Resolve.
_rec.durationEcts: 2 years, 4 semesters, 120 ECTS, full-time (cu frecvență) — CONFIRMED on both the programme page and the foreign-citizens page.
_rec.language: Romanian — CONFIRMED. Not an English-taught programme. UNATC's Faculty of Film does run English-taught master's programmes (Design for New Media, Visual Effects, Audiovisual Preservation and Programming, Interactive Technologies for Performing and Media Arts, Art of Game Design), but Arta sunetului de film is not among them.
_rec.languageRequirement: CORRECTED AND SHARPENED — this is stricter than the previous record implied. UNATC's own foreign-citizens page states that foreign nationals may be enrolled in the admission contest / aptitude test only AFTER completing the Romanian-language preparatory year („Cetățenii străini pot fi înscriși la concursul de admitere/testul de aptitudini după absolvirea anului pregătitor de limba română“). Exemption requires one of: Romanian study documents or school records showing at least FOUR consecutive years of study in Romanian within the Romanian national system; or a certificate of linguistic competence of minimum CEFR level B1 issued specifically by an accredited Romanian higher-education institution that organises the Romanian preparatory year, by a Romanian language-and-culture lectorate at a foreign university, by the Institutul Limbii Române, or by the Institutul Cultural Român. A generic B1 certificate from any other provider does not qualify. No IELTS/TOEFL anywhere in this admission.
_rec.entryRequirements: CONFIRMED. A completed bachelor's degree worth 180 or 240 credits, with NO field restriction for this programme (contrast Arta imaginii de film on the same page, which requires graduates 'ai facultăților de profil'). Plus a Europass CV, the portfolio, proof of registration-fee payment, baccalaureate diploma, birth certificate, passport valid 6+ months, foreign-credential recognition certificate, a medical fitness certificate from a family physician, and the GDPR declaration. Minimum admission average 6.00/10 for both budget and fee-paying places. Registration is exclusively online via the 2BitsEDU/Edubits platform; portfolios are uploaded to a secure institution-provided folder issued only after registration.
_rec.auditionSpec: CONFIRMED. Single stage, two exams, each marked 1–10, final mark the arithmetic mean. Proba 1 — written: film-culture test based on the competition bibliography plus technical sound-design knowledge. Proba 2 — oral: a colloquium on one project of the candidate's choice from his portfolio, presented with the openable DAW session. Tie-break is decided on Proba 2, then Proba 1. No appeals are admitted against oral or practical exams. Both exams are in Romanian.
_rec.portfolioSpec: MANDATORY AND SUBSTANTIAL — CONFIRMED, and the binding practical constraint for him. Required at registration: a portfolio of artistic projects with sound design created by the candidate himself (digital copies of films or other relevant sound-design-for-film-and-media projects), plus a Europass CV. At Proba 2 he must present an actual DAW session file from one portfolio piece and be able to open, run and discuss it; candidates are explicitly responsible for verifying the completeness and functionality of the DAW project. He has none of this today. Building it is a genuine twelve-month project and must be spent sound-designing SHORT FILMS, not producing club tracks — the portfolio must show film-sound work.
_rec.equipmentRequired: A working DAW project in one of the six named applications. The university provides Pro Tools, Nuendo, Reaper, Audition, Premiere Pro and Fairlight/DaVinci Resolve at the exam; if the required software is unavailable, candidates may bring their own equipment. Practically: a laptop plus a licence for one — Reaper is the cheapest, DaVinci Resolve's free tier includes Fairlight.
_rec.facilities: No published studio inventory on the admissions site. UNATC is the national film school with production facilities. Ask secretariat.film@unatc.ro for a facilities list and the studio-access policy for master's students.
_rec.tuitionEU: 13,750 lei per academic year for fee-paying places — CONFIRMED VERBATIM in Hotărârea Senatului nr. 290/27.05.2026, Annex 1, section II.2 (Faculty of Film), line 'Arta sunetului de film 13.750'. NEW AND IMPORTANT: the programme has only 3 budget-funded places and 3 fee-paying places. Six seats in total.
_rec.tuitionNonEU: STILL NOT PUBLISHED — the previous record's caution was correct and I confirm it. I extracted the full text of Hotărârea Senatului nr. 290/2026: it contains no euro figure and no reference to 'cont propriu valutar', 'străin' or 'terțe' anywhere. All figures are in lei and apply to the domestic fee-paying regime. Romanian non-EU tuition is set per institution above a Government Ordinance 22/2009 floor and is normally quoted in EUR per month; comparable Romanian arts faculties sit around €750–950/month payable nine months a year. DO NOT assume the 13,750 lei figure applies to him. Ask study@unatc.ro and secretariat.film@unatc.ro in writing for the euro rate for a non-EU master's student in Arta sunetului de film — and note that if he wins a Romanian government scholarship the question becomes moot, because scholarship holders occupy budget places.
_rec.otherFees: CORRECTED — previously UNVERIFIED, now confirmed from the same Senate decision. Master's admission registration fee: 400 lei (Annex 1, TAXE DE ÎNSCRIERE, item 2), payable online in the admission application. Optional admission preparation courses: 150 lei per course (15% discount if paid in full). Document legalisation/apostille, authorised translation, credential recognition and Letter of Acceptance processing are additional. Bucharest living costs additional — UNATC's own page points candidates to Numbeo rather than publishing a figure.
_rec.scholarships: CONFIRMED WITH IMPORTANT CORRECTIONS. (1) Romanian Government / MFA scholarships via scholarships.studyinromania.gov.ro, under Government Decision 288/1993 — open to citizens of ALL non-EU countries, so a Tunisian national qualifies; requires an average of the study years for the last graduated school of at least 7/10 or equivalent 'Good'; excludes only Medicine, Dental Medicine and Pharmacy; at master's level beneficiaries study ONLY IN ROMANIAN, with a fully financed Romanian preparatory year for non-speakers. Covers: exemption from registration, language-testing and aptitude-test fees; tuition for the preparatory year; tuition for the degree; a monthly stipend during both the preparatory year and the degree; and dormitory accommodation subject to availability. 2026/2027 cycle: applications 16 February – 31 March 2026, results announced around 15 July 2026, then the Ministry issues the Letter of Acceptance. TWO CAVEATS THE PREVIOUS RECORD MISSED — the Ministry expressly reserves the right to assign a DIFFERENT university in the same field if the candidate's choice cannot be honoured, and later requests to change field or university are refused; and the scholarship does not waive UNATC's own aptitude test, so he must still pass Proba 1 and Proba 2 in Romanian and place within three budget seats. (2) ARICE scholarships — CORRECTED AND DOWNGRADED. 40 scholarships for 2026/2027, files emailed 11 May – 12 June 2026 to burse2026@arice.gov.ro, Romanian-taught with a free preparatory year to B1. But ARICE explicitly PRIORITISES economics and business administration, agricultural sciences, technical sciences, and oil and gas; other fields are considered only 'to the extent of the places available'. Film sound is not a priority field, so ARICE is a long shot, not a parallel route of equal weight.
_rec.englishTest: None required or accepted for this programme. His untaken IELTS/TOEFL is irrelevant to Arta sunetului de film — but it WOULD be needed for UNATC's English-taught master's programmes, which is a reason to sit it anyway.
_rec.intakes: September/October (one intake)
_rec.applicationOpens: 2026/2027 cycle, Romanian-taught route (which is the route for this programme, including for foreign citizens): online registration 4 August – 9 September 2026; file verification 10–11 September; admission exams 15–20 September 2026. Separately, the English-taught non-EU route ran 10–27 June 2026 with file verification 28–30 June and exams 1–8 July 2026 — that route does NOT include Arta sunetului de film. PRIOR CYCLE — confirm 2027 dates.
_rec.deadline: Expect an August–September 2027 registration window for a September 2027 start. The operative deadline for him is far earlier: the Romanian Government / MFA scholarship closes around 31 March 2027, roughly five months before the university's own window, and the preparatory-year requirement means a scholarship awarded in July 2027 would put him into the Romanian language year in September 2027 and into the master's proper in September 2028.
_rec.visaEligible: Yes — CONFIRMED. UNATC operates a published admission route for foreign citizens at Faculty of Film master's level; the Ministry of Education issues a 'Letter of acceptance for studies in Romania', which is expressly required to obtain a Romanian long-stay study visa and to enrol, and which for scholarship holders states any obligation to complete the Romanian preparatory year.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: YES — CONFIRMED. The published condition is simply a completed bachelor's of 180 or 240 credits, with no field restriction and no music-degree clause. His BSc Software Engineering is an acceptable academic qualification. The barriers are the portfolio, the Romanian language, and six seats.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: Two scenarios. SELF-FUNDED: unquantifiable until UNATC publishes or states the non-EU euro rate; if it lands in the €750–950/month band typical of Romanian arts faculties, roughly €6,750–8,550 per year over two years, plus a Romanian preparatory year, plus Bucharest living, plus 400 lei registration and legalisation costs. SCHOLARSHIP: tuition, preparatory year and accommodation covered, a monthly stipend paid, and registration and aptitude-test fees waived — his cost collapses to visa costs, travel, document legalisation and the gap between the stipend and Bucharest living costs.
_rec.recommendation: STILL THE BEST PROSPECT OF THE SIX, AND NOW THE ONLY ONE THAT IS BOTH A GOOD FIT AND OPEN TO HIM — BUT NARROWER THAN THE PREVIOUS RECORD SUGGESTED. Everything structurally good about it holds up under verification: a real 2-year, 120-ECTS, ARACIS-accredited degree at Romania's national film school; no music-degree requirement; the professional film-sound toolchain and canon; and a Romanian government scholarship a Tunisian national genuinely can win, which covers tuition, a free Romanian preparatory year, accommodation and a monthly stipend. Four corrections tighten the picture. First, the programme admits only SIX students a year — 3 on budget, 3 fee-paying — so this is a highly competitive seat, not a place he walks into. Second, the language rule is stricter than reported: foreign nationals may sit the admission exam only after completing the Romanian preparatory year, unless they hold a B1 certificate from a specific short list of Romanian issuers (an accredited Romanian HEI running the preparatory year, a Romanian lectorate abroad, the Institutul Limbii Române or the Institutul Cultural Român) — an ordinary B1 certificate will not do. Third, the MFA scholarship does not buy him admission: he must still pass a written film-culture exam and an oral DAW colloquium in Romanian and place in the top three, and the Ministry reserves the right to send him to a different university in the same field if UNATC cannot take him. Fourth, ARICE is a much weaker parallel route than described — film sound is outside its four priority fields and is considered only if places remain. The non-EU euro tuition rate genuinely is unpublished; I extracted the full Senate decision and it contains no euro figures at all, so the previous record's refusal to guess was right. Concrete plan for a realistic 2028 master's start via a 2027 preparatory year: (a) confirm his SMU MedTech average converts to at least 7/10 — this is a hard eligibility gate, check it first; (b) start Romanian now and aim for a qualifying B1 certificate from an accepted issuer; (c) redirect the portfolio year to sound-designing student short films, not DJ tracks, and finish with an openable, functional Pro Tools or Reaper session he can walk a panel through; (d) email study@unatc.ro and secretariat.film@unatc.ro for the non-EU euro rate and for confirmation of the number of places open to non-EU candidates; (e) apply to the MFA scholarship in the 16 February – 31 March 2027 window, and treat the university's own August–September 2027 registration as the second gate, not the first. One additional option worth putting in front of him: UNATC's English-taught non-EU master's route — in particular Interactive Technologies for Performing and Media Arts (digital control of sound, light, image and code) and Art of Game Design, both 2-year, 13,750 lei, admitted on a separate June–July calendar with an English-language file competition and no Romanian required. Those are not funded by the MFA scholarship, which is Romanian-only at master's level, but they are the same university, the same faculty, adjacent to his interests, and they play directly to a software-engineering background. That is the pairing to research next.

_rec.program: Master akademske studije Audiovizuelni mediji — modul Dizajn zvuka (Sound Design)
_rec.university: Academy of Arts, University of Novi Sad (Akademija umetnosti, Univerzitet u Novom Sadu)
_rec.institutionType: Public art academy within a public university
_rec.degree: Master akademske studije; professional title 'Мастер аудиовизуелни уметник' (Master audiovisual artist)
_rec.focus: Sound Design; Film & Game Sound; Immersive / interactive audio
_rec.language: Serbian. Foreign applicants must supply 'доказ о познавању српског језика' (proof of Serbian-language knowledge) as part of the application.
_rec.durationEcts: 1 year / 60 ECTS — confirmed on the official curriculum sheet (mas-dizajn-zvuka.pdf): 'Дужина трајања студија: 1 година; Обим студија изражен у ЕСПБ бодовима: 60'.
_rec.whatYouStudy: VERIFIED from the official curriculum sheet. Core: Супервизија звука (Sound Supervision, 2+4 weekly hours — by far the heaviest course); Драматургија савременог филма; Режија - анализа и синтеза; Авангардни филм; Завршни рад and Завршни рад - истраживање. Electives, choose 12 ECTS: Аудиовизуелна артикулација; Звук у филмској уметности; Постпродукција филмске слике; Светлосна артикулација у визуелним медијима; Продукција музике за нове медије (Production of Music for New Media); Филмска и телевизијска продукција; Имерзивне игре (Immersive Games); Видео арт. Note the sibling MAS Музичка продукција (also 1 year / 60 ECTS) is far closer to club/electronic production — its courses include Музичка продукција, Звук и музика на филму, Савремене тенденције у музичкој продукцији 1 and 2, Историја електроакустичке музике and Историја популарне музике — but its entry is restricted to a four-year degree in the artistic field Музичка продукција or a cognate programme, so it is closed to him.
_rec.portfolioSpec: STILL UNPUBLISHED. The 2026 konkurs states only: 'Програм пријемних испита прописан је Правилником Академије уметности о критеријумима и поступку избора кандидата за упис на мастер академске студије и Информаторима о програмским садржајима пријемних испита'. The Academy publishes Informator PDFs for Pozorišni oblici, Dizajn video igara, Kreiranje serija and Muzička produkcija — but NOT for Dizajn zvuka. Request the Informator for Dizajn zvuka directly from aofarts@uns.ac.rs.
_rec.auditionSpec: An entrance exam (пријемни испит) is compulsory and on-site — 'У прву годину мастер академских студија може се уписати лице које положи пријемни испит' — held 07–13 October 2026 (first round) or 23–28 October 2026 (second round). Its content for Dizajn zvuka is not published. Scoring context from the konkurs: a threshold of at least 36 of a possible 70 exam points is applied.
_rec.entryRequirements: VERIFIED verbatim: 'Модул Дизајн звука: завршене основне академске студије у четворогодишњем трајању' — completed FOUR-YEAR undergraduate academic studies, i.e. the general 240-ECTS floor, with NO artistic-field restriction. Foreign nationals: 'Страни држављанин се може уписати на студијске програме мастер академских студија под истим условима као и домаћи држављанин', submitting additionally (1) решење о извршеном признавању стране дипломе (formal recognition of the foreign degree), (2) доказ о здравственом осигурању, (3) доказ о познавању српског језика. Places for Dizajn zvuka 2026/27: 4 budget + 1 self-financing = 5 total.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: YES on subject — this is the key correction. The 2026 konkurs restricts the sibling modules by field (Дизајн светла requires the artistic field Дизајн светла 'или неки сродан студијски програм'; Анимација и визуелни ефекти likewise; Мултимедијална режија requires Режија) but for Дизајн звука it requires ONLY 'завршене основне академске студије у четворогодишњем трајању'. No artistic or musical field is named. The binding constraint is therefore LENGTH (four-year / 240 ECTS), not subject — a 3-year Tunisian licence would fail, a 4-year or 5-year engineering degree would satisfy it.
_rec.deadline: 2026/27 CYCLE, NOT 2027 — confirm new date. VERIFIED from the official 'Текст Конкурса Мастер Докторске 2026' (published June 2026): Департман драмских уметности — electronic application 05.10.2026; entrance exam 07.10.–13.10.2026; preliminary ranking 15.10.2026; final ranking and enrolment 20.10.2026. SECOND ROUND: application 21.10.2026, exam 23.10.–28.10.2026, enrolment 03.11.2026. Expect the same early-to-mid-October pattern in 2027 — note this is an OCTOBER intake, not September.
_rec.applicationOpens: 2026/27 cycle: 5 October 2026 (first round), 21 October 2026 (second round). 2027/28 dates not yet published.
_rec.scholarship: None found for foreign nationals. Budget (tuition-free) places exist — 4 of the 5 Dizajn zvuka places are budget places — but they are awarded on entrance-exam rank in Serbian and in practice go to domestic candidates.
_rec.fundingLevel: None found for a foreign applicant, but the self-pay cost is very low (see tuition)
_rec.tuitionIntl: VERIFIED from the 2026/27 konkurs fee table: 'Школарина за странце (евра): 1800' per year for every programme including Audiovizuelni mediji / Dizajn zvuka. Domestic self-financing rate is 125,000 RSD. At €1,800/year for a one-year 60-ECTS master, this is by far the cheapest verified option in this batch.
_rec.facilities: No inventory published. The Academy runs a four-year undergraduate Snimanje i dizajn zvuka line (established 2003) and a separate Muzička produkcija degree, so working studio infrastructure exists.
_rec.fitNotes: Substantially better than previously assessed: entry is explicitly field-neutral (unlike every sibling module), foreign nationals are admitted 'under the same conditions as domestic', it is one year / 60 ECTS, and tuition for foreigners is a confirmed €1,800/year. The electives (Продукција музике за нове медије, Имерзивне игре) are genuinely interesting for him. Two real obstacles remain: he must have a FOUR-YEAR bachelor (240 ECTS) — a 3-year licence disqualifies him — and he must produce documented proof of Serbian-language knowledge plus formal Serbian recognition of his diploma. Content is film/AV-sound-led rather than club/electronic. Worth one concrete e-mail asking for the Dizajn zvuka Informator and whether his specific degree meets the four-year condition.
_rec.verificationNotes: Re-verified from the current official documents, both read in full: the 2026/27 master konkurs 'Текст Конкурса Мастер Докторске 2026' (akademija.uns.ac.rs/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Tekst-Konkursa-Master-Doktorske-2026.pdf, published June 2026) and the official curriculum sheet mas-dizajn-zvuka.pdf. This replaces the prior report's reliance on a 2022/23 konkurs. NEWLY CONFIRMED: 60 ECTS / 1 year; the four-year (240-ECTS) entry condition with NO field restriction for Dizajn zvuka specifically; €1,800/year foreign tuition; 4 budget + 1 self-financing places; October 2026 dates in two rounds; foreign-national requirements (diploma recognition, health insurance, PROOF OF SERBIAN). STILL UNVERIFIED: the entrance-exam content and portfolio spec for this module — the Academy publishes Informators for four other master programmes but not for Dizajn zvuka. The prior report's sourceUrl (/programi/) was replaced with the admissions page, which is where the konkurs actually lives.

If he were ever willing to spend a year on Slovak, this is the cheapest serious Atmos training found — but the first step is a direct email to the Ateliér zvukovej skladby asking (a) whether a non-film, non-music bachelor is admissible and (b) what the entrance exam consists of.

_rec.publicPrivate: PUBLIC — CONFIRMED. Hochschule Luzern is the university of applied sciences and arts of central Switzerland, carried by the six central Swiss cantons under the FH Zentralschweiz concordat (its own site footers as 'FH Zentralschweiz' on every page) and institutionally accredited under the federal HFKG — the footer states 'Institutionell akkreditiert nach HFKG 2019–2026'. _rec.qualification: Master of Arts in Music, Major Music and Digital Creation. 4 semesters, 120 ECTS — CONFIRMED ('A Master's programme comprises 120 ECTS-Credits and typically consists of a Major and a Minor'). A genuine second-cycle Swiss degree.
_rec.focus: MAJOR CORRECTION — THE PREVIOUS RECORD EXAMINED THE WRONG PROGRAMME. It assessed Major Komposition plus electronic minors and concluded the candidate could not clear a conservatory gate. HSLU actually runs a Major MUSIC AND DIGITAL CREATION, launched autumn 2022 jointly by HSLU Musik and HSLU Informatik, built specifically for people coming from computing. Its stated aim (official Studienführer): building 'Information and Communications Technologies' competencies and linking them to musical content, with depth in 'Data Science' and 'Digital Creation'. There are two published curricula — 'Curriculum Major Music and Digital Creation MIT BA Informatik' and 'OHNE BA Informatik' — i.e. the programme is explicitly designed around applicants who already hold a computing bachelor. That is exactly him. The Minor Electronic Music Composition, Minor Groove und Electronics and Minor Media Composer are all confirmed as Master-level minors and can be stacked on top.
_rec.whatYouStudy: Data science and digital creation applied to music; independent development, planning and execution of projects; elective modules in music practice, pedagogy or theory. Stackable Master minors confirmed from the official minors index: Electronic Music Composition, Groove und Electronics, Media Composer, Digitale Kompetenzen für Musik/Bildung/Kultur, Komposition, Jazz, Improvisation, Music Research and 13 others. Teaching is split across Lucerne School of Music (Arsenalstrasse 28a, Luzern-Kriens) and Lucerne School of Computer Science (Campus Zug-Rotkreuz).
_rec.durationEcts: 4 semesters, 120 ECTS, full time — CONFIRMED. NOTE ON THE PREVIOUS RECORD'S 'THEORY PLACEMENT' WARNING: it is real but overstated. The official exam-contents page describes the master 'theory assessment' as something candidates complete only 'under certain conditions', where 'the result determines their PLACEMENT IN THE THEORY MODULES' — a streaming test, not a pass-or-leave gate. Whether he must sit it is 'communicated upon admission to the entrance examination'. Content, if required: two harmonic dictations with secondary dominants and altered chords, a two-part polyphonic dictation, and analysis of a Viennese Classical movement. That is still hard for a self-taught producer and he should prepare for it, but it does not by itself end the application.
_rec.language: GERMAN is the language of instruction at HSLU – Musik. CAVEAT WORTH CHECKING: because this major is co-delivered with HSLU Informatik at Campus Zug-Rotkreuz, part of the data-science content may run in English. Not published — UNVERIFIED. Ask Daniella Gerszt (Studienkoordinatorin Major Music and Digital Creation, +41 41 249 26 05) directly, because the answer materially changes how feasible the first year is for him.
_rec.languageRequirement: MAJOR CORRECTION — THE PREVIOUS RECORD OVERSTATED THIS BADLY. It claimed B1 German must be certified before studies begin. The official admission-requirements page (German original) says the opposite for Master's programmes: 'das Beherrschen der deutschen Sprache (im ersten Studienjahr A2-Niveau, danach B1-Niveau)' — A2 in the FIRST YEAR of study, rising to B1 from the second year. Higher levels apply only to other majors (B2 from the start for Instrumental/Vocal Pedagogy; B1 then B2 for Church Music; C1 from the start for Musiktheorie and Schulmusik II; C1 English from the start for Artistic Research — none of which is his). And 'knowledge of German is not required for the entrance examination'. NO English certificate is required for this major. Practical effect: he can sit the entrance exam with no German, and only needs A2 — a genuinely low bar, a few months of evening classes — during his first year. This turns German from a blocker into an errand.
_rec.entryRequirements: MAJOR CORRECTION, AND THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT FINDING IN THIS RE-CHECK. The official Studienreglement für die Ausbildung (Musik), section on master admission, states: 'Für den Master of Arts in Music, Major Music and Digital Creation gelten, weil es sich um ein interdisziplinäres Angebot in Zusammenarbeit mit der Hochschule Luzern – Informatik handelt, gesonderte Zulassungsvoraussetzungen: a. das Bachelor-Diplom EINER FACHHOCHSCHULE (Sur-Dossier-Aufnahme); b. das Bestehen des Zulassungsverfahrens (Praxis, Theorie, Gespräch), mit dem die Eignung für die musikspezifischen Module abgeklärt wird; c. das Erbringen der für die verschiedenen musikspezifischen Ausrichtungen zusätzlich formulierten Zusatzqualifikationen. Die Voraussetzungen a–c müssen kumulativ erfüllt sein.' The public admission page puts it more simply: 'Für den Major Music and Digital Creation genügt ein an einer Fachhochschule erworbener Bachelor-Abschluss («Sur-Dossier-Aufnahme») – EGAL IN WELCHEM STUDIENGANG' — a UAS bachelor in ANY subject suffices. So NO music degree is required for this major. The previous record's flat 'NO, not realistically' was correct for Major Komposition and wrong for the programme he should actually be looking at. THE ONE REAL UNKNOWN: 'Bachelor-Diplom einer Fachhochschule' means a university-of-applied-sciences diploma. His BSc is from SMU MedTech, a private Tunisian university, not a Swiss-style FH. Whether HSLU treats it as equivalent under the sur-dossier route is THE decision-changing question and must be asked in writing before anything else.
_rec.portfolioSpec: CORRECTED — no conventional portfolio and no score dossier is required for this major (that requirement belongs to Major Komposition, which demands three scores plus recordings, none older than two years). For Music and Digital Creation the official exam-contents page requires: 'At the latest three weeks before the entrance exam, a short description (ONE A4 PAGE) must be submitted outlining a project combining music and computer science that the candidate wishes to realise within the major studies.' That is the entire written submission. For a software engineer with a year to think, this is an extraordinarily low-friction entry document — but it must be a genuinely good idea, because the whole interview turns on it.
_rec.auditionSpec: CORRECTED — no conservatory audition, but not nothing either. Official exam contents, verbatim: 'Candidates with a Bachelor of Arts in Music — Examination interview with the jury on the candidate's project description, expectations of the programme, training content and objectives, and previous knowledge of computer science / IT. Candidates with NO Bachelor of Arts in Music («sur dossier») — PRACTICAL AND THEORETICAL EXAMINATION ADDRESSING THE CANDIDATE'S MUSICAL ORIENTATION, plus examination interview with the jury on the candidate's project description, expectations of the programme, training content and objectives, and previous knowledge of MUSIC.' So he faces a practical and theoretical music examination — but one framed around HIS OWN musical orientation, not a fixed classical repertoire. A serious electronic-production practice, demonstrated live and discussed knowledgeably, is a legitimate answer to it. Ask Daniella Gerszt exactly what the practical part looks like for an electronic-music applicant; this is not published.

_rec.facilities: Not published — UNVERIFIED, and worth pressing on. Ask musik@hslu.ch and Daniella Gerszt for a studio and equipment inventory before applying — for a candidate whose goal is production this matters more than the curriculum text.

_rec.visaEligible: Yes in principle — an accredited Swiss hochschule degree programme supports a student residence permit. But Swiss student permits for non-EU nationals are discretionary, cantonally handled, quota-constrained, and require proof of funds and of intent to leave. He should also expect to need a visa merely to travel to Lucerne for the entrance examination — HSLU states all entrance examinations take place ON SITE, with no published remote option (unlike Kunstuni Linz, which offers Webex). Budget months for this.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: YES FOR THIS MAJOR — REVERSING THE PREVIOUS RECORD'S 'NO'. The Studienreglement grants Major Music and Digital Creation a sur-dossier admission route on the strength of a Fachhochschule bachelor in ANY subject. No music degree, no conservatory bachelor. He must still pass the practical/theoretical music examination and the interview, and satisfy any additional major-specific qualifications, all three cumulatively — but the door is open in a way it is emphatically not for Major Komposition. THE OPEN QUESTION IS INSTITUTIONAL, NOT MUSICAL: does a Tunisian private-university BSc count as 'ein an einer Fachhochschule erworbener Bachelor-Abschluss'?
_rec.recommendation: PROMOTED FROM 'FILE IT, DO NOT CHASE IT' TO A LIVE TARGET — the previous record assessed Major Komposition and reached a verdict that does not apply to the major he should actually pursue. Corrected picture: HSLU's Major Music and Digital Creation is a joint Musik/Informatik master, expressly built for computing graduates, with a published curriculum variant for holders of a computing bachelor, an admission rule that accepts a UAS bachelor in any subject sur dossier, an entrance submission consisting of ONE A4 PAGE describing a music-plus-computing project, German at only A2 in year one, and a standing 28 February deadline that lands inside his planning window. On top of the major he can stack Minor Electronic Music Composition, Minor Groove und Electronics or Minor Media Composer — the closest thing to electronic-music-production training in central Switzerland. THE REAL CAVEATS, and they are why this is B and not A. (1) He must pass a practical AND theoretical music examination as a sur-dossier candidate — soft compared with a composition audition, but not a formality for someone with no training at all; he needs a year of serious, demonstrable practice. (2) The 'Fachhochschule bachelor' wording may not stretch to a Tunisian private university — unresolved and decisive. (3) Cost: ~CHF 7,300 institutional plus Lucerne living costs, the highest in this set, with no funding he is known to qualify for beyond the Swiss Government Excellence Art Scholarships, whose country list must be checked. (4) Entrance exams are on site only, so budget for a separate exam visa. (5) The major leans data science and digital creation, not DJing or record production. THREE EMAILS TO SEND NOW, all free, all decision-changing, to Daniella Gerszt (Studienkoordinatorin, +41 41 249 26 05) and musik@hslu.ch: (a) does a BSc from a private Tunisian university satisfy the 'Bachelor-Diplom einer Fachhochschule' sur-dossier condition; (b) what exactly does the practical and theoretical music examination consist of for an applicant whose musical orientation is electronic production; (c) how much of the major is taught in English at Campus Zug-Rotkreuz. If (a) comes back yes, this becomes his strongest non-Austrian option and he should build the year around the one-page project idea and the practical exam.

_rec.entryRequirements: CONFIRMED verbatim from the official 2025-26 exam guide admission table: ALES Puanı Şartı = 'Aranmaz' (not required); Yabancı Dil Taban Puanı = 'Aranmaz' (not required); Mezuniyet Taban Notu = 2.50/4.00 or 65/100 or 3.1/5.00; Programa Kabul edilen Mezunlar = 'Herhangi bir lisans programından mezun olmak' (graduation from ANY bachelor's programme). _rec.acceptsNonMusic: YES — EXPLICITLY AND CONFIRMED. The official guide states the accepted graduates are 'Herhangi bir lisans programından mezun olmak' — any bachelor's programme whatsoever. A BSc in Software Engineering is formally, unambiguously eligible. This remains the single most important fact about this programme for him. _rec.portfolioSpec: REQUIRED and CONFIRMED in detail. Weighted 10% of the entrance score (dosya değerlendirmesi). The candidate must upload to the designated area on the university site by 23:59 on the closing day, AND hand the jury three (3) printed copies of a file containing: (A) ONE single work he produced himself reflecting his interest/aptitude in the area he intends to study, in sound recording, sound programming, instrument making, sound electronics or acoustics — supplied as (a) a digital copy on CD/DVD/external USB and (b) an explanatory text describing the work's content; (B) a digital copy (CD/DVD/USB) of his other personal works in the field with the associated audio files, software and/or written documents plus an index of those materials; (C) his CV. Scoring, confirmed: Özgeçmiş (CV) 11/11/11 for form/language/content, Alana Ait Özgeçmiş (field-specific CV) 11/11/11, Çalışma Raporu (work report) 11/11/12. Total 100.
_rec.auditionSpec: Two-stage entrance exam, entirely in Turkish — CONFIRMED in full. STAGE I (60% of the entrance score), six assessed areas with exact point weights: Müziksel İşitme (musical ear-training — distinguishing musical elements in a played recording and describing them in technical language) 27 pts; Mesleki İşitme (technical listening — analysing, classifying and describing played sounds) 27 pts; Mesleki Bilgi (professional technical/theoretical knowledge) 9 pts; Problem Çözme 9 pts; Analitik Düşünme 19 pts; Akademik Araştırmaya Yatkınlık 9 pts. For that last component candidates must read IN ADVANCE a named Turkish journal article on determining the acoustic properties of small-scale popular-music production spaces (dergipark.org.tr/tr/download/article-file/203754), answer a question on it in writing in the first part of the exam, then defend that written answer orally. Electronic devices of any kind are banned from the exam. STAGE II (30%): oral examination on the submitted file — Ana Çalışma Yeterliği (command of his main submitted work) 57 pts, Yazılı Sınav Değerlendirmesi (review of his written exam) 28 pts, Genel Değerlendirme 15 pts. ENTRANCE SCORE = 10% file + 60% Stage I + 30% Stage II. PASS MARK 60/100. FINAL RANKING = 70% entrance-exam score + 30% bachelor GPA. Appeals within 2 working days, decided within 3.

_rec.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. ČVUT is a veřejná vysoká škola established under Act No. 111/1998 Sb.; its admission conditions are issued as a dean's decree (příkaz děkana FEL_PD_2025_05_V01) explicitly governed by that Act and the CTU Statute.
_rec.language: TWO PARALLEL TRACKS — this is the key finding. The specialization exists in a CZECH-TAUGHT version (free of charge) and the Electronics and Communications master's is ALSO delivered in ENGLISH (fee-paying), with the faculty's English programme page confirming the audiovisual technology and signal processing content among its seven specializations. _rec.languageRequirement: For the English track: proof of English knowledge, assessed by the admissions committee, with a certificate required if the applicant is not a native speaker — NO named IELTS/TOEFL band is set in the dean's decree, the committee judges it. _rec.qualification: Ing. (inženýr) — a real, state-recognised second-cycle engineering degree.
_rec.accreditationStatus: Nationally accredited public university programme (NAÚ). Supports a Czech long-term residence permit for study.

_rec.focus: Engineering of audiovisual signals — acoustics, sound and image technology, signal processing — with the human perceiver as the organising principle. NOT a creative sound-design or music-production degree.
_rec.whatYouStudy: Sensing, processing and reproduction of audiovisual signals; practical acoustic design and measurement; image and sound technology; modern methods of processing, compression and reconstruction of image, sound and other signals; explicit orientation toward 'the human as recipient of audiovisual information'. Graduates go into television and radio operations, audiovisual and acoustics design, automotive, and biomedical applications. Specialization guarantor: prof. Petr Páta (pata@fel.cvut.cz).
_rec.entryRequirements: A completed bachelor's degree, evidenced before enrolment. Entrance examination consists of an ONLINE INTERVIEW plus an optional test if the admissions committee decides to set one — for the English track. Documents required: transcript of results, English certificate (if not a native speaker), and a MOTIVATION LETTER. Documents not in Czech, Slovak or English need a certified translation. Nostrification (recognition) of the foreign higher-education qualification must be completed by the end of October of the first semester — the application itself does not require it up front, which materially lowers the barrier at application time.
_rec.portfolioSpec: NONE. No portfolio, no creative dossier, no artistic assessment. Applicants are merely 'recommended' to submit evidence of significant personal achievements or professional/academic excellence in electrical engineering, informatics, mathematics or physics — which a software-engineering graduate can supply directly from his degree and projects.
_rec.auditionSpec: None. There is no audition and no musical assessment of any kind.
_rec.equipmentRequired: None.
_rec.facilities: FEL acoustics and audiovisual-technology laboratories at ČVUT Prague; measurement and signal-processing infrastructure rather than creative studios.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: YES — EMPHATICALLY. This is an electrical-engineering faculty programme that actively prefers applicants from electronics, informatics, mathematics or physics. A BSc in Software Engineering is a normal, expected feeder profile. Of every programme in this slice, this is the one where his existing degree is an asset rather than a liability.
_rec.englishTest: No fixed band. The dean's decree requires 'a certificate of English proficiency if the applicant is not a native speaker', with the admissions committee assessing the level — no IELTS/TOEFL minimum is published. He should still sit IELTS Academic (target 6.5) to be safe, but the absence of a hard threshold means a modest score is unlikely to be an automatic bar. UNVERIFIED which certificates the committee accepts — ask the FEL admissions office.
_rec.tuitionEU: 0 CZK for the Czech-taught track (all nationalities). For the English-taught track, EU citizens pay the same fee as everyone else.
_rec.tuitionNonEU: CZECH-TAUGHT TRACK: 0 CZK for a Tunisian national — CTU FEE states plainly that students in Czech-language programmes 'do not incur these costs, regardless of citizenship'. ENGLISH-TAUGHT TRACK: fee-paying — 'All students enrolled in programs taught in English are supposed to pay tuition fees', with the amount depending on the level of study and the faculty reserving the right to adjust it each semester. THE EXACT AMOUNT IS NOT PUBLISHED on the faculty's tuition-fees page and I will not guess it: e-mail the FEL admissions office or the programme guarantor prof. Páta (pata@fel.cvut.cz) and ask for the per-semester fee for the English-taught Electronics and Communications master's for 2027/2028. A secondary source quoted 66,000 CZK/semester for CTU English-taught programmes generally — TREAT AS UNCONFIRMED until the faculty states it.
_rec.otherFees: Application fee 950 CZK per programme AND per specialization — applying to two specializations costs 1,900 CZK. _rec.totalCostEstimate: Czech track: ~500,000-670,000 CZK (~20,000-27,000 EUR) for two years, all of it living costs. English track: add the unpublished tuition — if the unconfirmed 66,000 CZK/semester figure is right, that would add ~264,000 CZK (~10,700 EUR) over the degree.

_rec.recommendation: TOP PICK OF THIS ENTIRE SLICE FOR THIS CANDIDATE. It is the only programme found where every one of his weaknesses is irrelevant: no portfolio, no audition, no music degree, no conservatory training, no fixed IELTS band, and an admissions process that is an online interview plus a motivation letter. His BSc Software Engineering is the preferred feeder. The Czech-taught version costs a Tunisian national nothing; the English-taught version removes the language barrier at an unpublished but probably manageable cost. It is emphatically NOT a DJ or music-production degree — it is audiovisual signal engineering — but it is a credible, fundable, visa-supporting European master's that puts him inside a Prague audio-engineering ecosystem where he can build the production career on the side. Three actions now: (1) e-mail pata@fel.cvut.cz asking whether Audiovizuální technika a zpracování signálů is available in the English track for 2027/2028; (2) ask FEL admissions for the exact English-track fee; (3) start Czech from zero anyway, because the Czech track is free.

_rec.tuitionNonEU: CRITICAL AND NEW. Décret n°2026-385 of 19 May 2026 (part of the 'Choose France for Higher Education' plan), effective 1 September 2026, changes how differentiated fees work at French PUBLIC UNIVERSITIES. Reference amounts (2025-2026 basis; 2026-2027 amounts 'not yet known' per service-public.gouv.fr): LICENCE €2,895/yr vs €178 standard; MASTER €3,941/yr vs €254 standard. EXEMPTION QUOTAS: universities may exempt at most 30% of their non-EU students in 2026-2027, 25% in 2027-2028 (THE CANDIDATE'S ENTRY YEAR), and 20% long-term. Previously universities exempted non-EU students en masse, making the regime largely theoretical; that is no longer safe to assume. Students already exempted keep the exemption to the end of their cycle. Exempt by right: EU/EEA/Swiss nationals, Canadians resident in Quebec, students enrolled since 2018/2019, doctoral students, holders of a French government scholarship (bourse du gouvernement français), refugees/subsidiary protection, legal French residents. A TUNISIAN IS NOT EXEMPT BY RIGHT. IMPORTANT: this regime targets universities; Ministry-of-Culture establishments (CNSMD Paris/Lyon, ENSATT, ENS Louis-Lumière, Le Fresnoy, écoles nationales supérieures d'art) charge their own low flat fees (€300–€760/yr observed) and no differentiated non-EU rate was found for them.
_rec.otherFees: CVEC approx. €105/yr at French institutions. Campus France Tunisie procedure fee: 400 TND to validate the application file.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: Budget approx. €4,000/yr in tuition for a public UNIVERSITY master vs approx. €300–800/yr for a Ministry-of-Culture school. This is the single biggest cost variable in this sweep and it points the candidate towards the Culture-ministry schools and Belgium.

Crucial nuance, confirmed verbatim: for bachelor's and master's programmes generally (Gymnasiallehramt, Musikpädagogik and Musikwissenschaft excepted), the B2 certificate must be produced 'vor Ablauf der Rückmeldefrist für das dritte Fachsemester' — i.e. by the re-registration deadline for the THIRD semester, not at application. Semesters 1–2 centre on the applicant's own project, supported by design-research seminars, individual supervision (mostly remote) and up to four subject-specific workshops per semester with external experts, plus one smaller interdisciplinary project with students from the other part-time masters. From semester 3 the master's project takes over (it may but need not build on the first-year work). The page is unusually blunt about what this is not: 'This is not music production. Bei Audio Experience Design gestaltest du Klang als Erfahrung, nicht nur Tracks.' and, as a tagline, 'Stop producing. Start designing. Sound ist Material. Sound ist UX'. New programme, first intake October 2026, up to 10 students per year.

Submit: a motivation letter with a chronological account of prior musical and/or design background plus any publications or competition results; certificates (Zeugnisse); the Zulassungsantrag; proof of the transfer (fee payment); further documents per the Zulassungsantrag; and the media materials described below. Baden-Württemberg's LHGebG applies: 'Studiengebühr Internationale Studierende: 1.500 € pro Semester gem. § 3ff LHGebG für Studierende aus Ländern außerhalb der EU / des EWR ohne inländische Hochschulzulassungsberechtigung ... für alle Bachelor- und konsekutiven Master-Studiengänge'. Over four semesters that is €6,000, plus Verwaltungskostenbeitrag €80.00 and Studierendenwerksbeitrag €58.60 per semester (as of May 2026) — about €6,554 total. Exemptions exist under §§5–7 LHGebG (e.g. permanent domestic residence, spouses/children of EU/EEA nationals) and a waiver 'aufgrund besonderer Begabung gemäß § 6 Abs. 4 LHGebG' is possible on application; waiver applications are due 21 January / 21 June for the following semester.

A special-talent tuition waiver under § 6 Abs. 4 LHGebG is the one real lever. _rec.fitNotes: The entry process is the friendliest anywhere in this batch — computer science named as a welcome background, no on-site exam, a 15-minute video interview, up to seven free-form works, and a German requirement he can defer to his second year. But almost everything after entry works against him. The school itself says 'This is not music production' and 'Stop producing. Start designing' — the deliverable is audio UX and design research, not tracks. It is 50% part-time and only 60 ECTS, which is a serious problem for a Tunisian national: German study visas and residence permits are premised on full-time study, so the part-time structure puts the whole immigration basis in doubt and should be checked with the German embassy before anything else. As a non-EU student he pays €1,500 per semester (about €6,554 all-in over two years) with no institutional funding and DAAD effectively off the table. And Trossingen is a village in rural Baden-Württemberg, roughly the opposite of a DJ's environment. Pursue only if he genuinely wants to become a sound designer for interfaces, installations and spatial experiences — and only after the visa question is answered.
