_rec.auditionSpec: Six-part entrance examination, CONFIRMED: (1) presentation of a portfolio — mandatory, uploaded via Dropbox at least one week before the practical exams; (2) practical analysis of electroacoustic repertoire using DAW software and headphones, with analysis tools such as Acousmographe permitted; (3) a test of knowledge in mathematics, informatics, music informatics and electroacoustics, including programming in Max, PureData, Csound or SuperCollider — explicitly 'NON CONDIZIONANTE' (non-binding), so it informs placement rather than gating entry; (4) a motivational interview covering general knowledge of electronic music; (5) a practical composition test, 'SOLO PER I CANDIDATI CHE NON PROVENGONO DA CORSI DI MUSICA ELETTRONICA A INDIRIZZO COMPOSITIVO', consisting of building a short electroacoustic piece from assigned samples — this WOULD apply to him; (6) the Italian language test, only for foreign-nationality candidates. Nothing here assumes conservatoire performance ability.
_rec.portfolioSpec: MAJOR CORRECTION, AND THE MOST IMPORTANT FINDING OF THIS ENTIRE RE-CHECK. The official page does not ask for a 'portfolio compositivo' as previously recorded. It asks for 'un portfolio di composizioni E/O lavori di carattere tecnico-scientifico' — a portfolio of compositions AND/OR WORKS OF A TECHNICAL-SCIENTIFIC CHARACTER. Technical and scientific work is an accepted alternative to composition, not a supplement to it. That single conjunction transforms this programme for a software engineer with no music degree: an audio DSP library, a spatialisation engine, a synthesis tool, a machine-listening project or a published technical write-up can carry the portfolio. Uploaded by Dropbox at least one week before the practical exams. The previous instruction to build 'original electroacoustic works, not DJ mixes' was directionally right about DJ mixes but wrong to exclude the technical route, which is where his actual advantage lies.
_rec.equipmentRequired: The analysis exam uses DAW software and headphones; whether these are supplied or brought is UNVERIFIED — bring his own headphones. A personal laptop with a DAW is effectively assumed, and familiarity with at least one of Max, PureData, Csound or SuperCollider should be treated as required preparation given the technical test.

_rec.tuitionEU: CONFIRMED on the official fee page. Contributo onnicomprensivo annuale of €2,300 for most schools, Triennio and Biennio alike, but €2,500 specifically for Musica Elettronica and Direzione d'Orchestra. Paid in three instalments: first €156.00 (tassa EDISU + marca da bollo) between 20 May and 10 June; second by 30 December; third by 15 March, this last calculated against certified ISEE documentation. A 30% reduction applies to part-time enrolment. Late payment incurs a €60.00 surcharge. Payments run through PagoPA.
_rec.tuitionNonEU: €3,500 PER YEAR — THE RATE HE WOULD PAY, CONFIRMED on the official fee page as the contributo onnicomprensivo annuale for extra-UE students not resident in Italy. Over two years: €7,000. It follows the same three-instalment schedule with €156 due first. This flat rate appears to be charged instead of the ISEE-scaled system that applies to EU and Italy-resident students — the official page presents ISEE certification as governing the third instalment for the ordinary regime while stating a single figure for extra-UE non-residents. Whether an ISEE parificato can nonetheless reduce it is UNVERIFIED and worth one email, because a yes would save €5,000 over two years. Torino remains the most expensive Italian conservatoire in this sweep and the one where the low-income route is least clearly available.

_rec.totalCostEstimate: Approximately €7,000 tuition over two years, plus roughly €312 in EDISU and bollo, plus Turin living costs of roughly €800–1,100/month — Turin is among the cheaper large Italian cities. Two-year all-in approximately €27,000–34,000 before any scholarship. An EDISU Piemonte award would cut this substantially.

A typical Tunisian family income should place him in the lowest bracket. The bando normally opens in the summer preceding the academic year. _rec.recommendation: APPLY — and this now rates higher than in the previous sweep because of one verified phrase. The portfolio requirement is 'un portfolio di composizioni e/o lavori di carattere tecnico-scientifico': technical-scientific work is an accepted alternative, not a supplement. That means his software-engineering output — a DSP library, a synthesis or spatialisation tool, a machine-listening project, a game-audio engine — can carry the single most important element of the application, alongside original electronic pieces rather than instead of a music degree he does not have. Combined with an entry requirement that explicitly accepts a foreign triennale, a non-binding technical test, and a sample-based composition task aimed precisely at candidates like him, this is the clearest path in the set. Three actions in the portfolio year: (1) Italian to a tested B2, fastest of any language option available to him; (2) build a dual portfolio — three or four original electroacoustic pieces PLUS two documented technical-scientific audio projects, and get fluent in Max or SuperCollider since the technical test names them; (3) map the Universitaly pre-enrolment calendar in autumn 2026 and verify the non-EU contingent for Musica Elettronica, because a tiny quota can close an otherwise open programme. Note honestly that this is an electroacoustic composition and music-informatics degree, not a route to commercial dance-music production — it would make him an excellent audio programmer and sound designer, and a technically formidable producer, but the DJ career would be built alongside it, not by it.

_rec.program: Arta sunetului de film (Film Sound Art) — master
_rec.university: UNATC 'I.L. Caragiale' — National University of Theatre and Cinematography, Faculty of Film
_rec.institutionType: Public national arts university (film and theatre school)
_rec.degree: Master (2nd cycle), full-time (IF), domain Cinematografie și media
_rec.focus: Film & Game Sound; Sound Design; Foley; Multichannel / immersive mixing
_rec.language: Romanian. Confirmed: Arta sunetului de film is NOT among UNATC's English-taught Film Faculty masters, which per the 2026-2027 fee schedule are Design for New Media, Visual Effects, Audiovisual Preservation and Programming, Interactive Technologies for Performing and Media Arts, and Art of Game Design.
_rec.durationEcts: 2 years / 4 semesters / 120 credits — confirmed on the official admission page.
_rec.whatYouStudy: Year 1: Sound Design; Sound Capture and Editing; Foley Art; Research and Creative Cinematography Workshop; Internship and Practice. Year 2: Advanced Sound Design; Film Sound Production/Post-production; Multichannel Mixing; Research and Creative Cinematography Workshop; Internship and Practice; Dissertation. Master's students concentrate on recording and processing sound for film, games and virtual reality, working on real fiction, documentary and animation productions in collaboration with the directing, cinematography and editing departments. The admission page names the DAWs in scope: ProTools, Nuendo, Reaper, Adobe Audition, Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve.
_rec.portfolioSpec: CONFIRMED verbatim. The dossier must contain a CV in EuroPass format and 'un portofoliu ce va conține lucrări artistice cu design sonor realizat de către candidat' (a portfolio containing artistic works with sound design created by the candidate), which may include digital copies of films or relevant sound-design projects. In addition the candidate must bring to the oral exam the DAW PROJECT FILE for one portfolio work of their own choosing, in ProTools, Nuendo, Reaper, Adobe Audition, Premiere Pro or DaVinci Resolve. No minimum or maximum number of works and no duration requirement is published. Portfolios are uploaded electronically through the 2BitsEDU / Edubits candidate platform after registration.
_rec.auditionSpec: On-site, one evaluation stage in two parts. Proba 1 (written): film-culture exam based on a set bibliography, plus technical knowledge of sound design. Proba 2 (oral/colloquium): presentation and discussion of one self-selected portfolio work, with a live DAW project demonstration. Each part scored 1-10; tiebreaker is Proba 2 then Proba 1. Minimum passing grade 6.0/10. No live musical performance.
_rec.entryRequirements: Completion of 'o specializare cu 180 credite sau 240 credite' — a study programme worth 180 or 240 credits, with NO field of study specified. A three-year Tunisian licence in software engineering (180 ECTS) satisfies this. HARD CONSTRAINT FOR HIM: UNATC's own admission pages state that foreign citizens must complete 'anul pregătitor de limba română' — the Romanian language preparatory year — BEFORE sitting the admission exams. Exemptions apply only to candidates who present Romanian educational credentials, prove at least four consecutive years of study in Romanian, or hold a minimum B1 certificate from an accredited Romanian institution or cultural organisation. Registration is exclusively via the 2BitsEDU online platform. Places: 3 state-funded (buget) + 3 tuition-based (taxă) for the 2026 cycle.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: YES — unambiguously. Published eligibility is purely credit-based: 'absolvit o specializare cu 180 credite sau 240 credite', with no discipline named. There is no music-degree requirement, no theory exam, and no audition. The written exam tests film culture and sound-design technical knowledge, both of which are learnable from a bibliography. This is the most open eligibility rule in the slice.
_rec.deadline: CURRENT CYCLE (September 2026 entry) — NOT his target, and currently OPEN. 2026 cycle: registration 4 August - 9 September 2026; file verification 10-11 September 2026; exam period 15-20 September 2026. The 2027 calendar is NOT YET PUBLISHED — expect the same August-to-September 2027 pattern. Note a separate, earlier May-to-July pre-registration window applies to the English-taught masters (for 2026: 1 May - 1 July 2026), which does not cover this programme.
_rec.applicationOpens: CURRENT CYCLE: 4 August 2026. 2027 window unpublished; expect early August 2027.
_rec.scholarship: Romanian Government scholarships administered through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MAE), open specifically to non-EU citizens — Tunisia qualifies. Applications are made through scholarships.studyinromania.gov.ro. Eligibility confirmed on that portal: 'good results in education, respectively an average of the study years, for the last graduated school, of at least 7 (seven)' or an equivalent 'Good'. Excluded categories include persons of Romanian origin, those seeking protection in Romania, stateless persons, diplomatic staff, international-organisation employees, and existing state scholarship holders.
_rec.fundingLevel: Full if the Romanian Government / MAE scholarship is awarded; plus 3 domestic tuition-free 'buget' places at programme level (competitive and normally taken by Romanian candidates).
_rec.stipend: PARTIAL, and the prior record over-promised. Confirmed on studyinromania.gov.ro: the scholarship covers tuition, and provides free preparatory Romanian language instruction for those lacking proficiency (exemptions for prior Romanian-language education or a certified B1). Master's-level study is 'only in Romanian'. IMPORTANT CORRECTION: the portal states the scholarship does NOT cover 'personal expenses and international transport', and that accommodation in university dormitories remains the student's responsibility. The exact monthly stipend figure in lei for master's level could not be retrieved — UNVERIFIED. Do not assume airfare or free housing.
_rec.tuitionIntl: NOW VERIFIED for the taxă place. UNATC Senate Decision 290/2026, annexed fee schedule 'TAXE DE STUDII – CICLUL II – STUDII UNIVERSITARE DE MASTERAT, studenți înmatriculați în anul I începând cu anul univ. 2026-2027': Arta sunetului de film = 13,750 lei per year (roughly 2,750 EUR). By comparison the same schedule prices Producție de film and Conținut și producție TV at 10,000 lei and Scenaristică and Filmologie at 6,875 lei. The schedule contains NO separate euro-denominated rate for foreign citizens — a distinct non-EU 'own funds' fee may be set by ministerial order and is UNVERIFIED. Contact secretariat@unatc.ro or study@unatc.ro.
_rec.facilities: UNVERIFIED in detail — no equipment inventory is published. The curriculum implies a Foley stage and multichannel mixing rooms, and the department confirms students work on live fiction, documentary and animation productions alongside the directing, cinematography and editing departments, building professional portfolios. 13 specialised teaching staff. The admission page's named DAW list (ProTools, Nuendo, Reaper, Adobe Audition, Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve) indicates the toolchain in use.
_rec.fitNotes: The most open door in the slice on paper — eligibility is purely 180 or 240 credits with no subject restriction, there is no music-theory exam and no audition, and the oral exam rewards demonstrable DAW craft over conservatory training. A government scholarship route exists that covers tuition and a free Romanian language year. Two things keep it off the top spot. First, timing: as a non-EU citizen he must complete the Romanian preparatory year BEFORE he can sit the admission exams, so a September 2027 target realistically means starting the prep year in 2027 and entering the master in 2028 — unless he obtains a B1 Romanian certificate independently. Second, direction: this is film, game and VR sound with Foley and picture-locked mixing, not club music production or DJing. It would make him an excellent sound designer with a bankable post-production skill, but it does not advance the DJ half of his ambition, and he currently has no sound-design-to-picture work to put in the portfolio.
_rec.verificationNotes: Confirmed against https://admitere.unatc.ro/arta-sunetului-de-film/ (2 years, 120 credits, Romanian, 180/240-credit eligibility with no field named, 3 buget + 3 taxă places, EuroPass CV plus sound-design portfolio, DAW project file at the oral exam with the named software list, two-part exam with 6.0/10 pass mark and the tiebreaker rule, and the 4 August - 9 September 2026 / 10-11 September / 15-20 September 2026 calendar), https://admitere.unatc.ro/ and the non-EU film-masters admission page (Romanian preparatory year required before admission testing, B1 exemption rules, English-taught alternatives), UNATC Senate Decision 290/2026 fee annex (Arta sunetului de film 13,750 lei/year for students enrolling in year I from 2026-2027; confirmed the annex contains no euro or foreign-citizen rate), and studyinromania.gov.ro plus scholarships.studyinromania.gov.ro for the MAE scholarship (non-EU eligibility, exclusions, master's taught only in Romanian, free preparatory language year, minimum average of 7). Corrections to the prior record: tuition is now a confirmed figure rather than unverified; the scholarship does NOT cover international transport and does not guarantee accommodation, contradicting the earlier claim of covered housing and airfare; the preparatory-year requirement is a pre-condition for sitting the exams, not merely an entry condition to be satisfied later. _rec.whatYouStudy: CONFIRMED verbatim from the official accredited curriculum table 5.1b. Compulsory: MA701 Žanrovska analiza i sinteza video igara (2+4, 12 ECTS); MA703 Studije video igara (2+0, 4 ECTS); MP2102 Grafičke komunikacije u interaktivnim medijima (2+1, 6 ECTS); MA7002 Imerzivne igre / Immersive Games (2+2, 6 ECTS); MAZRD Završni rad (12 ECTS); MAZRI Završni rad – istraživanje (12 ECTS). Electives MAIZ1, 12 ECTS chosen from — and this is where all the audio content lives: MSMIM Muzika u medijima (6); MA1002 Audiovizuelna artikulacija (6); MA1003 Zvuk u filmskoj umetnosti (6); MA2002 Postprodukcija filmske slike (6); MA4003 Produkcija muzike za nove medije (6); MLVIA Video art (6). Hard ceiling: at most 12 of the 60 ECTS can be audio, and only two of those courses (Muzika u medijima, Produkcija muzike za nove medije) are music-production-adjacent.
_rec.entryRequirements: CONFIRMED — clean, permissive, and identical in both official documents, with no contradiction (unlike Music Production). Konkurs §2, programme clause: 'Студијски програм – Дизајн видео игара: завршене основне академске студије у четворогодишњем трајању' — a four-year bachelor, full stop, with NO artistic-field restriction. Informator: 'лица која су завршила основне академске студије у четворогодишњем трајању (240 ЕСПБ)'. The 240-ECTS / four-year rule is the binding gate: konkurs §2.2 permits 180 ECTS only for Konzervacija i restauracija, the Guitar/Performing Arts joint programme, Kreiranje serija and Pozorišni oblici modul Lutkarstvo — Dizajn video igara is NOT among them, so a Tunisian three-year 180-ECTS licence is ineligible here too. Foreign nationals additionally file the diploma-recognition decision, health-insurance proof and Serbian-language proof.
_rec.portfolioSpec: CONFIRMED and EXPANDED. Informator required documents: diploma or certificate of a four-year 240-ECTS bachelor; CV; motivation letter; scanned/read ID; photo 1200x800 px JPG under 1 MB; proof of application-fee payment. Separately 'uz prijavu kandidati prilažu': (1) an EXPLICATION of the artistic-research project the candidate plans to realise as the master's thesis; (2) a motivation letter; (3) a PORTFOLIO of the candidate's previous works IN THE FIELD OF VIDEO GAME DESIGN. Additionally required by konkurs §5 and omitted from the previous record: the completed prijavni list and the uverenje o položenim ispitima (transcript). Confirmed: NO medical certificate and NO audiogram is demanded here, unlike Music Production. Submission electronic to aunsprijemni.dramski@uns.ac.rs, one e-mail, 12 MB total, files named with the candidate's name.
_rec.auditionSpec: CONFIRMED verbatim. Two stages. PART ONE (pass/fail): test of knowledge of the history and aesthetics of video games; a combined test of creative solution of design tasks; analysis of the submitted entry work plus interview with the commission. Those who pass proceed to multi-day exercises and PART TWO: assessment of works submitted with the application up to 25 points; practical work in video game design up to 25 points; oral examination in the professional-artistic field of video game design (commission interview) up to 30 points. BA grade average adds up to 20 points on the same scale as Music Production. Under 50 total points = fail, no ranking. Conducted in Serbian.
_rec.equipmentRequired: Practical exam work is done at the Academy; no personal equipment requirement published. The real requirement is a demonstrable body of game-design work.
_rec.facilities: Not published — UNVERIFIED, unchanged. The compulsory MA7002 Imerzivne igre course implies some interactive/VR capability but nothing is documented. Ask Katedra za audiovizuelne medije.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: YES — explicitly and unambiguously, in both the konkurs and the informator. Any four-year 240-ECTS bachelor in any field qualifies; there is no artistic-field restriction. A nationally registered accredited MAS (NAT entry 92) at a state university, delivered in person, which is the category supporting a Serbian temporary residence permit for education. Tunisian nationals need a long-stay visa D first. Document lists, fees and timelines are not published by the Academy — UNVERIFIED; authoritative sources are the Serbian MUP and the Serbian embassy accredited to Tunisia. _rec.applicationOpens: 2026/27 konkurs published 29 May 2026; informator posted July 2026. Expect the 2027/28 equivalents around May–July 2027 — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. The informator itself defers the Drama Department dates to the Academy website.

FIRST ROUND: electronic application 05.10.2026; entrance exam 07–13.10.2026; preliminary list 15.10.2026; final list and enrolment 20.10.2026. SECOND ROUND: electronic application 21.10.2026; entrance exam 23–28.10.2026; preliminary list 30.10.2026; final list and enrolment 03.11.2026. Applications close in early October of the year of entry; appeals within 24 hours of the preliminary list.
_rec.recommendation: Everything the previous record said about this programme checks out against the official documents, and the accreditation is now pinned down precisely (NAT register, accredited 05.11.2024, intake 10). It remains the only programme in the Novi Sad sweep whose published entry rule admits ANY four-year bachelor with no artistic-field restriction, and his software-engineering background is directly relevant to the curriculum. But it should not be presented to him as a music option in disguise. Audio is capped at 12 of 60 ECTS and only two of those six electives are production-adjacent; the other 48 ECTS are genre analysis, game studies, graphic communications in interactive media, immersive games and a game-design thesis. It will not make him a DJ or a record producer, and spending 2027–28 on it would be a career pivot, not a step toward his stated goal. It also does not solve the two gates that actually block him: the 240-ECTS / four-year first-degree rule applies identically here, and the Serbian-language requirement plus a Serbian-language entrance exam apply identically here. On top of that it demands a video-game-design portfolio he has even less basis to build than an audio one. Report it accurately as what it is: a cheap, accredited, unusually open Serbian master in the wrong subject. It only becomes interesting if he decides he wants to work in games audio and is prepared to learn Serbian.

_rec.institutionType: Public film/drama faculty within the University of Arts
_rec.focus: Recording / Engineering; Film & Game Sound; Sound Design; radio and theatre sound
_rec.language: Serbian
_rec.durationEcts: 1 academic year / 2 semesters. Entry requires a completed undergraduate degree of at least 240 ECTS, so the master is 60 ECTS (total ECTS figure not stated explicitly on the pages read).
_rec.whatYouStudy: Core courses: 'Sound Recording and Design for FTV 7 and 8', in which 'students perfect their knowledge in the field of sound recording and post-production for the most complex film and television structures'; and 'Sound Recording and Design for Theater and Radio 7 and 8', covering 'highly esthetic forms of radio creativity such as musique concrète' and stage sound design. Additional artistic courses in classical and popular music recording, plus sound design in multimedia, and elective theoretical and artistic courses. The department has 9 full professors plus associate professors; 8 of its 11 teachers are graduates of the department itself.
_rec.portfolioSpec: EXACT: 'portfolio — pregled do tri reprezentativna samostalna autorska rada u minimalnom ukupnom trajanju od 10 minuta' — a portfolio reviewing UP TO THREE representative independent authored works with a MINIMUM TOTAL DURATION OF 10 MINUTES, drawn from domains including film sound design, television/streaming audio, radio production, live event sound design, creative music production, or video game / interactive audio design. Submitted with detailed PDF documentation. Also required: a motivation letter of maximum two A4 pages, 1.5 line spacing, font size 12, in Latin or Cyrillic script; a professional biography; a certified copy of the undergraduate diploma with average grade; proof of the 8,000 RSD application fee; and a health certificate INCLUDING AN AUDIOGRAM not older than three months.
_rec.auditionSpec: Yes — on-site entrance exam in three parts: presentation of the candidate's individual authored work in sound design; completion of a practical work during the exam itself; and an interview assessing artistic potential. Scoring out of 100: up to 30 points from prior undergraduate success (average grade × 3) plus up to 70 points for aptitude. Budget-financed admission requires ≥80 points; self-financed requires ≥60 points.
_rec.entryRequirements: Completed undergraduate academic studies with at least 240 ECTS. Serbian-language instruction. Total intake across the 9 specializations of the Dramske i audiovizuelne umetnosti master is up to 92 students (57 budget-financed and 58 self-financed places faculty-wide).
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: PROBABLY NOT — this is the key caution. The department page states: 'A precondition for enrolling M.A. Studies are previously completed undergraduate ARTISTIC academic studies.' Combined with the 240-ECTS floor, a three-year non-artistic BSc in Software Engineering appears to fail on two counts. Verify directly with the faculty before investing effort.
_rec.deadline: 2026/27 CYCLE, NOT 2027 — confirm new date. Registration of candidates 7 and 8 October 2026, 09:00–14:00, at the Faculty Secretariat; entrance examinations 12–13 October 2026. Expect an equivalent early-October 2027 window for a 2027/28 start.
_rec.applicationOpens: 2026/27 cycle: 7 October 2026. 2027/28 dates not yet published.
_rec.scholarship: None found for foreign nationals. Budget-financed (tuition-free) places exist but require ≥80/100 and in practice go to domestic candidates.
_rec.fundingLevel: None found for a non-EU foreign applicant (budget places are effectively domestic)
_rec.tuitionIntl: 2026/27 self-financing rates for Snimanje i dizajn zvuka: 440,000 RSD for Serbian citizens; 550,000 RSD for foreign students from neighbouring countries; 660,000 RSD for other foreign students (roughly €5,600). Application fee 8,000 RSD.
_rec.facilities: UNVERIFIED — no studio inventory published on the pages read. Strong regional reputation as the main Serbian film-sound school; teaching staff are almost entirely its own alumni working in the industry.
_rec.fitNotes: Technically excellent and genuinely craft-focused, and the portfolio spec is unusually generous in scope — 'creative music production' and 'video game / interactive audio design' are explicitly listed as acceptable domains, so his own tracks could count toward the 10-minute minimum. The blocker is eligibility: the stated precondition of completed undergraduate ARTISTIC studies plus a 240-ECTS floor likely rules out his 180-ECTS engineering BSc. Confirm before anything else; if refused, Novi Sad is the fallback.

_rec.university: Vysoká škola múzických umení v Bratislave (VŠMU), Filmová a televízna fakulta (FTF) — Ateliér zvukovej skladby
_rec.institutionType: Public film and television faculty of a national academy of performing arts
_rec.focus: Film/Game Sound; Sound Design; Immersive Audio; Recording/Engineering
_rec.language: Slovak only. Verified verbatim: "Štúdium sa uskutočňuje iba v slovenskom jazyku."
_rec.durationEcts: 2 years / 4 semestre / 120 ECTS, full-time (denná forma). CONFIRMED on the official programme page.
_rec.whatYouStudy: CONFIRMED named courses on the official page: Mixáž a mastering (Mixing and Mastering); Zvuková tvorba – Audiovizuálna tvorba; Teória filmového zvuku (Film Sound Theory); Hudobná réžia (Music Direction); Zvuková syntéza (Sound Synthesis); plus music recording theory and practice and sound design theory. Master level explicitly targets film sound in surround, Dolby Surround 7.1 and Dolby Atmos, and film music. Official aim (portalvs description): to develop independent creative thinking and the ability to be a full partner in a film or TV crew across preparation, shooting and post-production; the graduate as a "zvukový majster" adapts sound expressive means to a dramaturgical intent, and is also equipped for radio production, classical-music recording, live recording and sound reinforcement, and work in music recording studios.
_rec.entryRequirements: Formal condition is simply a completed bachelor's degree ("Základnou podmienkou prijatia na magisterské štúdium je úspešné ukončenie bakalárskeho štúdia", §56 of the Higher Education Act), with conditional admission possible if the degree is awarded by enrolment day. LANGUAGE CONDITION NOW VERIFIED and lower than expected: "Minimálne kritérium na prijatie zahraničného uchádzača na študijný program uskutočňovaný v slovenskom jazyku, je znalosť slovenského jazyka na úrovni A2 doložená certifikátom" — a Slovak A2 certificate, not B1 or B2. Foreign applicants must also supply a recognition statement (uznávacia doložka) and officially certified, translated copies of prior qualifications. Note the framing caveat: "Magisterské štúdium študijného programu STRIHOVÁ A ZVUKOVÁ SKLADBA nadväzuje na bakalársky študijný program s rovnakým názvom" (the MA follows on from the bachelor programme of the same name). Application via ePrihláška; fee €40 electronic / €60 paper. Approximately 5 places.
_rec.portfolioSpec: Still UNVERIFIED at the level of exact specification — no number of works, duration or format is published. What IS now confirmed: home works must be submitted, and there is a hard upload deadline separate from the application deadline — "Domáce práce k prijímaciemu konaniu je potrebné nahrať podľa zaslaných inštrukcií najneskôr do 12. 6. 2026. Práce zaslané po termíne nebudú akceptované a uchádzač nebude pripustený k prijímaciemu konaniu" (works uploaded after the deadline are not accepted and the applicant is excluded). Instructions are sent individually after the application. Request the prospekt / požiadavky na prijímacie skúšky from the FTF study department (study coordinator Jana Mihoková, jana.mihokova@vsmu.sk, +421 2 2100 6511 ext. 511).
_rec.auditionSpec: On-site entrance examination in Bratislava. Form confirmed on portalvs as: talentová, písomná, ústna, testy (talent, written, oral, tests). Single published exam date — 23 June 2026 in the prior cycle, with home works due 12 June 2026. No remote or online option is published for FTF; the Music and Dance Faculty of the same university runs a different process with an online interview for internationals, but that is a separate faculty and does not apply here. Worth asking the study department directly whether any remote accommodation exists.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: Check, leaning cautiously positive. The published basic condition is only "successful completion of bachelor's study" with NO named field — better than any other programme in this slice. The soft caveat is the statement that the MA "follows on from the bachelor programme of the same name", and the ateliér trains sound masters and sound engineers, so a strong practical portfolio would have to carry the case. No statement anywhere bars a non-music or non-film bachelor. Ask the coordinator directly.
_rec.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Prior cycles: application by 9 April 2025 (2025/26) and 8 April 2026 (2026/27); home works upload by 12 June 2026; entrance exam 23 June 2026. For September 2027 entry expect roughly early April 2027, a mid-June 2027 works deadline and a late-June 2027 exam. Nothing for 2027/28 is published as of July 2026.
_rec.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Via ePrihláška on the FTF VŠMU site; opening date not published. Fee €40 electronic, €60 paper.
_rec.tuitionIntl: €0 per year for full-time study in Slovak within the standard length of study — CONFIRMED: "Ročné školné — Štandardná dĺžka štúdia: bezplatne", and VŠMU states that study in Slovak-language programmes is free, with foreign students treated on the same terms as Slovak ones. Fees apply only in defined cases: exceeding the standard length or parallel study costs €2,150/year at master's level in the arts field for 2025/26 (CORRECTED — the prior record's €1,650 is the BACHELOR-level rate). Programmes delivered in a foreign language cost €4,500/year regardless of nationality, but that does not apply to this Slovak-taught programme.
_rec.scholarship: None found that this programme is eligible for. CRITICAL CORRECTION: the Slovak Ministry's "Scholarships for talented students from all over the world" (scholarships.portalvs.sk) is NOT available here. It is restricted to selected study programmes falling under the Smart Specialisation Strategy SK RIS3 2021+, and VŠMU does not appear anywhere in the official "List of selected smart specialization study programmes SK RIS 3 2021+" (checked directly — zero occurrences of VŠMU, Múzických, zvuk or skladba in the list). The scheme also requires an SAT score of at least 1100 or SCIO tests at the 63rd percentile, and pays €500/month up to €15,000 over two master's years — not the €1,025/month or €10,000 previously recorded, which conflated it with the separate National Scholarship Programme (NSP), a short-term mobility scheme for students already enrolled abroad, not a full-degree award.
_rec.fundingLevel: Partial (tuition-free only). NOT full — no stipend scheme is available to him for this programme.
_rec.stipend: None available. Tuition waiver by default. The €500/month national talent scholarship is closed to VŠMU programmes (not on the SK RIS3 list). The NSP is a mobility grant for stays of 1–10 months, not full degree study. Living costs in Bratislava would be entirely self-funded.
_rec.facilities: Founded 1999. Described on the official page as one of Slovakia's most modern audio complexes and holding DOLBY ATMOS MUSIC STUDIO certification: five sound mixing suites, a cinema hall, professional microphones and field-recording equipment, working from stereo through multichannel for cinema and streaming. A development project upgrades one mixing suite to Dolby Atmos 12.1 and the cinema to Dolby Atmos 39.2. Head: Mgr. art. Tobiáš Potočný, ArtD.; staff include prof. Peter Mojžiš, doc. Dušan Kozák, doc. Marek Piaček. Facilities claims come from the ateliér's own page and were not independently corroborated.
_rec.fitNotes: Still the best facilities-per-euro in the slice — Dolby Atmos Music certified, five mixing suites, 120 ECTS, and genuinely €0 tuition for a Tunisian. The formal entry bar is also the lowest here: any bachelor's degree, plus only Slovak A2 by certificate. But the funding case has collapsed on verification: there is no stipend he can win for this programme, so he would self-fund roughly two years of living costs in Bratislava. Add full instruction in Slovak, an unpublished portfolio spec with a hard June upload cut-off, an on-site June exam, only about 5 places, and a curriculum aimed at film/TV sound and immersive audio rather than club production.
_rec.verificationNotes: Programme confirmed to exist at Mgr. art. level in Bratislava, Slovak-taught, 4 semesters / 120 ECTS. Verified against: the ateliér programme page (sourceUrl) for courses, 120 ECTS, the 8 April 2026 deadline, 23 June 2026 exam and €40 fee; the official portalvs.sk record https://www.portalvs.sk/sk/studijny-program/vsmu-strihova-a-zvukova-skladba2 for the Slovak-only rule, the A2 certificate requirement, the general admission condition, exam form, ~5 places, the 12 June 2026 home-works deadline and free standard-length tuition; VŠMU's fee pages for the €2,150 master's overrun rate and €4,500 foreign-language rate; and the Slovak scholarship portal plus the official SK RIS3 programme list PDF. CORRECTIONS MADE: (1) the scholarship claim is reversed — VŠMU is absent from the SK RIS3 list, so the national talent scholarship is unavailable, and its terms are €500/month up to €15,000 with an SAT/SCIO test requirement, not €1,025/month and €10,000; funding therefore drops from 'potentially Full' to Partial; (2) a previously unrecorded Slovak A2 certificate requirement for foreign applicants is now documented, along with the uznávacia doložka and translation requirements; (3) the overrun fee is €2,150 at master's level, not €1,650; (4) a separate hard home-works upload deadline (12 June in the prior cycle) is now documented, distinct from the application deadline; (5) ~5 places and the caveat that the MA follows the same-named bachelor are now recorded. STILL UNVERIFIED: the exact portfolio specification; whether any remote exam option exists at FTF; the ateliér's Dolby Atmos certification and suite count beyond its own page.

_rec.institutionType: Private university (Catholic, private, Murcia) — a fully recognised Spanish private university.
_rec.qualification: TÍTULO PROPIO — specifically a 'Máster de Formación Permanente', 60 ECTS. VERIFIED on both the official programme page and the official UCAM brochure PDF. This is UCAM's OWN diploma. It is NOT an official Máster Universitario, does not appear in the RUCT catalogue of official degrees, and does not give direct access to a Spanish doctorate.
_rec.accreditationStatus: NOT OFFICIAL AS A DEGREE. It is a título propio / Máster de Formación Permanente issued by UCAM under its own authority. The INSTITUTION is legitimate — UCAM is a recognised Spanish private university listed in RUCT and legally entitled to issue títulos propios under art. 7 of Ley Orgánica 2/2023. But THIS AWARD is not ANECA-verified and is legally a university certificate, not an official master's degree. In practice: credible and university-branded with genuine industry weight, but it will not be treated as a master's degree by a foreign ministry, a public-sector employer or a doctoral programme.
_rec.visaEligible: HIGH RISK — probably NOT, on the verified schedule. This is the decisive finding and it corrects the prior reasoning in both directions. First, the good news: Spain's official management criteria for student authorisations (Ministerio de Inclusión, June 2025, under RD 1155/2024) state explicitly that for higher education 'existen los títulos oficiales y los títulos propios. Ambos son admisibles para la obtención de una autorización de estancia por estudios' — and universities are named as centres entitled to offer them. So being a título propio is NOT itself disqualifying, contrary to the earlier assumption. Semipresencial delivery is also permitted, provided at least 50% of the programme is taught in person. Now the bad news, which is decisive. The same criteria set a weekly teaching load of 'un mínimo de 20 horas semanales' as the general rule, with an exception for intensive or concentrated programmes only where the applicant can justify that 'al menos 12 horas son presenciales' with the remainder being assessed coursework. UCAM's own official brochure publishes the timetable: Fridays 16:30–20:30 and Saturdays 09:30–13:30 and 15:30–19:30 — a total of 12 contact hours per week, delivered at weekends, in a SEMIPRESENCIAL format meaning not all 12 are in person. That falls far below the 20-hour general rule and sits exactly at, and realistically below, the 12-in-person-hour exception floor. The 50%-in-person test is also unverified and doubtful for a weekend hybrid course. CONCLUSION: he must not assume this supports a residence permit. He must obtain written confirmation from UCAM's international office, stating the in-person percentage and weekly presencial hours, before paying anything. On the published evidence the answer is likely to be no.
_rec.focus: Music production: composition techniques, production, artistic development, recording, mixing and mastering.
_rec.whatYouStudy: VERIFIED module structure and credit weights from the official brochure: I. Herramientas de trabajo para la producción musical (13.2 ECTS); II. Note the shape: only 34 ECTS is taught content — 26 ECTS, well over a third, is final project plus work placement. Stated career outcomes: productor musical, técnico especialista en mezcla, técnico de mastering, técnico asistente en estudio de grabación. Graduates receive official Steinberg Cubase professional certification, and a Cubase licence is included in the materials.

Named teaching producers, verified: Ludovico Vagnone, Antonio Escobar, Ed Is Dead, Pablo Rous, Baghira and Luis del Toro. _rec.reputationSignals: Genuine industry partnership with Sony Music España; recognised Spanish producers on the teaching staff, with Ed Is Dead and Baghira being real names in Spanish electronic music; Steinberg Cubase certification is a concrete, verifiable, portable credential. The brochure name-checks Bizarrap, Baghira, Pablo Rous, Zef, Marz and Dani Ruiz as the model of the modern producer the course is aimed at, which is well aligned with his ambition. UCAM absorbed its older 'Máster en Ingeniería de Sonido y Producción Discográfica' into this programme, so any listing of that older master should be treated as superseded. RED FLAGS: only 12 places; the award is a certificate, not a degree; the timetable is weekend-only at 12 contact hours per week; over a third of the credits are TFM plus work placement rather than taught content; and the visa position is weak.
_rec.recommendation: On paper the best value in this slice by an enormous margin — EUR 4,194.12 all-in, verified to the cent, for a 60-ECTS university-branded music production master with Sony Music España involvement, named Spanish electronic producers teaching, an included Cubase licence and Steinberg certification. His software-engineering degree is named explicitly as a welcome entry profile, no portfolio is demanded, no IELTS is needed, foreign degrees are accepted without homologation, and it starts in September, matching his target. If he were already living legally in Spain, this would be the clear recommendation. But he is not, and that is where it breaks. THREE ISSUES, in order of severity. (1) THE VISA. I verified Spain's actual rules rather than assuming: títulos propios ARE admissible for a student authorisation, which is better than feared — but the binding constraint is the teaching load, and UCAM's own brochure publishes a weekend-only timetable of 12 contact hours per week in a semipresencial format. The requirement is 20 hours per week, or at minimum 12 hours that are genuinely in person for concentrated programmes, plus at least 50% in-person delivery overall. This programme sits at or below that floor. On the published evidence it likely does NOT support a student residence permit. (2) LANGUAGE. It is taught entirely in Spanish, including a 16-ECTS final project. (3) THE AWARD is a certificate, not a degree — acceptable for industry, worthless for a future PhD or any title-dependent role. VERDICT: outstanding return on euro, but probably not a relocation route. ACTION: before anything else, email UCAM's international office and ask three specific questions in writing — what percentage of the programme is delivered in person, how many presencial hours per week, and has UCAM successfully supported non-EU students onto a student visa for THIS programme. If the answers are weak, this option is worth nothing to him as a route to Europe, however cheap it is.

Also extracted and read the Spanish Ministerio de Inclusión 'Criterios de gestión sobre autorizaciones de estancia por estudios' (signed 23 June 2025, under RD 1155/2024) directly from the PDF, plus Instrucción SEM 3/2025. ALL MONEY CONFIRMED EXACTLY: EUR 3,900 tuition, EUR 235 pre-enrolment, EUR 59.12 school insurance — total EUR 4,194.12. Award confirmed as Máster de Formación Permanente (título propio), 60 ECTS, semipresencial, 12 places, Murcia. NEWLY VERIFIED AND DECISIVE: the September start; the three-cuatrimestre calendar (Sept-Dec, Jan-Apr, May-Jul); the exact class timetable of Fridays 16:30–20:30 plus Saturdays 09:30–13:30 and 15:30–19:30, i.e. 12 contact hours per week; the full module credit breakdown showing 16 ECTS TFM and 10 ECTS work placement; the verbatim entry-profile sentence naming 'Ingenierías en Telecomunicaciones e Informática'; the no-homologation provision for foreign degrees; and the full named teaching roster. Rating lowered to C on that basis despite the excellent price and content fit. STILL UNVERIFIED: in-person percentage, Spanish level required, portfolio requirement, scholarships, 2027 dates.

_rec.scholarships: CONFIRMED ROUTE, AND BETTER THAN IT FIRST APPEARS. Because CPM is an AFAM institution, its Diploma Accademico students are eligible for the LOMBARDY REGIONAL DSU right-to-study scholarship (Legge Regionale Lombardia 33/2004), awarded by competition on combined merit and income criteria, with the amount varying by ISEE band and by the student's geographic origin — out-of-region and international students receive the highest bracket because they are classed as 'fuori sede'. Non-EU students are not excluded from DSU in principle, but they must produce home-country income documentation to obtain an ISEE parificato. CPM does not state non-EU eligibility explicitly (contact borsedistudio@cpm.it). Awards are paid at the end of the academic year, so they do not reduce the up-front cash needed.
_rec.visaEligible: YES in principle — a MUR-authorised AFAM institution awarding an official second-level diploma, so Universitaly pre-enrolment and a type-D national study visa apply. The legal basis is sound; the institutional support for a non-EU applicant is thin. Get the procedure in writing before relying on it.

Two-year total €22,984 to €29,586 in tuition and fees, plus Milan living costs of roughly €10,000–14,000 per year. THE ISEE TRAP IS REAL: a non-EU applicant who does not go through a CAF to obtain an ISEE parificato using Tunisian income documents will be charged the TOP band by default. A Tunisian household income will usually place him in band 1 once that paperwork is done — a difference of about €6,600 over two years. Do the ISEE parificato.
_rec.reputationSignals: Founded 1984 by Franco Mussida (PFM); among the best-known contemporary-music schools in Italy. Alumni named by the school include Mahmood, Tananai, Chiara Galiazzo, producer Francesco Fugazza, sound artist Francesco Fabris, arranger Alberto Cipolla. Faculty includes Lorenzo Cazzaniga, Taketo Gohara, Paolo Jannacci. Genuine industry embedding and real AFAM status. Pricing transparency is in fact GOOD — the earlier concern that fees were hidden was wrong; full ISEE-banded figures are published per course. Remaining red flag: no international-student infrastructure at all.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: EFFECTIVELY NO. The formal requirement is any first-level degree 'o titolo estero equivalente', so a BSc in Software Engineering satisfies the paper requirement. But admission is decided by an entrance exam that assesses 'musical competence, technical level and motivation', and the course is explicitly aimed at musicians, authors and producers who already have a compositional language to deepen. Combined with the mandatory Italian B2 test, a candidate with no music training and no Italian cannot realistically be admitted.
_rec.recommendation: REAL DEGREE, REAL SCHOOL, WRONG CANDIDATE. The good news corrects the earlier record: CPM publishes its fees in full (€11,242–€14,615 in year one, plus €490 in registration and regional tax), it is genuinely MUR/AFAM accredited, the award is a full laurea-magistrale-equivalent, and its students can compete for Lombardy DSU scholarships. The bad news is structural and cannot be fixed with money. Admission requires Italian at B2 — evidenced by certificate or a 90-minute written test — and an entrance examination in musical and compositional competence. He has neither, and fourteen months is not enough to acquire both to examination standard alongside building a portfolio. On top of that, this is a COMPOSITION degree; CPM offers no second-level diploma in production or sound engineering at all, so even if he passed he would be studying the wrong subject. Do not apply for September 2027.

_rec.tuitionEU: RE-VERIFICATION FAILED THIS PASS — consbo.it fee pages returned 404 or a bot-check interstitial. Carried forward from the 2025/2026 Regolamento tasse e contributi and to be reconfirmed: for Bienni in Direzione d'Orchestra, Direzione di Coro, Musica Applicata, MUSICA ELETTRONICA and Jazz, imposta di bollo €16.00 + assicurazione €10.00 + tassa regionale ER.GO €140.00 + contributo di funzionamento up to €2,000.00, so a maximum of €2,166.00 per year. Other bienni cap at €1,800; trienni at €1,600. The contributo is reduced on a sliding ISEEU scale, with full exoneration at ISEEU up to €22,000 subject to merit conditions, and percentage-based figures across the €22,001–€40,000 bands. Admission application fee €100.00 for Bienni, non-refundable.
_rec.tuitionNonEU: THE RATE HE WOULD PAY, carried forward and NOT re-verifiable this pass — treat as high-value but provisional. Bologna's Art. 14 on non-EU international students provides that a non-EU student can access the income-based reduction on the contributo di funzionamento only by presenting ISEEE certification (the foreign-income equivalent of the ISEE) issued by an authorised body such as a CAF or Patronato. Failure to present the ISEEE means automatic assignment to the highest contribution band, and an ISEEE returning €0.00 is rejected and likewise triggers the highest band. Practical consequence: with a correctly filed ISEEE reflecting a typical Tunisian family income he would very likely fall at or below the €22,000 threshold and pay little or no contributo, i.e. roughly €166/year in bollo, insurance and ER.GO tax; without it he pays roughly €2,166/year. That paperwork is worth roughly €4,000 over two years — but confirm the current-year figures with the segreteria didattica before planning on them.
_rec.otherFees: Imposta di bollo €16.00/year; assicurazione €10.00/year; tassa regionale ER.GO €140.00/year, paid separately by postal order or bank transfer rather than through PagoPA and NOT reducible by ISEE; admission application fee €100.00 per application. Late-payment penalties apply. Fuori corso students pay higher contributo. Diploma issue fee UNVERIFIED. All carried forward and pending reconfirmation.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: Best case with ISEEE filed: roughly €166/year in unavoidable charges, about €330 over two years, plus the €100 admission fee. Worst case without ISEEE: about €4,332 over two years. Bologna living costs are high for Italy at roughly €900–1,300/month and student housing is notoriously scarce — factor that in seriously, as it can outweigh the fee advantage over Turin. Two-year all-in approximately €25,000–34,000 depending on housing, before any ER.GO award.
_rec.scholarships: ER.GO, the Emilia-Romagna right-to-study agency, runs income-based scholarships open to non-EU students covering a maintenance grant, fee exemption and subsidised accommodation and meals. Combined with a low ISEEE this is the closest thing to full funding in the Italian state conservatoire system. The bando typically opens in summer. Obtaining the ISEEE through a Patronato or CAF is the prerequisite for both the fee reduction and the scholarship — the single most valuable piece of Italian paperwork he can prepare. MAECI government scholarships are the alternative national route.
_rec.intakes: Autumn, Italian academic year, with admission exams in the spring or summer preceding.
_rec.applicationOpens: For a.a. 2025/26, applications for ammissioni and trasferimenti ran 17 March – 12 April 2025 (PRIOR CYCLE — could not be re-verified this pass; the ammissioni page was behind the bot check). Expect a comparable mid-March opening in 2027 for a 2027/28 start. Non-EU applicants must separately complete Universitaly pre-enrolment on the Ministry's earlier calendar before enrolling for the entrance examinations.
_rec.deadline: 12 April 2025 for a.a. 2025/26 (PRIOR CYCLE — confirm the 2027/28 date). After the ranking list is published, admitted candidates must enrol within 10 days — a very short window that requires funds and documents ready in advance.
_rec.visaEligible: Yes. A state conservatoire second-level diploma supports an Italian student visa and permesso di soggiorno per studio. Non-EU citizens not resident in Italy must submit a pre-enrolment request on the Universitaly portal before enrolling for the entrance examinations. Missing the Universitaly window invalidates the whole application regardless of academic merit.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: UNCERTAIN, and now explicitly unconfirmed. The course page states no entry requirement whatsoever; the restrictive 'three-year electronic music studies or equivalent' wording lives on international pages that were unreachable this pass. Note the useful asymmetry: Torino runs the same ministerial course code DCSL34 and its confirmed published requirement accepts any foreign triennale. That is a strong argument to put to Bologna's segreteria. Until they answer in writing, treat Bologna as uncertain rather than as closed.
_rec.recommendation: WORTH PURSUING, but the eligibility question must be answered before he invests anything in it. The syllabus is confirmed and is the best technical fit in this entire sweep for a software engineer — programming languages and systems for audio (7 CFA), multimedia programming, interactive multimodal environments, digital audio spatialisation, and 15 CFA of integrated audiovisual composition covering sound for film, theatre, dance and videogames. Those are modules where his background is an asset. What could NOT be verified in this pass is everything else: the conservatoire's site is behind an active bot-verification layer, so the entry requirements, the B2 Italian requirement, the fee regulation and the ISEEE rule are all carried forward from the prior sweep unconfirmed. First action, autumn 2026: phone or email the segreteria didattica (051 221483 / 051 233975) and ask three things — whether a foreign three-year Software Engineering degree plus a documented electronic-music and technical portfolio is accepted as 'equivalent' for DCSL34 admission, what the Bando di ammissione requires, and whether the ISEEE route to contributo exoneration still stands for a non-EU non-resident. Cite Torino's DCSL34 wording, which accepts any foreign triennale outright, when asking the first question. Meanwhile treat Torino as the primary Italian target and Bologna as the strong second: Torino's door is confirmed open, Bologna's is merely not confirmed shut. Two preparations serve both: tested Italian B2, and the ISEEE paperwork route mapped with a Patronato well before enrolment. And be clear with him about what this is — an electroacoustic composition and sound design degree that would make him a formidable sound designer and audio programmer, not a commercial dance-music production course.

_rec.program: Interactive Environments — Nuove tecnologie per l'arte, la cultura e il territorio (Biennio Specialistico)
_rec.institution: IED — Istituto Europeo di Design, Roma
_rec.qualification: CONFIRMED on the course page: "Diploma Accademico di Secondo Livello in Nuove Tecnologie dell'Arte - Indirizzo Interactive Environments", 120 CFA/ECTS. IED's own award page (ied.edu/courses/master-of-arts) states verbatim: "Our Master of Arts award a Diploma Accademico di Secondo Livello, recognised by the MUR - Ministero dell'Università e della Ricerca." This is a genuine second-cycle Italian academic award — the SAME level as a laurea magistrale, NOT a 60-credit 'master universitario'. Do not confuse it with IED's one-year 'Master' courses, which the site lists as a separate and lesser product.
_rec.institutionType: Private international design school chain (IED Istituto Europeo di Design S.p.A. — Società Benefit); campuses in Milan, Rome, Turin, Florence, Cagliari, Como, plus Spain and Brazil.
_rec.accreditationStatus: OFFICIAL — Diploma Accademico di Secondo Livello, MUR-recognised (AFAM-framework second cycle). Verified from IED's own award page. The MUR statement is NOT repeated on the Rome course page itself, so get it confirmed in writing for THIS course code before paying anything. Note the structural trap at IED: its 'Master' (one-year) courses are private certificates and are NOT this award — always read the award line on each individual course page.
_rec.focus: Interactive and multimedia environments, immersive experiences, digital installations applied to heritage and territory. Sound appears as one named output strand ('visual & sound design') inside a course that is fundamentally about interaction design for cultural heritage — it is NOT a music production or mixing course.
_rec.durationEcts: 2 years, 120 CFA/ECTS, full time, in person, Rome campus. CONFIRMED on the course page.
_rec.language: ITALIAN ONLY. CONFIRMED on the course page. No English track exists for this course.
_rec.intakes: One intake per year. CONFIRMED: the currently published start is OCTOBER 2027 — the only entry in this batch whose published start date actually matches his target intake.
_rec.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED — IED runs rolling admissions via an Admission Advisor and a reserved online platform; no opening date is published.
_rec.deadline: UNVERIFIED — IED publishes no fixed deadline for this course. Rolling admissions, places allocated until full. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date does not apply because no date has ever been published; treat 'apply early' as the operative rule.
_rec.entryRequirements: CONFIRMED verbatim from IED's master/second-cycle admissions page: "A three-year degree, an equivalent diploma, or minimum two years of work experience in the chosen field." Three steps: (1) application via Admission Advisor and reserved platform, (2) admission test, (3) enrolment.
_rec.auditionSpec: No audition. CORRECTION to prior data: the admission test is now confirmed to comprise (a) "valuation of school record and/or work experience", (b) a language proficiency assessment where the applicant has no certificate in the teaching language — for this course that means ITALIAN, (c) a digital portfolio (course-specific), and (d) an admission interview.
_rec.portfolioSpec: CORRECTED from 'UNVERIFIED'. IED's admissions page confirms a "digital portfolio submission (course-specific)" forms part of the admission test, plus an admission interview. The exact brief for Interactive Environments is not published — request it from the Admission Advisor. Given his portfolio is still being built, this is a real workload item.
_rec.englishTest: IELTS IS IRRELEVANT HERE. The course is delivered in Italian, so the admission language test would be an ITALIAN test for a non-native speaker. IED does not publish the required CEFR level. For a Tunisian applicant with no Italian, this is a multi-month prerequisite, not a formality.
_rec.whatYouStudy: Design of interactive and multimedia spaces, services and devices as platforms that revitalise historic, artistic and cultural heritage; digital arts, immersive experiences, digital installations, interactive environments; design methodologies and digital/physical technologies for visual, sound and interactive communication; hybrid narrative forms across physical and digital space; social, cultural and ethical impacts of digital media. Framed inside IED's 'DesignXCommons' agenda.
_rec.facilities: IED Rome campus. Course leaders Saverio Villirillo and Gregorio Comandini (transmedia artists); faculty includes Filippo Gualazzi (new media artist/creative technologist), Marcello Cualbu, Federica Patti, Valerio Mattioli. NO audio-specific studio inventory is published for this course — no control rooms, no consoles, no Atmos. UNVERIFIED and probably absent.
_rec.tuitionPerYear: Published as "A partire da 8.500 €" (from €8,500) — CONFIRMED on the course page, and that is the ONLY number IED publishes. NO NON-EU RATE IS PUBLISHED ANYWHERE IN THE FUNNEL. IED prices Italian students by declared income band; a non-resident, non-EU self-payer has no published band. NON-EU TUITION: UNVERIFIED.
_rec.tuitionTotal: UNVERIFIED for a non-EU student. €17,000 over two years IF the €8,500 floor applied — there is no evidence it applies to a non-EU applicant, and third-party reports of IED second-cycle pricing running to €20,100 total plus a €3,000 registration fee suggest it does not. Do not budget on the floor.
_rec.otherFees: UNVERIFIED. IED states 'On the page of each course you will find information on the price, including enrolment fee and tuition fee', but the Rome Interactive Environments page as published does NOT break out an enrolment/registration fee. Application fee: not published. Third-party reporting cites a €3,000 registration fee at IED second-cycle level — UNCONFIRMED by IED. This is a genuine transparency failure.
_rec.equipmentRequired: UNVERIFIED — not published. An interaction-design course of this type normally assumes a personal laptop capable of running Max/MSP, TouchDesigner or similar, plus Adobe licences. Budget for it.
_rec.paymentPlans: IED advertises 'agevolazioni' (facilitations and funding); specific instalment terms are NOT published. UNVERIFIED.
_rec.scholarships: IED's scholarships page CONFIRMS the competition covers "First-level Academic Diplomas, Second-level Academic Diplomas and Master courses" — so this course is in scope. BUT the page currently reads 'Novità in arrivo' (updates coming) with no amounts, no criteria and no deadlines published. Non-EU eligibility: UNVERIFIED. Nothing here can be counted on.
_rec.visaEligible: YES IN PRINCIPLE — a MUR-recognised Diploma Accademico di Secondo Livello at an AFAM-framework institution supports Universitaly pre-enrolment and a type-D study visa, and IED publishes a 'Procedure for Visa-Seeking students' PDF for non-EU applicants. NOT explicitly confirmed for this specific Italian-language course code; IED's own 'study in Italy' pages do not spell out visa sponsorship. Get it in writing.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: UNVERIFIED — IED publishes no non-EU price. Working range for planning only: €17,000–€40,000+ tuition over two years, plus an unquantified enrolment fee (possibly ~€3,000), plus Rome living costs of roughly €900–1,200/month. Treat '€8,500 from' as a domestic marketing floor, not a quote.
_rec.reputationSignals: Large, established international design chain with genuine MUR accreditation for its academic diplomas and a strong design-industry brand. RED FLAG: total opacity on non-EU pricing — no rate published at any point in the funnel, and scholarship details replaced by 'coming soon'. Second red flag for his goal: despite IED's prominence in sound design education, there is NO IED master-level sound design course anywhere in Italy — IED's sound design offer stops at bachelor level (Milan and Rome).
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: YES, explicitly. Quoted from IED's admissions page: "A three-year degree, an equivalent diploma, or minimum two years of work experience in the chosen field." No music prerequisite whatsoever, and his BSc Software Engineering is arguably a strong fit for interaction design and creative coding. The barrier is language, not background.
_rec.recommendation: THE ONLY THING GOING FOR IT IS THE DATE. October 2027 is exactly his target, and a MUR-recognised second-cycle award is real currency. Everything else argues against: it is Italian-only (so he needs a year of language study first), sound is one clause in a course about heritage installations rather than music production, there are no published audio facilities, and IED will not publish a non-EU price. For a budget-sensitive self-payer, a school that hides its price is disqualifying until a written quote arrives. If he contacts IED at all, the first email should ask three questions only: (1) the exact non-EU annual tuition and enrolment fee in writing, (2) the required Italian CEFR level, (3) whether they issue the Universitaly pre-enrolment for this course. If the answer to (1) is above €12,000/year, walk away.

_rec.program: Master of Arts in Multimedia Design and Creative AI (Diploma Accademico di II livello)
_rec.institution: RUFA — Rome University of Fine Arts
_rec.qualification: Second-Level Academic Diploma (Diploma Accademico di Secondo Livello), 120 CFA, described on the course page as 'equivalent to a Master's Degree'. CONFIRMED. This is the OFFICIAL Italian second-cycle award, laurea-magistrale equivalent — distinct from RUFA's one-year 'Academic Master' courses, which are a lesser 60-credit post-degree qualification priced at a flat €13,800 plus €1,800 enrolment.
_rec.institutionType: Private legally-recognised academy of fine arts (Rome University of Fine Arts srl, under the direction of Plena Education S.p.A.). Campuses in Rome and Milan.
_rec.accreditationStatus: OFFICIAL — RUFA is a MUR-recognised AFAM institution and the II livello award is a Diploma Accademico di Secondo Livello worth 120 CFA, EHEA-valid and valid for a type-D student visa. This is the real thing, not a private certificate.
_rec.focus: Transdisciplinary multimedia design and creative AI, built around creative coding. IMPORTANT CORRECTION: sound design is NOT merely incidental here — it is a dedicated 6-credit, 75-hour module in year one. RUFA has no standalone sound-design master, but it does partner with Saint Louis College of Music on sound-design projects.
_rec.durationEcts: 2 years, 120 CFA/ECTS. CONFIRMED.
_rec.language: ITALIAN ONLY — CONFIRMED on the course page, and a B2 language certificate is required of both EU and non-EU applicants. Compulsory on-campus attendance at RUFA's Rome venues. Other RUFA second-level courses are delivered in English at a higher fee band, but this one is not. This is the decisive obstacle.
_rec.intakes: One intake per year, October. CONFIRMED.
_rec.applicationOpens: Not published as a fixed date; admission runs in multiple sessions through the year, with an early-bird enrolment window referenced to 31 August 2026 for the current cycle. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date.
_rec.deadline: Early-bird enrolment (enrolment fee plus signed form) by 31 August 2026 for a 10% tuition reduction; single-payment tuition settlement by 31 December for a further 5% discount. Application sessions run in multiple rounds. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new dates for the 2027/28 cycle.
_rec.entryRequirements: A First Level Academic Diploma, bachelor's degree or equivalent, PLUS a portfolio, PLUS a B2 language certificate (required of both EU and non-EU applicants — in Italian for this Italian-taught course). Selection is by admission testing, with direct enrolment available in some cases and guidance interviews offered. Foreign-degree documentation (Dichiarazione di Valore / CIMEA) not detailed on the pages read — Partial.
_rec.auditionSpec: NO AUDITION — confirmed. Access is by selection: portfolio plus admission testing, with optional guidance interviews. No musical competence test of any kind.
_rec.portfolioSpec: PORTFOLIO REQUIRED — confirmed on the course page as an entry requirement (this corrects the earlier UNVERIFIED). Format, quantity and submission specification are not published (Partial) — request the spec in writing.
_rec.englishTest: IELTS IS IRRELEVANT HERE — this course is taught exclusively in Italian and the confirmed requirement is a B2 certificate, which for an Italian-taught course means B2 ITALIAN (CILS, CELI, PLIDA or equivalent). RUFA's English-taught second-level courses would accept English evidence at a higher fee band, but Multimedia Design and Creative AI is not one of them. He would need B2 Italian by autumn 2027.
_rec.whatYouStudy: Transdisciplinary multimedia design premised on the role of digital media and new technologies in contemporary creative practice, with creative coding as the technological spine. Confirmed coursework includes interaction design, extended reality (XR), creative AI systems, digital video direction, SOUND DESIGN (6 credits / 75 hours in year one), and experience design for cultural contexts. Delivered through 'learning by doing' with workshops, exhibitions and industry collaborations. Confirmed graduate roles: interaction designer, AI and generative media designer, experience designer, creative technologist, multimedia art director, digital installation artist.
_rec.facilities: Rome campuses at Via Benaco 2, Via G. Libetta 7 and Via degli Ausoni 7; Milan campus at Piazzale Lugano 19. RUFALab, cinema facility, laboratories, library. Compulsory in-person attendance in Rome. Specific audio studio and monitoring inventory not published (Partial).
_rec.tuitionPerYear: CONFIRMED, non-EU applicants included, banded by declared household income. ITALIAN-TAUGHT courses (which is what this one is): €8,000 (€0–40k) / €8,800 (€40–70k) / €9,800 (€70–100k) / €12,800 (€100–130k) / €13,800 (€130–150k) / €14,800 (over €150k). ENGLISH-TAUGHT courses run higher: €10,500 / €11,600 / €13,000 / €14,500 / €15,500 / €16,500 across the same bands. Roughly a third of NABA's non-EU price at the lowest band, and — crucially — non-EU students ARE income-banded here, unlike at NABA.
_rec.tuitionTotal: Italian-taught MA over two years: €16,000 at the lowest band, up to €29,600 at the top band. English-taught equivalents: €21,000 to €33,000. Add €1,800 enrolment and €140 regional tax in EACH year.
_rec.otherFees: CONFIRMED: enrolment fee €1,800 PER YEAR (not one-off); regional tax €140 per year (newly confirmed, and additional to tuition — it is not included as it is at NABA); application fee for non-EU students €100 for all sessions. Fee exemption of €2,000 available for students with 66%+ disability. Materials, equipment and insurance fees not published (Partial). RUFA publishes its fee structure more completely than either NABA or CPM.
_rec.equipmentRequired: Not published — UNVERIFIED. Creative coding, XR and sound design work assume a capable personal laptop and software licences; budget €1,500–2,500.
_rec.paymentPlans: BEST TERMS IN THE BATCH, AND BETTER THAN PREVIOUSLY RECORDED. CONFIRMED: 3, 4, 6 or 12 INTEREST-FREE INSTALMENTS are available — this applies to the MA, correcting the earlier belief that instalments were restricted to the one-year Academic Master courses. Alternatively a 5% discount for settling in a single payment by 31 December. Stackable with the 10% early-bird tuition reduction for completing enrolment by 31 August. Also confirmed: 10% sibling reduction, 20% discount for RUFA graduates, state-guaranteed student loans of €3,000–€15,000 per year via Habacus requiring no payslip or financial guarantor, and merit-based/interest-free financing that requires Italian residency.
_rec.scholarships: The reliable, published savings for a non-EU applicant are the 10% early-bird tuition reduction and the 5% single-payment discount — together worth roughly €1,150 in year one at the lowest band. RUFA also references scholarships on a separate application page, but amounts and non-EU eligibility are not published (Partial). Habacus state-guaranteed loans (€3,000–€15,000/year, no payslip or guarantor required) are open in a way that most Italian financing is not, and are worth investigating given his position. Note that RUFA's merit-based loans and interest-free financing require Italian residency and so are closed to him at application time.
_rec.visaEligible: YES — MUR-recognised AFAM institution issuing an official Diploma Accademico di Secondo Livello, so Universitaly pre-enrolment and the type-D national study visa apply, and RUFA publishes an International Students section and charges a specific €100 non-EU application fee, which indicates a functioning non-EU pipeline. Institution-specific CIMEA/Dichiarazione di Valore procedure not detailed on the pages read.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: Italian-taught, lowest band, first year: €8,000 tuition + €1,800 enrolment + €140 regional tax + €100 application = €10,040, falling to about €9,240 with the 10% early-bird discount. Two years: roughly €19,880, or about €18,300 with early-bird applied twice — LESS THAN HALF of NABA's €44,500. Add Rome living costs of €10,000–13,000 per year (cheaper than Milan). Realistic two-year all-in: €40,000–€45,000, versus €65,000–€75,000 at NABA. CAVEAT: the income banding is opaque for a non-EU applicant with no Italian income declaration — establish IN WRITING which band applies to a Tunisian household before budgeting on €8,000.
_rec.reputationSignals: MUR/AFAM recognised; part of the Plena Education group; documented collaboration with Saint Louis College of Music and Vigamus on sound-design projects; Erasmus+ participant. Genuinely the most transparent fee and payment disclosure of the three institutions in this batch — every charge including the €140 regional tax and the €100 non-EU application fee is published, instalments are interest-free and explicit, and discounts are stated with dates. Red flag: the income banding is undefined for an applicant with no Italian ISEE, and no audio studio inventory is published.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: YES on paper — the requirement is a first-level degree or equivalent in any field, plus a portfolio and B2 language certificate, with no music prerequisite and no audition. A software-engineering graduate is a strong fit for a creative-coding and AI curriculum. The binding constraint is not his subject background; it is Italian at B2.
_rec.recommendation: THE BEST-VALUE OFFICIAL DEGREE HERE, GATED BEHIND ITALIAN. Verification improved this entry in three ways and worsened it in none. Sound design turns out to be a real, timetabled 6-credit / 75-hour module rather than an afterthought; the payment terms are the best in the batch, with 3, 4, 6 or 12 interest-free instalments available on the MA itself plus a stackable 10% early-bird and 5% single-payment discount; and the fee disclosure is honest and complete down to the €140 regional tax and the €100 non-EU application fee. At roughly €9,240–€10,040 in year one it costs less than half of NABA for an equally official MUR-recognised laurea-magistrale-equivalent, in a cheaper city, and non-EU students are income-banded here rather than penalised. Two things stop it being an A. First, it is taught exclusively in Italian with a mandatory B2 certificate and compulsory in-person Rome attendance — he has fourteen months to reach certified B2 from nothing, which is demanding but, given that a Tunisian francophone has a real head start in Italian, not impossible. Second, it is multimedia and creative-AI design, not music production; the sound design module is one component of a creative-technologist degree. Pursue this ONLY if he commits now to an intensive Italian programme and reframes his goal toward multimedia and interactive design with audio as a specialism. Get the income band confirmed in writing before budgeting. For music production specifically, his own Saint Louis lead remains the better door.

_rec.program: Master of Arts in Multimedia Design & Creative AI (Diploma Accademico di Secondo Livello)
_rec.institution: RUFA — Rome University of Fine Arts S.r.l. (private AFAM academy; company under the direction and coordination of Plena Education S.p.A.)
