_rec.qualification: OFFICIAL — 'Second-Level Academic Diploma, equivalent to a Master's Degree', 120 CFA, within the Italian AFAM system. RUFA is a recognised AFAM institute. Its separate one-year 'Academic Master' programmes are post-degree certificates and are NOT equivalent.
_rec.institutionType: Private art academy inside the state-recognised AFAM system, owned by Plena Education S.p.A.
_rec.focus: VERIFIED complete Master of Arts list: Computer Animation and Visual Effects; Film Arts; Fine Arts; Multimedia Design & Creative AI; Set Design; Visual and Innovation Design. Multimedia Design & Creative AI covers creative AI and generative systems, interaction design and extended reality (XR), experience design and audiovisual narratives, creative coding and physical computing. Sound is explicitly present as material to be orchestrated ('orchestrate sound, video and interactivity') but there is NO dedicated audio, music-production or sound-design second-level programme.
_rec.durationEcts: 2 years, 120 CFA. 60 CFA per academic year.
_rec.language: ITALIAN. VERIFIED on the official course page: 'LANGUAGE > ITALIAN'. Course start October, campus Rome. This is a hard barrier for him — see English test below.
_rec.intakes: October start. Admission runs across FIVE to SIX sessions per academic year, and both scholarship value and Early Bird value fall the later he applies.
_rec.whatYouStudy: Three published study areas. CREATIVE AI AND GENERATIVE SYSTEMS — AI inside the design workflow applied to sound, video, images and design; managing datasets, controlling machine-learning algorithms, integrating generative systems into multimedia production. INTERACTION DESIGN AND EXTENDED REALITY (XR) — 'phygital' ecosystems, physical computing, AR/VR, natural interfaces, immersive worlds. EXPERIENCE DESIGN AND AUDIOVISUAL NARRATIVES — narrative installations, immersive museums, directing audiovisual performances and adaptive digital sets, 'orchestrating light, sound and video'. Main disciplines: Interaction Design, Extended Reality (XR), Creative AI, Experience Design, Digital Video, Project Management. Also a strong Creative Coding strand framing code as 'a fluid and generative material'. Career outcomes listed: Interaction Designer, AI & Generative Media Designer, Experience Designer, Creative Technologist, Multimedia Art Director, Digital Installation Artist, Exhibit Designer, Media Arts Project Manager.
_rec.facilities: Rome campuses at Via Benaco 2, Via G. Libetta 7 and Via degli Ausoni 7; Milan campus at Piazzale Lugano 19. Published services include RUFALab, labs, library, Service Cinema, career services and internships, Erasmus+. Audio/studio inventory UNVERIFIED.
_rec.entryRequirements: VERIFIED and quoted from the official course page. ITALIAN STUDENTS: Bachelor's degree or equivalent qualification; Portfolio. EU AND NON-EU STUDENTS: 'First-cycle degree valid within the Italian education system'; 'Portfolio'; 'B2 certificate in the language of the course'. Plus: 'Following admission, NON-EU students will be required to begin the procedure for obtaining a study visa.' A Dichiarazione di Valore or CIMEA attestation will be needed to establish that the Tunisian BSc is 'valid within the Italian education system'.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: YES on subject — a BSc Software Engineering is arguably the single best-matched background for a Creative AI, creative-coding and XR degree; the published requirement is only a 'first-cycle degree valid within the Italian education system'. The barrier is not his discipline, it is the language.
_rec.portfolioSpec: A portfolio is a stated admission requirement for all applicants, and it is also the primary basis for the international scholarship — awards go to the 'Migliori portfolio e prova di ammissione', selected by academic commissions. RUFA publishes formal PORTFOLIO GUIDELINES (linked from the scholarship page). Scholarship applicants must submit the scholarship request form with portfolio AND a motivation letter, and must book the admission test at the same time.
_rec.auditionSpec: No musical audition. There is an admission test (prova di ammissione) plus a motivational interview assessed by an academic commission. Critically: 'Gli studenti che hanno presentato il portfolio ma non hanno sostenuto l'esame di ammissione nella sessione sopra indicata non saranno considerati idonei alla borsa di studio' — submitting a portfolio without sitting the test in that session forfeits the scholarship.
_rec.englishTest: IELTS IS IRRELEVANT HERE. The course is taught in ITALIAN and the published requirement for EU and non-EU students is a 'B2 certificate in the language of the course' — i.e. B2 ITALIAN, certified. For a September 2027 target starting from zero Italian, that is a 12-month intensive language project he would have to begin immediately, and it is the single biggest practical obstacle to this programme. (If he wanted an English-taught RUFA second-level programme he would pay the higher English-language tariff — see fees.)
_rec.tuitionPerYear: NOW VERIFIED — previously unpublished. RUFA bands second-level tuition by ISEE, BUT: 'For non-EU students, only the income bracket above 150 applies, with the exception of Türkiye.' A Tunisian therefore pays the TOP band automatically. Second-Level Academic Programmes, top band ('oltre 150'): ITALIAN-TAUGHT COURSES €14,800 per year; ENGLISH-TAUGHT COURSES €16,500 per year. Since Multimedia Design & Creative AI is Italian-taught, his figure is €14,800 PER YEAR. (For reference the lowest Italian/EU band, 0-40, is €8,000 Italian / €10,500 English — not available to him.) The annual total is split into an ENROLMENT FEE of €1,800 payable on enrolment plus the remaining TUITION FEE of about €13,000.
_rec.tuitionTotal: €29,600 over the two years for the Italian-taught Multimedia Design & Creative AI (2 × €14,800) at current rates. An English-taught RUFA second-level programme would be €33,000. Rates are the current published cycle — confirm for 2027/28.
_rec.otherFees: VERIFIED list of EXCLUDED COSTS, none of which are in the €14,800: admission test fee, first year only — €100.00 for international students (€50 or €100 for Italians depending on session); regional university study tax to DiSCo Lazio — €140.00 per year, paid via laziodisco.it; Diploma examination fee, payable in the second year of a Second-Level programme — €400.00; Diploma tax to the Government Concessions Tax Office Rome, postal account 1016 — €90.84; and 'all teaching materials required for personal projects'. So the two-year non-tuition add-ons come to roughly €100 + €280 + €400 + €90.84 = about €871, plus materials.
_rec.equipmentRequired: Not itemised, but 'all teaching materials required for personal projects' are explicitly excluded from the fee. For an XR, creative-coding and generative-AI programme budget a high-specification laptop or workstation and software; UNVERIFIED as a formal list.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: About €14,800 + €140 + €100 = €15,040 in year one, and €14,800 + €140 + €400 + €90.84 = €15,431 in year two, so roughly €30,500 in fees over two years before aid, plus materials. With Rome living costs of €11,000-€14,000 a year, the two-year all-in is about €53,000-€59,000. Best realistic case with a €5,000 international award in year one: about €48,000-€54,000.
_rec.scholarships: SIGNIFICANTLY CORRECTED — the previous account conflated two entirely separate bandi. (1) THE 10 SECOND-LEVEL SCHOLARSHIPS ARE FOR ITALIAN AND EU STUDENTS ONLY. They sit under the heading 'Bando per studenti italiani e UE', are worth €5,000 down to €2,000 a year depending on session, carry an ISEE ceiling of €40,000 for 2026, and cover Scenografia, Pittura, Performance Art, Scultura, Grafica d'arte, Visual and Innovation Design, Multimedia Arts and Design, Computer Animation and Visual Effects and Arte cinematografica. A TUNISIAN IS NOT ELIGIBLE FOR THESE. Session deadlines were 18 January, 5 April, 5 June, 15 July (extraordinary), 12 September and 24 September 2026. (2) THE ROUTE THAT IS ACTUALLY OPEN TO HIM is the 'Bando per studenti UE e NON-UE' for Corsi Triennali e Biennali: thanks to special International Office funding, international students who take part in the BA/MA Admission Session of 20 JULY are automatically eligible for extraordinary financial support of BETWEEN €2,000 AND €5,000 towards tuition, awarded on candidates' performance in the admission test and on the best portfolios, selected by the academic commissions. Deadline for the extraordinary July session: 15 JULY 2026 — PRIOR CYCLE, confirm the 2027 date. HARD CONDITIONS: 'le borse di studio RUFA non sono cumulabili con altre riduzioni/borse RUFA' — NOT combinable with any other RUFA reduction, which specifically means NOT combinable with the Early Bird discount; a candidate may apply ONCE per academic year only; and submitting a portfolio without sitting the admission test in that session voids eligibility. RENEWAL for year 2 of a second-level course requires 40 CFA with a weighted average of 27/30 — a genuinely demanding bar. (3) EARLY BIRD, first- and second-level diplomas, EU AND NON-EU students, first year only: €1,800 off the annual tuition if enrolled by 31 March, €1,200 by 15 June, €600 by 31 July — but 'It cannot be combined with scholarships and/or other financial benefits'. So he must choose: Early Bird by 31 March (a certain €1,800) or the July international scholarship (an uncertain €2,000-€5,000). (4) Academic Master scholarships (30%/50% of tuition, 9 July deadline) apply only to the one-year Masters, not to this degree. (5) DiSCo Lazio regional right-to-study is available in principle on the same statutory basis as the Lombardy scheme (non-EU students treated as fuori sede) — RUFA-specific amounts UNVERIFIED. (6) Financing: Intesa Sanpaolo 'per Merito' and Habacus are offered but 'Applicants must be resident in Italy' — useless to him before arrival.
_rec.paymentPlans: VERIFIED, AND THIS IS A SERIOUS CASH-FLOW ISSUE. Italian and EU students may pay the tuition fee in a single payment by 30 November with a 5% discount, or in 3, 4, 6 or 12 instalments (the 12-instalment route is an interest-free financing plan requiring a guarantor's payslip or tax return, identity document and ITALIAN TAX CODE). NON-EU STUDENTS GET NONE OF THAT: 'The remaining tuition fee must be paid by 30 September.' He must pay the €1,800 enrolment fee on enrolment and then the remaining roughly €13,000 IN FULL BY 30 SEPTEMBER — no instalments, no 5% discount. Non-EU payment is by bank transfer or credit card via rufa.flywire.com.
_rec.accreditationStatus: OFFICIAL — RUFA is a recognised AFAM institute and this is a Diploma Accademico di Secondo Livello, 120 CFA, described on RUFA's own page as 'equivalent to a Master's Degree'. It is the Italian official second-cycle qualification, equivalent to a laurea magistrale for public competitions and doctoral entry in artistic fields.
_rec.visaEligible: YES, and stated explicitly on the course page: 'Following admission, NON-EU students will be required to begin the procedure for obtaining a study visa.' RUFA has a dedicated International Students office, charges a distinct non-EU admission-test fee, uses Flywire for non-EU payments and runs a non-EU-specific payment schedule — this is a normal, well-worn non-EU pathway.
_rec.applicationOpens: Five to six admission sessions a year. 2026 session dates: 18 January, 5 April, 5 June, 15 July (extraordinary), 12 September, 24 September. The international scholarship is tied to the 20 July BA/MA admission session. Scholarship value and Early Bird value both fall the later he applies — the earliest session is materially the most valuable.
_rec.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new dates for 2027 entry. Verified 2026 cycle: 15 JULY 2026 for the international (UE and NON-UE) scholarship, tied to the 20 July admission session. Early Bird deadlines: 31 March (€1,800), 15 June (€1,200), 31 July (€600). Non-EU balance of tuition due 30 September.
_rec.reputationSignals: Recognised AFAM institute with Rome and Milan campuses, a PhD programme, Erasmus+ participation, published portfolio guidelines, a dedicated international scholarship fund and fully transparent published fee tables. RED FLAGS: no sound-design or music-production programme at second level; the flagship programme he was matched to is taught in ITALIAN and requires certified B2; non-EU students are placed automatically in the top fee band with no income relief; non-EU students cannot pay in instalments and must clear roughly €13,000 by 30 September; the international scholarship is non-cumulable with Early Bird and can only be attempted once a year; the renewal bar of 40 CFA at a 27/30 weighted average is hard; and RUFA has restructured its website so several previously cited URLs (including the one originally supplied) now 404.
_rec.recommendation: RUFA is the best SUBJECT bridge in this batch between what he already is and what he wants to become: Multimedia Design & Creative AI is built on creative coding, generative AI, XR and physical computing, with sound explicitly one of the materials being orchestrated. A software engineer walks in with an advantage, and the portfolio-and-test scholarship rewards exactly the kind of self-built work he is producing. But three verified facts have to be faced. FIRST, THE COURSE IS TAUGHT IN ITALIAN and requires a certified B2 — from zero, that is a full-time twelve-month language project he must start now, or the application is void. SECOND, the money is worse than it looked: non-EU students pay the top band automatically (€14,800/yr Italian-taught, €29,600 over two years plus about €871 of excluded fees), and the 10 scholarships he was matched to are the ITALIAN AND EU bando — he is not eligible for them. His actual route is the €2,000-€5,000 international award tied to the July admission session. THIRD, non-EU students cannot pay in instalments: about €13,000 must clear by 30 September, on top of €1,800 at enrolment. Concrete plan if he pursues it: begin certified Italian immediately; build the portfolio to RUFA's published guidelines; then make a deliberate choice between locking the certain €1,800 Early Bird by 31 March and gambling on the July international session for €2,000-€5,000 — they cannot be combined, and he gets one attempt per year. Do not count on renewal: 40 CFA at 27/30 in a second language is a real risk of losing the award in year two.

_rec.recommendation: THE MOST ON-TOPIC COURSE IN ITALY, AND THE ONE HE ALMOST CERTAINLY CANNOT USE. Read the curriculum and it is uncanny how well it matches him: beat and synth programming, vocal production, mix and mastering, Ableton licence included, Pioneer DJ and Roland partnerships, no exams, portfolio as the output, and SAE literally names 'electronic music performer' and 'remixer' as the outcomes. But four facts kill it for HIS situation: it is not a degree and carries no ECTS or MUR recognition, it is taught in Italian with a hard B2 certification gate for international students, its only scholarship is restricted to women, and it will very probably not carry a student visa for a Tunisian national. This is a course for someone who already has the right to live in Milan. For a September 2027 non-EU entrant it fails the threshold test before the quality question is even reached. If he ever secures EU residence by another route, revisit it — on merit it is excellent.

_rec.institutionType: International chain campus – specialist audio academy (SAE / Navitas)
_rec.focus: Electronic music production, sound design, remixing, artistic identity, release-ready output
_rec.whatYouStudy: VERIFIED on the official page. Two 4-month quadrimesters. First: electronic music production fundamentals — composition, programming and arranging, integrating external hardware with DAWs and plugins, developing a personal workflow. Second: developing artistic identity, refining production technique, remixing, and mastering an EP ready for publication. Entirely project-based with no traditional exams. Stated career outcomes: Music Producer, Remixer, Electronic Music Performer, Live Performer, MIDI Programmer. This is the only entry in this batch whose content is actually electronic music production and performance rather than media/post-production sound.
_rec.durationEcts: 8 months (two 4-month quadrimesters), full time. No CFA, no ECTS — carries no academic credit. VERIFIED.
_rec.language: Italian. VERIFIED — the course page states the language as "Italiano" and requires international students to hold Italian certification at B2 CEFR. No English stream exists.
_rec.accreditationStatus: NOT OFFICIAL — VERIFIED AND CONFIRMED. SAE Italia's ministerial authorisation (art. 11 DPR 212/2005, Ministerial Decree 280/2017) authorised it, from a.a. 2018/19, to activate and award first-level academic diplomas ONLY in Produzione Audio and Produzione Cinetelevisiva e Nuovi Media. Electronic Music Production is not covered by that decree and is not in the Italian academic system at all: it is neither a Diploma Accademico di II livello nor a Master universitario di I/II livello nor even a first-level diploma. It is a private certificate. The trap here is real — SAE Milano genuinely IS an AFAM-authorised non-state institution, which makes its private certificates look more official than they are. Do not blur the two.
_rec.visaEligible: UNVERIFIED and unlikely. SAE Italy's internationalisation page mentions only the Erasmus Charter for Higher Education 2021-2027 and an "International Admissions" contact route; it publishes nothing on permesso di soggiorno support, Universitaly pre-enrolment, or whether visa assistance extends to certificate courses at all. An 8-month unaccredited private certificate falls outside the AFAM recognition that underpins the three-year diploma's visa standing. Treat a study visa on this course as unproven. Confirm in writing before paying anything.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: Yes — irrelevant either way. VERIFIED requirements are age 18+ and "È consigliabile essere in possesso di nozioni musicali di base" (basic musical knowledge recommended). No degree of any kind is required, so his BSc neither helps nor hinders. He is over-qualified for the entry bar and under-served by the award.
_rec.entryRequirements: VERIFIED. Domestic: minimum age 18; basic musical knowledge recommended; "la direzione didattica si riserva" the right to conduct interviews and skills assessments. International: minimum age 18; Italian language certification at B2 CEFR per the Common European Framework; basic musical knowledge recommended; subject to interview and competency verification.
_rec.portfolioSpec: None published. VERIFIED — no portfolio requirement appears anywhere on the course page. This would suit a portfolio-less applicant, but the language bar replaces it as the real obstacle.
_rec.auditionSpec: No formal audition. The academic direction reserves the right to conduct an interview and a skills assessment ("verifica delle competenze"). VERIFIED.
_rec.englishTest: IELTS is neither accepted nor relevant. VERIFIED requirement is ITALIAN at B2 CEFR, certified. For a Tunisian applicant with no Italian, this is roughly 600-800 hours of study plus a CELI/CILS/PLIDA exam before he could even apply — a far heavier lift than the IELTS 6.0-7.5 demanded elsewhere.
_rec.intakes: CORRECTED. _rec.tuitionPerYear: UNVERIFIED — VERIFIED AS DELIBERATELY UNPUBLISHED. SAE Italy publishes no price for this course anywhere. Both the /courses/ and /study/ pages gate the figure behind a brochure-download form that promises "dettagli dell'offerta formativa, rette di frequenza". Third-party source Studentville reports SAE Milano's THREE-YEAR AFAM diplomas at "da un minimo di circa 7.500 euro ad un massimo di circa 13.600 euro all'anno" by income bracket — but that is the degree courses, NOT this certificate, and must not be used as a proxy. That is a sibling-campus reference, not a Milan quote.
_rec.tuitionTotal: UNVERIFIED. No figure is published for this course in Italy.
_rec.otherFees: UNVERIFIED. No application, enrolment, materials, insurance or exam fees are published. Note that AFAM enrolment in Italy normally carries a regional right-to-study tax, but that applies to the accredited diplomas, not to this certificate. Ask specifically what is charged on top.
_rec.equipmentRequired: VERIFIED: an Ableton Live educational licence is included in the tuition — the page states "Ableton Live (licenza inclusa nella retta di frequenza)". No other required purchases are published. A personal laptop is not stated as required but should be assumed. UNVERIFIED whether headphones/controller are expected.
_rec.paymentPlans: UNVERIFIED for short courses. SAE Milano's degree fees "può essere pagata in due modalità: annuale o per ciclo didattico" (annually or per teaching cycle); whether the certificate can be split across the two quadrimesters is not published.
_rec.scholarships: None applicable. Italian regional right-to-study (Diritto allo Studio) grants at SAE Milano attach to enrolment on the AFAM-recognised Produzione Audio and Produzione Cinetelevisiva diplomas. A private certificate outside the AFAM system carries no access to DSU funding, no regional grants, and no ministerial scholarship route. He would be paying an unpublished price with zero fee-reduction mechanism available.
_rec.facilities: Named industry partnerships confirmed: Ableton, ADAM Audio, Steinberg, Pioneer DJ, Roland. Studio and lab access is shared with the degree programmes, and SAE promotes interdisciplinary collaboration with its video, music-business and games cohorts. Specific studio inventory for certificate students UNVERIFIED.
_rec.reputationSignals: SAE Institute is a genuine, long-established international audio-education chain and SAE Milano holds real ministerial AFAM authorisation for two first-level diplomas — the institution is credible. The course design is also genuinely strong for a producer: no exams, entirely project-driven, ending in a mastered, publication-ready EP with an original remix, which is precisely the deliverable a portfolio-less applicant needs. The Ableton and Pioneer DJ partnerships are real and relevant to a DJ/producer path. The red flags are specific and serious: the price is deliberately unpublished and only released after you surrender your contact details; the course sits OUTSIDE the AFAM recognition that gives SAE Milano its standing; there is no scholarship access whatsoever; and visa support is unproven. No consumer complaints found.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: UNVERIFIED — no published figure exists. Using the SAE Amsterdam sibling course as a crude anchor (€4,910-€5,700 for the same 8-month certificate), plus Milan living costs at roughly €1,000-€1,400/month for 8 months (€8,000-€11,200), a plausible all-in range is €13,000-€17,000 — but the tuition component is a guess, not a quote, and none of it is offset by any scholarship. Milan is the most expensive city in Italy for students.

_rec.recommendation: Right content, wrong language, wrong status, and a price he is not allowed to see before handing over his details. The syllabus is arguably the best-designed short electronic-production course in this entire research set — no exams, pure project work, ending in a mastered EP with an original remix, which is exactly what his empty portfolio needs, and the stated outcomes (producer, remixer, live performer) map directly onto his goal. But four things kill it for September 2027. First, it is taught in Italian with a CERTIFIED B2 requirement — for a Tunisian applicant with no Italian that is 600-800 hours of study plus a formal exam before he can even apply, a far bigger obstacle than any IELTS. Second, it carries no academic recognition of any kind: SAE Milano's ministerial decree covers only Produzione Audio and Produzione Cinetelevisiva, and this course is explicitly outside it. Third, the price is unpublished — a school that will not show you the number before capturing your contact details is not one to commit to sight-unseen. Fourth, a study visa on an 8-month unaccredited certificate is unproven, and no scholarship or regional grant is available to soften any of it. One genuine correction in his favour: intakes are October AND February, and an October 2027 start IS offered — so the timing would have worked. It is everything else that does not. Carry forward the structural lesson: an 8-month project-based course whose output is a finished, mastered EP is a better portfolio-building instrument than a year of lectures. That is the right criterion to apply to every option — he should just apply it to a course taught in a language he speaks, with an award that means something, and a price printed on the page.
_rec.verificationNotes: Official SAE pages fetched and confirmed for: qualification ("SAE Certificate"), 8-month two-quadrimester structure, Italian language with B2 for internationals, entry requirements verbatim, project-based no-exam delivery, EP capstone, Ableton licence included in tuition, and career outcomes. CORRECTION MADE: intakes are October and February (not February only), and the enquiry form offers October 2027 as a start date — an autumn 2027 entry is plausible. CONFIRMED: the AFAM ministerial authorisation (DM 280/2017, art.11 DPR 212/2005, effective a.a. 2018/19) covers only Produzione Audio and Produzione Cinetelevisiva e Nuovi Media — Electronic Music Production is a private certificate outside it, exactly as flagged. ALL MONEY REMAINS UNVERIFIED and this was confirmed as deliberate: SAE Italy publishes no price on either course page, gating it behind a brochure form. The Studentville figure of €7,500-€13,600/year applies to the AFAM triennali only and must not be applied here. Visa support could not be established — SAE's internationalisation page contains no policy on permesso di soggiorno, Universitaly, or certificate-course eligibility. Rated Partial because accreditation, curriculum, language and entry are fully verified while every financial figure is unobtainable from official sources.

Sem 1 = 30 cr (Composition of Electronic Music 1, Computer Based Music Analysis, Electronic Music Performance 1, Music Media and New Media, Theories of Music Composition and Interpretation); Sem 2 = 30 cr (Composition for Cinema, TV and Computer Games; Electronic Music Composition 2; Electronic Music Performance 2; Virtual Music Instruments; + 6 cr elective from Composition and Performance of Electroacoustic Music / Programming of Electronic Music / Sound Design Studio); Sem 3 = 30 cr Master's Degree Final Project.

Competition score = passed entrance exam + motivation assessment (oral, 10-point scale, weight 0.1) + up to 4 bonus points (up to 2 for scientific/artistic activity; 0.5 each for ≥1 year relevant work experience, partial studies abroad ≥24 ECTS, completion of a talent-development programme, diploma with distinction).

_rec.program: Mestrado em Produção e Tecnologias do Som
_rec.institution: Universidade Lusófona (private university — Grupo Lusófona / COFAC)
_rec.qualification: OFFICIAL Portuguese 2nd-cycle 'mestrado' (120 ECTS). VERIFIED on the official programme page: A3ES status 'Acreditado', registration R/A-Cr 34/2018/AL01. This is a real accredited master's degree, NOT a 'pós-graduação'.
_rec.institutionType: Private university, inside the Portuguese higher-education system (DGES/A3ES oversight)
_rec.focus: Sound production and technology: acoustics, audio capture, digital audio computing, sound design and composition, audio signal synthesis, musical computing, studio theory and practice.
_rec.durationEcts: VERIFIED: 4 semesters (2 years), 120 ECTS, in-person (presencial).
_rec.language: VERIFIED: Portuguese. No English track published.
_rec.intakes: Annual, in multiple application phases. The published 5th phase for 2026/27 ran 18 July – 1 September 2026. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date for the 2027/28 cycle.
_rec.whatYouStudy: VERIFIED 120-ECTS structure across 4 semesters. Y1S1: Acoustics, Audio Capture, Digital Audio Computing, Sound Design & Composition, Audio Signal Synthesis. Y1S2: Sound History & Aesthetics, Musical Computing, Interdisciplinary Project, Studio Theory & Practice. Y2S1: Art & Technology, Research Methodologies, Dissertation Project. Y2S2: Dissertation. Software focus: Avid Pro Tools, Max/MSP, Arduino. Note this is a technical/academic sound-technology master ending in a dissertation — it is NOT a DJ or electronic-dance-music performance course.
_rec.facilities: Lisbon campus with studio provision (a dedicated 'Studio Theory & Practice' module). Detailed console/room inventory NOT published — UNVERIFIED.
_rec.entryRequirements: VERIFIED: holders of a licenciatura or legal equivalent; OR holders of a recognised foreign higher-education qualification aligned with the Bologna Process; OR candidates whose academic/professional record is recognised by the scientific council as demonstrating capacity for this cycle. Selection: 25% previous qualification, 75% interview and portfolio/curriculum assessment. Candidates without a degree are assessed 100% by interview.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: YES. The published rule requires only a 'licenciatura ou equivalente legal' or a recognised foreign Bologna-aligned qualification — NO music degree is required, and no subject restriction is published. His BSc Software Engineering qualifies on level. The 75% interview-and-portfolio weighting means his portfolio, not his subject, decides the outcome.
_rec.portfolioSpec: Portfolio plus interview together carry 75% of the selection score; prior qualification carries 25%. The exact portfolio format/content specification is NOT published — UNVERIFIED, request it from the course director (Prof. Dr. João Marques Carrilho).
_rec.auditionSpec: Interview combined with portfolio/curriculum review. No musical audition is published.
_rec.englishTest: NOT APPLICABLE — the programme is taught in PORTUGUESE. IELTS is irrelevant here and taking it will not help for this programme. Portuguese proficiency is the binding requirement and he does not have it. The required Portuguese level is NOT published — UNVERIFIED, ask directly.
_rec.tuitionPerYear: VERIFIED 2026/27 official table: propina 'valor médio mensal para 30 ECTS' = €380.40/month; 'valor por ECTS' = €12.68. (2025/26 comparison: €365.40/month, €12.18/ECTS — so the table rose ~4%.) Billed monthly, due by the 8th. On the standard 10-instalment Portuguese billing year that is approximately €3,804 per year. NUMBER OF INSTALMENTS PER YEAR IS NOT EXPLICITLY PUBLISHED — treat the 10-month assumption as UNVERIFIED and confirm with SIGA. Lusófona states international students benefit from the SAME tuition table as all other students — there is NO non-EU tuition surcharge.
_rec.tuitionTotal: Approximately €7,608 for the full 120-ECTS programme at 2026/27 rates (2 years × ~€3,804). Confirm the 2027/28 table, which will likely rise again by ~4%.
_rec.otherFees: CORRECTED — THE PARENT BRIEF HAD THE APPLICATION FEE BACKWARDS. VERIFIED 2026/27 official emolumentos: 'Candidatura a Mestrados (International)' = €180; 'Candidatura a Mestrados (EU)' = €460. The NON-EU rate is the CHEAPER one — he pays €180, not €450/€460. Also: Matrícula/Inscrição/Renovação da Inscrição €350; Seguro Escolar €50; Candidatura de Reingresso €110. (2025/26 equivalents were €175 international / €450 EU, €300 matrícula, €47 seguro.) Materials and exam fees: UNVERIFIED.
_rec.equipmentRequired: Software focus is Avid Pro Tools, Max/MSP and Arduino. Whether personal licences must be purchased is NOT published — UNVERIFIED. Pro Tools and Max are commercial products; budget roughly €300–600 for student licences plus a capable laptop and monitoring.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: Year one (2026/27 rates): €180 candidatura + €350 matrícula + €50 seguro + ~€3,804 tuition = approximately €4,384. Year two: ~€3,804 + €350 renovação + €50 seguro = ~€4,204. TWO-YEAR FEE TOTAL approximately €8,588 — about €1,300 MORE than the parent brief's €8,100 estimate on tuition, but roughly €270 LESS on entry fees because of the corrected €180 international application fee. Plus Lisbon living costs of roughly €9,000–12,000/year. All-in two-year estimate: €27,000–33,000. This remains by far the cheapest accredited master's in this slice.
_rec.scholarships: NO institutional scholarship is published for this programme — UNVERIFIED whether an internal fund exists. The Portuguese national scheme is CLOSED to him: DGES bolsas de ação social direta require Portuguese nationality, a PERMANENT residence permit, a cooperation agreement, reciprocity, or refugee/stateless status. Under Decreto-Lei 36/2014 as amended by Decreto-Lei 62/2018, 'estudantes internacionais' receive only INDIRECT social action (canteens, facilities) and are EXCLUDED from direct monetary grants. DGES does note some private institutions run their own bolsas for students outside the national scheme, so ASK Lusófona directly (siga@ulusofona.pt). Erasmus+ mobility may be available once enrolled but is not entry funding.
_rec.paymentPlans: Monthly by default and interest-free — a genuine instalment arrangement, not credit. Tuition is billed as mensalidades due by the 8th of each month. VERIFIED rule for foreign students: the application fee is due at candidatura, and the enrolment fee + insurance + THE FIRST TWO MONTHLY INSTALMENTS are all due at matrícula. Up-front outlay at enrolment (2026/27) = €180 + €350 + €50 + (2 × €380.40) = approximately €1,340.80 — LOWER than the parent brief's €1,527 figure, because of the corrected international application fee. Payment by credit card and PayPal online, or Multibanco/cash in person. No interest or finance charge is stated.
_rec.accreditationStatus: OFFICIAL — VERIFIED on the official programme page: A3ES status 'Acreditado', registration R/A-Cr 34/2018/AL01. A full second-cycle mestrado of 120 ECTS, not a pós-graduação and not a certificate. Universidade Lusófona is a private university operating inside the Portuguese higher-education system under DGES/A3ES oversight, so the degree is an EHEA-valid master's, transferable and valid for doctoral entry.
_rec.visaEligible: Yes in principle — an A3ES-accredited, DGES-registered 120-ECTS mestrado at a recognised private university is a standard basis for a Portuguese student residence visa, and Lusófona operates a dedicated international-student admissions channel with its own published emolumentos line for international candidates (which presupposes enrolment from abroad). Status: UNVERIFIED as a written entitlement; confirm documentation with SIGA (siga@ulusofona.pt). This is materially stronger than either Dutch option, both of which are confirmed dead ends.
_rec.applicationOpens: 18 July 2026 for the 2026/27 5th phase. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm the 2027/28 opening (expect roughly July 2027, with earlier phases from around February 2027).
_rec.deadline: 1 September 2026 for 2026/27. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date for September 2027 entry. Apply in an EARLY phase, not the final one — a 1 September deadline leaves no time for a visa before a September start.
_rec.reputationSignals: A3ES-accredited with a published registration number that can be checked independently. Genuinely technical, hands-on curriculum (acoustics, digital audio computing, synthesis, Max/MSP, Arduino, studio practice) that maps unusually well onto a software-engineering background. VERIFIED pós-laboral timetable: 'Todos os dias úteis a partir das 18 horas' — every weekday from 6pm, leaving daytime free for studio work or a job. RED FLAGS: taught entirely in Portuguese; no published scholarship; ends in a dissertation rather than a portfolio of releases; and it is a sound-technology master, not a DJ/electronic-music career course.
_rec.recommendation: The strongest value proposition in this batch and the one to look at hardest. An A3ES-accredited master's — a real EHEA degree, not a certificate — in close to his subject, at roughly €7,600 tuition over two years with interest-free monthly instalments and NO non-EU premium. Two corrections in his favour versus the earlier brief: the international application fee is €180, not €450, and the enrolment-moment outlay is about €1,341, not €1,527. The curriculum is arguably better suited to a software engineer than any conservatory route, and the 75% portfolio-and-interview weighting means his portfolio matters far more than his lack of a music degree. TWO REAL OBSTACLES, both of which he must confront honestly: (1) LANGUAGE — it is taught in Portuguese and he has roughly 13 months to reach study level; (2) FIT — this is an academic sound-technology degree ending in a dissertation, not a DJ/producer career programme, so it serves the 'credential + technical depth + EU residence' goal far better than the 'international DJ' goal. Actions: email the course director now to confirm the required Portuguese level and whether any English accommodation exists; ask explicitly whether an internal bolsa for international students exists; request the portfolio specification in writing; and budget ~€1,341 for the enrolment moment.
_rec.verificationNotes: Programme page fetched and confirmed. A3ES accreditation and registration number R/A-Cr 34/2018/AL01 verified on the official page. 120 ECTS / 4 semesters / Portuguese / presencial verified. Full 2025/26 AND 2026/27 emolumentos tables retrieved verbatim. _rec.program: Mestrado em Produção e Tecnologias do Som
_rec.institution: Universidade Lusófona — Centro Universitário de Lisboa (COFAC)
_rec.qualification: MESTRADO — Portuguese 2nd-cycle degree, 120 ECTS, 4 semesters, presencial. A real degree, NOT a pós-graduação. VERIFIED on the official course page.
_rec.institutionType: Private university, owned by COFAC (Cooperativa de Formação e Animação Cultural) — Portugal's largest private university group.
_rec.accreditationStatus: OFFICIAL — VERIFIED. The course page publishes A3ES status 'Acreditado' with registration R/A-Cr 34/2018/AL01 and a linked A3ES deliberation. This is a fully accredited Portuguese 2nd-cycle degree: valid across the EHEA, valid for doctoral entry, and a valid basis for a D4 student residence visa. Not a título propio equivalent, not a certificate. On the accreditation question — the thing most likely to cost him his visa or leave him with worthless paper — this one is clean and the reference is publicly checkable.
_rec.focus: Sound production and sound technology: audiovisual sound, immersive and spatial audio, sound art, music computing, studio practice, and sound as a functional element in devices and environments.
_rec.whatYouStudy: VERIFIED module set. Year 1 S1 (30 ECTS): Acústica e Instrumentação, Captação de Som, Computação de Áudio Digital, Design e Composição Sonora, Síntese de Sinal Áudio. Year 1 S2 (30 ECTS): História e Cultura do Som, Computação Musical, Projeto Interdisciplinar, Teoria e Prática de Estúdio. Year 2 S1: Arte e Tecnologia, Metodologia de Investigação Científica, Projeto de Dissertação. Year 2 S2: Dissertação (30 ECTS). Core software confirmed as Avid Pro Tools, Max/MSP and Arduino. Published career outcomes include sound director, sound designer, music producer, recording and mastering technician. THIS IS THE CLOSEST CONTENT FIT TO WHAT HE ACTUALLY WANTS of any accredited option in this batch — synthesis, sound design, studio practice and music computing are all core, not electives. And Max/MSP plus Arduino is where his software engineering background becomes an asset rather than a liability.
_rec.durationEcts: 2 years / 4 semesters / 120 ECTS, in-person. VERIFIED schedule: 'Pós-laboral: Todos os dias úteis a partir das 18 horas' — every weekday from 18:00. The evening format is a genuine strategic advantage for him: days free for studio work, freelance production and building the DJ side.
_rec.language: PORTUGUESE. No English-taught delivery is published for the mestrado and none could be verified. The English-medium route in this same department is ReSound (listed separately) — which strongly implies the domestic mestrado is not English-medium. Treat Portuguese as required.
_rec.entryRequirements: VERIFIED: holders of a licenciatura or legal equivalent; OR a foreign degree conferred following the Bologna Process by a signatory State; OR a foreign academic qualification recognised as equivalent; OR a recognised academic/professional curriculum demonstrating capacity for this cycle of studies. VERIFIED SELECTION WEIGHTING, which is the number that actually matters: 25% prior qualification + 75% interview and portfolio/curricular evaluation. Candidates without a degree are assessed 100% on interview.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: ELIGIBLE ON PAPER, BUT THE SCORING IS THE REAL TEST. The regulation accepts 'titulares de grau de licenciado ou equivalente legal' with no field restriction, so a Software Engineering BSc is formally admissible — but unlike UCP Porto, the wording does NOT name engineering or computing among its target fields (it names musicology, sound technologies, audiovisual production, digital and performing arts, and media professionals). Combined with the verified 25/75 split, his degree is worth at most a quarter of the decision and his portfolio plus interview is worth three quarters. He currently has no portfolio. Verdict: admissible, but he must earn it entirely on work he has not yet made. His engineering background is a genuinely strong story here IF he frames it through Max/MSP, Arduino and audio DSP — the curriculum itself hands him that framing.
_rec.portfolioSpec: Required, and jointly with the interview carries 75% of the selection score — VERIFIED. But NO published format, length or content specification exists — UNVERIFIED. This is a meaningful gap: the single most heavily weighted element of the application is undefined in public. He must request the 'critérios de seriação' from info.cul@ulusofona.pt before building anything, or he risks producing the wrong thing.
_rec.auditionSpec: Interview (entrevista) — mandatory, combined with portfolio review as 75% of the score. VERIFIED. No performance audition or instrument test. Lusófona's international-student route separately references internal entrance examinations ('provas de ingresso internas'); whether those apply to 2nd-cycle entry is UNVERIFIED — ask, because an internal exam sat in Lisbon would be a serious logistical problem from Tunis.
_rec.englishTest: No IELTS requirement — the programme is Portuguese-medium, so IELTS is not the relevant test. Lusófona requires proof of proficiency in the language of instruction. Note the trap the draft correctly flagged: documents issued in Portuguese, Spanish, French or English are exempt from certified translation — that is a DOCUMENT rule, not a language-proficiency waiver, and his French-language Tunisian paperwork will benefit from it without saying anything about his Portuguese. Portuguese proficiency evidence for him: UNVERIFIED, assume it will be required.
_rec.tuitionPerYear: NOT PUBLISHED AS AN ANNUAL FIGURE — this is the central money problem with this entry, and it is now verified as a genuine gap rather than a research failure. VERIFIED 2026/27 values, quoted exactly from the official fee table: 'Valor médio mensal para 30 ECTS para disciplinas semestrais 380.4€' and 'Valor por ECTS 12.68€'. VERIFIED 2025/26 comparison: €365.40 monthly for 30 ECTS, €12.18 per ECTS — a 4.1% year-on-year rise, so budget a further rise for 2027/28. Lusófona bills in monthly instalments but the NUMBER of instalments per academic year is nowhere stated. On a 10-instalment year that implies roughly €3,804/year; on 12 instalments roughly €4,565/year. DO NOT TREAT EITHER AS CONFIRMED. Cross-check: 60 ECTS/year × €12.68 = €760.80/year, which is obviously not the annual tuition — the per-ECTS figure clearly does not multiply out to an annual total, which is itself a warning that this fee page cannot be reasoned about arithmetically. Demand a written annual figure in euros before he plans anything.
_rec.tuitionTotal: UNVERIFIED as a single published number — none exists. Derived range for the full 120 ECTS at the 2026/27 rate: approximately €7,600 (10 instalments/year) to €9,130 (12 instalments/year). NON-EU POSITION VERIFIED AND FAVOURABLE: Lusófona's international-student page confirms international students receive 'the same tuition table as all other students', with no premium for non-EU status. There is no non-EU surcharge.
_rec.otherFees: VERIFIED VERBATIM from the 2026/27 fee table: 'Candidatura a Mestrados – 460€' AND 'Candidatura a Mestrados – 180€' — both lines genuinely appear, with NO distinguishing text between them. I confirmed the same duplication in the 2025/26 table (€450 and €175), so it is a persistent structure, not a typo; the near-certain explanation is a national vs international (or standard vs early/online) split that the page simply fails to label. He must get written confirmation of which applies to him — the difference is €280. Also VERIFIED 2026/27: 'Candidatura de Reingresso 110€'; 'Matrícula/Inscrição/Renovação da Inscrição 350€'; 'Seguro Escolar 50€'; isolated curricular units €640 / €450. 2025/26 comparison verified: reingresso €105, matrícula/inscrição €300, seguro €47. Lusófona's international page elsewhere quotes a €425 application fee, which appears to belong to the 1st-cycle route — UNVERIFIED for 2nd cycle and a third conflicting number. Materials, equipment and exam fees: not itemised — UNVERIFIED.
_rec.equipmentRequired: Not published — UNVERIFIED. The department supplies professional multitrack studios, acoustic labs and 3D/Atmos facilities. A personal laptop and a Pro Tools licence are realistically necessary given the named core software, but neither is stated as a mandatory purchase. Budget €1,500–€2,500 anyway.
_rec.paymentPlans: Monthly instalments are the default billing unit — VERIFIED. CRITICAL NON-EU CASH-FLOW CONDITION, NOW VERIFIED ON THE OFFICIAL INTERNATIONAL PAGE: international students must pay TWO MONTHS OF TUITION IN ADVANCE at matriculation, together with registration, enrolment and school insurance; subsequent instalments fall due by the 8th of each month. So his day-one outlay is roughly €760 tuition + €350 matrícula + €50 seguro + candidatura, not one month's fee. VERIFIED payment methods: credit card, PayPal, Multibanco/ATM transfer, cash in person. Early-bird, alumni or referral discounts: none published for Lisbon — UNVERIFIED (the Porto campus advertised a 5% internal-student discount, which does not apply to him).
_rec.scholarships: No Lusófona scholarship specifically open to non-EU students is published on any page reviewed — UNVERIFIED, and I would not plan on one existing. Portuguese State DGES social scholarships are not realistically open to a newly arrived non-EU student. The practical funding route in this department is ReSound (Erasmus Mundus), not the domestic mestrado. ASSUME FULL SELF-PAY.
_rec.intakes: One September intake, fed by MULTIPLE application phases across the year — the 2026/27 cycle ran to at least a 5th period, and the draft's count of seven is plausible though I could only confirm the 5th. Multiple phases, single start.
_rec.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. VERIFIED for 2026/27: the 5th application period opened 18 July 2026, which means earlier phases opened well before that — expect the 2027/28 cycle to open in the first months of 2027. He should be watching from January 2027.
_rec.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. VERIFIED published 2026/27 window: 5th application period 18 July – 1 September 2026. For a September 2027 start he must apply in an EARLY phase (spring 2027), NOT a late one. A 1 September deadline with a September start is incompatible with obtaining a D4 visa from Tunis — the consular processing alone will not fit. The multi-phase structure is a trap for non-EU applicants: it looks flexible, but only the first two phases are actually usable by him.
_rec.facilities: Professional multitrack recording studios; specialised acoustic laboratories; cinema post-production facilities; 3D/Dolby Atmos audio system. Faculty described as working producers, sound designers, researchers and artists. The department (som.ulusofona.pt) also runs the BSc Ciência e Tecnologias do Som and hosts the ReSound Erasmus Mundus master, and sits inside the FilmEU European University alliance — a genuine international-network signal, not marketing.
_rec.visaEligible: YES. Lusófona is a State-recognised private university awarding an A3ES-accredited 120-ECTS degree over 2 years, which supports a Portuguese D4 study residence visa. It operates a formal 'Estudante Internacional' admission statute and a CLAIM migrant-integration service on campus, and the international page's explicit rules on advance payment show it routinely processes non-EU enrolments. Institutionally set up for someone in his position.
_rec.reputationSignals: POSITIVE: A3ES accreditation with a published, checkable registration reference; a dedicated sound department with Atmos and acoustic labs; FilmEU European University alliance membership; host of an Erasmus Mundus joint master, which is not awarded without external quality scrutiny. NEUTRAL/NEGATIVE: Lusófona is a large-volume private group running an admissions funnel of five-plus phases per year, which is a commercial-intake pattern rather than a selective one; the group has periodically attracted press scrutiny in Portugal over governance; and its Pós-Graduação em Produção e Tecnologia do Som has been withdrawn (confirmed 404 — see the separate entry), so programme-portfolio churn is real. The mestrado itself shows no sign of instability, but he should ask directly whether it is confirmed to run in 2027/28.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: First-year outlay approx. €4,400–€5,400 (derived tuition €3,800–€4,565 + matrícula €350 + seguro €50 + candidatura €180 or €460), noting that roughly €760 of the tuition is payable up front at enrolment. Full-programme tuition + fees roughly €8,200–€10,000. EXCLUDES Lisbon living costs, which are the real expense — realistically €900–€1,300/month, i.e. €21,600–€31,200 over two years, and Lisbon rent has been rising hard. Excludes €1,500–€2,500 equipment. Realistic all-in two-year figure: €31,000–€44,000, of which tuition is under a third.
_rec.recommendation: BEST CONTENT FIT AMONG THE ACCREDITED OPTIONS, AND CHEAPEST — BUT DO NOT COMMIT UNTIL THE TUITION IS IN WRITING. The curriculum is genuinely the closest of anything in this batch to what he says he wants: synthesis, sound design, studio practice, music computing, Pro Tools and Max/MSP, on an evening timetable, in Lisbon, a real electronic-music city. Accreditation is solid and publicly verifiable. Non-EU students pay the same as locals. Three hard warnings. (1) The annual tuition is not published as a single number, the per-ECTS figure does not multiply out sensibly, and the fee page lists two different master's application fees with no explanation — I verified all of that directly, so this is a fee page that cannot be trusted to arithmetic. Get a written annual euro figure and a written instalment count before he transfers anything. (2) It is taught in Portuguese. This programme runs Monday–Thursday 19:00–21:30 = 10 hours per week — exactly HALF the legal minimum. Important nuance that corrects a widespread misconception: títulos propios ARE an accepted study type for estancia por estudios, so the non-official award is NOT itself the problem; the timetable is. DJP does operate a real international-student service (djpmusicschool.com/comunidad/estudiantes-extranjeros) listing passport, 'Carta Certificación de matrícula otorgada por DJP Music School', medical insurance, proof of funds and housing, plus criminal-record and medical certificates for stays over 180 days; it warns 'DJP Music School no se hace responsable del resultado de la solicitud de visado' and refunds 60% of enrolment if the visa is refused. But it also tells applicants to 'confirmes el mínimo de horas que debes estudiar a la semana' with their consulate — DJP itself is pointing at the hours problem. That visa machinery almost certainly exists to serve DJP's FULL-TIME BA (Hons) and HND programmes, not this evening master.

_rec.visaEligible: UNVERIFIED AND DOUBTFUL — this is the decisive risk. Two things point in opposite directions. In favour: the course is genuinely full-time and in person, Monday to Friday, 25 hours a week, which clears Spain's ~20 h/week full-time test for an estancia por estudios. Against: microFusa's own 'Permisos y visados para estudiar en Microfusa' page (escuela.microfusa.com/permisos-y-visados) NO LONGER EXISTS — it 301-redirects to a generic school page, so the school has withdrawn its published visa guidance; and third-party Spanish immigration commentary states microFusa is not a centre registered/recognised for student-visa purposes, meaning most international applicants will not obtain the visa. DO NOT PAY A CENT until microFusa confirms IN WRITING (a) its centre authorisation number and issuing administration, and (b) that it issues an admission letter accepted for a long-stay estancia por estudios.

_rec.reputationSignals: POSITIVE: three decades of training producers, deep roots in the Spanish and Barcelona electronic-music scene, a pro-audio retail arm, named alumni including VICCO, a signed progression agreement with two real UK universities, a genuinely practical curriculum, small cohorts (24 max) and a hard 14-day statutory withdrawal right. _rec.recommendation: Be clear about what this is: it is not a master's and must never be entered in the same column as one. On craft it is the single best-matched curriculum in this batch for a DJ/producer — Ableton and Logic in year one, Pro Tools, studio technique, mastering, sound design and a final project in year two — and at €6,360 prepaid for year one it is honest value for the teaching. But he has a BSc already; a non-recognised Spanish vocational diploma adds no credential he can use in Tunisia, the EU or for any further study, and it comes with no funding and no confirmed visa basis. Two concrete actions if he pursues it at all: (1) get the centre-authorisation evidence and a written statement on the study visa BEFORE any payment — the removal of their own visa page is a warning sign, not a neutral fact; (2) ask for the year-two 2027-28 price in writing so he is budgeting €13,000 and not €6,800. _rec.program: Máster en Producción de Música Urbana
_rec.institution: SAE Institute Spain – Madrid and Barcelona campuses
_rec.qualification: NOW VERIFIED — and the finding is damaging. Official page states: 'Máster Profesional en Producción de Música Urbana acreditado por UDIMA' and 'Máster en Formación Permanente en Producción de Música Urbana acreditado por UDIMA (25 ECTS)', plus a SAE Diploma Profesional. TÍTULO PROPIO, not official. CRITICAL: 25 ECTS. Under Spanish Real Decreto 822/2021 art. 37.6, a 'Máster de Formación Permanente' must carry a MINIMUM of 60 ECTS (max 120). At 25 ECTS this award falls in the 'Experto' band (15–29 ECTS) — it is legally NOT a master of any kind, yet it is marketed as one. This is a serious mislabelling.
_rec.institutionType: International chain campus – specialist audio academy (SAE / Navitas)
_rec.focus: Urban music production — trap, reggaeton, hip-hop, dub, dancehall. Beatmaking and vocal production.
_rec.whatYouStudy: NOW VERIFIED. Semester 1: sound theory fundamentals, music theory, Akai MPC X sampling, production by subgenre (trap, reggaeton, hip-hop, dub, dancehall), audio processing, mixing techniques, sequencers (Ableton Live, FL Studio, Logic Pro X), vocal recording and processing. Semester 2: advanced mixing and production, hardware and modular synthesis (Moog Sub 37, Prophet 12, Doepfer), sound design, advanced harmony, live performance, in-the-box mastering, industry operations, artist management, digital marketing, copyright and contracts. Gear/software: Logic Pro, Ableton Live, FL Studio, Native Instruments, Universal Audio, Moog, Dave Smith, Doepfer, Elektron, Roland, Akai.
_rec.durationEcts: NOW VERIFIED: 8 months, 25 ECTS. Not 2 years. This is a short post-degree certificate, roughly one third of the study volume the word 'Máster' implies.
_rec.language: Spanish — CONFIRMED. International applicants must demonstrate Spanish proficiency in speaking, listening, reading and writing.
_rec.accreditationStatus: NOT OFFICIAL, and additionally MISLABELLED. Título propio via UDIMA, which classifies its own títulos propios as 'enseñanza no reglada y sin carácter oficial'. No ANECA verification, no RUCT entry, no EHEA standing, no doctoral access. Beyond that, the 25-ECTS volume is below the 60-ECTS statutory floor for a Máster de Formación Permanente under RD 822/2021 — so calling it a 'Máster' is not merely marketing gloss over a título propio, it is inconsistent with the Spanish regulation governing that exact award name. Treat the word 'Máster' in the title as unsupported.
_rec.visaEligible: DOUBTFUL — and materially worse than the 2-year audio programme. At 8 months it exceeds the 6-month threshold, so it triggers the medical-certificate and criminal-record requirements and can in principle support a long-stay student visa via SAE's Certificado de Admisión/Aceptación. But weekly contact hours are unpublished and Spanish consular assessment turns on full-time intensity; a 25-ECTS load spread over 8 months is thin (roughly 12–15 hours a week equivalent) and is exactly the profile that draws refusals. Do not assume approval. Get weekly contact hours in writing before applying.

_rec.portfolioSpec: No portfolio required — admission by questionnaire and interview only.
_rec.auditionSpec: No audition. Admission interview only, in Spanish.
_rec.englishTest: Not applicable — Spanish-language programme. IELTS is neither accepted nor relevant.

But the headline finding overrides it: a 25-ECTS award marketed under a protected award name whose statutory minimum is 60 ECTS. That is a documentation and honesty problem, not a technicality, and it is the kind of thing that will not survive scrutiny by a credential-evaluation body or a visa officer.

Newly established: 8-month duration, 25 ECTS, full two-semester module list, exact UDIMA award names, entry requirements, intakes. The decisive new finding is the conflict between the 25-ECTS volume and the 60-ECTS statutory minimum for a 'Máster de Formación Permanente' under RD 822/2021, verified against the BOE text.
_rec.recommendation: Decisive reason to avoid: it is sold as a 'Máster' but carries 25 ECTS, when Spanish law sets a 60-ECTS minimum for the very award name it uses — so he would pay master-level money for what is legally an 'Experto'-level certificate, in Spanish, from a non-official título propio route. Everything else is secondary, but it all points the same way: 8 months, no September intake, a thin credit load that weakens the visa case, and a genre (reggaeton, trap, dembow) that is Latin urban production, not the international club and electronic scene he is aiming at. The syllabus itself is respectable and the hardware is real — if he ever wanted this specific genre training he could take it as a short course without pretending it is a degree. As a master's route it should be struck off the list.

_rec.program: Máster en Producción de Audio (60 ECTS, 24 months) — with sister titles Máster en Producción de Música Electrónica (25 ECTS, 8 months), Máster en Producción Musical, Máster en Producción de Música Urbana and Máster en Industria Musical
_rec.institution: SAE Institute Spain — Madrid and Barcelona campuses (SAE Creative Media Institute, Navitas group); academic title issued by UDIMA (Universidad a Distancia de Madrid, private)
_rec.qualification: TÍTULO PROPIO — VERIFIED, with a three-way structure confirmed from SAE's own announcement of the UDIMA agreement. (a) Applicants WITH a prior university degree receive a 'Máster de formación permanente, acreditado por UDIMA y con una carga lectiva que oscila entre 25 y 60 ECTS, según el programa elegido'. (b) Applicants WITHOUT a university degree (but with 2+ years' professional experience) receive a 'título de Máster Profesional emitido por SAE Creative Media Institute España'. (c) Every route also carries the 'Diploma Profesional emitido por SAE Creative Media Education'. A 'Máster de Formación Permanente' is expressly a university's OWN permanent-education title — NOT a Máster Universitario Oficial, NOT ANECA-verified. He, holding a BSc, would take route (a).
_rec.institutionType: Specialist audio academy (international chain, campuses worldwide) partnered with a private distance university for the academic title
_rec.focus: Audio production, recording, mixing and mastering, music production, audio post-production for film and TV, sound design for video games, live sound, Dolby Atmos and immersive audio. Parallel dedicated titles in ELECTRONIC music production and urban music production.
_rec.durationEcts: IMPORTANT DISTINCTION — the input conflated two different products. VERIFIED: Máster en Producción de Audio = 24 MONTHS, 60 ECTS (Máster de Formación Permanente route), roughly 8 contact hours per week over 4 days, attendance compulsory. Máster en Producción de Música Electrónica = 8 MONTHS, 25 ECTS only. For a Tunisian needing a student visa and real depth, the 60-ECTS/24-month Producción de Audio is the substantive option; the 25-ECTS electronic-music title is a short course wearing the word 'Máster'.
_rec.language: Spanish — VERIFIED and binding. SAE requires international applicants to demonstrate the ability to 'hablar, escuchar, leer y escribir en castellano'. There is no English delivery.
_rec.intakes: TWO intakes per year — VERIFIED. Madrid: February 2026 and October 2026. Barcelona: October 2026 and February 2027. A September/October 2027 start is therefore realistic. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm 2027 dates.
_rec.whatYouStudy: VERIFIED module structure for Producción de Audio. Year 1: Principios del Sonido; Fundamentos de la Producción Musical; Técnicas de Grabación; La Producción de Audio y la Industria; Proyectos Creativos. Year 2: Planificación Empresarial, Marketing y Aspectos Legales; Composición Musical; Sonido en Directo; Sonido para Videojuegos; Proyectos Profesionales Avanzados. Embedded industry certifications: Pro Tools Specialist (level 110), Ableton Live Certified User, Wwise Certified User (level 110), Midas Pro Series operator, Digico SD Series operator. For contrast, the 25-ECTS Producción de Música Electrónica covers production fundamentals, sound and music theory, MIDI, audio processing, synthesizers, samplers and mixing in Ableton Live and Logic Pro X in term 1, then advanced techniques, hardware/modular synths, sound design, mastering, live performance and artist management in term 2 — the closest content match to his DJ/electronic goal, but at a third of the credit load.
_rec.facilities: VERIFIED: '8 estudios de audio' (eight specialised audio studios) plus a lab with multiple workstations, bookable through an online reservation system, across the Madrid and Barcelona campuses. Vendor certifications (Avid, Ableton, Audiokinetic, Midas, Digico) are published and genuine.
_rec.entryRequirements: VERIFIED: an official university degree — 'Grado, Licenciatura, Ingeniería Superior o Técnica, Arquitectura Superior o Técnica, Diplomatura o equivalente' — OR, failing that, a minimum of 2 years' demonstrable professional experience (which routes you to the SAE/UDIMA Máster Profesional instead). Age 18+ for international students (16+ for nationals). Demonstrated Spanish in all four skills. A compulsory admission interview with an educational adviser, by Zoom/Skype or in person. Non-EU applicants must obtain a student visa. Enrolment documentation: 'Formulario de admisión • Convenio de Matriculación • Oferta educativa • Fotografía tamaño carnet • Comprobante de la transferencia • Copia de visado (si fuera necesario)'.

A BSc Software Engineering from SMU MedTech qualifies him directly for the 60-ECTS Máster de Formación Permanente route. _rec.scholarships: VERIFIED on SAE Spain's becas page, assessed for a Tunisian applicant. (1) BECAS MEC — listed by SAE, but Ministry general scholarships are for OFFICIAL studies (grado / máster oficial), which this título propio is not, and non-EU nationals additionally need legal RESIDENCE in Spain, which a study stay does not confer. EFFECTIVELY DOUBLY EXCLUDED. (2) BECAS GENERALITAT DE CATALUNYA (non-university studies, 2026-2027) — €1,700 income-based, €2,700 relocation, €300–350 basic, €50–125 academic merit, plus variable amounts from €60; but tied to family income, Catalan residency and academic-performance conditions, and SAE lists it against its 'Título de Grado en Música'. A newly arrived non-EU student would not qualify on arrival. (3) YAMAHA MUSIC EUROPE FOUNDATION (YMEF) — €1,000–€2,000 single payment, for music students aged 25 OR UNDER who are 'formándose para desarrollar una carrera musical profesional' at a recognised European educational institution; applications typically February–March; available at BOTH campuses. THIS IS THE ONE SCHEME GENUINELY OPEN TO HIM — no nationality bar — provided he is 25 or under at application. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm the 2027 window. (4) SAE BARCELONA INTERNAL DISCOUNTS — Excelencia Bachillerato 60% (requires a Spanish Bachillerato average ≥9.0, which he cannot produce); Excelencia Primer Curso 60% (requires completing SAE year 1 with ≥9.0 — reachable only in year 2); Desempleo/ERTE 10% (requires Spanish SEPE documentation); Familias Numerosas 10% (Spanish official family status); Discapacidad 30% (≥33% recognised in Spain); Alumno Activo/Ex Alumno 40% (prior SAE enrolment); Familiares de Alumnos 20% (relative of an SAE student); Víctimas de Violencia de Género 40%; Familias de Acogida / refugiados ucranianos 100%. NONE is reachable by a newly arrived Tunisian at entry — every one requires a Spanish administrative certification or prior SAE enrolment. NOTE THE ONE EXCEPTION WORTH PLANNING FOR: 'Excelencia Primer Curso' gives 60% off SECOND-YEAR tuition for a ≥9.0 first-year average — on a 24-month programme that is a real, achievable target for a strong student and is worth putting in writing at offer stage.
_rec.paymentPlans: Partially verified. Enrolment requires signing a Convenio de Matriculación and a Payment Plan, with monthly direct debit as the standard model. A third-party listing describes 'Plan A' (single up-front payment with an early-payment discount) and 'Plan C' (monthly instalments), and notes that enrolling during an Open Day can secure the reduced Plan A price while still paying monthly — this is SECOND-HAND and must be confirmed in writing. Instalment counts, any interest and administrative charges are UNVERIFIED. PRACTICAL WARNING: Spanish monthly direct debit normally requires a Spanish bank account, which he cannot open before arrival — ask explicitly whether the first instalments can be paid from a non-Spanish account or by international transfer.
_rec.accreditationStatus: NOT OFFICIAL. VERIFIED: the academic award is a UDIMA 'Máster de formación permanente' of 25–60 ECTS depending on programme, or a 'Máster Profesional' — both are títulos propios of a private distance university, not ANECA-verified, not registered as official titles in RUCT, conferring no automatic EHEA recognition and no right of entry to a Spanish doctorate. SAE's own award is a 'Diploma Profesional', a vocational certificate rather than a degree. The vendor certifications (Avid Pro Tools Specialist 110, Ableton Live Certified User, Wwise Certified User 110, Midas Pro Series, Digico SD Series) are genuine industry credentials with real labour-market value — but they are industry certifications, not academic accreditation, and should not be confused with one.
_rec.visaEligible: YES — the clearest visa statement of any private option in this batch, though it is the school's own claim rather than a government guarantee. VERIFIED quote from SAE's UDIMA agreement announcement: 'En ambos casos, las titulaciones permiten acceder al visado de estudiante para alumnos internacionales' — i.e. both the UDIMA Máster de Formación Permanente route AND the SAE Máster Profesional route are stated to support a student visa. SAE additionally runs a dedicated 'Tu VISA de estudiante' page setting out two routes: applying at the Spanish Consulate with jurisdiction over his residence (recommended at least 3 months ahead, but confirm with the consulate as it varies by country), or applying for a study authorisation from within Spain in regular status at least 1 month before the legal stay expires. The admission documentation list expressly includes 'Copia de visado (si fuera necesario)'. CAVEAT: because the title is a título propio, issuance is not automatic — Spanish consulates assess contact hours and centre authorisation, and this programme is only about 8 contact hours per week over 4 days, which is on the low side for full-time study. GET THE VISA POSITION CONFIRMED IN WRITING, referencing the weekly contact hours, before paying anything.

It is the only programme here that openly accepts any bachelor's degree, requires no portfolio and holds no audition, which matters enormously for someone whose portfolio is still being built. It also carries the clearest published statement on student visas and the most job-relevant certifications. Three conditions, though, and they are not small. FIRST, LANGUAGE: it is taught entirely in Spanish and SAE requires all four skills; he has roughly 14 months before a September/October 2027 start, so if he is serious he should start Spanish NOW and target B2 — this is the make-or-break item. SECOND, PRICE: nothing is published, so he must obtain the written Oferta educativa, Offer Letter and Payment Plan before committing, and must not rely on the ~€14,000 figure circulating online, which refers to the bachelor's degree, not the master. THIRD, EXPECTATIONS: he would receive a título propio, not an official Spanish degree — the industry certifications, not the academic title, are what he is actually buying. Two concrete actions: apply for the YAMAHA MUSIC EUROPE FOUNDATION award (€1,000–2,000, under-25, NO nationality bar — the only scholarship in this batch genuinely open to him), and ask at offer stage about the 'Excelencia Primer Curso' 60% second-year discount for a ≥9.0 first-year average, which on a 24-month programme is a real and achievable saving. _rec.accreditationStatus: NOT OFFICIAL — and now verified by the strongest possible evidence, TAI's own side-by-side listing. TAI's master catalogue separates its awards into two groups. Only THREE are official Másteres Universitarios: Interpretación Audiovisual, Fotografía Artística y Documental, and Creación de Animación Audiovisual. The Máster en Producción Musical is NOT among them — it sits under the propios, tagged 'Título propio · 60 ECTS'. So: no ANECA verification, no EHEA official master status, no PhD access. The institution's name — 'Escuela Universitaria' — invites precisely the misreading he must avoid; the school genuinely holds official programmes, but this is not one of them.
_rec.visaEligible: UNVERIFIED, but the fee structure is a warning worth reading carefully. TAI is charging half as much and promising less for the propio track. That does not prove a título propio cannot carry a residence permit (Spanish rules do accept títulos propios for estancia por estudios provided the course exceeds 90 days and delivers 20+ contact hours a week in person, and a full academic year at 60 ECTS should clear that), but it does mean TAI's own visa service is materially thinner for this programme. Get the position in writing before paying anything.

If his true goal is "work in international electronic music" rather than "be the person at the desk", this is a real door — and his software-engineering degree is a genuine asset in ticketing and music-data roles. Two hard conditions before he would ever consider it: get the total non-EU price in writing, and get written confirmation that UAX will issue a carta de admisión supporting a student visa for a título propio. If the official-degree route matters to him more than the subject, the sister Máster Universitario en Gestión de la Cultura, el Deporte, los Medios y el Entretenimiento (Málaga) is the one genuinely ANECA-official title in this family.

Spain's official management criteria for estancia por estudios (Ministerio de Inclusión, June 2025, under RD 1155/2024) require studies of at least 91 calendar days, full-time enrolment defined as at least 90% of the credits, and a weekly teaching load of 'un mínimo de 20 horas semanales', with a narrow exception for intensive or concentrated programmes only where at least 12 of those hours are delivered in person. UFV publishes the timetable as Monday to Friday, 18:00 to 20:00 — exactly 10 contact hours per week. That fails the 20-hour general rule outright AND falls below the 12-in-person-hour exception floor. The programme's four-month span (September 2026 to January 2027) does clear the 91-day minimum, but the teaching load does not clear either threshold. He should treat this as definitively NOT a relocation route, not as an open question. Its only viable use is as a paid short course taken while already legally resident in Spain on some other basis.

Module 3 — production processes and creative direction (32 hours). Module 4 — post-production, mixing, mastering and industry contracts (57 hours). Roughly 152 contact hours in total. Taught inside a working production facility.

RED FLAGS: it is marketed alongside master's programmes but is a 30-ECTS, three-month, two-hours-a-night evening certificate; UFV's own published price breakdown does not add up (EUR 6,100 headline versus EUR 6,500 in components); and there is no degree at the end of it.

On the positive side it is a genuinely good short skills course — real facilities, Warner Music Spain professionals, and two portable certifications (Avid PT101/PT110 and a perpetual Ableton Live 12 Suite licence) that he would otherwise pay for separately. The only scenario where it makes sense is as a paid upskilling course taken once he is already legally resident in Madrid on some other basis. _rec.portfolioSpec: Round 1 (documents only, candidate not present): (1) a LIST of all own sound works made during bachelor's study — audiovisual/multimedia works, music recordings, radio and theatre sound design — each with title, genre, director, production company, duration, year; (2) TWO audiovisual works on which the applicant made a substantial sound contribution, each with a detailed written explication; (3) the applicant's own theoretical work or an essay in the field; (4) a written project/statement for the master's study at FAMU (intended specialisation, expected outcomes, elective courses wanted at FAMU or other universities, interest in international internships). All works must be the applicant's own authorship, confirmed by a signed declaration. Works are uploaded by the separate works deadline (1 Sept in the 2026/27 cycle), not with the application form.
_rec.auditionSpec: Round 2 is an IN-PERSON oral examination in Prague: interview testing technical and artistic knowledge of the field, musical competence, and readiness for master's-level work, plus defence of the submitted works and the study project.

_rec.scholarships: THIS ENTRY EARNS ITS PLACE BECAUSE IED'S DSU BANDO IS THE CLEAREST PUBLISHED PROOF THAT A NON-EU STUDENT AT AN ITALIAN PRIVATE ACADEMY CAN WIN REGIONAL STATE AID. All of the following are VERIFIED verbatim from Bando DSU 25/26, BAN 8203 rev 06 of 04/09/2025, total fund €354,392.15 under D.G.R. XII/4704 of 14.07.2025. ELIGIBILITY expressly includes 'i cittadini di Stati non appartenenti all'Unione Europea' alongside Italians and EU citizens, for students admitted or enrolled on a Diploma Accademico di Primo or Secondo Livello at Milan, Rome, Turin, Cagliari or Florence. INCOME TEST: ISEE Universitario must not exceed €26,516.70 AND ISPE must not exceed €57,645.03 — 'I due limiti indicati devono essere rispettati entrambi congiuntamente', breaching either one disqualifies. MERIT for a first-year II livello student: simply be regularly enrolled by 31 October and hold the first-level title by 31 January; full confirmation then requires 40 credits by 10 August. AMOUNTS, inclusive of the €140 regional-tax reimbursement and an €818 meal allowance: in sede €3,383 / €2,950 / €2,114 by income band; pendolari €4,754 / €4,134 / €3,254; FUORI SEDE €8,134 / €7,073 / €5,776. Awards can rise by up to 40% for students with disability. THE DECISIVE PROVISION, quoted from footnote 7: 'L'Art. 13 comma 3 del D.P.C.M. 9/04/2001 stabilisce che gli studenti stranieri non appartenenti all'Unione Europea sono considerati comunque studenti fuori sede indipendentemente dalla sede della loro residenza in Italia ad eccezione del caso in cui il nucleo familiare dello studente risieda in Italia' — a Tunisian student is AUTOMATICALLY placed in the highest bracket, €5,776 to €8,134 a year, provided the accommodation is paid for and a registered rental contract is filed by the deadline (failure to file downgrades him to 'pendolare'). NON-EU DOCUMENTATION: an ISEEU-ISPEU parificato is required, built from foreign family-composition and income declarations issued by the official tax agency of the country of residence — 'L'autocertificazione relativa a redditi e/o patrimoni esteri non può essere presentata', self-certification is refused outright — all translated into Italian and legalised. Tunisia appears on neither the London-Convention exemption list (Moldova, Sweden) nor the Apostille shortcut list (Albania), so full consular legalisation applies. A floor applies: 'il reddito degli studenti stranieri appartenenti a paesi Extra-EU non potrà essere inferiore a € 7.002,97 annuali', the visa subsistence minimum. Free ISEEU assistance is available via CAAF CGIL Lombardia (Corso di Porta Vittoria 43, Milan) under an IED agreement. EXCLUSIONS THAT MATTER: anyone already holding an equal or higher qualification is excluded (his BSc does NOT block a II livello application); anyone benefiting from another income- or merit-based grant for the same year is excluded; Foundation-course students are excluded; and the bando covers ONLY Diploma Accademico di I/II livello, so IED's one-year 'Master' courses get nothing. IED separately runs a commercial scholarship competition covering 50% of tuition on Master of Arts and Master programmes, open to international students — details UNVERIFIED on the pages read, request the current bando.
_rec.paymentPlans: UNVERIFIED — not published in the DSU bando or the tariffario. Request the instalment schedule in writing. Remember DSU is not a fee waiver: fees are paid in full first and the scholarship arrives afterwards in instalments.

And note again that IED's dedicated SOUND DESIGN programme is a FIRST-level triennio, not a master.
_rec.visaEligible: YES for the Diploma Accademico route. IED publishes a dedicated 'Procedure per studenti richiedenti visto — Universitaly' document, the DSU bando treats the permesso di soggiorno as a routine document for extra-EU students, and the €7,002.97 visa subsistence figure is written into the income rules. This is a standard, well-supported non-EU pathway.
_rec.applicationOpens: Admission and enrolment procedures for the Diploma Accademico di 2° Livello are published annually (the 2026 edition is dated April 2026). DSU applications opened 9 September 2025 for 2025/26 — PRIOR CYCLE, expect early September 2027 for the 2027/28 round.
