Verified 2025/26 DSU calendar: applications 9 September to 7 November 2025; provisional rankings from 28 November 2025, and from 6 February 2026 for first-year II livello students; rental contract and proof of rent payment for fuori sede status by 10 December 2025. Enrolment regularisation by 31 October. Expect the 2027/28 window to run early September to early November 2027.
_rec.reputationSignals: Major international private design chain inside the AFAM system, campuses across Italy, Spain and Brazil, a substantial published DSU fund (€354,392.15 for 2025/26), a formal CAAF agreement to help foreign students obtain the ISEE parificato, and now-published transparent tariffs. RED FLAGS for this candidate: NO second-level sound-design or music programme (Sound Design is BA-level only); a flat top-band non-EU price of €20,800 a year with no income relief; the Rome interactive programme is Italian-taught; and the DSU documentation burden for a Tunisian is severe.
_rec.recommendation: IED is not a destination for him and should not be on his shortlist as one — its only audio programme is an undergraduate triennio, and the second-level catalogue (verified in full) contains nothing in sound or music. Worse, the tariff is now confirmed: as a Tunisian resident he would pay €20,800 a year flat, €41,600 over two years, the same as the highest Italian income band, for a programme that is not in his field and is taught in Italian. Keep IED in the file for one reason only: its DSU bando is the clearest published proof that a non-EU student at an Italian PRIVATE academy is automatically classified 'fuori sede' under Art. 13(3) d.p.c.m. 9/04/2001 and can therefore win €5,776-€8,134 a year in regional state aid. That is a mechanism he should exploit at Saint Louis (LazioDisco) instead. Two practical warnings that transfer to any Italian application: start collecting the Tunisian tax-agency income certificates, property statements, family-composition certificate, sworn Italian translations and consular legalisations at least four to five months before the September-November window — self-certification is refused outright and employer letters are not accepted; and file a registered rental contract before the December deadline or he is downgraded from fuori sede (€8,134) to pendolare (€4,754), losing over €3,000.
_rec.verificationNotes: The DSU bando PDF was fetched in full and every figure previously carried was checked against the source text and CONFIRMED: €354,392.15 fund; ISEE €26,516.70 and ISPE €57,645.03 jointly; fuori sede €8,134/€7,073/€5,776; in sede €3,383/€2,950/€2,114; pendolari €4,754/€4,134/€3,254; €140 regional-tax reimbursement and €818 meal allowance included; €7,002.97 extra-EU income floor; the Art. 13(3) automatic fuori-sede rule quoted verbatim; deadlines 09.09.2025-07.11.2025 and 10.12.2025; exclusions for prior equal/higher titles, other grants and Foundation students; CAAF CGIL Lombardia agreement; Tunisia absent from the Moldova/Sweden and Albania exemption lists. NEW FINDINGS THAT CORRECT THE ENTRY: (1) TUITION IS NOW VERIFIED, not unpublished — non-EU/non-EEA residents pay €2,500 + €18,300 = €20,800 per year for 2026/27, the top band, with no income relief; (2) the regional enrolment tax for 2026/27 is €190, not €140 — the €140 figure is the 2025/26 DSU reimbursement amount and the two should not be conflated; (3) the complete biennio catalogue was enumerated and contains NO sound design or music programme at second level anywhere in Italy — this is now positively confirmed; (4) the Rome Interactive Environments course is taught in ITALIAN and currently advertises an OCTOBER 2027 start, 120 CFA, with a headline '€8,500 a partire da' that is the EU Fascia I price and is misleading for a non-EU applicant.

Mohole advertises a "Laurea Europea Bachelor of Arts — riconosciuto in UE, UK e USA", EQF Level 6, 180 ECTS. It also issues an Attestato di competenza professionale from Regione Lombardia and RSL (Rockschool London) certifications. It is NOT a MUR/AFAM Diploma Accademico and Mohole is NOT in the AFAM system. The one-year option (60 ECTS) is simply year one of the same undergraduate course — not a postgraduate qualification of any kind.
_rec.institutionType: Private academy of cinema, visual arts, music and writing (Milan, operating since 2003). Accredited as a training provider by Regione Lombardia; a member school of the private EABHES network. Not an AFAM institution and not a university.
_rec.accreditationStatus: NOT OFFICIAL in the Italian system — and the accreditation claim is now RESOLVED rather than merely doubted. Accrediting body: EABHES, verified on eabhes.eu as "one of the largest PRIVATE networks of internationally recognised professional and academic institutions", ~60 member schools, ~300 accredited programmes, self-described as aligned to ECTS and the Bologna Process. EABHES is a PRIVATE ASSOCIATION, not a state or national accreditation agency, and its own site does not claim its awards are state-recognised degrees. What this means in practice: the "Bachelor of Arts / Laurea Europea" carries NO valore legale in Italy — it is not a titolo di studio recognised by MUR, cannot be used for Italian public competitions, and is not automatically recognised by any EU, UK or US authority despite the marketing wording "riconosciuto in UE, UK e USA". Recognition would fall to each receiving institution or employer case by case. The only credentials here with a defined Italian legal identity are the regional Attestato (Regione Lombardia) and the RSL music certifications. So: the prior entry's red flag was correct on substance — the marketing overstates what a private-network accreditation delivers — but the awarding body IS named, just not the kind of body the wording implies.
_rec.focus: Music production and sound design — genuinely and precisely on-topic for him: DJ technique, DJ live performance, Ableton Live, Logic Pro, game audio, AI in music. Content-wise it is the closest match in Milan to what he says he wants.
_rec.durationEcts: 3 years / 180 ECTS (EQF 6 claimed), or a 1-year / 60 ECTS single annuality which is year one of the same course. Monday–Friday full-time attendance. October 2026 start.
_rec.language: ITALIAN. English is taught only as a subject (Inglese 1/2/3). No English-taught delivery.
_rec.intakes: One October intake per year (October 2026 for the current cycle). Separate short evening/weekend courses run through 'Formazione Continua'.
_rec.applicationOpens: Rolling. Entry is by booking a 'colloquio conoscitivo' (orientation interview) online at any time; a 'Super Early Bird' promotion rewards enrolling well ahead.

_rec.entryRequirements: Orientation interview (colloquio conoscitivo). No prior experience required — the school's own wording is "si parte da zero" ("you start from zero"). A secondary-school diploma is required for conferral of the Bachelor of Arts; minimum age 18 for the professional competency certificates. _rec.tuitionTotal: Approx. €25,500 for the three-year Bachelor of Arts at €8,500/year, BEFORE the undisclosed multi-year discount. €8,500 for the one-year annual course alone.
_rec.otherFees: UNVERIFIED — Mohole's dedicated costs page (/iscrizioni/costi-agevolazioni/) publishes NO figures at all: no enrolment fee, no materials fee, no exam or certification fee, no RSL certification cost. _rec.equipmentRequired: UNVERIFIED but materially certain: Logic Pro (macOS only) and Ableton Live are core from year one, so a Mac laptop plus DAW licences are effectively mandatory — realistically €1,500–3,000 up front. Headphones/controller likewise. None of this is costed by the school.
_rec.paymentPlans: PARTIALLY VERIFIED, all amounts undisclosed. Confirmed to exist on the school's own costs page: (1) a 'Super Early Bird' promotion that locks a reduced rate for early enrolment — amount NOT published; (2) a discount on total tuition for enrolling in the full three-year Bachelor up front rather than year by year — amount NOT published; (3) interest-free financing via a Deutsche Bank partnership with personalised terms and no activation fee. _rec.scholarships: UNVERIFIED and now looking weaker than the prior entry suggested. The costs page does NOT publish any scholarship amounts, criteria or eligibility, and says nothing about non-EU applicants. 'Borse di studio' are discussed only at the orientation interview. For a non-EU applicant who must budget before applying for a visa, an undisclosed discretionary discount decided in a sales conversation is not a financial plan.
_rec.visaEligible: NO / UNVERIFIED — and this is the decisive practical problem. Mohole is outside the MUR/AFAM system; its EABHES accreditation is private and confers no Italian legal recognition, which is what the Universitaly pre-enrolment route for a type-D study visa is built on. Neither the course page nor the costs page mentions international students, study visas, Universitaly or residence permits at all. Do not assume a residence permit is obtainable. For a Tunisian national this alone is close to disqualifying, regardless of how good the syllabus is.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: €8,500/year verified tuition; approx. €25,500 over three years before discounts; plus €1,500–3,000 of Mac/DAW equipment, plus undisclosed enrolment and certification fees, plus Milan living costs of roughly €12,000–15,000 per year. Realistic three-year all-in exposure: €65,000–80,000 — for a qualification with no Italian legal value and no clear visa route.
_rec.reputationSignals: POSITIVES: operating since 2003; the most on-topic curriculum in Milan for a would-be DJ/producer (DJ mix technique, DJ live performance, game audio in Unreal, AI and music); real in-house studios and booths; RSL Rockschool certification adds an externally-issued, internationally-legible music credential; claimed 82% of alumni working professionally (self-reported and unaudited). RED FLAGS, updated after verification: (1) the 'Laurea Europea riconosciuto in UE, UK e USA' wording is backed only by EABHES, a PRIVATE accreditation network — this is exactly the pattern of dressing a private-network validation in the language of state recognition; (2) the only Italian credential with defined legal identity is a regional attestation; (3) fees are published on the course page but the dedicated costs page hides every discount, scholarship and extra fee behind a phone call; (4) no AFAM/MUR status means no clear student-visa route and no ministerial protection if the school ever folds — see Accademia del Suono in this same batch, closed July 2026.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: Yes — no prerequisites at all. The school's own wording is "si parte da zero"; entry is by orientation interview and a secondary-school diploma is the only formal document needed for the BA. But this cuts against him, not for him: it is undergraduate-entry, so a graduate with a BSc would be starting a first degree over again, alongside school-leavers.
_rec.valueVerdict: AVOID — decisive reason: it is an unrecognised undergraduate qualification with no reliable non-EU student-visa route, at €8,500 a year. The syllabus being the best in Milan does not survive the fact that he probably cannot legally get into the classroom, and would leave with a bachelor's that Italy does not recognise.
_rec.recommendation: RIGHT SUBJECT, WRONG EVERYTHING ELSE — and verification has now hardened this from suspicion to fact. Three things changed since the prior entry: the €8,500/year fee is CONFIRMED on Mohole's own page; the awarding body is CONFIRMED as EABHES; and EABHES is CONFIRMED, from its own website, to be a private association rather than a state accreditation agency. So the 'Laurea Europea recognised in EU, UK and USA' is a private-network award marketed in the vocabulary of official recognition. Add the rest: it is an undergraduate course for a man who already has a degree, taught entirely in Italian, with no published visa pathway and no AFAM status to fall back on. If he ever contacts them, three questions in writing, and do not enrol without all three answered on paper: (1) is the Bachelor of Arts recognised by MUR and does it carry valore legale in Italy — yes or no; (2) can you issue the documentation for Universitaly pre-enrolment and a type-D study visa for a Tunisian national — yes or no; (3) send the full itemised cost sheet including enrolment fee, RSL certification fees and the actual value of the early-bird and three-year discounts. Expect the answer to (1) to be no and to (2) to be evasive. Until then, unusable.
_rec.verificationNotes: Mohole course page and costs page both fetched; eabhes.eu fetched to establish what the accreditation actually is. CORRECTIONS AND UPGRADES TO THE PRIOR ENTRY: (1) the accrediting body, previously flagged as unnamed, IS named — EABHES — and is verified as a PRIVATE association, not a state body; the substance of the red flag stands but the gap is closed. (3) Regione Lombardia accreditation as a training provider and RSL Rockschool certification confirmed. (4) Unreal Engine and MuseScore added to the verified software list. (5) Entry wording confirmed verbatim as 'si parte da zero', with a secondary-school diploma required for BA conferral and 18+ for the professional certificates. (6) The costs page was read in full and publishes NO figures whatsoever — the Super Early Bird, three-year discount, scholarships and Deutsche Bank financing are all confirmed to EXIST but every amount is withheld pending a phone call, and there is no mention of non-EU students or visas anywhere. STILL UNVERIFIED: all discount and scholarship amounts, any enrolment/materials/certification fee, and visa sponsorship. The /iscrizioni/ index path returns 404; /iscrizioni/costi-agevolazioni/ is the working costs URL.

BUT the relevant correction for him is different: this is contemporary art-music electroacoustic composition — scores, research-catalogue output, experimental studio work — not electronic dance music, DJ practice, or commercial production. The study-plan project topics confirm the register: 'interpretation, performance practice, style, musical understanding/analysis, improvisational methods, aesthetics, instrumental techniques, oral traditions, collaboration between composer and performer, the study of historical recordings, experimental exploration, cross-over projects'. There is no production, mixing, mastering or DJ content. Wrong discipline for his stated career goal even where the technology exists.

_rec.recommendation: KEEP THIS ENTRY, BUT AS A PRICE SIGNAL — DO NOT APPLY. Corrections made to the previous record, in order of importance. (1) THE COST WAS UNDERSTATED BY HALF: two years is EUR 68,000–70,000, not EUR 34,000–35,000; EUR 34,000 is the annual figure. (2) The English requirement is now verified and is a hard gate: IELTS 6.5 overall AND 6.5 in every single component, or TOEFL iBT 90, with no One Skill Retake and no MyBest Score — he has taken neither test. (3) There is a SECOND deadline the previous record missed: 15 December 2026 for the application, then 15 JANUARY for the portfolio/audition video upload. (4) The claim that the Grieg Academy has no electronic/electroacoustic capacity is WRONG — it has a Composition Research Group, an experimental studio under Prof. Daniel Péter Biró, and Assoc. Prof. Stylianos Dimou teaching electroacoustic composition and music technology at graduate level. The correct objection is not absence of technology but wrong genre: this is contemporary art-music composition with scores, not DJ practice or commercial production. (5) Verified figures replacing 'UNVERIFIED': semester fee NOK 700/semester (NOK 650 without the voluntary SAIH contribution); UDI proof of funds NOK 170,368 per year for 2026/27. (6) The portfolio requirement is an 'artist statement', not a 'two-page reflection'. Everything else in the previous record — NOK 401,704, the no-scholarships statements, the 15 December 2026 date, the no-instalments rule — checks out against the official pages. Bottom line for him: Norway is the most expensive unfunded destination in the sweep, UiB says twice in its own words that it offers no scholarships at all, the fee must be paid in full before the visa is even applied for, and the artistic bar is a 45-minute catalogue of notated and recorded compositions he does not have and cannot build in twelve months. Strike Norway from the funded list entirely.

_rec.valueVerdict: CONDITIONAL. But the entry wording assumes you already ARE an audio person, no degree-classification floor is stated so the studio-competence expectation carries the whole gate, and the full-time programme specification is titled MA while the page says MSc. Conditional on (a) a portfolio year that produces demonstrable studio and DAW competence, (b) written confirmation of the award title, and (c) accepting a roughly £15,000 self-funded tuition bill plus a £5,000 deposit to capture the scholarship.
_rec.recommendation: CORRECTIONS MADE. Two things in the prior record were wrong or incomplete and both matter. FIRST, fundingLevel was 'Check' and scholarships were recorded as 'Not stated / UNVERIFIED'. That is now corrected: Hertfordshire runs automatic, no-application international scholarships — a Chancellor's International Scholarship of £500–£4,000 assessed automatically from the course application, plus one-off postgraduate awards of £3,500 (deposit by 30 April), £3,000 (by 17 July) or £3,000 (by 14 August), plus a £1,000 full-payment discount. Awards generally do not stack, so assume about £3,000–£4,000, bringing net tuition to roughly £14,000–£15,000 — materially cheaper than the prior record suggested and cheaper than USW's headline. SECOND, a real cost was missing: those early scholarships require a minimum £5,000 TUITION DEPOSIT cleared by the stated date. That is a big early cash call he must plan for. CONFIRMED UNCHANGED: £17,950 international 2026/27, IELTS 6.5 with no band below 5.5, the 26/09/2027 start with apply links already live, the entry wording, and the Neve studio estate. The MSc-versus-MA discrepancy is CONFIRMED and is sharper than the prior record stated — it is specifically the FULL-TIME 2026 specification that reads 'MA Audio Engineering' while the part-time one reads 'MSc'. Since he would study full-time, get the parchment title in writing before paying a deposit. Net judgement: strong programme, best facilities, viable net cost, but of the two Herts music options this one has the narrower subject wording ('related subjects' rather than 'related discipline'), no stated classification floor to lean on, and content aimed at studio engineering rather than at becoming an artist. Prefer the MA Music Production and Artist Development unless he specifically wants to be an engineer rather than a producer.

Second, the entry wording asks for a music-family degree or five years of industry experience, and expects everyone to already know their way around a studio and a DAW; he has neither a music degree nor pro experience, so his admission depends on convincing the programme tutor with self-taught production work. Concrete plan if he wants it: spend the next twelve months building a real body of Ableton production and sound-design work, then email Bruce Aisher directly for a read on his eligibility before spending anything.

_rec.whatYouStudy: VERIFIED module-by-module from the official DCSL34 accreditation PDF. YEAR 1 (60 CFA): Storia della musica elettroacustica 6; Ritmica della musica contemporanea 6; Esecuzione e interpretazione della musica elettroacustica — Ambienti esecutivi e di controllo per il live electronics 6; Composizione musicale elettroacustica 18 (INDIVIDUAL lesson); Informatica musicale 6; Tecnologie e tecniche della ripresa e della registrazione audio 2; Analisi compositiva 6; Acustica degli spazi musicali 4; Lingua straniera comunitaria 6. YEAR 2 (60 CFA): Storia della musica elettroacustica 6; Esecuzione e interpretazione — Ambienti esecutivi multimodali e interattivi 6; Composizione musicale informatica 18 (INDIVIDUAL); Informatica musicale 6; Tecnologie e tecniche della ripresa e della registrazione audio 2; Acustica degli strumenti musicali 4; a scelta dello studente 6; Prova finale (COME/02, composizione musicale elettroacustica) 12. THE DECISIVE DETAIL, newly verified from the published syllabus of Prof. Mario Salvucci (Informatica musicale COME/05): BIENNIO YEAR 1 = programming in Max MSP + java/javascript/nodejs; gen~/genexpr/C++ implementation of synthesis algorithms; adaptive filters; deterministic chaos, self-similar structures, strange attractors, flocking; MACHINE LEARNING — Markov chains, generative grammars, genetic algorithms, neural networks, GAN/StyleGAN/VAE, Stable Diffusion and GPT; ML libraries in Max (ml5js, MediaPipe, Magenta, Essentia); TensorFlow. BIENNIO YEAR 2 = introduction to C++ (control structures, functions, classes, pointers, dynamic memory) and to JUCE, culminating in implementing a full subtractive synthesizer AS A PLUGIN (MIDI in/sound out, oscillators, envelopes, polyphony and voice handling, modulation, filtering, GUI, host parameter communication); sound design of dynamic systems (artificial, natural, idiophone, mechanical, organic sources); Jitter, matrix/tensor operations, real-time video-audio interaction, OpenGL pipeline and SHADER PROGRAMMING, glitch/pixel-sort/databending algorithms, raytracing/raymarching; physical modelling (mass-spring, string, bowed instrument, waveguides). The composition syllabus (Prof. Silvia Lanzalone, COME/02) biennio year 1 covers composing the soundscape and acoustic ecology, intermedia Sound Art, SOUND INSTALLATION projects, multimedia/intermedia interaction with image and dance, electronic lutherie and sound design for augmented instruments (sensors, feedback systems, embedded systems); year 2 covers generative music, open forms, ecosystems and non-deterministic processes. Each year you deliver an original composition project supervised by the teacher.
_rec.entryRequirements: Diploma accademico di primo livello, OR a university degree (laurea) or equivalent recognised foreign qualification, plus passing the entrance exam. Non-EU visa applicants pre-enrol through Universitaly (the conservatory's own admission notice points explicitly to www.universitaly.it for entry, residence, enrolment and credential recognition). Registration is on Esse3 Cineca (https://consrm.esse3.cineca.it/) and the conservatory warns NOT to use SPID or CIE when registering. IELTS/TOEFL are irrelevant here — Italian is the operative language.
_rec.portfolioSpec: NOW VERIFIED — this was previously marked unverified and the actual spec is far lighter than assumed. From the official PDF 'PROGRAMMA DI AMMISSIONE A.A. 2025/2026 — CORSO ACCADEMICO DI SECONDO LIVELLO IN MUSICA ELETTRONICA' (https://conservatoriosantacecilia.it/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/musica-elettronica-biennio-25-26.pdf), there are TWO tracks. Candidates holding a first-level academic diploma IN MUSICA ELETTRONICA: Prova 1 = presentation and discussion of their first-level graduation thesis; Prova 2 = individual interview. CANDIDATES HOLDING ANY OTHER FIRST-LEVEL DEGREE — this is his track: Prova 1 = 'Presentazione di almeno due lavori originali – acustiche, elettroniche e/o audiovisive' (presentation of AT LEAST TWO original works — acoustic, electronic and/or audiovisual); Prova 2 = 'Colloquio individuale volto a verificare la motivazione e l'interesse all'approfondimento degli argomenti caratterizzanti il percorso di studi, nonché la coerenza del profilo formativo con gli obiettivi del corso' (individual interview on motivation, interest, and the coherence of the applicant's profile with the course objectives). NO minimum duration, NO minimum channel count, NO score requirement and NO stylistic restriction are published. 'Audiovisivi' is expressly allowed, so a video/audio piece counts. Caveat: this is the 2025/26 programme; confirm the 2027/28 version is identical.

Italian proficiency verification applies to foreign candidates; the exact format/level is NOT published on the pages read. NOT confirmed as remote-sittable.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: Yes — and the admission programme is explicitly built around it. The official programma di ammissione has a dedicated track headed 'Candidati in possesso di altro Diploma di Primo Livello', which is precisely a BSc holder from outside music. CORRECTION: the previously stated teaching attribution to Nicola Bernardini is NOT supported by the current published syllabi. The composition chair (COME/02) is M° Silvia Lanzalone, with M° Gemini also publishing programmes (Composizione Musicale Elettroacustica, Composizione Audiovisiva Integrata); Informatica musicale (COME/05) is M° Mario Salvucci. _rec.fitNotes: The strongest single find in this batch. Two things now verified change the picture completely: (1) the admission bar for a non-music graduate is just TWO original works plus an interview — the lowest documented bar of the six; (2) the biennio informatics syllabus is, in substance, an audio-software-engineering degree — he would spend year 2 writing C++ and building a polyphonic synthesizer plugin in JUCE, and year 1 doing ML for music in Max/TensorFlow. His BSc is a direct, compounding asset, not a handicap. The composition side is also more craft-oriented than assumed: sound design, DAW editing and montage, installations, augmented instruments, generative music. THE OBSTACLE IS ITALIAN — instruction is in Italian, the exam is on-site in Rome, and non-EU entry runs through Universitaly. Also note the aesthetic: this is art electronic music and sound art, not club or dancefloor production; it will make him a formidable sound designer and audio programmer, not a house producer. Realistic path: start Italian now (roughly 12 months to a usable level before the spring 2027 exam), and build two strong original audiovisual/electronic works.

_rec.entryRequirements: CONFIRMED AND VERBATIM: 'L'accesso ai corsi di II livello è riservato a chi in possesso di Diploma Accademico di I livello, di Laurea di I livello o di Diploma di Conservatorio vecchio ordinamento.' A Laurea di I livello — any three-year university degree — is accepted as a plain qualifying title. His BSc qualifies. _rec.auditionSpec: CONFIRMED, TWO-PART, and the second part is the problem. FIRST EXAM (early September): a WRITTEN component, 'Analisi di un brano elettroacustico' — analysis of an electroacoustic piece supplied by the commission. Exemption applies only to holders of a first-level diploma in Musica Elettronica or Musica Applicata, so HE IS NOT EXEMPT and must sit it. Plus an ORAL component: presentation of his own composed works, demonstrated knowledge of audio editing software, twentieth-century music history, history of electroacoustic music, acoustics and psychoacoustics, and a motivational interview. SECOND EXAM: verbatim, 'I candidati in possesso di diploma accademico di I livello di conservatorio sono esonerati dalla prova' — exemption is limited strictly to holders of a first-level CONSERVATOIRE academic diploma. A foreign university BSc does NOT exempt him. He must therefore sit a conventional musicianship examination covering ear training, lettura cantata (sight-singing), intonation and rhythm, and music history to triennio standard. For someone with no conservatory training and no music degree this is a real, substantial obstacle requiring roughly a year of dedicated preparation. CORRECTION: the previous report claimed the METS FAQ describes biennio admission more lightly, as merely a motivational interview, and flagged a 'tension' to resolve. The FAQ as fetched says no such thing — it simply links to the two admission-exam pages. There is no conflicting lighter description and no ambiguity to exploit. The exam pages are authoritative and they are strict.

Before the exam date, candidates email 'alcuni propri lavori (audio, multimediali, etc…) ed un curriculum vitae' to mets@conservatoriocuneo.it using PERMANENT sharing links (Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive) — explicitly not time-limited links. The oral then requires him to present and defend his own electronic compositions. NOTE ON A PREVIOUS OVERSTATEMENT: the previous report claimed the oral demands 'documentation of live-set executions', and treated that as a unique reward for a DJ practice. That specific requirement was not visible on the admission page in this pass. Live-set documentation is very likely welcome as supporting evidence, but do not treat it as a published requirement or as a structural advantage he can bank on.

_rec.tuitionEU: UNVERIFIED as to amounts — not published on the METS pages, and the conservatoire's fee page could not be reached in this pass. Mechanism per the Manifesto degli Studi: fees are organised in ISEE income bands (fasce di reddito), paid in up to three instalments via PagoPA through Isidata, governed by a separate Regolamento sulla contribuzione studentesca annexed to the Manifesto. Request that Regolamento from the segreteria for real figures.
_rec.tuitionNonEU: UNVERIFIED as to amount; mechanism documented and the lever is clear. Per the Manifesto, foreign students must present an ISEE parificato, and anyone who does not present an ISEE certificate is placed automatically in the HIGHEST income band. This is the single most important financial action item: filed correctly against a Tunisian family income the ISEE parificato should place him at or near the bottom band; not filed, he pays the maximum by default. There is no flat non-EU surcharge, which is favourable — but the exemption is not automatic, it must be actively claimed through the ISEE parificato process, which itself takes weeks and requires consular-legalised income documents from Tunisia. Start it early. Exact band figures: request the Regolamento contributi.
_rec.otherFees: Tassa regionale per il diritto allo studio (EDISU Piemonte) plus marca da bollo, payable with the first instalment via PagoPA through Isidata. Contributory irregularity blocks exam sittings, so payment discipline matters.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: Cannot be stated precisely without the contributi table. On the Italian ISEE pattern with a parificato filed, expect low hundreds of euros per year in fees; without it, the top band. Cuneo is a small Piedmontese city with the lowest living costs of the four locations, roughly €550–800/month, about 90 minutes from Turin. On cost alone this is the cheapest genuinely relevant option here — but cost is not what decides this one.
_rec.scholarships: EDISU Piemonte income-based scholarships are open to non-EU students and can cover fee exemption, a maintenance grant and subsidised housing — the main realistic route, and means-tested rather than merit-gated. MAECI Italian government scholarships are the national alternative and open to Tunisians. Admission exams sit in early September, teaching starts November. Non-EU applicants must complete Universitaly pre-enrolment on the Ministry's separate and earlier calendar. _rec.acceptsNonMusic: PARTIALLY — the formal door is open, the examination door is not. Entry qualification: a Laurea di I livello is explicitly and unconditionally accepted, so his BSc qualifies him to APPLY. But he is exempt from neither exam: he must sit the written electroacoustic analysis (exemption limited to Musica Elettronica/Musica Applicata first-level diploma holders) AND the second exam covering lettura cantata, intonation, rhythm, ear training and music history (exemption limited to conservatoire first-level diploma holders). That is a full musicianship examination for a man with no conservatoire training, no music degree and no formal theory. Eligible to apply is not the same as able to pass.
_rec.recommendation: VALUE VERDICT: CONDITIONAL. RATING: B. — A genuine, cheap, well-accredited degree at a serious electronic music school, blocked by one real obstacle that he can only remove with a year of deliberate work. Downgraded from the previous report's enthusiasm on two counts: the supposed FAQ 'tension' suggesting a lighter interview-based admission does not exist, and the 'documented live-set executions' requirement that was said to reward his DJ practice was not found on the page. Neither of the softening factors the previous agent relied on survives verification. What survives is solid: METS is a dedicated electronic music school inside a state conservatoire, a Laurea di I livello is unconditionally accepted as an entry title, the ISEE parificato should drive his fees to near-nothing, and Cuneo has the lowest living costs of any option here. Against that: he must pass an ear-training, sight-singing and music-history examination to triennio standard, plus a written analysis of an electroacoustic piece, in Italian, with no published language level to prepare against. Actions for autumn 2026, in writing to mets@conservatoriocuneo.it: (1) confirm that a foreign three-year Software Engineering degree does not exempt him from either prova, and ask what standard the second prova expects; (2) ask what Italian level is required or tested; (3) request the Regolamento contributi for the lowest ISEE parificato band. Practical judgement: he should apply here as a SECOND choice behind Rovigo, and treat the musicianship gap as work to do rather than a reason to walk away — basic ear training and solfège are the recurring obstacle across the whole Italian conservatoire sector and closing that gap raises his ceiling everywhere, not just at Cuneo. Do not make this his only application.

_rec.acceptsNonMusic: PARTIALLY — CORRECTED DOWNWARD. The previous report called this 'LIKELY THE MOST OPEN OF ANY ITALIAN OPTION FOUND' and speculated that a sound-engineering degree would have no reason to demand solfège. That is now disproven from source: the second prova covering lettura cantata, intonation, rhythm, ear training and music history applies to this track identically, with exemption limited to conservatoire first-level diploma holders. He would sit it. The entry TITLE is open (Laurea di I livello explicitly accepted) and the FIRST exam is genuinely well-matched to him — a practical mix, a foley reel, an engineering portfolio and a motivational interview are all things a software engineer can build toward. _rec.recommendation: VALUE VERDICT: CONDITIONAL. RATING: B. — CORRECTED SIGNIFICANTLY. The previous report flagged this as 'INVESTIGATE AS A PRIORITY — potentially the best fit of all' on the hypothesis that admission rested on an aptitude interview rather than a musicianship exam. That question is now answered, and the answer is no: METS publishes a dedicated Biennio TS admission page the previous agent never found, and it imposes the same second prova (lettura cantata, ear training, storia della musica) on anyone without a conservatoire first-level diploma. The previous record also cited the wrong source URL. This is not the open door it was billed as. What remains genuinely attractive, and it is not nothing: DCSL61 is a real state second-cycle degree in SOUND ENGINEERING, the subject closest to his actual background and stated career interest; the entry title requirement explicitly accepts his Laurea di I livello; and the first exam — mixing a supplied multitrack, presenting an original foley/video sound work, presenting prior engineering projects, and a motivational interview — is the most learnable and most engineer-friendly assessment of any programme here. His BSc is a real asset in that room. On cost it ties with DCSL34 for cheapest. Verdict for him: apply, but as a co-equal second choice with DCSL34 and behind Rovigo, and only if he commits to closing the ear-training and solfège gap during the portfolio year. Between the two Cuneo tracks he should prefer THIS one over DCSL34 — same musicianship hurdle, but a first exam that plays to his strengths instead of testing compositional skills he does not have. Actions: write to mets@conservatoriocuneo.it in autumn 2026 confirming that a foreign three-year Software Engineering degree exempts him from neither prova, asking the expected standard of the second prova, asking the required Italian level, and requesting the Regolamento contributi. Build a technical portfolio — foley to picture, multitrack recordings, mixes, masters, DSP work — not a compositional one. If Cuneo does not work out, DCSL61 also runs at Frosinone, Reggio Calabria and Vibo Valentia and those are worth checking, as entry rules vary by institution even under a shared ministerial code.

_rec.whatYouStudy: Theoretical foundations of informatics; digital and analogue processing of IMAGE AND SOUND SIGNALS; processing and transmission of multimedia streams over communication technologies, networks and services; interface and application development. Through compulsory-elective subjects a student can specialise narrowly in AUDIO INFORMATION PROCESSING rather than image or graphics. Creatively oriented subjects are built in so graduates can create and process multimedia works at an appropriate technical, aesthetic and artistic level; the faculty names 'audio technician and designer' as a target job.
_rec.entryRequirements: A completed first-cycle degree. CONFIRMED verbatim that a foreign graduate must submit, with the application or at latest at enrolment, a decision recognising equivalence of the first-cycle qualification from a competent Slovak institution, OR may ask UNIZA itself to recognise the document — UNIZA doing it in-house is a real convenience versus separate ministry nostrification. Slovak/Czech graduates in the SAME field with a weighted average up to 2.00 are admitted to Multimedia Engineering without an entrance exam; everyone else — including every foreign applicant and every applicant from a different field — goes through the selection procedure with an interview.
_rec.portfolioSpec: YES, AND THE SCORING IS NOW EXACT. CORRECTED AND SHARPENED from the previous record's vague 'up to 70 points combined'. The official rule sets a 100-point maximum built from: (a) weighted GPA from the first-cycle degree, scored 0-30 points scaled linearly from 30 points for a GPA of 1.50 or better down to 0 points at 3.00, then MULTIPLIED BY A COEFFICIENT OF 1.0 if the bachelor's was in the study field 'informatika' and 0.75 if in any other field; (b) at interview, demonstration of general knowledge of informatics and multimedia technologies, 0-40 points; (c) at interview, PRESENTATION OF THE APPLICANT'S CREATIVE ACTIVITY AND OUTPUTS in informatics and multimedia plus overall motivation to study, 0-30 points. Admitted candidates are ranked down to a 61-point floor. So a creative portfolio is worth up to 30 of 100 points and is scored ALONGSIDE, not instead of, IT knowledge — precisely the blend he will have. His Software Engineering degree should attract the 1.0 coefficient as an informatics-field award, but confirm that classification with the study office. Exact portfolio format still UNVERIFIED — request the current 'Zásady a pravidlá prijímacieho konania' and see https://kmikt.uniza.sk/index.php/uchadzaci/moznosti-studia/inzinierske-studium

RED FLAGS, and they are serious: (1) 'Máster' marketing against a 'Curso' award; (2) NO price published anywhere, and the school blocks automated access to its own site; (3) no ECTS and no accreditation of any kind; (4) a part-time 8-hours-per-week schedule with no student-visa value for a non-EU national; (5) conflicting published durations (248 vs 500 hours); (6) only 2 aggregator reviews of the school overall, averaging 3.0/5, one of which reads 'No está preparado'.

Structurally it is disqualifying regardless of content: eight contact hours a week cannot support a Spanish student visa, so as a non-EU national he could not legally relocate to Barcelona on this programme at all. Add no accreditation, no ECTS, no published price, a school that blocks its own pages from being read, and marketing that calls a 'curso' a 'máster', and the verdict is straightforward. The Atmos 7.4.1 studio and the free Pro Tools licence are real assets and would matter to someone already living in Barcelona who wanted film sound — that person is not him. It is a legally distinct category from 'Máster Universitario', which is the ANECA-verified official degree. The words 'Máster' and 'UDIMA' on the marketing page do not make it official.

(2) AWARD: a título propio, not an official degree, despite three master-sounding names. (3) PRICE: no published figure at all for a two-year commitment, which is indefensible for a budget-sensitive self-payer. (4) VISA: published contact time of ~8 hours per week is well below the full-time intensity Spanish consulates expect, so the residence permit is at real risk. On top of all four, the content drifts from what he actually wants — this is general audio engineering, post-production, live sound and game audio, not club music, DJing or electronic performance. If he insists on pricing one SAE Spain programme, this is the one to price-check, and he should demand weekly hours, total two-year cost and the exact UDIMA award name in writing before any payment. But an accredited route, or Berklee Valencia MPTI with a scholarship, dominates it comfortably.
_rec.verificationNotes: Official course page fetched and read in this pass — the only programme in this batch I was able to re-verify at source before the session's web-fetch and web-search budgets were exhausted. NEWLY CONFIRMED: full 12-module curriculum; five industry certifications; eight studios with named equipment and online booking; 24-month in-person duration; both UDIMA award names; 60 ECTS on the Formación Permanente; entry requirements for domestic and international applicants; Spanish-proficiency requirement; intake dates. I could not capture the verbatim Spanish wording on weekly hours before the budget ran out — that specific number must be reconfirmed with SAE in writing, since the whole visa analysis turns on it.

Entrance score = 10% dossier + 30% Stage I + 60% Stage II (the guide's summary table shows 10/70/20 — inconsistent in the source). _rec.program: Звукорежисура (Sound Engineering) — Master's degree, specialty B5 Musical Art
_rec.institution: Національна академія керівних кадрів культури і мистецтв / National Academy of Culture and Arts Management (NAKKKiM)
_rec.publicPrivate: PUBLIC — CONFIRMED. I extracted the text of the rector's order on 2026-2027 tuition for foreign citizens: it is headed 'МІНІСТЕРСТВО КУЛЬТУРИ УКРАЇНИ / НАЦІОНАЛЬНА АКАДЕМІЯ КЕРІВНИХ КАДРІВ КУЛЬТУРИ І МИСТЕЦТВ', is signed 'Ректор Валерій МАРЧЕНКО', and enacts a decision of the academic council of 27 April 2026, protocol No 9, effective 29 April 2026. A state institution subordinate to the Ministry of Culture. No correction needed.
_rec.language: UKRAINIAN, IN PRACTICE — AND THIS IS NOW VERIFIED, NOT SPECULATION. THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT CORRECTION IN THIS RE-CHECK. The official 2026 OPP does state 'Мова (и) викладання: Українська, англійська'. But the SAME DOCUMENT, in section 9, settles the question against the English reading. It states verbatim: 'Навчання іноземних здобувачів вищої освіти: Отримання вищої освіти іноземними здобувачами можливе після вивчення курсу української мови.' — 'Education of foreign students: obtaining higher education by foreign students is possible AFTER completing a course in the Ukrainian language.' The Academy's own programme document therefore requires him to complete Ukrainian language study before he can study at all. The previous record said this was UNVERIFIED and should be assumed; it is now VERIFIED from the official OPP and it is a hard blocker. The 'англійська' in the language line is explained by a single taught module, ОДЗ.03 'Ділова іноземна мова' (Business Foreign Language, 3 ECTS) — a foreign-language subject inside a Ukrainian-medium degree, not an English-taught route. The department's own web page separately lists the language of instruction as Ukrainian.
_rec.languageRequirement: Ukrainian, preceded by a Ukrainian language course — CONFIRMED as a requirement in principle by the OPP text quoted above. The specific level, the certificate, and whether the preparatory course is a full підготовче відділення year remain UNVERIFIED at institutional level; NAKKKiM does not publish a readable foreign-applicant language rule. Ask the admissions office. Do NOT read the OPP's 'Українська, англійська' line as removing the Ukrainian requirement — the same document contradicts that reading.
_rec.qualification: Магістр музичного мистецтва (Master of Musical Art) — CONFIRMED VERBATIM from the OPP: 'Кваліфікації мовою оригіналу: Магістр музичного мистецтва'; level 'НКР України – 7 рівень, FQ-EHEA – другий цикл, EQF-LLL – 7 рівень'; 'Тип диплому: диплом магістра, одиничний, 90 кредитів ЄКТС'. Specialty B5 'Музичне мистецтво' in field of knowledge B 'Культура, мистецтво та гуманітарні науки', built on the Ukrainian state standard for specialty 025 'Музичне мистецтво' (MON order of 04.03.2020 No 358). A genuine second-cycle state degree; Ukraine is an EHEA member, so it is recognisable in the EU via ENIC-NARIC.
_rec.accreditationStatus: CONDITIONAL / DEFERRED — CONFIRMED VERBATIM, and the previous record was exactly right. The OPP states: 'Освітньо-професійна програма «Звукорежисура» (ідентифікатор у ЄДЕБО 35623) акредитована умовно (відкладена акредитація) рішенням Національного агентства із забезпечення якості вищої освіти від 13.01.2026, протокол № 1 (92), акредитаційна справа № 1769/АС-25.' Conditional accreditation means NAZYAVO found shortcomings and set a remediation period with re-assessment to follow. It is a valid accreditation and the degree is a state degree, but it is precisely the status that adds friction to later foreign recognition. Check the current status on the NAZYAVO register before applying and ask what the identified shortcomings were.
_rec.institutionType: National academy under the Ministry of Culture. The programme sits in the Кафедра музичного мистецтва within the Навчально-науковий інститут перформативних мистецтв. The department also runs bachelor's programmes in Звукорежисура and Музичний продакшн (both 240 ECTS, 3 years 10 months).
_rec.focus: CORRECTED. The previous record described this as 'the closest thing in the four countries to a music-production master's'. Having now read the actual component list, that is wrong. This is a RESEARCH-AND-TEACHING master's in sound engineering, not a production master's. See whatYouStudy.
_rec.whatYouStudy: MAJOR CORRECTION — THE PREVIOUS MODULE LIST WAS NOT THE MASTER'S CURRICULUM. The previous record listed Mastering, Sound Engineering in MIDI, Sound-technical Apparatus, Multimedia Technologies, Creative Mixing Techniques, Digital Sound Recording, Electronic Music, Audiovisual Producing, Fundamentals of Sound Design and Postproduction as the syllabus. Those are BACHELOR-level subjects from the department's document library. I extracted the actual master's component table from the official 2026 OPP. The real 66 ECTS of mandatory components are: GENERAL CYCLE, 9 ECTS — ОДЗ.01 Methodology and Organisation of Scientific Research (3), ОДЗ.02 Higher-School Pedagogy and the Teaching Mastery of the Lecturer (3), ОДЗ.03 Business Foreign Language (3). PROFESSIONAL CYCLE, 29 ECTS — ОДФ.01 The Art of Sound Engineering (5), ОДФ.02 Methodology of Teaching Sound Engineering (5), ОДФ.03 Performance Technologies in Scientific Research (5), ОДФ.04 Musical Acoustics (5), ОДФ.05 Producing Activity in Musical Art (5), ОДФ.06 Creative-Performance Workshop of the Sound Engineer (4). PRACTICE, 15 ECTS — studio (3), concert (3), pedagogical (6), pre-diploma (3). ATTESTATION, 13 ECTS — preparation of the master's qualifying work (10.5), defence (1), attestation exam (1.5). Plus 24 ECTS of free electives (6 x 4). Total 2700 hours / 90 ECTS, split 66 mandatory (73.33%) / 24 elective (26.67%). READ WHAT THAT MEANS FOR HIM: only about 9 ECTS of the mandatory load is hands-on craft (The Art of Sound Engineering plus the Creative Workshop), against 8 ECTS of pedagogy and teaching methodology, 8 ECTS of research methodology, 6 ECTS of PEDAGOGICAL practice, and a 13 ECTS thesis-and-exam block. The degree trains sound-engineering LECTURERS AND RESEARCHERS. The general profile text does genuinely include the strands the previous record quoted — computer musicology, digital and multimedia technologies in audio production, electrical engineering, musical acoustics, and 'технології штучного інтелекту для аналізу, синтезу та обробки аудіо контенту' (AI technologies for the analysis, synthesis and processing of audio content) — but those are described as the programme's subject area, not as a set of production modules. Attestation is by public defence of a qualifying work plus an attestation exam; the OPP requires the thesis to present 'науково обґрунтоване розв'язання складної наукової задачі або мистецької проблеми' — a scientifically grounded solution to a complex research or artistic problem. For a man who wants to be an international DJ and producer, this is an academic degree with a studio attached, not a producer's education.
_rec.durationEcts: 90 ECTS, 1 year 4 months — CONFIRMED VERBATIM from the OPP ('диплом магістра, одиничний, 90 кредитів ЄКТС, термін навчання: 1 рік 4 місяці') and from the department page. Both очна (full-time) and заочна (part-time) forms, each 1 year 4 months. Internal split confirmed: general cycle 9 ECTS (10%), professional cycle 81 ECTS (90%), of which 57 mandatory and 24 elective.

The OPP lists the instruments and equipment base as 'музичний інструментарій, джерельна база, звукотехнічне обладнання, програмне забезпечення, мультимедійні засоби'. _rec.scholarships: UNVERIFIED and realistically none. Ukrainian state-order (державне замовлення) places at arts institutions are generally reserved for Ukrainian citizens and specific protected categories; other foreign nationals are admitted on a paying basis within quotas. No international scholarship scheme is published by NAKKKiM.
_rec.visaEligible: Legally yes — Ukraine issues type D student visas and temporary residence permits to enrolled foreign nationals through a state electronic invitation system. But legal eligibility is not the operative question here; see the recommendation.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: YES ON THE PUBLISHED RULE — CONFIRMED VERBATIM ('Ступінь бакалавра, спеціаліста, магістра', no subject named). This is the most open entry rule of the three. But it is now clear that the openness is neutralised by the language prerequisite in the same document, and by a curriculum that turns out to be a teaching-and-research degree rather than a production one. Confirm the content of the professional entrance examination before relying on the open rule.
_rec.recommendation: DO NOT APPLY — AND THE ACADEMIC CASE FOR IT IS WEAKER THAN THE PREVIOUS RECORD CLAIMED. That record called this 'academically the best-matched programme in this slice' with a syllabus 'close to ideal' for a software engineer who wants to produce. Having extracted the actual master's component table from the official OPP, I am correcting that outright. The 90 ECTS break down as roughly 9 ECTS of hands-on craft (The Art of Sound Engineering, Creative-Performance Workshop) against 8 ECTS of pedagogy and teaching methodology, 8 ECTS of research methodology, 6 ECTS of pedagogical practice and a 13 ECTS thesis-and-attestation block. Ukrainian arts master's degrees of this shape train lecturers and researchers; the qualifying work must present a scientifically grounded solution to a research or artistic problem. That is not what turns a software engineer into a producer. Three further blockers, one of them newly verified. FIRST AND DECISIVE: Ukraine is at war. Kyiv is under regular missile and drone attack and martial law is in force. No responsible adviser sends a 22-year-old there for a discretionary arts master's starting September 2027, and an application he must commit to in late 2026 offers no way to hedge. SECOND, NEWLY VERIFIED: the OPP itself states that foreign students may obtain education only after completing a course in the Ukrainian language. The previous record treated this as an assumption; it is now confirmed from the Academy's own document. That is a year of his life on a language with no bearing on a career as an international DJ and producer. THIRD: the programme is only CONDITIONALLY accredited (deferred accreditation, NAZYAVO 13.01.2026, protocol No 1 (92), case No 1769/АС-25) — friction on top of the friction a Ukrainian wartime degree already carries. FOURTH: nobody will tell him the price; the official foreign-citizen tuition PDF exists but pages 2-3 contain no extractable digits, which I verified myself. VERDICT: record it, do not apply. Rating C. His September 2027 effort belongs in the EU, with Tbilisi as the paid fallback.

_rec.totalCostEstimate: EUR 0 tuition + EUR 107 per semester (EUR 428 across four semesters) + travel to the Leipzig blocks. Nominally one of the cheapest master's degrees in Europe — and entirely beside the point, because he cannot get in and could not get a visa on it.
_rec.scholarships: None published.
_rec.englishTest: None — German-taught, so IELTS/TOEFL is irrelevant here.
_rec.visaEligible: NO in practice — and the legal reasoning in the previous record needed correcting rather than just repeating. The correction: part-time study is not legally excluded. Section 16b(1) AufenthG grants a residence permit as an ENTITLEMENT ('wird erteilt') for Vollzeitstudium — full-time study. Part-time study appears separately in section 16b(5), where the permit 'kann erteilt werden' — purely DISCRETIONARY. So the honest statement is not 'part-time is refused by law' but 'part-time carries no entitlement, only official discretion'. That discretion will not be exercised in his favour, for a reason specific to this programme: it delivers roughly 20 attendance days over two years and presupposes concurrent employment in the German media industry. An Ausländerbehörde will not accept five contact days a semester as a residence purpose, and he cannot hold the German media job that would supply an alternative residence basis, because he would need a residence permit to take it. The requirement and the remedy are circular.
_rec.recommendation: AVOID — and the case against it is now stronger than the previous record made out, on three independently fatal grounds. First, entry: the German page requires a year of experience in the media and communications industry, not merely a year of any work; the English page's looser wording is not the governing text and the previous record was misled by it. He has none. Second, visa: this is a part-time programme with about 20 attendance days total, built for people already employed by Central German media companies. Part-time study carries no residence entitlement under section 16b(1), only discretion under 16b(5), and no authority will grant it on this contact load. He cannot take the job that would fix the problem without the permit the job is supposed to justify. Third, and new: the programme itself is listed as not accredited — the university's system accreditation (held since April 2023) covers the institution and lets it seal its own programmes, but this one launched in winter 2025/26 and has not yet been sealed. None of this is a knock on the institution, which is a legitimate state UAS charging EUR 0 tuition and EUR 107 a semester. It is simply not a migration route, and it is not open to him. Spend no application effort here for September 2027.

_rec.program: Master of Music – Elektronische Komposition (Electronic Composition)
_rec.university: Hochschule für Musik und Tanz Köln (HfMT Köln)
_rec.institutionType: Public conservatory (Musikhochschule) — one of Europe's largest music academies; the 'largest' claim is marketing, not verified here
_rec.durationEcts: 4 semesters (2 years) / 120 credits — confirmed on the official programme page
_rec.language: German. Applicants who did not graduate from a German-speaking institution must prove German 'min. level A2 according to the European Framework of Reference' — an unusually low bar, but teaching and the colloquium are in German.
_rec.focus: Electronic Music / Live Electronics; Electroacoustic and mixed instrumental-electronic composition (art-music, not commercial production)
_rec.whatYouStudy: Independent compositional work and professionalisation: mixed instrumental/electronic composition, installations and internet works, self-organised concerts of student work. The electronic and instrumental composition classes cooperate closely, so students may join the other class's projects and take main-subject lessons there. All practical work happens in the Studio für Elektronische Musik. CONFIRMED on the official page. Note the aptitude exam explicitly tests knowledge of 'Literatur und Satztechniken der zeitgenössischen elektronischen und auch instrumentalen Musik' — i.e. contemporary art-music repertoire and compositional technique. No DJing, no club-music production, no mixing/mastering curriculum.
_rec.entryRequirements: Official page: 'Successful completion of a four-year bachelor's degree in composition or equivalent. Admission to the electronic composition program is also possible with an undergraduate degree in instrumental composition.' The binding Eignungsprüfungsordnung annex (09.12.2025) is stricter and names the required bachelor as: 'Studiengang Elektronische Komposition oder Studiengang Instrumentale Komposition'. Plus German A2 minimum, application via muvac, €50 admission-procedure fee. The exam also requires proof of 'grundlegende Computerkenntnisse und Basiswissen in Musikelektronik' (basic computer skills and basic knowledge of music electronics).
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: No, other than as a rare exception — CONFIRMED in the binding regulations: 'Nur in Ausnahmefällen, bei außerordentlicher Begabung und Vorbildung kann ein Bachelorabschluss aus anderen Kunst- oder aus Informatikbereichen akzeptiert werden.' ('Only in exceptional cases, given extraordinary talent and prior education, can a bachelor's degree from other art or computer-science fields be accepted.') Computer science is named, but only as an exception route conditional on demonstrated extraordinary talent — not a normal pathway for a software-engineering graduate with no music training.
_rec.portfolioSpec: NOW EXACT (from the Eignungsprüfungsordnung annex, Anhang §5, 09.12.2025 — the programme page itself does not state it): 'Vorauswahl (digital) – Arbeitsproben: Erwartet werden Dokumentationen oder Produktionen von mindestens drei Kompositionen, welche ganz oder teilweise mit elektronischen Medien erstellt wurden, ggf. mit Partituren als PDF. Jede einzelne Arbeit muss mit Titel, Genre, Besetzung und Namen der Komponistin/des Komponisten versehen sein.' So: at least THREE compositions created wholly or partly with electronic media, documentation or production files, scores as PDF where applicable, each labelled with title, genre, instrumentation and composer name. No duration limit is published. Upload via muvac.
_rec.auditionSpec: No instrumental audition. Digital pre-selection on the work samples, then a main-subject examination: 'Die Hauptfachprüfung besteht aus einem Kolloquium mit der Vorstellung und Diskussion weiterer auf Anforderung eingereichter Werke, mit anspruchsvollen Fragen zur eigenen musikalischen Ästhetik und zur Kenntnis von Literatur und Satztechniken der zeitgenössischen elektronischen und auch instrumentalen Musik. Es sind grundlegende Computerkenntnisse und Basiswissen in Musikelektronik nachzuweisen.' Note 'anspruchsvolle Fragen' (demanding questions) and that FURTHER works may be requested. The aptitude-test period for winter 2026/27 was 'expected end of May 2026 until 19 June 2026', i.e. an on-site examination window in Cologne; remote participation is not offered on the published pages.
_rec.applicationOpens: Not published as a fixed opening date; the muvac application link is opened by the school ahead of each deadline. UNVERIFIED.
_rec.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Officially published: 'Master of Music degree programs: 02.03.2026' for winter semester 2026/27, and 01.10.2025 for summer semester 2026. There is a summer- and a winter-semester intake. For a September/October 2027 start, expect a deadline around early March 2027 — not yet published (today is July 2026).
_rec.tuitionIntl: No tuition fees (NRW public institution; no non-EU tuition in North Rhine-Westphalia). €50.00 fee 'for participating in the admission procedure' (once, even for multiple programme applications) — CONFIRMED. Semester social contribution (Semesterbeitrag, incl. NRW transport ticket) is payable but the amount is not published on the pages checked — UNVERIFIED.
_rec.scholarship: DAAD 'Study Scholarships – Master Studies for Artists and Architects' (music is in scope; Tunisia is DAAD-eligible). Deutschlandstipendium may exist at HfMT Köln but was not confirmed on the pages checked.
_rec.stipend: DAAD master's scholarships pay €992/month plus health/accident/liability insurance contributions, a €460 annual study allowance and a travel allowance; funding typically starts 1 October. Amount verified from DAAD, not from HfMT Köln. No HfMT Köln institutional stipend found — UNVERIFIED.
_rec.facilities: CONFIRMED on the official page: training takes place 'in the rooms of the Studio for Electronic Music' with 'several workstations', 'comprehensive software and hardware equipment and excellent listening facilities'. Cologne's historic association with the WDR Studio for Electronic Music (Stockhausen) is context, not part of the school's facilities — treat as background, UNVERIFIED as a student resource.
_rec.fitNotes: Free and prestigious, and the A2 German bar is remarkably low — but the entry gate is the wrong shape for him. The binding regulations require a bachelor in Electronic or Instrumental Composition; a software-engineering BSc lands him in the 'außerordentliche Begabung' exception, which he has no evidence to satisfy. And even if admitted, the content is contemporary art-music composition assessed on knowledge of new-music repertoire and compositional technique — the colloquium would expose the gap immediately. Nothing here builds DJ or dance-music production craft.
_rec.verificationNotes: Programme page fetched and confirmed: name, M.Mus., 4 semesters / 120 credits, German A2 minimum, entry wording, colloquium, muvac, Studio für Elektronische Musik. The binding annex to the Eignungsprüfungsordnung (rahmen_epo_mm_ma_2025_07_10_mit_Anhang_09_12_2025.pdf) was downloaded and read, which upgraded the portfolio spec from UNVERIFIED to exact (at least three compositions made wholly/partly with electronic media, labelled) and tightened the required bachelor to 'Elektronische Komposition oder Instrumentale Komposition'. _rec.whatYouStudy: Two majors: Classical Acoustic Music Production, and Jazz and Pop Music Production. Three interwoven strands over four semesters: practical production work across genres and formats using the most recent production methods; instrumental/vocal tuition with ensemble performance; and technical methodology plus musical analysis including acoustics and ear training. Goal is artistically independent, methodically grounded professional production work. CONFIRMED on the official page — genuinely the most production-focused public master in this batch.
_rec.entryRequirements: CRITICAL CORRECTION — the official Eignungsprüfungsanforderungen page states: 'Voraussetzung ist der Nachweis eines abgeschlossenen künstlerischen Bachelor- oder Diplomstudiums oder eines gleichwertig anerkannten künstlerischen Studiengangs mit Schwerpunktsetzung im Bereich Musikproduktion (z.B. Tonmeister, Soundengineering, Musikregie etc.). Im Sinne eines künstlerischen Abschlusses gilt auch ein Bachelorstudium im Studiengang Ton und Bild.' A completed ARTISTIC bachelor or diploma (or equivalent recognised artistic degree) WITH AN EMPHASIS IN MUSIC PRODUCTION is mandatory. Plus German B2 (Goethe), plus passing the concentration-specific Eignungsprüfung. Aptitude-test fee €50 for the first application, €10 for each additional application (confirmed).
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: No — this is a hard correction to the earlier 'Check'. The requirement is not merely 'a bachelor's degree': it must be an artistic bachelor/diploma with a music-production emphasis, and the examples given are Tonmeister, sound engineering, Musikregie, or RSH's own Ton und Bild bachelor. Jazz/Pop major pre-selection: a portfolio of FOUR TO SIX already-realised works (or excerpts) in different styles from the jazz/popular-music production field; one audio file/track package per work sample; TOTAL DURATION 15–20 MINUTES; accepted formats stereo, 5.1/7.1 or Atmos; stereo mixes as stereo .wav, multichannel as clearly labelled mono .wav files (5.1/7.1) or as an ADM file (Atmos); each work sample accompanied by a short description of how it was made. PLUS unedited videos of the applicant's own artistic performance on instrument/voice (jazz/pop) with improvisation or ad-libs, tempi and styles varying, own composition allowed, max 20 minutes total — with an important alternative for keyboard/jazz piano: 'die Einreichung von bis zu drei Stücken mit Improvisation mit Hilfe von elektronischen Instrumenten wie Keyboards, Synthesizern, DAWs (z.B. Ableton live) mit deutlich erkennbarem spielerisch-handwerklichem Anteil sowie erkennbar eigener Soundgestaltung' (up to three pieces with improvisation using keyboards, synths or DAWs such as Ableton Live, with clearly recognisable playing craft and own sound design). PLUS a motivation letter referencing the chosen major and a CV with certificates. (Classical major differs: 5–6 works, 30–45 minutes, plus three works from different stylistic periods on video.)
_rec.auditionSpec: Yes — a substantial ON-SITE examination (Präsenzprüfung) in Düsseldorf, in four parts: (1) artistic presentation on instrument or voice with the same repertoire as the pre-selection, plus a prepared solo transcription (or a short a cappella piece for jazz/pop voice) AND sight-reading / sight-singing; six copies of the scores or lead sheets must be brought. (2) An UNPREPARED practical task in the chosen major, e.g. a mix or an edit, typically one to two hours. (3) Written examinations of both musical and technical hearing: musical ear (~40 min: dictations from piano and from recordings, intonation hearing, error detection, short aural analysis, instrumentation hearing) and technical ear (~40 min: listening examples including technical artefacts, level judgement, formant hearing). (4) A Fachgespräch with the selection panel, max 30 minutes. Fee €50.

WARNING RESTATED AND STILL VALID — a 23 October deadline falls AFTER the semester has started and leaves no time whatever to obtain a visa. Paderborn's own general winter-semester application deadline is 21 September with enrolment by 30 September (extended to 23 October), which confirms these are late domestic dates, not international ones. _rec.tuitionNonEU: CONFIRMED IDENTICAL — no tuition for non-EU nationals in NRW.

_rec.totalCostEstimate: About EUR 702/year in semester contributions at the confirmed 2026/27 rate, plus German-course fees, plus living costs in Paderborn (one of the cheaper German university towns), plus the blocked account for the visa.

_rec.recommendation: Every factual claim in the previous record held up: M.A., zulassungsfrei, 20 places, no audition, deadlines 23 October and 21 March, EUR 351.15 a semester. The problem is not accuracy, it is fit. This is an academic degree ABOUT popular music — he would spend two years analysing the music industry in German, not producing. It does not advance the DJ/producer craft by a single hour of studio time, and it demands DSH/TestDaF-level German, which is the same 12-18 month investment TH Köln demands but for a much smaller payoff in his chosen direction. Two specific risks the previous record understated: the committee may simply rule a software-engineering BSc not fachverwandt to musicology and reject him on subject grounds regardless of how open the admission is, and the published 23 October deadline is a domestic date that is visa-impossible for a Tunisian national. Keep it only as a low-priority visa-and-network route into Germany, and only if he independently decides he wants the academic study of music culture for its own sake.

_rec.accreditationStatus: OFFICIAL — CONFIRMED, and the only officially accredited programme in this batch. SAE Institute Milano appears BY NAME on MUR's official register of legally recognised AFAM institutes, listed under Lombardia as 'SAE Institute. Creative media education – Milano'. It is a non-state institution operating inside the national AFAM framework, ministerially authorised under Ministerial Decree 280 of 16 May 2017 pursuant to Art. 11 of DPR 212/2005. An AFAM first-level diploma is equated to a three-year laurea within the Italian higher-education qualifications framework. CRUCIAL CAVEAT, now firmly established: this official status covers the FIRST-LEVEL diploma only. Any SAE Italy course not on that ministerial list — including the Electronic Music Production and Urban Music Production short courses — is a purely private certificate with no legal academic value.

_rec.valueVerdict: AVOID for this candidate — though on its own merits it is the only legitimately accredited, visa-viable programme in the batch. Decisive reason: it is a three-year BACHELOR-level qualification he does not need, gated behind certified B2 Italian he does not have.
_rec.recommendation: Officially accredited, visa-viable, and still the wrong programme — the mismatch is level and language, not quality. This is the only programme in this batch verified at the ministry itself: SAE Institute Milano is named on MUR's official AFAM register, which means a real Italian qualification and, uniquely here, a plausible route to a study visa. But it is a three-year bachelor-equivalent he does not need, and international entry demands certified Italian at B2 — a requirement that bilingual English/Italian teaching does not waive, and which he cannot realistically reach and certify before an October 2027 start. _rec.institutionType: Public university of music and performing arts

_rec.language: German — proof of German at level B2 is a condition of admission (Goethe-Zertifikat B2, ÖSD B2, or the mdw German test)
_rec.durationEcts: 2 years / 4 semesters; ECTS UNVERIFIED on the pages read (curriculum PDF not parsed)
_rec.whatYouStudy: Managing complex audio productions end to end — artistic-technical planning, creative realisation, completion — with a large elective share so you sharpen an individual artistic profile within one of three specialisations: classical music production, popular-music production, or film sound. Sound reinforcement and sound design can be taken as additional emphases regardless of specialisation. A master project is central.
_rec.entryRequirements: Passed admission examination; a completed subject-relevant bachelor's or diploma degree; proof of German at B2; and proof of unimpaired hearing. The admission info sheet is explicit: you must upload "Nachweis über ein abgeschlossenes Studium (Bachelor o. Diplom) in einem facheinschlägigen Studium Tonmeister_in" — i.e. a Tonmeister-type degree. Also required: a current specialist medical certificate with audiogram (not older than two months) confirming physiologically unimpaired hearing across 125–8,000 Hz.
_rec.portfolioSpec: Very heavy and fully specified. (a) Motivation video, max 3 minutes, answering a fixed question list for your specialisation. (b) Instrument/voice video: for Popularmusik, 2 jazz/popular works with improvisation or ad libs (an own composition is allowed; for piano, one piece may be improvisation using keyboards/synths/DAWs such as Ableton Live with clearly audible playing craft and own sound design); band or play-alongs permitted; total video duration max 15 minutes. (c) Piano video if piano is not your main instrument. (d) PORTFOLIO — Popularmusik: SIX popular-music productions in different styles, produced, recorded and mixed substantially by you, at least three with vocals and at least two involving recording of acoustic instruments, all delivered as stereo audio (5.1/Dolby Atmos versions optional), each at least 2:30 and max 30 minutes in total, plus written documentation of 7,000–12,000 characters (approach, microphone choices, session photos, DAW screenshots, challenges, critical reflection). Klassik: three music-recording projects, two pure stereo audio productions with different ensembles plus one free project (audio or video, stereo/5.1/Dolby Atmos, with a stereo version supplied), total 20–40 minutes, plus the same 7,000–12,000-character documentation. Filmton: three film-sound projects (production sound, sound design, mixing), two with more complex sound design or mixing and one at least in 5.1, plus documentation. Formats: one work per file, .wav (5.1 as labelled single wavs), ADM BWF for Atmos, .mp4/.mov video, max Full HD, max 8 GB per file, documentation as PDF.
_rec.auditionSpec: Two-part commission exam. Part 1 is the submitted video/audio package. If the commission invites you, Part 2 is an ON-SITE oral exam at the mdw in Vienna: a practical studio task (e.g. editing, mixing or sound design), questions on music theory and music literature, ear-training tasks, analysis of a listening or film example, questions on acoustics and audio/studio technology, and a technical discussion of your portfolio.

Diplom) in einem facheinschlägigen Studium Tonmeister_in", and the MA page requires "ein facheinschlägiges Bachelorstudium" with the mdw BA Tonmeister_in named as the intended route. A software-engineering BSc does not satisfy this, and German B2 plus an audiogram are hard gates.

_rec.focus: Sound Design; audiovisual/multimedia post-production; mastering; video editing and VFX. Post-production oriented rather than music-production oriented.

IMPORTANT CORRECTION/UPGRADE: a separate English-taught variant genuinely exists and is confirmed — 'MA Programme Audiovisual Design (in English)', listed under the same specialty, same 2-semester length, same director (Assoc. Prof. Dr. Silvana Karagyozova). However it carries EXACTLY the same bachelor-field restriction, so the English option does not unlock it for him.
