_rec.whatYouStudy: CONFIRMED. Theoretical grounding in digital audio and audiovisual technologies combined with specialised practical and elective courses: sound engineering/tonrezhisura, sound design, video editing, post-production and mastering, 2D compositing and visual effects. Graduates qualify as 'Multimedia Designer' and are placed as video editors in electronic media and as audiovisual specialists/editors for broadcast and online platforms. There is no composition, DAW-based music production, DJ practice or live-electronics content published.
_rec.portfolioSpec: One independently developed, already-realised media project, presented and discussed at the admission interview, submitted in electronic format on a standard digital storage medium. CONFIRMED that no number of works, no duration limit, no file-format specification and no genre requirement is published on either the Bulgarian or the English page.
_rec.auditionSpec: No live audition, no performance test and no written music-theory exam. Admission is by interview only, built around the presented realised media project. Whether the interview may be held remotely is not published — assume on-site in Sofia unless the department confirms otherwise.
_rec.entryRequirements: A completed bachelor's degree with a diploma grade not lower than 'добър' (Good), from one of two qualifying professional fields ONLY, plus the interview on the presented media project. Verbatim eligibility wording used across this specialty: 'завършили бакалавърска степен от професионални направления 1.3 Педагогика на обучението по музика и 8.3 Музикално и танцово изкуство'.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: NO — confirmed independently on BOTH the Bulgarian page and the English-language page. Eligibility is closed to professional fields 1.3 Pedagogy of Music Education and 8.3 Music and Dance Arts. A Software Engineering BSc sits in a different professional field entirely and does not qualify. There is no published bridging, equivalence or 'for graduates of other specialties' variant of this programme — notable because the same faculty DOES publish explicit 'за завършили други специалности' (for graduates of other specialties) variants of several of its pedagogy and logopedics masters, and deliberately does not do so here.
_rec.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Nothing is published for a September 2027 intake. Confirmed pattern: ФНОИ runs an annual 'Кандидатмагистърска кампания'; the campaign for academic year 2026-2027 was announced on 17.07.2026 and explicitly includes the 'Музикални медийни технологии и тонрежисура' specialty, but the announcement page as published lists only the programme set, with no dates. Historically a mid-to-late-summer campaign for a winter-semester (autumn) start. Expect the 2027-2028 call around July 2027.
_rec.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Announced annually in mid-July for the coming academic year (the 2026-2027 campaign was posted 17 July 2026). Exact opening date not published on the pages verified.
_rec.scholarship: None found. No scholarship, waiver or stipend attached to this programme is published, and the programme is explicitly designated fee-paying ('платено обучение'), which in the Bulgarian system means it is outside the state-subsidised places that carry stipend eligibility.
_rec.fundingLevel: None found — programme is fee-paying by design
_rec.tuitionIntl: Partially resolved. The official ФНОИ semester fee table for 2024-2025 lists 'Аудиовизуален дизайн — 1400 лв' per semester, i.e. approximately BGN 2,800 (~EUR 1,430) for the full two-semester programme. CAVEAT: that table is the standard domestic/EU schedule. Sofia University sets a separate, higher fee for non-EU foreign nationals under a national tariff, and that non-EU figure could NOT be located on any official page — treat the non-EU cost as UNVERIFIED and expect it to be materially higher than BGN 1,400 per semester.
_rec.facilities: Partially verified. Run by the Катедра 'Музика и мултимедийни технологии', which maintains a dedicated block-2 facility (the faculty publishes a virtual walkthrough of it). No studio, console, monitoring or immersive-audio inventory is published; no industry partnerships, notable alumni or named staff beyond the director are listed. Programme director: Assoc. Prof. Dr. Silvana Karagyozova, skkaraguoz@uni-sofia.bg — CONFIRMED on both the Bulgarian and English pages.
_rec.fitNotes: Keep as a documented NEGATIVE, and note that the input's proposed workaround is wrong. The subject matter (sound design, post-production, mastering) is genuinely appealing and the fee is low by European standards, but entry is formally closed to anyone outside professional fields 1.3 and 8.3, on both the Bulgarian and the English-taught versions. CRITICAL CORRECTION TO THE INPUT: there is NO programme called 'Audio Production and Mastering' (Аудиопродуциране и мастеринг) at this faculty — it does not exist. The specialty contains exactly four entries: Аудиовизуален дизайн, MA Audiovisual Design (in English), Аудиовизуална реставрация (Audiovisual Restoration) and Звуков дизайн (Sound Design). I verified Звуков дизайн directly and it imposes the IDENTICAL 1.3/8.3 restriction, so the advice to 'apply to the sibling programme instead' must be struck — the whole specialty is closed to him. The only remaining action, and a low-probability one, is a direct email to Assoc. Prof. Karagyozova asking whether a software-engineering bachelor plus a strong media project can be admitted by exception. Do not build the application plan around this faculty.
_rec.verificationNotes: CONFIRMED from official Sofia University / ФНОИ sources: the programme exists at MA level and is included in the live 2026-2027 admissions campaign; 2 semesters, full-time, fee-paying; Bulgarian language of instruction; the professional qualification 'Multimedia Designer'; curriculum content (digital audio, sound design/engineering, video editing, post-production, mastering, 2D compositing, VFX); the eligibility restriction to professional fields 1.3 and 8.3, quoted verbatim in Bulgarian; the 'not lower than Good' diploma-grade condition; the interview-on-realised-media-project admission format with electronic submission on a standard digital medium; the director's name and email; a semester fee of BGN 1,400 from the official ФНОИ 2024-2025 fee table PDF. NEWLY DISCOVERED AND CONFIRMED: an English-taught variant 'MA Programme Audiovisual Design (in English)' exists with identical structure AND identical 1.3/8.3 eligibility restriction. DISPROVED: the input's claim that a sibling programme 'Audio Production and Mastering' at this faculty is open to any bachelor — no such programme is listed anywhere in the specialty, and the actual sibling programme Звуков дизайн (Sound Design) was fetched and carries the same 1.3/8.3 restriction. ALSO DROPPED: the input's 'also listed via the Burgas branch' claim, which does not appear on the programme page. NOT CONFIRMED: total ECTS; the non-EU foreign-national tuition rate (the BGN 1,400/semester figure is the standard domestic/EU tariff); exact 2026-2027 or 2027-2028 application dates; whether the interview can be conducted remotely. There is no overlap of any kind with his stated field or with a DJ/producer career.
_rec.entryRequirements: CORRECTED against ΦΕΚ 4568/2018, Άρθρα 3-4. Άρθρο 3: holders of a first-cycle degree from ANY department of a Greek ΑΕΙ, or from an equivalent foreign institution RECOGNISED BY ΔΟΑΤΑΠ (the Greek foreign-qualification recognition body). The prior record's paraphrase about the Coordinating Committee being satisfied of 'specialised knowledge or experience in the cognitive subjects' does not appear in the founding text — the real gate is not a discretionary clause but a hard competitive examination. Mandatory documents: application form; CV; certified copy of degree; peer-reviewed publications if any; evidence of professional/research/artistic activity if any; ID; TWO letters of recommendation from university professors; C1 English certificate; Greek proficiency certificate for foreign applicants; ΔΟΑΤΑΠ certificate of equivalence for foreign degrees. Selection criteria: (a) degree grade of AT LEAST 7.5/10 — the Committee may waive this by specially reasoned decision only if the candidate holds a second university degree, a master's, notable published/research/artistic work, or significant professional experience in cognate fields; (b) WRITTEN ENTRANCE EXAMINATIONS for BOTH specialisations on the programme's subject matter, with syllabus and prescribed bibliography announced in advance; (c) a PRACTICAL EXAMINATION before a panel of professors for the Psaltic Art specialisation; (d) a PERSONAL INTERVIEW before the Coordinating Committee. Final ranking: Byzantine Musicology = 50% written exam + 50% interview; Psaltic Art = 30% written + 50% practical + 20% interview. Intake is 20 students per academic year, selected separately per specialisation.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: Formally yes — Άρθρο 3 admits graduates of any department, and a Software Engineering BSc is not excluded on paper. In substance no. He must pass a written entrance examination in Byzantine musicology, sat in Greek against a prescribed Greek bibliography, and then a Greek-language interview assessing his command of the field's scholarly literature. The departmental page further records that for the Psaltic Art specialisation candidates must hold a Diploma of Byzantine Music with grade 'Excellent' from a recognised Greek music school or equivalent studies. Formal eligibility here is meaningless without the chant training and the Greek he does not have.
_rec.portfolioSpec: No portfolio in the creative-industry sense. What is required instead is documentary: CV, certified degree, ΔΟΑΤΑΠ equivalence certificate, two academic reference letters, and optional evidence of research/artistic activity. His planned production portfolio would carry no weight — it is not a scored criterion.
_rec.auditionSpec: SPECIFIED, contrary to the prior record's 'UNVERIFIED'. Written entrance examination for both specialisations. For the Psaltic Art specialisation there is a compulsory PRACTICAL EXAMINATION in Byzantine chant before a faculty panel, worth 50% of the final ranking, with specifications set out in each year's call. Plus a personal interview for all candidates who pass the written stage. This is a competitive entrance-exam admission, not a portfolio review.
_rec.equipmentRequired: None specified. Teaching rooms, seminar rooms, amphitheatres with audiovisual equipment and departmental laboratories are provided (Άρθρο 9, ΦΕΚ 4568/2018).
_rec.facilities: Classrooms, seminar rooms, audiovisual-equipped amphitheatres and laboratories of the Department of Music Studies (Άρθρο 9). No recording studio, DAW suite or electronic-music facility is mentioned — none is relevant to this curriculum.
_rec.intakes: Once per year, autumn (winter semester) start. 20 places per year across the two specialisations.
_rec.applicationOpens: CORRECTED. Άρθρο 4 of ΦΕΚ 4568/2018: the call (προκήρυξη) is published EACH JUNE by decision of the Department Assembly, on the department and university websites, announcing the specialisations offered, places per specialisation, entrance-examination dates, examinable subjects, syllabus and bibliography per specialisation, and required documents. This directly contradicts his planning assumption that calls open October 2026 - February 2027: for a September 2027 start the call would not appear until around June 2027.
_rec.deadline: Set in each year's call, typically September, and extendable by decision of the Department Assembly. The most recent documented cycle (2022-23) had a deadline of 16 September 2022 with submission through the university's electronic protocol system. Successful candidates must enrol within 15 days of the Assembly's decision. Exact 2027 dates will only be known when the June 2027 call is published.
_rec.tuitionEU: €700 per semester, payable at the start of each semester — CONFIRMED verbatim in BOTH instruments (Άρθρο 5 of ΦΕΚ 2643/2018 and Άρθρο 8 para. 10 of ΦΕΚ 4568/2018). Over the 3-semester programme this is €2,100 in total, NOT the €3,000 the prior record stated. The founding decree itself characterises the fee as 'purely symbolic'.
_rec.tuitionNonEU: €2,100 total (€700 x 3 semesters) — the SAME rate he would pay as a Tunisian national. Greek public ΠΜΣ fees are set by decree as a single figure with no EU/non-EU differential, so the prior record was right that there is no separate non-EU rate but wrong on the amount. Caveat: these are the 2018 decreed figures and law 5094/2024 may have prompted a re-founding with revised fees — confirm with the Secretariat.
_rec.otherFees: ΔΟΑΤΑΠ recognition of his Tunisian BSc (a mandatory, slow and separately-charged process), certified translations of degree and transcripts, Greek student visa (type D) and residence-permit fees, mandatory health insurance, and proof of sufficient means for the visa. None of these are quantified in the official instruments — obtain current figures from the Greek consulate and ΔΟΑΤΑΠ if this were ever pursued.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: Tuition is genuinely cheap at €2,100 for the whole degree. Athens living costs over 18 months dominate — budget roughly €700-900 per month, i.e. approximately €12,500-16,000, plus ΔΟΑΤΑΠ, translation, visa, permit and insurance costs. Order of magnitude €15,000-19,000 all-in. Living-cost figures are my estimate, not an official publication.
_rec.scholarships: No dedicated scholarship. The only relief published in the regulation is the standard statutory fee EXEMPTION under ν. 4485/2017: full waiver of tuition for students whose individual income does not exceed 100%, and family income 70%, of the Greek national median equivalised disposable income per ELSTAT, capped at 30% of admitted students and usable for one ΠΜΣ only. This is means-tested against Greek statistical thresholds and in practice requires Greek tax documentation, making it awkward-to-impossible for a first-year non-EU arrival. Crucially it is a fee waiver worth at most €2,100 — it is NOT a stipend and would not cover a single month of living costs. There is no funded route here.
_rec.visaEligible: Technically yes — a full-time, in-person, state-recognised 90-ECTS second-cycle degree at a Greek public university supports a student residence permit. But this is moot: he cannot satisfy the Greek-proficiency certificate, the C1 English certificate, or the Greek-language written entrance examination, so he would never reach the point of applying for a visa.
_rec.recommendation: The programme is REAL, is a genuine master's, and is accredited — but almost every substantive claim in the prior record was wrong, and the record's central 'finding' collapses. CORRECTIONS: (1) LANGUAGE — it is taught in GREEK, not English. The founding decree ΦΕΚ 2643/τ.Β΄/6-7-2018 Άρθρο 4 says «Τα μαθήματα διεξάγονται στην ελληνική γλώσσα». Only the thesis may optionally be written in English. The prior agent appears to have mistaken the FEK's bilingual programme TITLE for the language of instruction. The claim that this is 'the only English-taught music master's in Greece' is therefore false. (2) FEES — €700 per semester, €2,100 total, not €3,000. (3) LANGUAGE CERTIFICATES — not 'unverified' but precisely specified: a C1 English certificate AND, for foreign applicants specifically, a certificate of proficiency in GREEK. (4) ADMISSION — not 'unverified' but a competitive written entrance examination in Greek on a prescribed Byzantine-musicology bibliography, plus interview, plus a 50%-weighted practical chant audition for the performance track, plus a minimum degree grade of 7.5/10, plus two academic reference letters, plus ΔΟΑΤΑΠ recognition of his foreign degree. (5) TIMING — calls are published each JUNE with a September deadline, not October-February as his planning assumed. (6) VALIDITY — the founding decree authorises operation only until academic year 2027-28, and law 5094/2024 may have superseded these 2018 instruments entirely. THE USEFUL CONCLUSION SURVIVES, AND IS STRONGER THAN THE PRIOR RECORD CLAIMED: the previous agent reached the right verdict on Greece by the wrong road. Greece is not 'closed except for this one English-taught programme' — it is closed, full stop, for this field. This programme was the supposed English exception and it is Greek-taught like all the others. He should treat Greece as unavailable for sound design, music production, audio engineering and music technology at master's level, and stop spending research effort there unless a specific department confirms English-language supervision in writing. Separately, even in a parallel universe where he spoke fluent Greek, this degree teaches Orthodox liturgical chant and would do nothing whatever for a career as a DJ and electronic-music producer.

Verification found no privately-run, NVAO-accredited master in sound design, music production, audio engineering, music technology, immersive audio or electronic music performance. What the private sector actually awards was confirmed on the schools' own sites: Abbey Road Institute Amsterdam awards an 'Advanced Diploma in Music Production & Sound Engineering' (confirmed on its course page — the word used is 'Advanced Diploma', never 'degree' or 'master'); SAE Institute Netherlands awards UK degrees, its own site stating programmes are 'developed, delivered and assessed by SAE Institute, and awarded by and quality assured by the University of Hertfordshire', including an 'MA/MSc Professional Practice' listed as a University of Hertfordshire award for 2025/6 cohorts. Neither is a Dutch degree. CORRECTION TO PRIOR ENTRY: the claim that SAE's MA/MSc is 'delivered fully online' could NOT be re-verified — the dedicated course page 404s. What IS verified is the load-bearing part: it is a UK University of Hertfordshire award, not an NVAO-accredited Dutch qualification.
_rec.accreditationStatus: NOT NVAO-ACCREDITED (private sector) — STRUCTURAL SPLIT CONFIRMED. (1) ACCREDITED = PUBLIC / BEKOSTIGD. Verified directly: Conservatorium van Amsterdam (AHK) Master in Immersive Audio awards a 'Master of Music (MMus)', 2 years, 120 ECTS, taught entirely in English, and the page confirms positive NVAO accreditation — an officially recognised Dutch qualification. HKU's Master of Music — Music Design likewise confirmed at MMus, 2 years, 120 ECTS, taught primarily in English. Both institutions are government-funded (bekostigd) and therefore outside a 'private-sector' brief — but they are the ONLY Dutch route that produces a real master's degree in this field. (2) PRIVATE = NOT ACCREDITED AS DUTCH HIGHER EDUCATION. Abbey Road Institute Amsterdam publishes no accreditation claim anywhere on its FAQ or course pages; its own FAQ states 'Since Abbey Road Institute Amsterdam is a private Institute, students are not eligible for a visa or a student loan', and 'As the Advanced Diploma is not a 3 year degree programme, the course is not eligible for any kind of student loan.' SAE Netherlands explicitly routes its degree-awarding through a UK university rather than NVAO. CRKBO (VAT-exemption register for short vocational training) and NRTO (private-training trade association mark) are NOT accreditations and confer no degree status — no evidence was found contradicting this. NOTE ON CONFIDENCE: the absence of a private NVAO master is an absence-of-evidence finding by nature; it is corroborated here by the fact that the two most credible private providers both position themselves outside the Dutch degree system in their own words.

_rec.recommendation: BOTTOM LINE: DO NOT BUILD THE SEPTEMBER 2027 PLAN AROUND A DUTCH PRIVATE SCHOOL. The verification confirms the two things he needs — an accredited master and a student residence permit — cannot both be bought from the Dutch private sector at any price. The visa finding is not an inference: SAE and Abbey Road each state in writing that their students are not eligible for a visa. Concentrate the accredited-master applications on the Spain, Portugal and Italy slices. IF HE WANTS THE NETHERLANDS SPECIFICALLY, there is exactly one workable route and it is public, not private: HKU's Master of Music — Music Design (Utrecht, MMus, 2 years, 120 ECTS, primarily English) is the realistic target, because it is the only accredited Dutch programme found whose published entry rules bend for someone like him — exceptions are possible without a music bachelor's for candidates showing 'exceptional talent and a steady track record' — and because HKU sponsors non-EU students, advising them to apply before 1 April for immigration processing. Treat November 2026 – February 2027 as his live application window and confirm the 2027 dates when published. DEPRIORITISE the Conservatorium van Amsterdam Master in Immersive Audio despite its NVAO accreditation: it demands a bachelor's in music or a related field AND professional-level audio engineering experience, and screens with a live Pro Tools mixing test on a 24-track session. He has neither the degree nor the experience today; applying for September 2027 would be a wasted application unless he spends the next year acquiring demonstrable professional mixing work. WHAT HE SHOULD ACTUALLY DO WITH THE NETHERLANDS IN THE MEANTIME: build the portfolio he does not have, to a published standard rather than a vague one. The CvA practical test tells him the benchmark precisely — a body of presentable recorded work plus the ability to deliver a clean 10-minute stereo mix from a 24-track Pro Tools session. Short courses in Amsterdam can be attended on an ordinary Schengen tourist visa and require no accreditation, and timing a visit around Amsterdam Dance Event in October adds scene contacts — but get every price in writing by email first, because none of the circulating figures survived verification. Also book IELTS early; 6.5 with no band under 6.0 clears every published bar found.

But for THIS candidate the verdict is negative and should be stated plainly: a composition entrance examination, a theory placement test with a first-semester bridging module he must pass to continue, B1 German certified before he starts, roughly CHF 7,500 in institutional fees plus Swiss living costs, and no funding he is known to be eligible for. _rec.program: Composition for Screen – InMICS (International Master in Composition for Screen)
_rec.institution: KASK & Conservatorium, School of Arts of HOGENT and Howest (Hogeschool Gent) — consortium with CNSMD de Lyon, Conservatorio di Musica G.B. Martini Bologna and (professional/associate role) Université de Montréal
_rec.city: Ghent, Lyon or Bologna — a student studies at TWO of the three European institutions (one per year)
_rec.institutionType: Publicly funded Flemish hogeschool School of Arts, in an Erasmus+/Creative Europe co-funded consortium of public conservatoires
_rec.publicPrivate: PUBLIC — CONFIRMED. All academic partners are public institutions: HOGENT/Howest (Flemish Community-funded), CNSMD de Lyon (French state conservatoire under the Ministry of Culture), Conservatorio di Musica G.B. Martini Bologna (Italian AFAM state conservatoire) and Université de Montréal (Quebec public university). The four professional partners (Festival International du Film d'Aubagne, Fondazione Cineteca di Bologna, Film Fest Gent, Permission Inc. Montréal) are non-degree-awarding associates. The programme was launched with Erasmus+ co-funding and the InMICS Composers Lab with Creative Europe co-funding.
_rec.qualification: CORRECTED — THIS WAS THE BIGGEST UNKNOWN IN THE PREVIOUS RECORD AND IT IS NOW RESOLVED. InMICS is a genuine JOINT MASTER'S DEGREE PROGRAMME, and the consortium states plainly: 'At the end of the two years, and upon validation of the study programme, students receive TWO MASTER'S DEGREES.' So it is a real double-degree award from the two hosting institutions the student attends, not a HOGENT master with a decorative consortium certificate. 2 years, 120 ECTS (60 + 60). On the Belgian side it sits inside HOGENT's accredited Flemish master in music. The previous record's warning that he might 'end up with one recognised diploma or several' is resolved: he would get two recognised European second-cycle degrees.
_rec.accreditationStatus: The Belgian component is delivered within HOGENT's accredited master in music (Flemish Higher Education Register); the Lyon and Bologna components sit inside those states' own accredited second-cycle music degrees (French CNSMD master, Italian AFAM biennio). Two national accreditations are therefore engaged rather than a single consortium accreditation. Specific decision references UNVERIFIED.
_rec.language: ENGLISH — CONFIRMED. The programme is delivered in English across the consortium. His fluent French is a real practical asset for the Lyon specialisation and for daily life there; Italian would help in Bologna. Note the curriculum tags each course by delivering country (BE/FR/IT/CA).
_rec.languageRequirement: No formal English test is published anywhere on inmics.org or on the KASK institutional page. KASK's general master admission page says only that there are 'no formal level requirements for English in the master programs, but the Vantage B2 level is strongly recommended'. UNVERIFIED for InMICS specifically — ask info@inmics.org. He should take IELTS regardless, since Lyon and Bologna will each run their own enrolment procedures.
_rec.durationEcts: 2 years, 120 ECTS (60 + 60). CORRECTED STRUCTURE: the student is enrolled at and studies at TWO of the participating institutes — one for the first year, one for the second — NOT at all four. Confirmed curriculum (Ghent-side listing): Year 1 — Composition for Animation, Documentary and Video (BE) 15; choice of Electro-acoustic Composition (BE) 6 or Scoring for Screen (BE) 6; two from Composition for Musical Theatre (BE) 4, Postproduction (BE) 4, Master seminars (BE) 4, Music Copyright on the ground (CA) 3, History of Film Music (IT) 3; two from Post-tonal composition techniques 3, Improvisation (BE) 3, Orchestral conducting (BE) 3; Internship (BE) 9; Research Master I (BE) 10. Year 2 — Masterproject: Composition for Animation, Documentary and Video 24; further electives; Analysis from Musical & Audiovisual Perspective (BE) 3; Ethnomusicology (FR) 3; Research Master II (BE) 14. All students also take collective digital learning courses accessible simultaneously in the four countries.
_rec.focus: Composing music for screen — film, animation, documentary, video, games — at international conservatoire level, embedded in a festival and cinémathèque network. From the 2024 intake the three specialisations, all EUROPEAN, are: Bologna — Electronic Composition for Media Arts; Ghent — Composition for Animation, Documentary and Video; Lyon — Scoring for Screen. (The former Montréal specialisation, Composition for Video Games, ran under the 2018-2024 curriculum and is not among the three current specialisations.)
_rec.whatYouStudy: Composition for animation, documentary and video; electro-acoustic composition; scoring for screen; postproduction; composition for musical theatre; history of film music; music copyright; post-tonal composition techniques; improvisation; orchestral conducting; ethnomusicology; a 9-ECTS internship; a two-part Research Master strand; and a 24-ECTS master project. Students come together during film festivals for workshops on artistic and entrepreneurial topics and collaborate with audiovisual arts students. Ghent coordinator: Dominique Pauwels; teacher: Ruben De Gheselle.
_rec.entryRequirements: CONFIRMED AND HARDENED. The institutional page states: 'We welcome applications from anyone already composing music for the screen. However, an undergraduate degree in music or equivalent is required.' The consortium's own application checklist turns this into a documentary gate that cannot be argued around: the administrative registration on the Cadence platform requires a 'CERTIFIED COPY OF THE FIRST CYCLE (BACHELOR) DIPLOMA OR DEGREE IN MUSIC, with transcripts in the original language' (or a signed, stamped statement of expected award date), plus a certified English translation if not in English, French, Italian or Dutch. He cannot produce a certified music bachelor. Applications are handled entirely through the CNSMD de Lyon platforms, not through HOGENT's webreg.
_rec.auditionSpec: NOW FULLY PUBLISHED — the previous record had this as UNVERIFIED. TWO PHASES. Phase 1, online application by the deadline, submitted on BOTH platforms (both mandatory): muvac (artistic portfolio and questionnaire) and Cadence at concours.cnsmd-lyon.fr (administrative data and the €92 application fee). Results of round 1 announced by end of April, with an invitation to interview and a COMPULSORY PRELIMINARY ASSIGNMENT — composing music for a short film of 5 to 10 minutes, due at a set deadline in early May. Phase 2: a 30-MINUTE ONLINE INTERVIEW with the recruitment committee/jury (mid-May). Results end of May; the jury also reveals which TWO of the partner institutions each admitted student will attend, and that decision is FINAL. Admission must be confirmed by mid-June, after which the student registers separately according to the procedures of both hosting institutions.
_rec.portfolioSpec: NOW FULLY PUBLISHED. Submitted on muvac: (1) a RESEARCH PAPER PROPOSAL for the two-year programme — provisional research question, provisional title, brief description, max 2,000 words, optionally with bibliography/filmography/music references, on a topic related to composition for screen; (2) A MINIMUM OF THREE AND MAXIMUM OF FIVE pieces of music, total duration across all works max 20 minutes, as mp3/wav or movie files, of which AT LEAST ONE must be a score for screen uploaded as a movie file with the music synchronised to the picture (recording, VST simulation or electronic piece all acceptable), with the written score if available; (3) a DECLARATION OF HONOUR on the authenticity and artistic authorship of all scores and recordings; (4) a COVER LETTER, max 1,000 words, stating motivation and a preference among the partner institutions; (5) a complete CV of experience and education in music and/or music for screen. All documents must use his legal name, not an artist or DJ name.
_rec.equipmentRequired: Not published. A scoring-capable DAW with orchestral VSTs is implied by the portfolio and by the phase-2 assignment. UNVERIFIED — ask info@inmics.org.
_rec.facilities: Access to the facilities of the two European conservatoires he is assigned to (from Ghent, Lyon, Bologna), plus festival and cinémathèque partners (Aubagne, Cineteca di Bologna, Film Fest Gent, Permission Inc. Montréal) providing workshops, coaching and internship placements. Specific studio specification UNVERIFIED.
_rec.intakes: CORRECTED — THIS IS THE DECISIVE ERROR IN THE PREVIOUS RECORD. The previous record said 'September (annual, aligned to the consortium recruitment cycle)'. That is WRONG. InMICS is BIENNIAL. The consortium states twice, in bold: 'The master recruits EVERY TWO YEARS' and 'Every two years, a new group of students starts the programme.' Cohorts run 2018-2020, ..., 2024-2026, 2026-2028, 2028-2030. THERE IS NO SEPTEMBER 2027 INTAKE AT ALL. His target intake does not exist for this programme.
_rec.applicationOpens: CONFIRMED for the most recent cycle: admissions for the 2026-2028 intake opened 2 MARCH 2026 and closed 12 April 2026 (deadline extended by the consortium from an earlier date to 12 April at 23:59 CET). That cohort is already recruited and started in September 2026. The NEXT opening, for the 2028-2030 cohort, would be expected around EARLY MARCH 2028. Monitor inmics.org/apply/deadlines and the 'Latest NEWS' page from late 2027.
_rec.deadline: NOW FULLY PUBLISHED — the previous record said 'NOT PUBLISHED on the institutional page', which was true of the KASK page but the consortium publishes a complete timeline. Confirmed 2026-2028 cycle: 12/04/2026 deadline for submitting applications online (23:59 CET, both platforms); 24 April 2026 results of round 1, plus instructions for the preliminary assignment and the interview date; beginning of May 2026 deadline for the preliminary assignment; 12 or 13 May 2026 round-2 jury interviews; end of May 2026 round-2 results and allocation of the two host institutions (final); mid-June 2026 deadline to confirm admission. Expect an equivalent March-to-June timeline in 2028. NOTHING IN 2027.
_rec.tuitionEU: €2,000 per year — the consortium sets a single flat fee that does not distinguish EU from non-EU.
_rec.tuitionNonEU: €2,000 PER YEAR — MAJOR CORRECTION. The previous record left this UNVERIFIED and warned it might be the Flemish non-EEA rate of €8,800.20. Both the caution and the guess are now superseded by the consortium's own published figure: 'The amount of tuition fees for 2026-2028 will be: First year: €2000 ... Second year: €2000. The two thousand Euros fee is payable to the institution at which the student will be studying. No fees are due to the institution where the student is not currently studying.' So the total tuition for the whole 120 ECTS double-degree is €4,000 — roughly one fifth of what the previous record feared, and about one sixth of the Maastricht bill. This is an Erasmus+/Creative Europe co-funded consortium fee, and it is outstanding value. Still worth getting in writing from info@inmics.org before relying on it for a future cycle, since the figure is quoted for the 2026-2028 cohort specifically.
_rec.otherFees: €92 NON-REFUNDABLE APPLICATION FEE, payable on the Cadence platform at the time of application — newly identified, absent from the previous record. Beyond that: the mobility now involves TWO European countries rather than four countries including Canada, so he would need one Schengen student residence permit procedure per host country (Belgium, France or Italy), each with its own cost and lead time — but NO Canadian study permit is required under the current curriculum. Certified diploma copies and certified translations are additional. Whether HOGENT levies its separate 'contribution towards study costs' on InMICS students UNVERIFIED — ask.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: Tuition: €2,000 × 2 = €4,000 total for 120 ECTS and two master's degrees, plus a €92 application fee. Living costs across two of Ghent/Lyon/Bologna, plus two residence-permit procedures and two relocations, dominate the real budget — call it €12,000–€18,000 per year in living costs and administration depending on city. The tuition itself is close to negligible. This is dramatically cheaper than the previous record's €17,600 tuition estimate.
_rec.scholarships: No InMICS-specific scholarship is published. The programme is itself co-funded by Erasmus+ and Creative Europe, which is why the fee is only €2,000/yr — the subsidy is delivered as a low fee rather than as an award. Possible additional routes: the Flemish Master Mind Scholarship if he were registered at HOGENT (a genuine full ride — €10,225 plus a fee waiver — but nomination runs through the institution and InMICS eligibility is UNVERIFIED), and any Erasmus+ mobility grant attached to the inter-institutional moves. Ask info@inmics.org and the HOGENT International Office. Given a €4,000 total tuition bill, funding is a much smaller problem here than at Maastricht.
_rec.visaEligible: Yes in principle — an accredited Flemish, French or Italian second-cycle degree supports a student visa and residence permit in each of those countries. CORRECTED RISK ASSESSMENT: the previous record warned about 'multi-country mobility (France, Italy, Canada)' and 'a Canadian study permit for the Montréal period'. Under the renewed curriculum in force since the 2024 intake, the three specialisations are all EUROPEAN (Bologna, Ghent, Lyon) and a student attends TWO of them, so the Canadian study-permit risk has fallen away. The remaining, still real, complication is that a Tunisian national would need to run TWO separate Schengen national-visa/residence-permit procedures back to back — one for each host country — with the year-two application filed while already resident in the year-one country. Get the consortium's written account of how it handles this before committing.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: NO — CONFIRMED and now airtight. The stated requirement is an undergraduate degree in music or equivalent PLUS being 'already composing music for the screen', and the Cadence administrative checklist demands a CERTIFIED COPY OF A BACHELOR DIPLOMA IN MUSIC as a mandatory upload. The 'or equivalent' wording in the prose does not survive contact with a documentary requirement for a certified music diploma. A BSc in Software Engineering cannot satisfy it, and the portfolio gate is separately out of reach: three to five works including at least one score synchronised to picture, plus a 2,000-word academic research proposal, judged against trained composers.
_rec.recommendation: EXISTS, IS REAL, IS A GENUINE DOUBLE MASTER'S DEGREE, AND IS EXCELLENT VALUE — BUT IS UNAVAILABLE TO HIM, AND UNAVAILABLE TO ANYONE FOR SEPTEMBER 2027. Three corrections matter. (1) INTAKE: this master recruits BIENNIALLY, not annually. The 2026-2028 cohort applied 2 March – 12 April 2026 and started in September 2026; the next cohort is 2028-2030, applying around March 2028. There is no September 2027 entry, so it cannot be on his 2027 list at all. (2) COST: tuition is €2,000 per year flat for EU and non-EU alike, total €4,000 for the whole programme plus a €92 application fee — not the €8,800.20/yr the previous record feared. (3) AWARD AND STRUCTURE: students receive TWO master's degrees, and study at TWO of the three European institutions (Ghent, Lyon, Bologna); Montréal is no longer a study location under the curriculum in force since 2024, so the Canadian study-permit worry is obsolete. What blocks him is not money and not accreditation — it is that the application requires a certified copy of a bachelor's diploma IN MUSIC, and a portfolio of three to five screen-scoring works plus a 2,000-word research proposal. Keep this on file as a strong LONG-TERM target: if he completes the Maastricht Master of Music (or any recognised music master) by summer 2029, he would hold the diploma the Cadence platform demands and could apply in March 2030 for the 2030-2032 cohort — cheaply, in English, with his French an asset for the Lyon track. If he contacts them now, the only useful question is whether the consortium would ever accept a non-music bachelor as 'equivalent'; ask info@inmics.org in writing, and expect no.

_rec.publicPrivate: PRIVATE. FAMO states on its own site: 'Jsme soukromá vysoká škola' (We are a private higher education institution). Its legal form is o.p.s. (obecně prospěšná společnost — a public-benefit non-profit company), i.e. a private non-state entity, not a veřejná vysoká škola established by act of Parliament. The 79,000 CZK/year tuition charged to Czech nationals is itself conclusive: a Czech public university cannot charge tuition for Czech-taught study.
_rec.language: Czech. The site has an English version but instruction language for non-Czech speakers is not addressed. UNVERIFIED whether any English-medium delivery exists — ask the school directly before assuming.
_rec.languageRequirement: UNVERIFIED. No published Czech-language certificate requirement was found. Given a private school's commercial incentive to enrol, this may be softer than at public institutions — but confirm in writing, because being admitted without the language and then failing is the classic trap at fee-charging private art schools.
_rec.qualification: MgA. (navazující magisterské studium), programme code N0211P310001 — the 'N' prefix and the code format indicate a programme entered in the Czech national register of accredited study programmes. VERIFY INDEPENDENTLY before paying anything: check the code N0211P310001 in the Czech National Accreditation Bureau (NAÚ) / MŠMT register of accredited programmes rather than relying on the school's own page.
_rec.accreditationStatus: REQUIRES INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION — this is exactly the category of institution the brief warns about (a private provider selling a 'Master'). The programme code N0211P310001 is consistent with genuine national accreditation, and the school describes itself as operating within the state education system, but I did not open the MŠMT/NAÚ register entry itself and will not assert it. Look up N0211P310001 at https://regvssp.msmt.cz before any commitment. If accredited, an MgA. from an accredited private Czech HEI does support a long-term residence permit for study.

_rec.recommendation: INCLUDED AS A DELIBERATE COUNTER-EXAMPLE AND A LOW-BAR FALLBACK, NOT A RECOMMENDATION. It is the one genuinely private, fee-charging, low-selectivity sound school found in this slice, and it is precisely the kind of institution the brief asks to be labelled clearly. Its merits are real: Pro Tools-equipped sound studio, industry teachers, small cohorts, and a price (~3,200 EUR/year) that is genuinely low. Its risks are equally real: he would pay ~6,400 EUR in tuition for a degree from a small private school when UTB Zlín and ČVUT offer nationally stronger degrees for FREE, and the master-level sound specialization is unconfirmed. Do not apply until three things are answered in writing: (1) the N0211P310001 entry in the MŠMT register, (2) whether sound is an actual master-level specialization, (3) whether the 79,000 CZK must be paid before or after the visa decision. Treat as a Plan C behind ČVUT and UNIZA.

The official entry rule is a licence de musique or an equivalent foreign degree, and the published prerequisites (practical musicianship, composition and production competence, popular-music history and aesthetics, advanced DAW work) describe someone with years of formal musical training. He has a software-engineering BSc, no conservatoire background and no portfolio. Applying for September 2027 would waste the application slot and the Études en France cycle. CORRECTION to the prior entry: this is NOT a fee-free German public master — it is a continuing-education master and it does charge tuition to everyone. CGL's own cost worksheet for a non-EU student over the whole programme: EUR 200 + EUR 1,240 semester fees + EUR 10,000 tuition + EUR 22,416 living costs, and the EUR 22,416 must be proved to the Immigration Office to obtain the residence permit.
_rec.scholarship: No programme scholarship. DAAD is a genuinely separate application track with its own much earlier deadlines and would need its own research.
_rec.entryRequirements: Three hard conditions, quoted from the official application page: (1) "The successful completion of a university degree with the degree 'Bachelor of Arts' or 'Bachelor of Sciences' or with an equivalent or higher degree... in any field." (2) "Proof of at least 12 months of professional experience relevant to the course of study, completed AFTER earning the first university degree... should be accumulated by the start of the program. It can, however, be acquired cumulatively... gained within the last five years prior to the application." (3) A portfolio documenting creative and scholarly achievements, plus English at minimum B2. International applicants must ALSO have their degree validated by uni-assist in parallel, by the same deadline, with certified copies and certified translations if the documents are not in English or German. He can pre-check whether SMU MedTech is recognised at anabin.kmk.org (needs status H+).
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: Yes, without qualification — "a university degree... in any field", and the FAQ adds "The MA Game Development and Research program welcomes applicants from all professional backgrounds." A software-engineering degree is an asset here, not a problem. The real gate is not the degree but the 12 months of post-bachelor professional experience in a games/media-relevant field: he graduates in 2026 with none, so for a September 2027 start he would need roughly a year of relevant work between graduation and enrolment (employment, self-employment, project work, internships and research-assistant posts all count, and can be accumulated in pieces).
_rec.portfolioSpec: Now fully documented. The portfolio is free-form work samples, explicitly NOT required to be game work: "These do not need to be works in game design, since we do not require that applicants have previous experience in that field." Submit as a PDF, a Dropbox/Google Drive link or an online portfolio; analogue work must be scanned or photographed. CGL's own list of acceptable content includes, under 'Samples of other Audiovisual Artwork': "Audio Work: If you have sound design or music composition skills, present examples" — so his production work would count. Alongside the portfolio, every MA GDR applicant must complete the annual application TASK, which consists of a project idea, an application video of maximum 10 minutes, and three short written assignments; the exact brief is published only when the portal opens on 1 March. Other uploads: CV, portrait photo, scanned certificates and degree, proof of the 12 months' experience (contracts or dated project documents), and optionally an English certificate.
_rec.auditionSpec: No audition. The formal selection is an "artistic-scientific aptitude test" made up of the submitted documents and application tasks. An interview is only sometimes used: "In some cases, the committee may invite applicants to an individual online-interview (approximately 10 minutes)... The interview is an additional method to evaluate an applicant's language skills." It is ONLINE, short, and about English proficiency, not performance. CORRECTION to the prior entry: the '11 and 13 June' interview dates came from a one-off news post about an extended cycle, not from the standing admission process.
_rec.applicationOpens: 1 March each year — "The application tasks are always published on March 1st", which is also when the application portal opens. For a September 2027 start, expect 1 March 2027.
_rec.deadline: 31 March at 23:59 CEST — published as a standing annual rule: "The application deadline is always March 31, at 23:59 CEST", with the uni-assist submission deadline also 31 March, and successful applicants notified in June to start in September. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date only for the extension: the news page that was originally cited as the source announced a one-off extension to 24 April with interviews on 11 and 13 June; that is not the standing rule and must not be planned around. Practical timing for September 2027: begin uni-assist paperwork by roughly January 2027 (evaluation takes up to four weeks or longer at peak), watch for the tasks on 1 March 2027, submit by 31 March 2027.
_rec.whatYouStudy: Confirmed module structure, four semesters. Semester 1 'Equalization & Exchange' — levelling projects 'Playing with Theater', 'Playing with Cinema', 'Playing with Video Games', plus Media and Game Studies 101, Visual Design 101, Game Design Theory 101. Semester 2 'Critical Play & Adaptation' — projects on Board Games, Serious Games and Non-Linear Adaptation, plus the 102-level theory courses. Semester 3 'Professionalization & Experimentation' — the commercial games market, financing, self-publishing versus publishers, pitch and marketing strategy, plus a larger experimental third-semester project and the 103-level theory courses. Semester 4 — Master's Project: thesis with a theoretical and a practical part, plus a colloquium. Only 20 students per year. THE DECISIVE FINDING: there is no audio, sound-design, music, Wwise/FMOD or middleware module anywhere in the published structure. The programme describes itself as research into "non-linear audio-visuality", which reads as audio-related but in practice means audiovisual media as a whole; the taught strands are game design, visual design, media and game studies, programming and professionalization. Graduate profiles listed by CGL: Game Designer, Game Artist, Game Programmer, Interactive Designer, Concept Author, Stage Director, Project Manager — no audio role.
_rec.facilities: Not itemised on the official pages. Confirmed instead: a dedicated games institute with its own building in Cologne, six named professors (Bartholdy, Freyermuth, Guardiola, Hoffmann, Klemke, Limpach) plus industry guest lecturers, a cohort of only 20, the Clash of Realities international games conference hosted in-house, and an incubator strand (The Game Starter Foundry, Broken Paternoster Games). No studio, console or audio facility is claimed.
_rec.fitNotes: Verified as existing, well-run and genuinely open to a software engineer — and verified as the wrong programme for him. It is English-taught, accepts any bachelor, accepts an audio portfolio, needs no audition, needs no IELTS, and costs a manageable EUR 10,000 plus fees. But it does not teach sound. If his goal shifts to games programming or games research it is a strong option; for becoming a producer, DJ or sound designer it teaches him nothing he needs. Secondary blocker even then: 12 months of post-degree professional experience in a media-relevant field, which he will not have until roughly late 2027 at the earliest. Recommend excluding from the audio shortlist.

The real programme pages were located and read in full: Overview (120 ECTS, 4 semesters, English, EUR 1,500/2,500 per semester, ~EUR 300 semester fee, 20 students, late-September start), Application Process (the three entry conditions verbatim, the application steps, the 1 March / 31 March timeline, the document list, the uni-assist requirement), Modules (the full four-semester structure — confirming the absence of any audio module), and FAQs (120 ECTS accreditation statement, the non-EU tuition comparison table, the portfolio guidance including audio work samples, how to evidence the 12 months' experience, the total cost worksheet, and the scholarship signposts). Everything above is first-hand from those official pages. Not verified: whether specific software-engineering employment would be accepted as 'relevant' professional experience — that is a committee judgement and worth an email to CGL's office before he counts on it.

The entrance exam content is itself the clearest evidence of the discipline's nature: melodic dictation, notation of transposing instruments, timbral hearing and instrument recognition. This is built entirely on classical-music aural skill. There is nothing here about electronic production, DJing, DAWs or club music.

(1) WRITTEN test: melodic dictation of up to 16 measures with a key signature of up to two sharps or flats, plus identification and notation of transposing instruments. (2) ORAL exam: identifying instrument timbres by ear and answering related questions. Taking a 16-bar melodic dictation in up to two accidentals is a skill built over years of formal solfège; identifying transposing instruments and their written-versus-sounding pitches is standard conservatoire theory. Someone with no music degree, no conservatoire training and one year of self-study will not pass this.

_rec.facilities: UNMB operates a Centre for Electronic Music and studio facilities, and runs a separate optional module 'Producție Muzicală în Studioul de Muzică Electronică' for its own students. Facilities inventory UNVERIFIED. Note that module is for enrolled UNMB students and is not a standalone entry route.
_rec.tuitionEU: 8,000 lei for Romanian participants, payable in three instalments — CONFIRMED.
_rec.tuitionNonEU: €1,600 for international participants, payable in three instalments — CONFIRMED VERBATIM on the official page. This is the rate he would pay as a Tunisian national, and it is one of the very few places in this sweep where a distinct non-EU figure is actually published rather than inferred. It is cheap because the course is short and non-degree, not because it is good value for him.
_rec.otherFees: 100 RON registration fee (taxă de înscriere) plus 150 RON enrolment fee (taxă de înmatriculare) — CONFIRMED.
_rec.scholarships: None. Romanian Government/MFA and ARICE scholarships fund licență, masterat and doctorat cycles at accredited institutions. A 15-ECTS postgraduate certificate is not a study cycle and would not be covered. Do not expect funding.
_rec.intakes: Not published on the official programme page — UNVERIFIED. Ask UNMB's Studii Postuniversitare office.
_rec.applicationOpens: Not published — UNVERIFIED. Ask UNMB.
_rec.deadline: Not published — UNVERIFIED. Ask UNMB's Studii Postuniversitare office. Moot in practice, given everything below.
_rec.visaEligible: ALMOST CERTAINLY NOT. A 146-hour, 15-ECTS postgraduate certificate is not a degree programme and will not support a Romanian long-stay study visa or student residence permit for a third-country national. Romania's Letter of Acceptance machinery is built around the licență, masterat and doctorat cycles. Do not plan a move to Romania around this.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: NO in practice — CONFIRMED. The formal condition is only a bachelor's degree in any field, but the entrance examination requires 16-bar melodic dictation, notation of transposing instruments, and aural timbre and instrument recognition. These are conservatoire skills. Without a music background he would fail the exam, and no amount of DAW proficiency substitutes.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: €1,600 tuition plus 250 RON in fees, plus Bucharest living costs for the duration. Irrelevant in practice, since it confers no degree and supports no residence permit.
_rec.recommendation: CONFIRMED IN FULL, NO CORRECTIONS NEEDED — DO NOT PURSUE. I re-checked every figure against the official UNMB page and all of them are exact: 146 hours, 15 ECTS, Romanian instruction, 8,000 lei domestic and €1,600 international in three instalments, 100 RON registration plus 150 RON enrolment, certificate of professional competency C.O.R. 265228 registered in the National Registry of Postgraduate Programmes. This entry was accurate. AVOID stands. Searching 'music direction Romania master' or 'regie muzicală' leads straight here, at Romania's national music university, at an apparently affordable €1,600 for international students. It is not a master's degree. It is a 146-hour, 15-ECTS professional certificate — one-eighth the volume of a real second-cycle degree — it will not support a student residence permit, it is taught in Romanian, and its entrance exam is a conservatoire aural test (16-bar melodic dictation in up to two accidentals, transposing-instrument notation, timbral recognition) that he cannot pass without years of solfège. The low price signals what it is; it is not a bargain. Note also that UNMB's genuine master's portfolio contains NO sound-technology programme: the Faculty of Composition, Musicology and Music Pedagogy offers only Stil și limbaj compozițional, Sinteză muzicologică, Stilistică dirijorală, Jazz și culturi muzicale pop, Educație muzicală contemporană and Culturi muzicale religioase, and the Faculty of Musical Interpretation offers only performance-stylistics masters. UNMB is a dead end for him and should be closed off entirely — the Romanian opening is at UNATC, whose English-taught MAs need no Romanian and no conservatoire ear.
_rec.sourceUrl: https://www.unmb.ro/oferta-educationala/studii-postuniversitare/regie-muzicala/ (official UNMB postgraduate programme page, re-verified: postgraduate status and National Registry inscription, 146 hours, 15 ECTS, Romanian instruction, written melodic dictation up to 16 measures and max 2 accidentals plus transposing instruments, oral timbre identification, 8,000 lei Romanian / 1,600 EUR international in 3 instalments, 100 RON registration and 150 RON enrolment, certificate C.O.R. 265228) and https://www.unmb.ro/admitere/ (official admissions page listing the actual master's programmes, none sound-related) and https://www.unmb.ro/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Metodologia_admitere-cetateni-straini-NON-UE_2026-2027.pdf (UNMB non-EU admission methodology, covering degree cycles)

_rec.program: Master akademske studije MUZIČKA PRODUKCIJA (MAS Music Production) — Interdisciplinary Studies
_rec.institution: Akademija umetnosti (Academy of Arts), Univerzitet u Novom Sadu
_rec.institutionType: State art academy; constituent faculty (članica) of the public University of Novi Sad, Đure Jakšića 7. Departments: Music, Fine & Applied Arts, Drama. This programme sits under 'Interdisciplinarne studije' and is administered by the Drama Department (application e-mail aunsprijemni.dramski@uns.ac.rs). CONFIRMED against the 2026/27 konkurs PDF, which lists the Academy's address, account number 840-32790845-46 and contact aofarts@uns.ac.rs.
_rec.publicPrivate: PUBLIC — CONFIRMED, no change. The 2026/27 master konkurs is issued on the University of Novi Sad's official template ('Obrazac za slanje teksta konkursa... Univerzitet u Novom Sadu') and publishes state-BUDGET-funded places: 152 budget + 108 self-financing across the Academy, of which this programme has 2 budget + 8 self-financing. Budget places exist only at state-founded institutions. Institution-level accreditation dates per the national register: 08.07.2011, 02.06.2017, 11.03.2025.
_rec.language: Serbian only — CONFIRMED and now independently corroborated. The konkurs, informator and accredited curriculum are all in Serbian; the entrance exam is conducted in Serbian. Decisive new evidence: the national accreditation register (NAT, 21.07.2026) flags English-medium programmes explicitly — the Academy has exactly ONE, 'MAS - GITARA / IZVOĐAČKE UMETNOSTI NA ENGLESKOM JEZIKU' (joint with Conservatorio Tartini, Trieste). MAS Muzička produkcija carries no such flag. There is no English track and no distance-learning ('-SND') variant.
_rec.languageRequirement: Konkurs §9 (Upis stranih državljana): a foreign national enrols 'pod istim uslovima kao i domaći državljanin' and additionally files (a) rešenje o priznavanju strane diplome, (b) dokaz o zdravstvenom osiguranju, (c) 'dokaz o poznavanju srpskog jezika'. The required LEVEL and the accepted certificate are still NOT published — UNVERIFIED, confirmed by re-checking the University of Novi Sad's general rule, which only refers back to 'the University Statute and the Faculty Statute'. Ask: Služba za studije i studentska pitanja, 021/422-177 lok. 2 or 021/422-176 lok. 2, aofarts@uns.ac.rs.
_rec.englishTest: None. No IELTS/TOEFL appears anywhere in the konkurs or informator. Confirmed. His untaken IELTS is genuinely irrelevant here — the language barrier is Serbian, and it is a much harder one for him than IELTS would be.
_rec.qualification: Master akademske studije (MAS) — a real, state-recognised second-cycle degree, 60 ECTS, 1 year, 2 semesters. Professional title per the accredited curriculum sheet: 'Мастер музички продуцент' (Master Music Producer). CONFIRMED verbatim from the official accredited curriculum PDF. Supports a Serbian study residence permit.
_rec.accreditationStatus: ACCREDITED — now verified at national level, correcting the previous 'decision could not be machine-read'. The National Body for Accreditation and Quality Assurance in Higher Education (NAT) register 'Vodič kroz akreditovane visokoškolske ustanove i studijske programe u Republici Srbiji', edition of 21 July 2026, lists under Akademija umetnosti, Novi Sad, entry 90: 'ИМТ МАС - МУЗИЧКА ПРОДУКЦИЈА, 03.10.2023, БС 10'. So: accredited 3 October 2023, field IMT (interdisciplinary/multidisciplinary), approved annual intake 10. Serbian accreditation runs 7 years, so this decision is valid through October 2030 and covers his September/October 2027 entry.
_rec.durationEcts: 1 year / 2 semesters, 60 ECTS. CONFIRMED from both the informator and the accredited curriculum sheet.
_rec.focus: Music production proper — not film sound. Content-wise this remains the closest match in the Serbian state sector to a producer/DJ goal.
_rec.whatYouStudy: CONFIRMED verbatim from the official accredited curriculum sheet (mas-muzicka-produkcija-2024.pdf). Compulsory: Muzička produkcija (2+2, both semesters); Zvuk i muzika na filmu (2+1); Savremene tendencije u muzičkoj produkciji 1 (1+2) and 2 (2+2); Muzika-događaj-publika (1+1, both semesters); Master rad – istraživanje (0+0+6); Master rad (0+0+5). Electives, 12 ECTS per semester block chosen from: Dramaturgija savremenog filma (2+1); Metode u muzičkom obrazovanju u digitalnom okruženju (2+0); Istorija elektroakustičke muzike (2+0); Istorija popularne muzike (2+0); Produkcija muzike za nove medije (1+2); Muzika u medijima (1+1). Hours are weekly, as (lectures)+(exercises)+(DON).
_rec.entryRequirements: THE DOCUMENTED CONTRADICTION IS REAL — I re-read both source documents and confirm it, but I now judge which one governs. (a) The 2026/27 konkurs, §2, programme-specific clause: 'Студијски програм – Музичка продукција: завршене основне академске студије у четворогодишњем трајању из уметничке области Музичка продукција, или сродан студијски програм (240 ЕСПБ)' — a four-year BA IN THE ARTISTIC FIELD of music production, or a cognate programme. (b) The informator, Opšti uslovi: 'Пријемни испит могу полагати лица која су завршила основне академске студије у четворогодишњем трајању (240 ЕСПБ)' — any four-year 240-ECTS bachelor. CORRECTION OF EMPHASIS: the konkurs is the legally binding enrolment act adopted on the University's template and issued on the basis of a Government decision; the informator is a summary of exam content. Where they differ the konkurs governs. Read that way, a BSc Software Engineering is NOT in the artistic field of music production and is unlikely to be accepted as 'srodan'. Second, the konkurs §2.2 general rule requires 'najmanje 240 ESPB' and lists the ONLY four exceptions permitted at 180 ECTS — Konzervacija i restauracija, the Guitar/Performing Arts joint programme, Kreiranje serija, and Pozorišni oblici modul Lutkarstvo. Muzička produkcija is NOT among them. A Tunisian three-year 180-ECTS licence is therefore ineligible, full stop. Foreign nationals additionally file the diploma-recognition decision, health-insurance proof and Serbian-language proof.
_rec.portfolioSpec: CONFIRMED and EXPANDED — the previous record omitted two konkurs-level documents. Informator required documents: diploma or certificate of a completed four-year 240-ECTS bachelor; CV (biografija); motivation letter; MEDICAL CERTIFICATE WITH AN AUDIOGRAM (ophthalmologist, ENT specialist, psychologist); scanned/read ID; photo min. 1200x800 px JPG under 1 MB; proof of payment of the application fee. Separately, 'uz prijavu kandidati prilažu': (1) the medical certificate with audiogram, (2) a PORTFOLIO of works created in the 3 years preceding the date of the entrance exam. ADDITIONALLY required by konkurs §5 and omitted from the previous record: the completed PRIJAVNI LIST (application form, downloadable as Prijavni-list-za-master-studije-2026-2027.pdf) and the UVERENJE O POLOŽENIM ISPITIMA (official transcript of passed exams). Submission is 100% electronic, one e-mail per candidate to aunsprijemni.dramski@uns.ac.rs, all files under 12 MB total, every file named with the candidate's full name, study programme named in the subject line. His one-year portfolio plan does map onto the 'previous 3 years' rule.
_rec.auditionSpec: CONFIRMED verbatim. Two stages. PART ONE (pass/fail): written test in the professional-artistic field of Music Production; written analysis/evaluation of a musical work against subjective and objective criteria set by the commission; interview with the commission. Those who pass proceed to multi-day exercises and PART TWO: assessment of submitted works up to 30 points; practical work on the Academy's own material/equipment up to 20 points; oral examination of knowledge in the professional-artistic field of AUDIOVISUAL MEDIA (interview with the commission) up to 30 points. BA grade average scores separately, up to 20 points (10.00 = 20 pts; 6.49–6.00 = 4 pts; below 6.00 scores nothing). A candidate not exceeding 50 total points fails and is not ranked. Mobile phones and auxiliary devices are strictly banned from the exam rooms. Conducted in Serbian.
_rec.equipmentRequired: Part two is 'практичан рад на материјалу Академије' — practical work on the Academy's own material, so no personal studio rig is needed for the exam. What he must supply is a portfolio of finished audio work. No published equipment inventory — UNVERIFIED.
_rec.facilities: Still UNVERIFIED. Practical studio work is implied (the exam is run on Academy equipment) but no inventory of studios, consoles, control rooms or immersive/Atmos capability is published on any official page. Ask the Katedra za audiovizuelne medije via aunsprijemni.dramski@uns.ac.rs.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: NO on the governing document — this is a correction of emphasis from the previous record, which left it 'ambiguous'. The konkurs restricts entry to a four-year bachelor in the artistic field of Music Production or a cognate programme. Software engineering is not cognate to music production in any ordinary reading. Even on the permissive informator reading he would still face a Serbian-language written subject test in music production, a written musical analysis, a commission interview and a portfolio. Unlike a conservatory master there is no instrumental audition, which is the one thing in his favour.
_rec.tuitionEU: Not an applicable category in Serbia. Domestic/self-financing rate for master studies at the Academy, per the Council decision quoted in the konkurs: 125,000 RSD per year. CONFIRMED.
_rec.tuitionNonEU: EUR 1,800 for the whole degree — THE RATE HE WOULD PAY. CONFIRMED verbatim: the konkurs quota table has a dedicated column 'Школарина за странце (евра)' showing 1800 against Muzička produkcija (and against every master programme at the Academy; doctoral studies are 2,400). Since the master is one year, EUR 1,800 is the total tuition, not an annual instalment of a longer degree.
_rec.otherFees: MATERIALLY CORRECTED — the previous record's '4,000 RSD to the University plus 4,000 RSD to the Academy' figure does not appear in any official document and is withdrawn. Actual published figures: (1) ENTRANCE-EXAM FEE 12,000 RSD — konkurs §6: 'Кандидати који приступају пријемном испиту уплаћују 12.000,00 дин' (previously UNVERIFIED); (2) ENROLMENT COST ON ADMISSION 5,500 RSD — konkurs §6 'Трошкови уписа за кандидате који положе пријемни испит износи 5.500,00 дин', corroborated by the official 'ZA UPIS 2026-2027 JE POTREBNO' sheet which also requires the original diploma for inspection, two 3.5x4.5 cm photos, an index book and two ŠV-20 forms; (3) both paid to account 840-32790845-46, poziv na broj 300 for the Drama Department and interdisciplinary studies; (4) DIPLOMA RECOGNITION at the University of Novi Sad — 30,000 RSD, or EUR 260 if paid from abroad, PLUS a 14,900 RSD administrative tax, applicant bears all bank charges (previously UNVERIFIED; source uns.ac.rs recognition page, applied for online at priznavanje.uns.ac.rs, contact priznavanje@uns.ac.rs / 021 485-2021). Compulsory health insurance for foreign students — cost still UNVERIFIED.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: Now largely computable. Tuition EUR 1,800 for the entire 60-ECTS degree. Plus institutional/administrative costs: 12,000 RSD exam fee + 5,500 RSD enrolment + 30,000 RSD (or EUR 260) recognition fee + 14,900 RSD administrative tax, i.e. roughly EUR 480–560 at ~117 RSD/EUR. So about EUR 2,300–2,400 in institution-side costs for the whole master, before living costs, visa fees, health insurance and Serbian-language tuition. Living costs in Novi Sad are not published by the Academy — UNVERIFIED. This remains among the cheapest genuinely accredited music-production masters in Europe.
_rec.fundingLevel: Check. 2 state-budget (fee-free) places against 8 self-financing places, per the konkurs quota table for Interdisciplinarne studije. The konkurs simultaneously says foreigners enrol 'under the same conditions as a domestic citizen' AND publishes a separate foreigner tariff of EUR 1,800 — an unresolved tension. Whether a Tunisian may actually compete for one of the 2 budget places is UNVERIFIED and must be asked in writing. Plan for EUR 1,800. Note also the konkurs caveat that anyone who previously studied at the same level in budget status cannot re-enrol in budget status.
_rec.scholarships: No programme-level or Academy-level scholarship for non-EU applicants is published on any official page — UNVERIFIED, unchanged after re-checking. Do not assume one exists. Realistic avenues to ask: (1) the Serbian Ministry of Education's bilateral scholarship offers, which are distributed through the applicant's home ministry — he should ask the Tunisian Ministère de l'Enseignement Supérieur whether Serbia offers Tunisia places in a given year; (2) the University of Novi Sad international office. Erasmus+ credit mobility is inbound-only for already-enrolled students and is not an admission route.
_rec.visaEligible: Yes in principle — CONFIRMED. This is a nationally registered accredited MAS at a state university (NAT register entry 90), delivered in person, which is the category supporting a Serbian temporary residence permit for education (privremeni boravak radi školovanja). A Tunisian national needs a long-stay visa D before travel, then converts to temporary residence. The konkurs itself confirms the institution enrols foreign nationals and lists the extra documents. Exact visa D document list, fees and processing times are not published by the Academy — UNVERIFIED; authoritative sources are the Serbian Ministry of Interior (MUP) and the Serbian embassy accredited to Tunisia. Serbia is outside the EU and Schengen, so this permit confers no EU mobility.
_rec.intakes: One academic intake per year, October start, but with TWO application rounds (see deadline).
_rec.applicationOpens: 2026/27 cycle: konkurs text published 29 May 2026 (per the Drama Department admissions page), informators posted July 2026 (the Kreiranje serija informator appeared as late as August 2026). For a September/October 2027 entry, expect the 2027/28 konkurs around May–June 2027 and informators in July 2027 — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Note the informator itself states that the Drama Department's application and exam dates 'will be published on the Academy website', so the konkurs is the document to watch.
_rec.deadline: CORRECTED — the previous record missed the SECOND application round entirely, which materially improves his odds. 2026/27 cycle, Drama Department / Interdisciplinary studies (PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new dates for 2027/28). FIRST ROUND: electronic application 05.10.2026; entrance exam 07–13.10.2026; preliminary ranking 15.10.2026; final ranking 20.10.2026; enrolment 20.10.2026. SECOND ROUND (DRUGI KONKURSNI ROK): electronic application 21.10.2026; entrance exam 23–28.10.2026; preliminary ranking 30.10.2026; final ranking and enrolment 03.11.2026. Appeals to the Dean within 24 hours of the preliminary list. The timing trap stands: applications close in EARLY OCTOBER of the year of entry, not the preceding winter — but the diploma-recognition process, the audiogram/medical certificate and Serbian-language study must start many months earlier.
_rec.recommendation: Content-wise this is still the best-matched accredited music-production master in the Serbian state sector, and at roughly EUR 2,300 all-in it is extraordinarily cheap. But after re-reading the governing documents I am less optimistic than the previous assessment, which called it 'the single best find'. Three gates, and he currently fails all three. (1) THE 240-ECTS RULE IS ABSOLUTE. Konkurs §2.2 lists the only four programmes at the Academy that accept 180 ECTS, and Muzička produkcija is not one of them. If his SMU MedTech BSc is a three-year 180-ECTS licence he is ineligible regardless of talent, portfolio or motivation. Verify this FIRST. (2) THE FIELD RESTRICTION IS REAL. The binding konkurs requires a four-year bachelor 'iz umetničke oblasti Muzička produkcija, ili srodan studijski program'. The permissive informator wording is a summary, not the rule. A software-engineering degree is very unlikely to qualify as cognate. (3) SERBIAN. The entrance exam is a written subject test plus a written musical analysis plus two commission interviews, all in Serbian. Going from zero Slavic to exam-level Serbian in twelve months while also building a first audio portfolio and arranging an ENT audiogram in Tunisia is not a realistic 2027 plan. Everything is verified and correct in the record; what has changed is the honest read of his odds. Concrete next step, one e-mail to aofarts@uns.ac.rs copying aunsprijemni.dramski@uns.ac.rs, asking: (a) can a 180-ECTS three-year foreign bachelor ever be accepted for MAS Muzička produkcija; (b) is a BSc in Software Engineering treated as a 'srodan studijski program' under the konkurs; (c) which Serbian-language certificate and level satisfies the requirement; (d) may foreign nationals compete for the 2 budget places.

Institution: Real Conservatorio Superior de Música de Madrid (RCSMM)
Programme / scheme: Máster en Enseñanzas Artísticas en Nuevas Tecnologías de la Música Actual: Creación e Interpretación
Scholarship: Becas del Ministerio de Educación (MECD) general grant; Comunidad de Madrid bonificaciones

_rec.program: Máster en Enseñanzas Artísticas en Nuevas Tecnologías de la Música Actual: Creación e Interpretación
_rec.institution: Real Conservatorio Superior de Música de Madrid (RCSMM)
_rec.institutionType: State conservatoire (Conservatorio Superior de Música), Enseñanzas Artísticas Superiores sector — outside the university system but at the same MECES/EQF level
_rec.publicPrivate: PUBLIC — CONFIRMED. RCSMM is a centre of the Consejería de Educación of the Comunidad de Madrid. Its own masters pages publish a regional 'precios públicos' scale with income-banded discounts, which is a public-price instrument, not a commercial price list.
_rec.qualification: Título Oficial de Máster en Enseñanzas Artísticas. CONFIRMED on the official page as MECES Nivel 3 (Real Decreto 1614/2009) / EQF Level 7, and the page explicitly states it 'habilita acceso al Doctorado'. This is a real state-recognised second-cycle degree, legally equivalent in rank to a Máster Universitario. Not a título propio.
_rec.accreditationStatus: Official. Título Oficial de Máster en Enseñanzas Artísticas, MECES 3 / EQF 7 with doctoral access, stated on the conservatoire's own programme page. Ministry-register listing and Fundación Madri+D verification are consistent with this but were not re-read in this pass.
_rec.language: Spanish. CONFIRMED verbatim on the official page: 'Tanto el documento del TFM como la defensa oral son en idioma español.' No English track.
_rec.languageRequirement: No certificate level is published. The admission process includes a personal interview (10%) plus motivation letter (10%) conducted in Spanish, and the TFM and its defence must be in Spanish. Whether a DELE/SIELE certificate is formally demanded remains UNVERIFIED — ask the Secretaría. Practically he would need solid B2+ Spanish.
_rec.englishTest: None. English is not the medium of instruction and no IELTS/TOEFL appears anywhere on the official pages. This removes one obstacle but replaces it with a harder one.
_rec.durationEcts: 60 ECTS, one academic year in two semesters. CONFIRMED breakdown: Formación General 16 ECTS; Formación Creativa 20 ECTS; Formación Complementaria 12 ECTS; Trabajo Fin de Máster 12 ECTS. NEW FACTS from the official masters page: attendance is mandatory ('asistencia obligatoria'); timetable is Thursday afternoon, Friday morning/afternoon and Saturday morning/afternoon; maximum permitted duration is 2 years, extendable to 3 with justification; a student must pass a minimum of 12 ECTS in the first year to continue.
_rec.focus: New technologies in contemporary art music, in two tracks: Interpretación (contemporary performance, optionally electroacoustic/multimedia) and Composición (contemporary composition with electroacoustic/multimedia creation).
_rec.whatYouStudy: Electroacoustic and multimedia creation and performance, contemporary repertoire, technology applied to current art music. It is an academic contemporary-music programme. There is no commercial production, DJ practice, mixing/mastering or music-business content, so even if he got in it would not directly serve the producer/DJ goal.
_rec.entryRequirements: CORRECTED AND MADE PRECISE. The official page states the programme is for 'Titulados en Enseñanzas Artísticas Superiores, de Composición o Interpretación' OR 'titulados superiores de Grado o equivalente' from Spanish or foreign universities 'en centros de educación superior musical'. The second route is a degree route, but the qualifying clause is that it must be from a HIGHER MUSIC EDUCATION institution. SMU MedTech is not one. Separately the general RCSMM masters page states the baseline as 'Título Superior de Música, Grado Universitario o equivalente' (MECES 2 / EQF 6) plus programme-specific requirements — marginally looser wording, but the programme-specific music clause governs. HARD BLOCKER stands.
_rec.auditionSpec: CORRECTED — the 40% component has TWO alternative forms, which the previous record collapsed into one. Official weighting: personal interview 10% + motivation letter 10% (20% combined); adecuación del programa al perfil 15%; CV, maximum two sides, 15%; related experience 10%; and then EITHER 'Interpretación de obra de música actual (máx. 20 min.)' 40% for the performance track OR 'Composición: presentación de tres obras originales' 40% for the composition track. The composition route is therefore a submitted portfolio of three original works, not a live audition — meaningfully different from what was previously recorded, though still assuming conservatoire-level compositional output.
_rec.portfolioSpec: For the composition track: three original works, worth 40% of the admission score, plus CV (max two sides) and motivation letter. For the performance track: a contemporary work of up to 20 minutes. Submission format and file specifications are not published — ask the master coordinator.
_rec.equipmentRequired: UNVERIFIED — not published. Ask the conservatoire.
_rec.facilities: UNVERIFIED — not detailed on the programme page. RCSMM has electroacoustic studios but no inventory is published.
_rec.tuitionEU: CORRECTED — the previously reported discount bands were wrong.
