_rec.program: Master of Arts in Music Composition & Theory — Major in Composition
_rec.institution: Scuola universitaria di Musica, Conservatorio della Svizzera italiana (affiliated to SUPSI — University of Applied Sciences and Arts of Southern Switzerland)
_rec.institutionType: University-level music school (scuola universitaria di musica) operated by a private-law foundation and affiliated to a public university of applied sciences
_rec.publicPrivate: AMBIGUOUS BY DESIGN — CONFIRMED, and the structure is the honest answer rather than a one-word label. The Conservatorio della Svizzera italiana is run by a private-law foundation, not by the canton directly. But since 2006 its University School of Music has been affiliated to SUPSI, the public UAS of Italian-speaking Switzerland, and its degrees are issued in the Swiss public UAS system. Two hard pieces of evidence it operates on the public side despite the private carrier: it charges the regulated Swiss two-tier fee (CHF 750 for Swiss nationals and residents versus CHF 1,500 for all others) and explicitly grants the lower rate to Swiss students 'under the ASUP / Intercantonal Agreement on Universities of Applied Sciences' — a purely private school has no access to intercantonal subsidy mechanisms. Practical answer: a state-recognised public-system music university with a private-foundation carrier. Get it in writing from the Conservatorio if a scholarship form forces a binary.
_rec.accreditationStatus: CONFIRMED. Real, state-recognised second-cycle Swiss degree — a KMHS-member programme delivered in the SUPSI/UAS system, awarding a Master of Arts. Supports a Swiss student residence permit; the institution runs its own visas-and-permits guidance for exactly this.
_rec.qualification: Master of Arts in Music Composition & Theory — Major in Composition. 4 semesters, 120 ECTS, full time — CONFIRMED. A genuine second-cycle degree. THE TRAP IS REAL AND CONFIRMED: the same institution separately offers a 'MAS in Music Composition' under continuing education. A MAS is a post-master continuing-education certificate, NOT a second-cycle degree, and it will not do the same job for a residence permit or for further study. He must apply for the MA, never the MAS.
_rec.focus: Composition and music theory, emphasising the creative dimension of composition and integrating reflection and craftsmanship. Only ONE major is offered — Composition; there are no alternatives within this MA. Electronic music is present but through an external arrangement: the electronic music section is run in partnership with IRMus at the Accademia Internazionale della Musica in Milan. Ask what that means for contact hours, travel and studio access — a Milan-delivered strand is not the same as an in-house studio.
_rec.whatYouStudy: Composition, with an electronic music section delivered in partnership with IRMus (Accademia Internazionale della Musica, Milan). Composition, orchestration and analysis are the spine of the assessment, which tells you what the teaching is.
_rec.durationEcts: 4 semesters, 120 ECTS, full time — CONFIRMED on the official programme page. Officially described as requiring total dedication in terms of time and emotional involvement.
_rec.language: ITALIAN. The course descriptor and study plan are published in Italian and the institution's language rule targets Italian. English web pages are available and are misleading — the teaching language is Italian. Note in his favour, though it does not save this application: matriculation documents are accepted in Italian, English, French, German, Spanish or Portuguese, so his French-language Tunisian paperwork does not need translating.
_rec.languageRequirement: Italian at CEFR B2 or CELI 3. Notably generous in timing: applicants who do not have that level at the start of studies must still demonstrate a sufficient level and reach B2/CELI 3 BY THE END OF THE FIRST YEAR of study. No English certificate is mentioned. For a French-fluent Arabic native, Italian to B2 in a year is more achievable than German to B2 — the single most forgiving language regime in this set, and worth remembering if he ever looks at Italian-language options, even though the rest of this record is negative.
_rec.entryRequirements: CORRECTED AND HARDENED. The official admission page for this master states the requirement verbatim as 'successful completion of a BACHELOR OF ARTS IN MUSIC OR EQUIVALENT MUSICAL EDUCATION' plus passing an admission exam. The previous record hedged this as 'specific academic prerequisites are not itemised — UNVERIFIED'. They are itemised, and they close the door: a music bachelor, or demonstrably equivalent musical education, is required in substance. Required documents: payment confirmation for the CHF 100 application fee, valid ID or passport copy, BA diploma (or self-certification if the exam is pending), CV in tabular form, and a motivation letter.
_rec.portfolioSpec: NOW VERIFIED — the previous record marked this UNVERIFIED. Candidates must submit 'own compositions, any orchestration work, any analytical work' for committee review and discussion. That is a composer's dossier, not a producer's showreel.
_rec.auditionSpec: NOW VERIFIED IN FULL, and it is decisive. Entrance examinations are held by invitation only after application review, in the window 30 MARCH – 29 APRIL. Three parts: (1) portfolio presentation and discussion with the admissions committee; (2) a WRITTEN TEST of maximum 60 minutes assessing 'competences in ANALYSIS AND EAR-TRAINING'; (3) an oral exam and interview covering SOLFÈGE, the portfolio, the candidate's musical education background, career goals, performance techniques and knowledge of technology. A written analysis-and-ear-training paper plus an oral solfège examination cannot be passed in a year by someone with no conservatory training. This is a conservatory gate, unambiguously.
_rec.equipmentRequired: None published — UNVERIFIED.
_rec.facilities: Not published — UNVERIFIED, and materially important because the electronic music section runs through the Milan partner (IRMus) rather than in-house. Anyone pursuing this should ask specifically: what electronic-music studio facilities exist in Lugano, and how much of the electronic strand is actually taught in Milan.
_rec.intakes: Autumn start, single annual intake — consistent with a 20 February deadline, exams 30 March–29 April, and matriculation in calendar week 36 (first half of September).
_rec.applicationOpens: Not published — UNVERIFIED. Applications close 20 February, so the window opens some months earlier; ask servizi.accademici@conservatorio.ch.
_rec.deadline: 20 FEBRUARY — CONFIRMED on the official programme page ('Application deadline: February 20') and on the application page ('Deadline application 20th February 2026'). Presented as the standing master's deadline. Entrance exams 30 March – 29 April (the institution reserves the right to change the schedule). ADDITIONAL AND SEPARATE: the scholarship deadline is 31 MARCH — later than the application deadline, so an applicant applies first and bids for money afterwards. For a September 2027 start, expect 20 February 2027 — INSIDE his October 2026 – February 2027 planning window.
_rec.tuitionEU: CHF 750 tuition + CHF 250 administrative fee = CHF 1,000 per semester — but ONLY for Swiss nationals and Swiss residents qualifying under the ASUP intercantonal agreement. There is no EU rate; EU nationals arriving from abroad pay the higher rate below.
_rec.tuitionNonEU: CHF 1,500 tuition + CHF 250 administrative fee = CHF 1,750 PER SEMESTER — CONFIRMED as the rate for 'all other students', which is what he would be. CHF 3,500 per year; CHF 7,000 over the 4-semester master.
_rec.otherFees: CONFIRMED AND EXPANDED — the previous record missed the application fee. Matriculation CHF 250 one-off; ADMISSIONS/APPLICATION FEE CHF 100 (payable with the application, confirmation of payment is a required document); student union CHF 5 per semester; Bachelor's/Master's final exam CHF 250; reassessment of a non-main subject CHF 100; reassessment of main subject CHF 200; reassessment of final exams CHF 350; extraordinary intermediate exam CHF 250; DEFERRED FINAL EXAM CHF 500; RETAKEN ECTS CHF 500 PER CREDIT; appeals CHF 100; leave of absence CHF 250 per semester. The CHF 500-per-retaken-ECTS charge is brutal and worth knowing about — Swiss music schools price failure aggressively.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: Institutional fees over 4 semesters: 4 × CHF 1,750 = CHF 7,000, plus matriculation CHF 250, application CHF 100, student union CHF 20, final exam CHF 250 — roughly CHF 7,620 before any re-sits. Living costs in Lugano are not published and are high by any non-Swiss standard. The Swiss student permit requires proof of means — figure UNVERIFIED; confirm with the Swiss representation in Tunis and the Ticino migration authority.
_rec.scholarships: MAJOR CORRECTION — the previous record said 'nothing published at programme level'. That is wrong. The Conservatorio publishes a SUM SCHOLARSHIP FUND on its Study Grants page. For academic year 2026-27 it offers 6 scholarships covering TUITION FEES, ADMINISTRATIVE FEES AND EXAMINATION FEES for the entire duration of studies — 3 for Bachelor's (3 years) and 3 for MASTER'S (2 years). Awarded to candidates who apply and obtain the best marks in the entrance examination, giving priority to those with the greatest financial difficulty. First-time applicants are explicitly eligible and NO NATIONALITY RESTRICTION is published. Application requires an online form plus CV in tabular form, motivation letter, letter of recommendation, family tax return and annual budget. DEADLINE 31 MARCH (incomplete or late applications are not evaluated). Anyone not awarded one is automatically placed on the list for Study Aid funded by the CSI's philanthropic partner network. This is effectively a full institutional-fee waiver — it would zero out the whole ~CHF 7,600 — though not living costs. It is gated entirely behind entrance-exam performance, which is precisely where he fails. Separately, the Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships Art Scholarships stream remains the external route; confirm Tunisia's presence on the art-stream country list for the 2027 call.
_rec.visaEligible: Yes — and the Conservatorio publishes its own visas-and-permits guidance with the operational warning that matters most here: EU/EFTA citizens do not need a visa to sit admission examinations, but citizens of all other countries must check the State Secretariat for Migration list, and 'in many cases, candidates must request a visa to be able to come to Lugano for the admission exam'. A Tunisian applicant may therefore need a visa merely to ATTEND the April entrance examination, months before any study permit — a real cost and a real timeline risk that almost no directory mentions. Contrast Kunstuni Linz, which offers Webex interviews.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: NO — CONFIRMED AND HARDENED. The official requirement is 'successful completion of a Bachelor of Arts in Music or equivalent musical education'. The assessment is a composition dossier plus a written analysis-and-ear-training paper plus an oral solfège examination. A candidate with no music degree, no conservatory training and no existing portfolio cannot clear this, in one year or three.
_rec.recommendation: RECORD IT, DO NOT APPLY — verdict unchanged, and now better evidenced. Two of the previous record's gaps are closed and one of its claims was wrong. CLOSED: the entry requirement is explicitly 'a Bachelor of Arts in Music or equivalent musical education', and the entrance exam is a portfolio of own compositions plus a 60-minute written analysis and ear-training paper plus an oral solfège examination. That is a conservatory gate and it definitively excludes him. WRONG: the previous record said there were no programme-level scholarships. There are — the SUM Scholarship Fund awards 3 Master scholarships for 2026-27 covering tuition, administrative and examination fees for the whole degree, open to first-time applicants with no published nationality bar, deadline 31 March. Worth correcting for the database even though he cannot reach it, because it means the real cost of this institution for a strong musician is near zero rather than CHF 7,600. FOUR THINGS FROM THIS RECORD REMAIN USEFUL TO HIM PERSONALLY EVEN THOUGH THE PROGRAMME IS NOT. (1) The visa-to-attend-the-audition problem, which applies to every Swiss music-school entrance exam he might ever consider, including HSLU Lucerne — plan it months ahead, and always ask whether a remote option exists. (2) The MA-versus-MAS trap at this institution: the 'MAS in Music Composition' is continuing education, not a degree, and applying for it would be a serious mistake. (3) The Italian B2-by-end-of-first-year rule — the most forgiving language regime found anywhere in this sweep. (4) The CHF 500-per-retaken-ECTS charge, a reminder that Swiss institutions price failure. As a September 2027 target it fails on the entrance examination, on composition not being music production, and on the fact that the one funding route is gated behind the exam he cannot pass.

_rec.program: Master of Music – Composition for Media, Video and Games (Master in de muziek – compositie voor media, video en games)
_rec.institution: KASK & Conservatorium, School of Arts of HOGENT and Howest (Hogeschool Gent)
_rec.institutionType: Publicly funded Flemish hogeschool (university college); KASK & Conservatorium is the joint School of Arts of HOGENT and Howest
_rec.publicPrivate: PUBLIC — CONFIRMED. HOGENT and Howest are Flemish Community-funded hogescholen. The school's official financial page publishes tuition using the Flemish decree formula (a fixed 'vast bedrag' plus a per-credit 'variabel bedrag'), including the decreed reduced rates for scholarship students (€139.40) and concessionary students (€623.40) — rate categories that only recognised, publicly funded Flemish institutions administer — alongside the officially decreed non-EEA 'verhoogd studiegeld'.
_rec.qualification: Master of Music / Master in de muziek, 120 ECTS (60 + 60). CONFIRMED on the official programme page, which lists the degree as 'master music' and shows a 1e Master of 60 credits and a 2e Master of 60 credits. A real, state-recognised Flemish second-cycle degree registered in the Higher Education Register of the Flemish Community; supports a Belgian type-D student visa and student residence permit for a non-EU national.
_rec.accreditationStatus: Accredited Flemish master (NVAO / Flemish Higher Education Register), delivered inside HOGENT's recognised master in music. The school describes it as 'the first school of arts in Flanders' to offer a comprehensive master's programme for composing music for moving images. Specific NVAO decision reference UNVERIFIED — check hogeronderwijsregister.be or ask the admissions officer, Paul Lamont (paul.lamont@hogent.be).
_rec.language: DUTCH — CONFIRMED THREE TIMES OVER, no correction needed. The official programme page lists the language of instruction as 'Dutch'; the orientation-test page states flatly 'This is a Dutch spoken programme.'; and the published curriculum is entirely in Dutch course titles ('Compositie voor media, video, games & artistiek onderzoek Master I', 'Electroakoestische compositie & producing Master I', 'Masterseminaries', 'Masterproef Compositie voor media, video & games'). Campus Grote Sikkel, Ghent.
_rec.languageRequirement: CORRECTED. The previous record asserted that 'a Dutch-language proof is required' and left the accepted certificate UNVERIFIED. That is wrong in form, though not in practical effect. The official master-level admission-requirements page — both the general one and the one specific to THIS programme — publishes NO formal language certificate requirement at master level at all. Verbatim: 'You can study all our master's programs in Dutch or English. There are no formal level requirements for English in the master programs, but the Vantage B2 level is strongly recommended.' The detailed Dutch certificate list the previous agent was reaching for (ITNA B2, CNaVT STRT/PROF, NT2 Programma II, NVA5, any University Language Centre or CVO B2) is published on the PROFESSIONAL BACHELOR section of that page and applies to professional bachelors, not to masters. PRACTICAL EFFECT FOR HIM IS UNCHANGED AND STILL FATAL: no certificate is demanded on paper, but the teaching, the orientation interview and the entire curriculum are in Dutch, which he does not speak. Do not read 'no formal requirement' as 'accessible in English'.
_rec.durationEcts: 2 years, 120 ECTS (60 + 60) — CONFIRMED from the official curriculum table. Year 1 (1e Master): Compositie voor media, video, games & artistiek onderzoek Master I; Electroakoestische compositie & producing Master I; Masterseminaries; plus film history and supporting subjects. Year 2 (2e Master): Masterproef Compositie voor media, video & games, audiovisual composition, film analysis, professional practice.
_rec.focus: Composing music for audiovisual production — fiction film, animation film, documentary, games, video and installation art — together with the electroacoustic and production craft behind it. The school's own framing: 'the first school of arts in Flanders' to offer 'a comprehensive master's program for composing music for moving images in all its diversity'.
_rec.whatYouStudy: Composition for documentary, animation, games, video and installation contexts; electroacoustic composition and producing; virtual orchestration; film history and film analysis; master seminars; and a substantial master's project (masterproef). Formal collaboration with HOWEST for game development ('offers the opportunity to become acquainted with the medium of games and develop the necessary technical competencies') and with Film Fest Gent for annual masterclasses, lectures and film-music concerts. The wider music department also runs four project weeks per academic year with guest speakers and interdisciplinary co-creation. Named staff CONFIRMED: Ruben De Gheselle and Dominique Pauwels.
_rec.entryRequirements: SHARPENED AND CORRECTED — the previous record understated how closed this is. The programme's OWN admission-requirements page states the hard rule verbatim: 'To start in the master in music, you need either a bachelor in performing music (for the master in classical music or jazz/pop), OR A BACHELOR IN COMPOSING MUSIC (for the master in music production, composition or music theory).' This master sits in the composition family, so the named requirement is a bachelor in COMPOSING music — not merely 'a music degree'. On top of that sits the diploma-rating cascade: an academic bachelor gains direct admission on passing the orientation interview; a professional bachelor must first complete a TRANSITION programme (schakelprogramma) built from third-bachelor-year courses; an academic bachelor in ANOTHER ARTISTIC discipline may have to take a PREPARATORY programme; and a bridging programme exists 'if you wish to begin a master's program, but do not have the appropriate underlying bachelor's degree'. Route: register at webreg.hogent.be, submit documents, sit the orientation test. NEW FINDING ON DOCUMENTS: KASK requires a physical copy bearing an original certification/apostille/legalisation stamp before it will issue an invitation to enrol (not needed to apply or audition, but needed before enrolment). Tunisia is listed by KASK in BOTH the apostille list AND the legalisation list — the page contradicts itself, so he must email and get it in writing which applies (Tunisia has been a party to the Hague Apostille Convention since 2018, so apostille should be correct). Named contact CORRECTED/ADDED: the admissions officer is Paul Lamont, paul.lamont@hogent.be (the previous record only had the generic toelatingsproeven@hogent.be).
_rec.auditionSpec: CONFIRMED EXACTLY. Orientation test in two parts. ASSIGNMENT: 'You provide soundtracks for 2 video clips (2-3 minutes). The soundtrack is your own choice consisting of several possibilities and genres.' The selection of video clips is emailed to the candidate three weeks before the deadline. INTERVIEW: an intake with the orientation committee — 'several teachers and experts in the field' — covering motivation, artistic discipline, communication skills and knowledge of the specific domain; the committee makes the final decision on enrolment. Location: 'All intakes take place at one of our campuses in Ghent and a personal presence is our preference. If you have to travel far, you can also participate in the interview or audition online' — the online option is confirmed and matters for a Tunisian applicant. Results by email within two working weeks of the interview.
_rec.portfolioSpec: A dossier is assessed alongside the assignment — official wording: 'Based on your dossier and the assignment, you will be invited for an interview.' The dossier contents are still not published anywhere on the site. UNVERIFIED — ask paul.lamont@hogent.be.
_rec.equipmentRequired: Not published. A personal DAW/scoring setup is implied by the assignment (scoring two video clips to picture). UNVERIFIED — ask paul.lamont@hogent.be.
_rec.facilities: Electroacoustic composition and producing are taught subjects with dedicated credits in both years; the music department operates from Campus Grote Sikkel in central Ghent, with structural links to HOWEST game development and Film Fest Gent. Specific studio and immersive-audio specification UNVERIFIED.
_rec.intakes: September, single annual intake, Flemish academic year. Orientation tests are 'organised several times per academic year' (typically an April session and an August session).
_rec.applicationOpens: Registration via webreg.hogent.be, with orientation-test sessions announced per season. For the 2026-27 cycle the April-session registration closed 27.03.2026. PRIOR CYCLE — confirm the new dates for a September-2027 start.
_rec.deadline: CONFIRMED from the official orientation-test page, published 2026 cycle: registration deadline for the APRIL session 27.03.2026 (23:59); interview April session 27.04.2026; deadline for the ASSIGNMENT for the AUGUST session 25.06.2026; interview August session 24.08.2026, with the agenda entry showing the test window as 24.08.26 – 26.08.26. (Minor correction to the previous record, which gave the August interviews as 24-26.08.2026 without distinguishing the single published interview date from the test window.) PRIOR CYCLE — for a September-2027 start expect an equivalent late-March/April 2027 session and a late-June/August 2027 session. A non-EEA applicant must aim at the SPRING session because of visa lead time. Confirm from autumn 2026 with paul.lamont@hogent.be or toelatingsproeven@hogent.be.
_rec.tuitionEU: €1,181.40 for a full-time 60-credit year in 2026-2027 — CONFIRMED on the school's official financial page (fixed €305.40 + €14.60 per credit). Also confirmed for context: Flemish scholarship students pay €139.40 and concessionary students €623.40, but neither category is open to him.
_rec.tuitionNonEU: €8,800.20 PER YEAR — CONFIRMED CORRECT, this is the rate he would pay. The school's official financial page publishes for 2026-2027 an increased tuition fee ('verhoogd studiegeld') for non-EEA students in drama, visual arts, audiovisual arts and MUSIC programmes of a fixed €916.20 plus €131.40 per credit, i.e. €8,800.20 for a full 60-credit year. The site notes some non-EEA students belong to a category exempted from the increased fee; whether a Tunisian national qualifies remains UNVERIFIED — ask HOGENT student administration. Do not assume he does.
_rec.otherFees: CONFIRMED to exist, amount still not published. On top of tuition, students pay a 'contribution towards study costs' (studio/atelier fee), which the school states is 'calculated individually based on the programme, the number of credits taken, and the ratio of practice-based credits to the total', with specifics set out in the Education and Examination Regulations. For a practice-heavy music master this is likely to be a meaningful three-figure sum. Amount UNVERIFIED — ask the KASK study administration. On top of that: Belgian type-D visa fee, residence-permit/city-registration costs, health insurance, and diploma apostille/legalisation and sworn-translation costs.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: Tuition alone: €8,800.20 × 2 = €17,600.40 for 120 ECTS, plus an unpublished study-cost contribution. Ghent living costs and the Belgian proof-of-sufficient-means figure for a student visa are not published on these pages — UNVERIFIED; get the current annual sufficient-means amount from the Belgian Immigration Office (Dienst Vreemdelingenzaken).
_rec.scholarships: UPGRADED FROM THE PREVIOUS RECORD, which called this 'Partial'. The realistic route is the FLEMISH GOVERNMENT MASTER MIND SCHOLARSHIP, and it is far stronger than previously described: verified on studyinflanders.be, a Master Mind Scholarship is a grant of €10,225 PLUS A TUITION FEE WAIVER per academic year — the host institution may charge the awardee no more than the lowest Flemish rate, €136.50 for 2026-2027. That is effectively FULL funding, not a partial offset. It is open to outstanding students from around the world with no exclusion of Tunisia; only a handful of places are RESERVED for priority countries (Japan 3, Mexico 3, Palestine 2, USA 5), and unfilled reserved places revert to the general ranked list. The 2026-2027 call is closed; the 2027-2028 call would open in the usual autumn/winter window. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: Master Mind is nominated through the institution, so HOGENT must put the programme and the candidate forward, and whether THIS Dutch-taught master is on HOGENT's Master Mind list is UNVERIFIED — ask the HOGENT International Office. No programme-specific scholarship is published on the course page. NOTE THAT NONE OF THIS HELPS HIM, because he cannot clear the entry gates below.
_rec.visaEligible: Yes — a recognised Flemish second-cycle degree at a publicly funded hogeschool supports a Belgian type-D student visa and student residence permit, applied for at the Belgian Embassy/Consulate with the acceptance letter. Note the enrolment-blocking document chain: KASK will not issue a formal invitation to enrol without a physical copy carrying an original apostille (or legalisation) stamp, and any diploma not in Dutch, French, German or English needs a sworn translation. Start that paperwork months early.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: NO — CONFIRMED, and the case against is now stronger than the previous record stated. The programme's own admission page names the required prior degree as 'a bachelor in composing music'. A BSc in Software Engineering is not a music bachelor, not a composition bachelor, and not even 'an academic bachelor in another ARTISTIC discipline' — it falls outside all three named categories, leaving only the discretionary 'bridging programme' for applicants without the appropriate underlying bachelor's degree. That would mean a bridging or preparatory year BEFORE the two master years, in Dutch. And the whole programme is Dutch-spoken. He is blocked on two independent gates, either of which alone would be disqualifying for a September-2027 start. The orientation-test assignment (scoring two 2-3 minute clips) is the one part he could plausibly do.
_rec.recommendation: A genuine, well-designed, fairly-priced accredited Flemish master — and a bad fit for HIM, confirmed on re-check and now with harder evidence than before. Two independent blockers: (1) the programme is DUTCH-SPOKEN end to end, verified in three separate places on the official site; (2) the named prior-degree requirement is 'a bachelor in composing music', which routes a software-engineering graduate at best into a discretionary bridging programme, and HOGENT warns that a student visa for a language-preparation year is only issued once enrolled in a full course at a university language centre. Do not spend effort here for September 2027. TWO THINGS WORTH SALVAGING FROM THIS CHECK, HOWEVER. First, the same admission page reveals that KASK runs a separate MASTER IN MUSIC PRODUCTION inside the same master-in-music family — much closer to his actual goal than composition for screen, and worth investigating as its own record (it carries the same 'bachelor in composing music' gate and probably the same Dutch-language problem, but that should be verified rather than assumed). Second, the Master Mind Scholarship is a true full ride at Flemish institutions (€10,225 plus a fee waiver down to €136.50, open worldwide) — that is a strong reason to keep Flanders on his map generally, provided he can find an English-taught Flemish master whose entry rules do not demand a music bachelor. If he ever does contact Ghent, write to Paul Lamont (paul.lamont@hogent.be), not the generic address.

_rec.accreditationStatus: CONFIRMED. NEAA-accredited state academy. Specialty listed in the official 2026/2027 handbook (SPRAVOCHNIK-magistur_sled_bakalavur_2026_2027), Theory-Composition-Conducting Faculty (ТКДФ), in both the one-year and the two-year sections.

_rec.whatYouStudy: Sound engineering and sound design for video games. Interview syllabus (unchanged 2025/26 → 2026/27): (1) physical acoustics, behaviour of sound in space, sound phenomena; (2) sound-technical devices — electroacoustic transducers, mixing desks, amplifiers, processors; (3) spatial sound formats; (4) computer and electronic music technologies. Reading: Ballou, Huber & Runstein, Huber (MIDI Manual), Eargle (Microphone Book, Loudspeaker Handbook), Blackstock, plus Malyakov, Malinovski and Kusev.
_rec.durationEcts: CORRECTED. Not 'two years only'. The 2026/2027 handbook offers this specialty as 'една или две учебни години' — ONE OR TWO academic years. The handbook also resolves the previously unverified credit total: one-year master's = minimum 60 credits (for holders of a bachelor's in the SAME specialty); two-year master's = minimum 120 credits (ECTS).
_rec.language: Bulgarian. CONFIRMED — no English-taught track for this specialty.
_rec.languageRequirement: CONFIRMED. Foreigners must demonstrate Bulgarian ('За чужденците се изисква да владеят български език'), by one of three routes: (1) a document issued by a Bulgarian higher-education institution; (2) passing written AND oral Bulgarian examinations before a commission appointed by the NMA Rector; or (3) completing NMA's one-year preparatory course in language and specialised preparation, which ends with examinations in all subjects including written and oral Bulgarian. IELTS/TOEFL are irrelevant and not accepted.
_rec.entryRequirements: CORRECTED — AND THIS REVERSES THE PREVIOUS RECORD'S CENTRAL FINDING. The 2026/2027 handbook, section IX, states verbatim: „Специалност „Звукорежисура и звуков дизайн за игри“, срок на обучение две години. Необходимо е кандидатът да притежава музикална образователно-квалификационна степен „Бакалавър“.“ A MUSIC bachelor's degree IS now required for the two-year track. The one-year track is worse: it requires a bachelor's specifically in „Звукорежисура, звуков и медиен дизайн“, and external candidates must have graduated in „Звукорежисура“ at another HEI. The previous agent's finding rested on the 2025/2026 handbook, where the clause was genuinely absent — I checked both PDFs side by side and the clause was ADDED for 2026/2027. Additional hard requirement for foreign-diploma holders: documents for the Bulgarian recognition procedure must be filed with the Учебен отдел during the academic year PRECEDING application and at least two months before the candidate documents themselves.
_rec.auditionSpec: Single-stage oral interview (събеседване) on the four technical topics. No instrumental audition, no solfège. Format CONFIRMED unchanged for 2026/2027 — but now academically out of reach for him.
_rec.portfolioSpec: CONFIRMED — no portfolio is demanded by the published exam programme for external candidates; admission is by interview on the technical syllabus. (NMA's own graduating students are instead admitted on their diploma-project defence: an independent sound-recording product plus a written theoretical exposition.)
_rec.equipmentRequired: Not stated in the 2026/2027 handbook. Ask the ТКДФ office (sbogdanova@nma.bg, 0882 33 50 43).
_rec.facilities: Not published for this specialty. NMA operates sound-engineering studios; no equipment inventory is published. Ask the department.
_rec.tuitionEU: State-commissioned (държавна поръчка) places, free of tuition, for Bulgarian/EU candidates; minimum grade Мн. добър 4.50 on each entrance/state exam to be ranked for them. Fee-paying places require minimum Добър 4.00. The domestic fee-paying rate is not published in the handbook.
_rec.tuitionNonEU: €8,500 per academic year — CONFIRMED VERBATIM on NMA's official non-EU page: „За магистратура – 8500 евро“. This is the rate he would pay as a Tunisian national. Preparatory language year: €5,500. (For reference: bachelor €7,000, doctorate €10,000.) Non-EU nationals are NOT eligible for state-subsidised places.
_rec.otherFees: CORRECTED. The candidate application fee is €100 / 195.58 BGN — not '100 leva'. The 300 BGN/€153.39 and 450 BGN/€230.08 figures the previous record cited are the fees for the RECOGNITION PROCEDURE for a foreign master's-level qualification (standard vs. after-deadline/expedited), not the application fee. Bulgarian-language examination fee €50. Legalisation, apostille and certified Bulgarian translation of all foreign documents, plus NACID recognition, are additional. Sofia living costs additional and not published.
_rec.scholarships: None a Tunisian national can win. State-subsidised places are closed to non-EU nationals. The ПМС 103/1993 and ПМС 228/1997 channels require Bulgarian origin or North Macedonian citizenship; ПМС 264/2024 requires temporary-protection status in Bulgaria. Only theoretical route: a Bulgaria–Tunisia bilateral education agreement — enquire at the Bulgarian Embassy in Tunis. Treat as fully self-funded.
_rec.englishTest: None. No IELTS or TOEFL is required or accepted anywhere in this admission. His untaken English test is irrelevant here — which is not an advantage, because the substitute demand is certified Bulgarian.
_rec.intakes: September / October (one intake per year)
_rec.applicationOpens: 2026/2027 cycle, ТКДФ: documents 26 May – 4 June 2026; exams 8–20 June 2026; ranking 23 June 2026; enrolment 23–26 June 2026. Non-EU direct admission (without preparatory course): до 12 юни 2026 г. Non-EU with preparatory course: до 25 юни, then 1–3 September. Non-EU nationals who completed a bachelor's at a Bulgarian HEI apply 1–15 June and 1–15 September. Documents are submitted online.
_rec.deadline: For a September 2027 start, expect the same shape: ТКДФ documents late May – early June 2027, non-EU direct-admission deadline around 12 June 2027. Exact 2027 dates publish on nma.bg/priem each spring. Because foreign-diploma recognition must start a full academic year earlier, the real deadline for him would have been autumn 2026.
_rec.visaEligible: Yes in principle — NMA runs a published „извън ЕС“ channel producing the MES Certificate of Acceptance required for a Bulgarian type-D visa and student residence permit. Irrelevant in his case because he cannot clear the academic entry rule.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: NO — CORRECTED. This is the single most important change to the previous record. The 2026/2027 official handbook explicitly requires a MUSIC bachelor's for the two-year track, and a sound-engineering bachelor for the one-year track. A BSc Software Engineering is not an eligible entry qualification for either. The previous record's headline claim ('unlike Musicology/Composition/Conducting, the sound-engineering specialties carry NO such clause') was true of the 2025/2026 handbook and is false for 2026/2027.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: Moot — he is ineligible. For reference had he qualified: €17,000 tuition over two years, plus €5,500 if the preparatory language year were needed, plus €100 application, €50 language exam, ~€153–230 recognition fee, plus Sofia living costs.
_rec.recommendation: PREVIOUS RECORD OVERTURNED — HE IS NOT ELIGIBLE. The 2025/2026 handbook did not require a music bachelor's for this specialty; the 2026/2027 handbook, section IX, does, in the same boilerplate sentence used for Musicology, Composition and Conducting. I verified this by extracting and comparing both official PDFs directly. Unless NMA reverses the clause again for 2027/2028 — worth one email to sbogdanova@nma.bg, but do not plan around it — a BSc Software Engineering graduate cannot apply. Everything that made this look like the best academic match in the sweep (technical interview instead of an audition, no portfolio, game audio and spatial sound content) is now behind a door he cannot open, and even if it reopened, the €8,500/year with no winnable scholarship and the certified-Bulgarian requirement would still stand. Remove it from the shortlist.

_rec.institution: Det Jyske Musikkonservatorium / The Royal Academy of Music Aarhus/Aalborg (RAMA) — host of DIEM, the Danish Institute of Electronic Music (founded 1986 as Denmark's national centre for electronic music; part of RAMA since 2003)

_rec.qualification: Master of Music (MMus), 2 years, awarded by RAMA

_rec.institutionType: State conservatoire
_rec.language: UNVERIFIED — RAMA teaches internationals in English in practice; no language test named in the 2026/27 admission-requirements document
_rec.durationEcts: 2 years (120 ECTS)
_rec.whatYouStudy: Electronic Composition (Aarhus): 'The target audience of the programme is composers who want to work professionally with the composition and production of electronic music.' Electronic Music Production (Aalborg): aimed at producers wanting to 'work professionally with electronic music production' and 'complete commercial and diverse professional electronic music production assignments' — THIS SECOND ONE IS THE CLOSEST THING IN EUROPE TO A DEGREE FOR AN ELECTRONIC-MUSIC PRODUCER.
_rec.entryRequirements: QUOTE from the official 2026/27 admission-requirements PDF: 'To be admitted to a master's programme at RAMA, applicants must have earned a relevant bachelor's degree or earn such a degree before starting on the master's programme. The following bachelor's degrees are PRE-APPROVED: Bachelor's degree from a music academy; Bachelor's degree from another artistic programme approved by the Danish Ministry of Culture*; Bachelor's degree from a university musicology programme*.' Footnote: '*The applicant may have to pass an extended admission test to verify that he/she possesses the skills, knowledge, or qualifications that are acquired on music academy bachelor programmes but which the applicant may not have acquired on his/her qualifying BA programme. Examples include ear training, music theory, general music skills, minor instruments, or technical disciplines.'
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: NOT PRE-APPROVED, BUT NOT EXPLICITLY EXCLUDED. The wording is 'a relevant bachelor's degree', followed by a list of PRE-APPROVED degrees — which implies other degrees are assessed case by case, possibly with an extended admission test. Given the electronic-production programme's professional (not conservatoire) orientation, a direct enquiry is warranted.
_rec.portfolioSpec: EXACT, from the official PDF. ELECTRONIC COMPOSITION (Aarhus): 'The applicant uploads a MAXIMUM OF 20 MINUTES OF MUSIC featuring works composed and produced by the applicant with the application form. The works can be cross-disciplinary and include video. Information about production location, equipment used, and any other participants must be clear.' Plus an application form covering motivation, expectations, ambitions after the programme, 'the applicant's familiarity with relevant hardware and software', work descriptions, education so far, artistic experience, and experience as a music communicator/teacher, with diplomas attached. ELECTRONIC MUSIC PRODUCTION (Aalborg): '15-20 MINUTES OF AUDIO featuring works produced by the applicant… The applicant is encouraged to demonstrate artistic coherence and at the same time a degree of variation'; plus a work description of 'maximum of two A4 pages' explaining the background of the music and how it was created; plus a CV emphasising music-production experience; plus the bachelor diploma.
_rec.auditionSpec: NO INSTRUMENTAL AUDITION — this is a portfolio-plus-interview model. ELECTRONIC COMPOSITION: works are evaluated by a board of examiners; shortlisted applicants are invited to an interview and 'will receive a SET ASSIGNMENT from the board of examiners prior to the interview'. Interview lasts approx. 25 minutes: applicant gives a presentation of MAXIMUM 7 MINUTES on software/hardware used, own artistic practice and ambitions; then 'the composition assignment is played back (2 minutes)' and the applicant explains it (4 minutes); then dialogue with the panel. 'The interview emphasises the applicant's capacity for aesthetic reflection, his/her ability to use electronics in an artistic context, and the applicant's general suitability for study.' Total 25 min + 20 min evaluation/feedback. ELECTRONIC MUSIC PRODUCTION: 'No later than 8 days prior to the admission test, the applicants receive a production assignment' — test is a 10-minute presentation plus a 20-minute interview, maximum 30 minutes. WHETHER THE INTERVIEW CAN BE DONE ONLINE IS UNVERIFIED (RAMA does allow non-EU bachelor applicants to upload 'an unedited video recording (one take)' instead of attending, which suggests remote accommodation exists — must be confirmed for master's).
_rec.tuitionNonEU: CONFLICTING FIGURES — Study in Denmark states EUR 6,600 PER TERM (approx. EUR 13,200/yr) for non-EU/EEA/CH; another source states DKK 114,578 per year (approx. EUR 15,350). EU/EEA/CH students pay EUR 0. MUST BE CONFIRMED with RAMA. Half-fee (DKK 29,348 per semester) applies only to certain postgraduate ensemble diplomas.
_rec.otherFees: Application fee DKK 500 (approx. EUR 67), non-refundable, 'contributes to the cost of admission tests'. Danish residence permit; living approx. DKK 8,000–10,000/month.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: approx. EUR 13,200–15,400 tuition + approx. EUR 12,000 living = approx. EUR 25,000–27,500/yr
_rec.scholarshipName: UNVERIFIED — Danish Cultural Ministry institutions have very limited scholarship provision for non-EU students
_rec.scholarships: UNVERIFIED
_rec.languageRequirement: No language test named in the admission-requirements document — UNVERIFIED
_rec.englishTest: UNVERIFIED
_rec.deadline: APPLICATION DEADLINE 1 DECEMBER at 12.00 noon (for the 2026/27 year it was 1 December 2025). Admission tests scheduled for JANUARY AND FEBRUARY. For non-EU/EEA applicants the application system opened 3 December 2025 for the following cycle. FOR A SEPTEMBER 2027 START THE DEADLINE IS APPROXIMATELY 1 DECEMBER 2026 — one of the earliest in this whole sweep.
_rec.applicationOpens: Autumn; apply via kum.studieoptag.dk / musikkons.dk
_rec.verdictForCandidate: ONE OF THE FIVE BEST FINDS. The admission test is literally: submit 15–20 minutes of your own electronic music, do a set production assignment, then talk for 25 minutes about your gear, your process and your ambitions. There is no instrumental audition, no score-reading, no music-theory paper. The Aalborg 'Electronic Music Production' master in particular is aimed at exactly what he wants to become. The obstacles are the non-pre-approved bachelor and the EUR 13,000+ non-EU fee with no confirmed scholarship.

He does not, and the rubric puts it at C for two published reasons that compound: the specialisation requires 80 credits in performing or electronic music that he lacks, and the entrance exam is 50% AUDITION with a hard pass threshold, which he cannot currently clear and may not even be able to sit remotely. Add a flat no-scholarship policy against his funding preference. That said, this is the one C in the batch worth actively contesting rather than abandoning — the 'or equivalent' clause plus a genuinely strong body of electronic-music work is the most plausible argument available anywhere in this slice. Highest-value action: email Per Elias Drabløs (per.e.drablos@uia.no) in autumn 2026 with a portfolio, asking directly (a) whether an engineering BSc plus documented electronic-music practice can satisfy the 80-credit rule, and (b) whether the audition can be submitted as a recording from Tunisia. _rec.qualification: A CEV school 'Máster' — a private award. No ECTS is published and no validating university is named.
_rec.accreditationStatus: NOT OFFICIAL — and CEV effectively admits it. The Educaweb listing carries CEV's own programme description stating the master has 'no equiparación en la formación universitaria en España' — NO EQUIVALENCE TO SPANISH UNIVERSITY EDUCATION. That is about as explicit a disclaimer as a Spanish private school ever prints. So: no ANECA verification, no validating university, no ECTS, no EHEA status, no PhD access — a school diploma, a título propio in substance. IMPORTANT distinction he must hold onto: CEV genuinely DOES deliver officially accredited qualifications — its Técnico Superior en Sonido para Audiovisuales y Espectáculos is a real Grado Superior homologated by the Ministerio de Educación y Formación Profesional. But that is a VOCATIONAL, SUB-DEGREE award, and its officialness does not transfer to this master. The school's homepage claim that its qualifications are 'homologados por el Ministerio' refers to the FP catalogue, not to this programme.
_rec.visaEligible: PLAUSIBLE ON STRUCTURE, UNCONFIRMED IN PRACTICE — and structurally the best of this batch. At 1,200 hours over one academic year, this works out to roughly 30 contact hours a week over a 40-week year, comfortably clearing Spain's 20-hours-per-week minimum, and it is fully in-person in Madrid, clearing the 50%-presencial rule, over a course far longer than 90 days. Spanish rules accept non-official private courses for estancia por estudios provided the centre is authorised and those thresholds are met, and CEV IS an authorised centre for its FP programmes. However, CEV publishes NOTHING about non-EU student visas, and the Oficina de Extranjería can refuse a visa where the specific course is not homologated — which this one is not. Structurally promising, but he must obtain written confirmation and, ideally, ask CEV to name a current non-EU student on this exact programme.
_rec.focus: Music production and composition spanning artist projects, film, television, video games and theatre — broader and more screen-oriented than a DJ/electronic path.
_rec.whatYouStudy: Five modules, VERIFIED and consistent across two aggregators: (1) Industria y Música Audiovisual — contemporary production methods, distribution channels, working in the music industry, audiovisual production and film scoring; (2) Producción de Proyecto Musical — the student independently produces a professional music project under tutor supervision, typically producing an artist or original compositions; (3) Formación Instrumental — practical piano, electric guitar, bass or drums with ensemble playing; (4) Grabación Avanzada en Estudio — capture of acoustic and electronic sources, DAWs, mixing, mastering, sound design software, synthesis and sampling; (5) Lenguaje Musical y Técnicas Creativas — harmony, arrangement and notation.
_rec.durationEcts: 1 year, 1,200 hours. No ECTS is published — a meaningful omission, since without ECTS the award cannot be positioned against anything in the EHEA.

_rec.intakes: One intake per year, October. Enrolment currently shown as open with 'últimas plazas'.
_rec.entryRequirements: Not published in detail. CEV states generally that its masters do not require a specific prior qualification but do demand advanced sector knowledge. The compulsory Formación Instrumental and Lenguaje Musical modules imply real musical grounding is expected in practice.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: NO FORMAL BAR, BUT A REAL PRACTICAL ONE — and this is the decisive fit problem. No published rule excludes a non-music bachelor, and CEV says masters need no specific prior qualification. But Module 3 is compulsory practical instrumental training on piano, electric guitar, bass or drums WITH ENSEMBLE PLAYING, and Module 5 is harmony, arrangement and notation. A candidate with no instrumental training and no conservatory background starts those two modules from zero alongside classmates who do not. Of the five programmes in this batch, this is the most conventionally musician-oriented and the worst match for his profile. _rec.recommendation: A credible, well-established school and a fair 1,200 hours for the money — but the wrong programme for THIS candidate, and I would not put it ahead of the alternatives. The decisive issue is fit, not price: two of the five modules are compulsory instrumental performance with ensemble playing and classical harmony/notation, and he has no instrumental training whatsoever. This is a musician's production master, and he would spend a third of the year fighting a deficit rather than building the electronic-production and DJ craft he actually wants. Layered on top: CEV itself concedes the award has no equivalence in Spanish university education, publishes no ECTS, no entry requirements, no fees and no scholarship figures on its own site, and says nothing about visas. Its structural advantage — 1,200 in-person hours, which is the only programme here that plainly clears the 20-hours-a-week visa threshold — is real and worth noting, but it does not outweigh a fundamental content mismatch. Consider only if he decides he wants formal musical grounding alongside production, which is not what he has asked for.

_rec.tuitionPerYear: MAJOR CORRECTION — the previously cited €8,000-€15,000/year range is badly wrong for a non-EU student. IED's official tariff document for a.a. 2026/27 (Milano, Roma, Torino, Firenze), Diploma Accademico di Primo Livello, states for STUDENTI RESIDENTI EXTRA EUROPA — which is his category as a Tunisian national — a tassa d'iscrizione of €2.500,00 plus a retta di frequenza of €18.300,00, giving a TOTALE ANNUALE of €20.800,00. _rec.reputationSignals: IED is one of the most established private design-education brands in Europe, ministerially accredited in Italy for first-level diplomas, and operating campuses across Italy, Spain and Brazil. It is credible and its accreditation is real. Its weakness for this particular search is subject coverage and price, not legitimacy: sound exists only at undergraduate level and only in Italy, its Spanish campuses (Madrid, Barcelona, Bilbao) offer no sound design programme at all — the closest Barcelona master is in Design for Interaction and Extended Reality, not audio — and its published non-EU rate of €20,800/year for a bachelor-level diploma is at the very top of the private-education market in Italy. _rec.recommendation: Rule out, and treat this as a negative finding rather than an option — but the reason is now far more damning than previously understood. The headline correction is the money: IED's official 2026/27 tariff puts a NON-EUROPEAN student on the top band with no income assessment available, at €2,500 enrolment plus €18,300 tuition = €20,800 per year, plus a €190 regional tax, so €20,990 a year and roughly €63,000 across three years before living costs. The previously cited €8,000-€15,000 range was IED's general marketing band and is simply not the price he would pay; the real figure is more than double the bottom of it. And he would be paying that for a Diploma Accademico di PRIMO livello — a bachelor-equivalent, 180 CFA, undergraduate qualification at exactly the level of the BSc he already holds. Two genuine corrections in IED's favour, neither of which rescues it: an English-taught stream DOES exist in Milan (IED's own page records the language as "Italian | English"), so the language barrier assumed earlier is not real there; and the credit total is confirmed at 180 CFA/ECTS with a proper ministerial accreditation behind it. It is a legitimate institution selling a legitimate degree — just the wrong degree, at the wrong level, at a price that would consume his entire budget. Also note that the ROME variant is the only IED sound page that explicitly mentions "performance and DJing" and music production, so it is nearer his interest than Milan's installation-and-events emphasis — but Rome is Italian-only and equally undergraduate, so it changes nothing. The useful conclusion for him is the one this batch keeps confirming from three directions: the international-chain landscape at genuine master's level in these four countries is far thinner than the marketing suggests. IED has no sound master anywhere despite campuses in both Spain and Italy; SAE's electronic music offering is an unpriced private certificate outside its own AFAM authorisation; and Portugal's best chain-adjacent option is a sub-bachelor BTEC. At master's level in this field it is essentially Berklee Valencia and little else — everything else is diplomas, certificates and título propio.

MAJOR FEE CORRECTION: STUDENTI RESIDENTI EXTRA EUROPA pay tassa d'iscrizione €2.500,00 + retta di frequenza €18.300,00 = TOTALE ANNUALE €20.800,00, plus a €190,00 regional tax required for all first-level diploma enrolments (note 4) — approximately €20,990/year and about €63,000 over three years, versus the €8,000-€15,000/year previously recorded. The document also confirms the six ISE contribution bands for Italian/EU residents (€8,500 to €20,800), a separate EFTA+ band at €15,800, that missing ISE documentation places a student automatically in the top band, and that the rates apply only to new first-year enrolments for 2026/27 at Milano, Roma, Torino and Firenze. LANGUAGE CORRECTION: the Milan course page's own structured data records courseLanguage as "Italian | English", confirming an English stream exists in Milan — previously assumed Italian-only. CREDITS CONFIRMED at 180 CFA/ECTS (previously UNVERIFIED). Exact award title confirmed as "First Level Academic Diploma in New Technologies of Arts – Specialization Sound Design". _rec.scholarships: STRONG ON PAPER, BUT ONE CORRECTION MATTERS ENORMOUSLY. (1) INTERNATIONAL POSTGRADUATE SCHOLARSHIP (portfolio-based): partial first-year tuition coverage; NON-EU students are placed at 'up to €6,000' on the postgraduate scholarship page, while the February 2027 competition page quotes 'up to €7,000 depending on income bracket' for Master of Arts. EU-resident MA candidates get €2,200-€3,000 in brackets 1-5 and up to €6,000 in bracket 6; Academic Master EU-passport candidates get €3,000. RENEWABLE for the second year if the call's conditions are met. Assessed by faculty and admissions jury with decisive weight on the portfolio. Winners must ENROL WITHIN 7 DAYS of notification or forfeit. (2) *** NOT COMBINABLE *** — NABA states these scholarships 'cannot be combined with other NABA scholarships, DSU scholarships or additional financial grants'. THIS KILLS THE STACKING ASSUMPTION: he CANNOT take the international scholarship AND the early-enrolment discount, and he CANNOT take it AND a DSU regional grant. He must pick one. (3) EARLY ENROLMENT SCHOLARSHIP: 10% off tuition for October 2026 starts, international students and new registrations only, applied automatically on enrolling by 29 January 2026 — no separate application; those who previously registered and postponed are excluded. For October 2027 NABA has announced 15% for Bachelor of Arts — the MA equivalent for 2027 is UNVERIFIED, ask. (4) EUROPEAN INTERNATIONAL SCHOLARSHIP COMPETITION for postgraduates: deadline 24 July 2026 (October 2026 entry). (5) FORMER NABA STUDENTS: 20% off total tuition excluding regional tax — not applicable. (6) AUSONIO ZAPPA SCHOLARSHIP: total tuition exemption, currently expired, registration open for future announcements — worth registering interest. (7) DSU / regional right-to-study: NABA administers it and non-EU students are eligible, but it is not combinable with the NABA international scholarship, and second-level places put to competition are extremely few.

_rec.reputationSignals: One of Italy's best-known private art academies, inside the state AFAM system, Milan and Rome campuses, genuinely international cohort, transparent published fee brackets, a scholarship that explicitly names non-EU students, and a clean visa pipeline. RED FLAGS: the non-EU fee is roughly double the lowest EU band; scholarships are explicitly NON-COMBINABLE so the headline reliefs cannot be stacked; and — decisively for him — there is no music, sound or audio programme anywhere in the catalogue.
_rec.recommendation: On process and money transparency NABA is the best-run non-EU institution in this batch, and the portfolio-judged scholarship genuinely names non-EU students at up to €6,000-€7,000, renewable. But two hard facts must land. FIRST, the stacking he might have been counting on does not exist: NABA states the scholarship 'cannot be combined with other NABA scholarships, DSU scholarships or additional financial grants', so the realistic best case for year one is €22,250 minus about €6,000-€7,000, i.e. roughly €15,000-€16,000 — not the €14,000 that a stacked 10% discount would have implied. SECOND, and more important, THERE IS NO MUSIC PROGRAMME HERE. I checked the entire MA and Academic Master catalogue: nothing in music, sound design, audio production or electronic music. Digital and Live Performance and Creative Media Production are performance-technology and media-production degrees where a software engineer would do well and where sound is one element among many. Pursue NABA only if he consciously reframes his ambition towards live/performance technology and media production and accepts that he will build his DJ/producer craft outside the curriculum. If he does apply: apply in the EARLIEST session, choose ONE relief (the scholarship, since it is worth more than 10%), and put everything into the portfolio because the portfolio is what the jury weighs.

The requirement of "two papers illustrating writing ability IN ANY AREA OF MUSIC SCHOLARSHIP" is in practice a serious barrier for someone who has never studied music academically — he would have to write two substantial music-scholarship papers from scratch.

This is a genuine, guaranteed, five-year funding commitment covering tuition and living — one of only a handful found in this search. Tunisians are eligible (UC doctoral support is internal and not nationality-restricted). Operational caveat: "International students must pass an English Language Proficiency Certification Exam before being eligible to be hired as a TA" — so a weak spoken-English score can delay the TA component of the package.
_rec.englishTest: EXACT, from the department: "The minimum TOEFL score is 550" (paper-based) or 90 computer/internet-based; "minimum IELTS score is 7"; "minimum DET score is 120" (Duolingo). GRE: "Graduate Record Examination (GRE) scores are not required for this application."
_rec.deadline: *** VERIFIED EXACT DATE *** "Wednesday, December 02, 2026 for the Fall 2027 application cycle." AFTER September 2026 — reachable, and this is one of the firmest dates confirmed in the whole search.
_rec.applicationOpens: UC graduate applications typically open in September. UNVERIFIED for 2027 cycle.
_rec._verdict: GUARANTEED FIVE-YEAR FUNDING, BUT A DOCTORATE AND A HARD ACADEMIC GATE. The money is real and guaranteed — better than almost anything else found. But there is no master's option, the emphasis is experimental-academic rather than artist-producer, and the requirement to submit two music-scholarship papers plus IELTS 7.0 makes this the least accessible of the funded US options for someone with a software-engineering BSc and no music background. _rec.valueVerdict: CONDITIONAL — leaning AVOID for him. This is unambiguously a genuine, state-recognised, accredited second-cycle degree from a Russell Group university, so it is not a diploma-mill AVOID. But it charges the highest fee of the six (£23,000) for a programme whose stated relevant subjects EXCLUDE his degree, whose alternative route requires professional experience he does not have, and whose content (sonic art, instrument design, musicology) points away from DJing and record production. The prior record's honest assessment also stands and I am reinforcing it: this is the weakest of the six FOR HIM. Three hard blockers stack. First, software engineering is not among the enumerated relevant subjects. Second, the only alternative route, RPEL, is written for applicants with 'extensive relevant professional experience' — a portfolio built over one year is not professional experience, and the four permitted work-sample formats (public performance extract, sound installation documentation, instrument-design demonstration, composition recording) do not naturally accommodate a set of electronic-music productions or a DJ mix. Third, £23,000 is £5,000 to £9,500 more than every other option here for content that is furthest from his goal. The Harrison bursaries are automatic on early application so there is zero cost to trying, but £3,000 off £23,000 does not change the economics. Treat this as a stretch application to make ONLY alongside a Chevening bid, and only if the portfolio year produces something that genuinely fits one of the four RPEL categories. If he wants one UK application at this tier, USW is the better use of the effort.

_rec.whatYouStudy: Composition at master level with the option to deepen electronic-music work; the EZMM strand continues the Academy's electronic music media art line (launched 2011) covering the history and compositional technique of electroacoustic and computer music, sound analysis, synthesis and transformation, MIDI/OSC, interactive and algorithmic music. Composition-related special courses are chosen freely according to the student's interests. Applicants who did NOT take electronic-music courses in their prior studies must complete a 2-semester 'Foundations of Electronic Music Composition' course during the first MA year.
_rec.entryRequirements: BA diploma. All applicants must submit a PRELIMINARY CREDIT RECOGNITION REQUEST to establish whether their BA diploma can be accepted for the MA, unless the BA was taken at the Liszt Academy — the request form plus the BA transcript/diploma supplement and English course descriptions go in with the application. _rec.portfolioSpec: Uploaded portfolio evaluated first: sheet music of THREE of the applicant's own compositions, with recordings if possible. For the EZMM specialisation the presented works must total NO MORE THAN 25–30 MINUTES and comprise (a) one recorded tape/fixed-media piece and (b) one work for instrument + electronics, OR an interactive live performance, OR an audiovisual work. Style exercises additionally required: one fugue in the style of J. S. Bach (EZMM candidates may realise the Bach-style task electroacoustically), one classical sonata or rondo movement, and one 20th-century etude in the style of a named composer. EZMM candidates also sit an electronic-music fundamentals test.

_rec.program: Corso accademico di secondo livello in Composizione audiovisiva e sound design (Biennio)
_rec.institution: Conservatorio di Musica "Giuseppe Verdi" di Como
_rec.institutionType: State conservatoire within the AFAM system, under the Ministero dell'Università e della Ricerca
_rec.publicPrivate: PUBLIC — CONFIRMED. A Conservatorio Statale di Musica in the AFAM system with a long-established electronic music department. Its being public is not in doubt; its being reachable is.
_rec.qualification: Diploma accademico di secondo livello — a real state second-cycle degree, EQF 7, equated to a Laurea Magistrale for public competitions and further study. CONFIRMED as a genuine second-cycle award: the programme exists and is a real master's-level qualification. It is simply closed to him.
_rec.accreditationStatus: State-accredited AFAM second-level academic course. Genuine EHEA second-cycle qualification. No accreditation concerns — this is not a case of an institution charging master-level money for a non-degree.
_rec.language: Italian — CONFIRMED on the official course page. No English-taught option.
_rec.languageRequirement: UNVERIFIED — no level published on the course page. Assume B2 Italian consistent with the sector. Academic: the entry qualification blocks him before language becomes relevant.
_rec.englishTest: None.
_rec.durationEcts: 2 years, 120 CFA — CONFIRMED.
_rec.focus: Audiovisual composition and sound design — music and sound for image at second level, framed as a specialisation building on competencies already acquired during first-level studies in Composition or Electronic Music. The framing is the point: this is designed as a continuation for people who already have a first-cycle music degree, not as an entry point for outsiders.
_rec.whatYouStudy: Year one: audiovisual communication theory, orchestration, audiovisual composition, music informatics, electives. Year two: advanced audiovisual composition, music applied to images, audio post-production technologies, integrated audiovisual composition. The presence of orchestration and the weight of composition modules confirm this is a composer's degree, taught to people who can already write music on paper.
_rec.entryRequirements: HARD BLOCKER — CONFIRMED, but the previous report's description needs CORRECTING as too narrow. The previous report stated entry is restricted to holders of a Composition diploma. In fact the official page accepts a wider set: Diploma in Composizione (previgente ordinamento), diploma accademico di primo livello in Composizione, diploma accademico di primo livello in MUSICA ELETTRONICA, and correlated first-level or previgente-ordinamento courses of the Conservatorio di Como. So Electronic Music graduates are admitted too — the previous report was wrong to exclude them. HOWEVER, the correction does not help HIM: unlike Rovigo and both Cuneo tracks, this course does NOT list a generic 'laurea triennale' or 'Laurea di I livello' among qualifying titles. Every accepted route requires a prior MUSIC qualification. His Software Engineering BSc is not a qualifying title. All candidates must additionally pass a selection examination.
_rec.auditionSpec: The hardest examination of the four, and HARDER than the previous report recorded. Verbatim framing: 'Per essere ammessi al biennio è necessario superare un esame di ammissione consistente in una Prova specifica di selezione relativa alla disciplina principale.' WRITTEN tests: 'Realizzazione di una esposizione, di un divertimento e di uno stretto di fuga a 4 voci' on a given subject — i.e. writing the exposition, divertimento and stretto of a FOUR-VOICE FUGUE; composition of a piano piece on a provided outline; orchestration of a piano piece chosen by the commission; and analysis of a significant twentieth-century score. ORAL: CORRECTION — the previous report said 'three original compositions' generically. The page is more specific and more demanding: 'almeno tre composizioni libere: una per piccola orchestra, una per gruppo da camera, una per voce e strumento' — at least three free compositions, one for small orchestra, one for chamber ensemble, one for voice and instrument — plus a discussion of musical competencies. Additionally, candidates arriving from 'un percorso non accademico (c.d. del Previgente ordinamento)' must pass a 'Verifica delle competenze musicali in ambito storico, musicologico e analitico'. Writing a four-voice fugue and orchestrating to commission are skills requiring years of formal harmony, counterpoint and orchestration training. This is categorically out of reach within any realistic timeframe.
_rec.portfolioSpec: Not a portfolio in the sense he means it. The three required works are notated scores for small orchestra, chamber ensemble, and voice and instrument — orchestral and chamber writing, not audio productions. A DAW-based electronic portfolio, however good, does not satisfy this requirement. This is the sharpest demonstration in this whole set of how differently Italian conservatoires interpret the phrase 'sound design'.

_rec.facilities: UNVERIFIED — not published on the course page. Como's electronic music department is well regarded. Moot given the entry blocker.
_rec.tuitionEU: UNVERIFIED — not published on the course page. Como will operate the standard Italian ISEE-banded contributo system. Not worth pursuing given he cannot enter.
_rec.tuitionNonEU: UNVERIFIED — not published. Expect the standard Italian pattern where an ISEE parificato unlocks the income bands and failure to file places the student in the highest band. Whether Como instead applies a flat non-EU rate is UNVERIFIED. Note also that Lombardy and Como's position on the Milan commuter belt make living costs materially higher than at Cuneo or Rovigo — so even setting aside the entry blocker, this was the weakest of the four on cost.
_rec.otherFees: UNVERIFIED. Expect tassa regionale per il diritto allo studio (Lombardy), marca da bollo and an admission application fee.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: Cannot be stated — no fee data published on the course page. Como living costs are moderate-to-high for Italy at roughly €800–1,100/month, the highest of the four locations.
_rec.scholarships: UNVERIFIED — none advertised on the course page. Lombardy regional right-to-study scholarships are open to non-EU students on the standard Italian pattern. MAECI as the national route. Moot.
_rec.intakes: Autumn — Italian academic year.
_rec.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED — governed by the annual bando di ammissione, typically spring. Universitaly pre-enrolment required separately for non-EU applicants.
_rec.deadline: UNVERIFIED.
_rec.visaEligible: Yes in principle — a state conservatoire second-level diploma supports an Italian student visa and permesso di soggiorno per studio. Irrelevant in practice, since he cannot be admitted.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: NO — CONFIRMED AND FINAL. Every qualifying entry title requires a prior music qualification (Composition or Electronic Music at first level, or the previgente-ordinamento equivalents); no generic three-year university degree route is published. And even for those who qualify, the entrance examination requires writing a four-voice fugue, composing a piano piece to a given outline, orchestrating to commission, analysing a twentieth-century score, and presenting three notated compositions for small orchestra, chamber ensemble and voice-plus-instrument. This is categorically closed to a candidate with no formal composition training. There is no angle, no exception route, and no amount of portfolio work in the next year that changes it.
_rec.recommendation: VALUE VERDICT: AVOID. RATING: C. — DO NOT APPLY. To be clear about why: this is not a scam and not a fake degree — it is a legitimate, accredited, state second-cycle qualification, and the AVOID verdict is about fit, not integrity. It is simply and completely closed to him. Two corrections to the previous record. First, its entry list was too narrow: the official page also admits holders of a first-level diploma in MUSICA ELETTRONICA, not only Composition graduates — so the course is somewhat more open than reported, just not open in any direction that includes him, because no generic laurea triennale route exists. Second, the audition is HARDER than reported: the three required compositions are specified as one for small orchestra, one for chamber ensemble and one for voice and instrument, i.e. notated ensemble scores, on top of the four-voice fugue, the piano composition, the orchestration and the twentieth-century score analysis. The value of keeping this record is that it marks the boundary of what is reachable. Italian state conservatoire second-level courses vary enormously in openness under similar-sounding titles: Rovigo's DCSL60 admits any three-year degree and assesses by portfolio and conversation; Como's course, in nearly the same subject area, demands a composition diploma and a fugue. Knowing Como sits at the closed end saves him an application, a fee and several weeks. If the audiovisual composition subject matter is what attracts him, Rovigo's DCSL60 Musica Applicata covers substantially the same ground — composition for music applied to images is its largest credit block — and is open to him on the published rules. Choose Rovigo over Como on every dimension that matters: entry, examination, cost of living, and probability of admission.

ALL PRINCIPAL FIGURES VERIFIED AGAINST THE IED BANDO DSU 2025/26 PDF AND THE NABA DSU 2025/26 GUIDE.

(1) NON-EU ELIGIBILITY — CONFIRMED VERBATIM. The IED bando lists as eligible applicants 'i cittadini italiani', 'i cittadini degli Stati membri dell'Unione Europea', and 'i cittadini di Stati non appartenenti all'Unione Europea (d.p.r. 31.8.1999, N.394 inter alia art. 44 bis, attuativo del d.lgs 25.7.1998, n.286 nonché d.p.r. 31.8.1999, n. 394, art. 46 comma 5)'. Non-EU students at a PRIVATE academy are explicitly in scope.

(2) THE 'FUORI SEDE' RULE — CONFIRMED VERBATIM, footnote 7 of the bando: 'L'Art. 13 comma 3 del D.P.C.M. 9/04/2001 stabilisce che gli studenti stranieri non appartenenti all'Unione Europea sono considerati comunque studenti fuori sede indipendentemente dalla sede della loro residenza in Italia ad eccezione del caso in cui il nucleo familiare dello studente risieda in Italia. Al fine dell'ammontare della borsa di studio l'alloggio deve essere a titolo oneroso.' Fuori sede is the top payment band, and he lands in it automatically provided he pays for accommodation.

(3) AMOUNTS (IED, 2025/26, inclusive of the €140 regional-tax reimbursement and the €818 meal allowance) — EXACT MATCH TO THE DRAFT: FUORI SEDE €8,134.00 / €7,073.00 / €5,776.00 for income bands 1/2/3; PENDOLARI €4,754.00 / €4,134.00 / €3,254.00; IN SEDE €3,383.00 / €2,950.00 / €2,114.00. Award can be increased up to +40% for students with disability over 66%. NABA quotes 'da un minimo di circa € 2.000 fino ad un massimo di circa € 8.000, comprensivo di un pasto giornaliero gratuito' — confirmed.

(4) INCOME TEST — CONFIRMED: ISEE Universitario not above €26,516.70 AND ISPE not above €57,645.03; both must be satisfied. Bands: 1ª €0.00–€13,258.35; 2ª €13,258.36–€17,677.80; 3ª €17,677.81–€26,516.70. Reference year for a first-time first-year student in 2025/26 is 31/12/2023 (i.e. income two calendar years back — plan documents accordingly).

(5) MERIT FOR A FIRST-YEAR SECOND-LEVEL STUDENT — CORRECTED. The draft said '38–40 credits'. The bando says 40: full confirmation of the benefit is conditional on obtaining a minimum of 40 CFA by 10.08.2026; the scholarship is REVOKED, with repayment of the first instalment, for first-year students who have still not reached 40 credits by 30.11.2026.

(6) NON-EU PAPERWORK — CONFIRMED AND IF ANYTHING HARDER THAN THE DRAFT SAID. Documents from employers are expressly NOT accepted; the income declaration must be issued by 'l'agenzia delle entrate ufficiale del governo del paese di residenza dello studente'; 'L'autocertificazione relativa a redditi e/o patrimoni esteri non può essere presentata' — self-certification of foreign income or assets is inadmissible, full stop. Everything must be 'tradotti in italiano da un traduttore riconosciuto e legalizzato dall'autorità locale competente nel Paese di residenza' (alternatively legalised by the Italian Prefettura). CRITICALLY: the bando prints the country lists, and TUNISIA APPEARS ON NEITHER — it is not in the legalisation-exempt list (Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Croatia, ... Spain, Switzerland, Turkey, Hungary) and not in the Apostille-only list (Andorra, Argentina, ... USA, South Africa, Ukraine, ...). Full consular legalisation therefore applies. Tunisia is ALSO NOT on the bando's 'Paesi particolarmente poveri' list (Afghanistan, Bangladesh, ... Senegal, Somalia, Sudan, ...), so he cannot use the simplified route of a certificate from the Italian diplomatic representation attesting the family is not high-income. INCOME FLOOR CONFIRMED: 'il reddito degli studenti stranieri appartenenti a paesi Extra-EU non potrà essere inferiore a € 7.002,97 annuali, corrispondente ai mezzi minimi di sostentamento ai fini della richiesta di visto per studio'. IED's CAAF convention is confirmed — the bando names a convention with CAAF CGIL Lombardia to help with the parificato.

(7) HOW MUCH MONEY IS ACTUALLY IN PLAY, AND THE COMPETITION — CONFIRMED AND SHARPENED. IED put €354,392.15 to competition for 2025/26 under D.G.R. n. XII/4704 of 14.07.2025, split across four ranking lists in proportion to the number of applicants: (1) first-year I livello, (2) 2nd/3rd year I livello, (3) 2nd year II livello, (4) FIRST YEAR II LIVELLO. NABA is far tighter: n. 1 borsa for first-year second-level students at Milano and n. 1 at Roma (plus 1 each for second-year second-level). So at NABA this is a single-winner competition. NEWLY FOUND AND STRONGLY IN HIS FAVOUR: the IED bando reserves a QUOTA by nationality for first-year students across all courses — '67% per gli interessati cittadini di Stati membri della UE; 33% per gli interessati cittadini di Stati non appartenenti all'UE'. A third of first-year awards are ring-fenced for non-EU students. This materially improves his odds and was not in the draft.

(8) INCOMPATIBILITY — CONFIRMED AND BROADER THAN THE DRAFT SAID: 'La Borsa di Studio non è cumulabile con analoghe forme di aiuto economico, ANCHE PRIVATE, comunque erogate da IED o da altri enti pubblici o privati, con le borse ... erogate dalle Università ovvero da altri istituti ai sensi del D.Lgs. 68/2012, con le Borse di Studio per stranieri erogate dal Ministero degli Affari Esteri, con posti gratuiti in collegi, residenze o convitti non gestiti dallo IED'. The student may OPT for one or the other. So a NABA international scholarship and the DSU borsa cannot be stacked — he must choose the larger.

(9) PAYMENT — CORRECTED AND WORSE FOR CASH FLOW THAN THE DRAFT SAID. For a first-year SECOND-LEVEL student at IED the first instalment (50% of the total) arrives by 15.03.2026 — i.e. roughly SIX MONTHS after fees are due. (First-year FIRST-level students are paid by 31.12.2025; the draft's 'roughly February' is not the second-level figure.) The second instalment follows only after the 40-credit check at 10.08.2026. Unclaimed sums lapse on 31.12.2026. Payment method confirmed: credit to a bank current account in the student's name or co-name, or to a rechargeable card carrying an IBAN (e.g. Postepay Evolution) in his name — so a European/SEPA account is genuinely required.
