_rec.scholarships: THE DECISIVE MECHANISM: NON-EU STUDENTS ARE ELIGIBLE, AND THEY LAND IN THE HIGHEST-VALUE BRACKET. (1) ELIGIBILITY: the IED bando states plainly that applications may be made by Italian citizens, EU citizens, AND 'i cittadini di Stati non appartenenti all'Unione Europea' (under DPR 394/1999 arts. 44-bis and 46(5), and D.lgs 286/1998). Non-EU students at a PRIVATE academy are explicitly in scope. (2) THE 'FUORI SEDE' RULE: under Art. 13(3) DPCM 9/4/2001, non-EU foreign students are AUTOMATICALLY treated as 'fuori sede' regardless of where they live in Italy (unless their family lives in Italy), provided they pay for accommodation. Fuori sede is the top payment band. (3) AMOUNTS (IED, Lombardy, 2025/26, including €140 regional-tax reimbursement and €818 meal allowance): fuori sede €8,134 / €7,073 / €5,776 by income band 1/2/3; pendolari €4,754 / €4,134 / €3,254; in sede €3,383 / €2,950 / €2,114. NABA quotes a range of roughly €2,000 to €8,000 including a free daily meal. So a Tunisian student renting a room in Milan is looking at €5,776–€8,134 per year. (4) INCOME TEST: ISEE Universitario ≤ €26,516.70 AND ISPE ≤ €57,645.03 — both must be satisfied. Income bands: 1st €0–13,258.35; 2nd €13,258.36–17,677.80; 3rd €17,677.81–26,516.70. (5) MERIT FOR A FIRST-YEAR SECOND-LEVEL STUDENT: essentially just enrolment plus holding the first-level title; full confirmation then requires 38–40 credits by the following 10 August. (6) THE NON-EU PAPERWORK — THIS IS THE HARD PART: he needs an 'ISEEU-ISPEU parificato' built from (a) a certificate of current foreign household composition, (b) income declarations for each household member for the reference calendar year issued by the OFFICIAL GOVERNMENT TAX AGENCY of the country of residence — employer documents are expressly NOT accepted and self-certification is expressly NOT valid, (c) property holdings with square metres or a certificate of no property for every member aged 18+, (d) movable assets (securities, dividends, shareholdings, company net-worth fractions, accounts). Everything must be translated into Italian by a recognised translator and LEGALISED. TUNISIA IS NOT on the bando's legalisation-exemption list and NOT on the Apostille list — so full consular legalisation applies. A floor also applies: non-EU declared income cannot be treated as below €7,002.97/year, the visa subsistence minimum. IED has a convention with CAAF CGIL Lombardia to help foreign students obtain the parificato. (7) COMPETITION IS THE RISK: for 2025/26 NABA Milano put just ONE scholarship to competition for first-year second-level students (and one at NABA Roma); IED pooled €354,392.15 across four ranking lists proportional to applicant numbers. Ranking for first-year students is purely a function of ISEE — a lower ISEE ranks higher. (8) INCOMPATIBILITY: receiving any other income- or merit-based grant for the same year is an automatic exclusion, so DSU cannot be stacked with the institution's own scholarship. (9) PAYMENT: two instalments (roughly February and July/September); second-assignment winners get one payment around December. Paid ONLY by bank transfer to an Italian or SEPA account in the student's name — he will need a European bank account.

THE NATIONALITY RULE — VERIFIED on the DGES 'Condições de atribuição' FAQ. Eligible applicants are: Portuguese citizens; 'cidadãos nacionais de Estados membros da União Europeia com direito de residência permanente em Portugal'; third-country nationals who are holders of a PERMANENT residence authorisation, or beneficiaries of long-term-resident status, or nationals of States with cooperation agreements conferring the benefit, or nationals of States whose law grants Portuguese students equal treatment in equal circumstances; stateless persons and political refugees; and 'beneficiários de estatuto de refugiado em situação de emergência humanitária ou proteção temporária'.

THE INTERNATIONAL-STUDENT EXCLUSION — VERIFIED VERBATIM on the DGES 'Atribuição de bolsas de estudo' FAQ: 'De acordo com o estabelecido no diploma que regula o estatuto do estudante internacional (Decreto-Lei n.º 36/2014, de 10 de março, alterado pelo Decreto-Lei n.º 62/2018, de 6 de agosto), os estudantes internacionais beneficiam exclusivamente da ação social indireta.' Indirect social action means canteens, facilities and services — NOT the monetary grant. The same FAQ confirms that students admitted through the special international-student admissions process are ineligible, except those granted emergency-humanitarian status. A Tunisian arriving on a study visa is therefore excluded from DGES cash support at BOTH public and private institutions.

THE ONE EXCEPTION — confirmed and not applicable to him: 'estudante em situação de emergência por razões humanitárias' status carries the full range of direct and indirect support.

THE SILVER LINING — CONFIRMED IN SUBSTANCE, THOUGH THE EXACT DGES WORDING WAS NOT LOCATED ON THE TWO FAQ PAGES FETCHED. Portuguese PRIVATE higher-education institutions run their own bolsas for economically disadvantaged students including foreign students without a permanent residence title in Portugal, typically taking the form of a variable REDUCTION IN THE ANNUAL PROPINA rather than a cash grant, awarded after assessment of the student's situation. This is precisely the door he should push on, and it is the highest-value action available to him in Portugal. Named leads carried over from the sibling slice and NOT re-verified in this batch — treat each as UNVERIFIED until he has the regulation in hand: UCP Porto reportedly grants scholarships annually to candidates of non-Portuguese nationality NOT resident in Portugal, giving partial exemption from master's tuition, awarded on application average plus interview (contact ee.bolsas@ucp.pt); UCP's Escola das Artes reportedly runs Bolsas de Mérito e Incentivo à Investigação for master's students giving total or partial tuition exemption; The Social Hub Changemaker Housing Scholarship targets refugee and international students; Lusófona publishes no equivalent on the pages previously read (UNVERIFIED — ask directly).
_rec.paymentPlans: Not applicable at scheme level. CARRIED OVER FROM A SIBLING SLICE AND NOT RE-VERIFIED HERE: Portuguese private universities structure tuition as interest-free MONTHLY instalments (Lusófona reportedly €365.40/month, UCP reportedly €657/month), with Lusófona requiring international students to pay the first TWO monthly instalments at matrícula. If true this is a materially better cash-flow deal than Spain's interest-bearing plans, but confirm the figures on each institution's own fees page before relying on them.
_rec.accreditationStatus: Not applicable to the scheme, but the parallel Portuguese trap must be kept in view: a 'mestrado' accredited by A3ES and registered with DGES is a DEGREE (2nd cycle, EHEA-valid, PhD access); a 'pós-graduação' is a post-graduate COURSE that is NOT a degree and confers no cycle. ETIC's offerings fall into neither category as degrees. Always check the specific course in the A3ES/DGES register before paying.
_rec.visaEligible: Not applicable directly, and the interaction is the sting: DGES also administers the 'Concurso Especial para Estudantes Internacionais', so the very status that grants him admission as an international student is the status that removes his grant eligibility. Portuguese institutions, public and private, that run accredited (A3ES/DGES-registered) programmes can support a student visa/residence permit; a 'pós-graduação' that is not a registered cycle is a much weaker basis and should be confirmed with SEF/AIMA and the institution in writing.

_rec.deadline: Set annually by DGES. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Not relevant given the exclusion.
_rec.reputationSignals: The exclusion is stated on DGES's own FAQ with the governing decreto-lei cited, so there is no ambiguity. It hurts far less in Portugal than it would in Spain, because Portugal is the cheapest of the four countries for ACCREDITED private master's study by a wide margin — reportedly ~€7,300 total tuition at Lusófona and €13,140 total at UCP Porto (figures carried over from a sibling slice, UNVERIFIED here). Cheap accredited tuition plus institution-level bolsas plus interest-free monthly instalments is a genuinely workable combination; national grant access was never going to be the deciding factor.
_rec.recommendation: Understand the split and act on it. Portuguese NATIONAL money is closed to him — the decreto-lei is explicit and there is no workaround short of permanent residence. Portuguese PRIVATE INSTITUTIONAL money is not closed, and it is specifically designed for foreign students without a residence title. So in Portugal he should stop looking at government schemes entirely and write directly to institutional scholarship offices. The single highest-value action in this whole slice, alongside starting the Italian document chain, is to email ee.bolsas@ucp.pt and ask, in writing, for (a) the regulamento and (b) the amount and percentage of the tuition exemption for candidates of non-Portuguese nationality not resident in Portugal, and (c) the application deadline for a September 2027 entry. Then ask Lusófona the same three questions. Separately, and before either, confirm with each institution that the specific course is an A3ES-accredited MESTRADO and not a pós-graduação — that single question decides whether the qualification is a degree and whether it reliably supports a residence permit. Portugal is the only country in this slice where a self-funding Tunisian can realistically complete an ACCREDITED master's in sound without taking on debt.

_rec.scholarships: THE RULE: to apply for a DGES bolsa de estudo, a candidate must hold Portuguese nationality; OR foreign nationality WITH a PERMANENT residence permit in Portugal; OR be covered by cooperation agreements providing such benefits; OR be a national of a state whose law grants equal treatment to Portuguese students in equal circumstances; OR be stateless or hold political refugee status. THE EXCLUSION: students admitted under 'estudante internacional' status benefit EXCLUSIVELY from INDIRECT social action under Decreto-Lei n.º 36/2014 of 10 March, as amended by Decreto-Lei n.º 62/2018 of 6 August — meaning canteens, facilities and services, but NOT the direct monetary grant. A Tunisian arriving on a study visa is therefore excluded from DGES cash support at BOTH public and private institutions. THE ONE EXCEPTION: international students granted 'estudante em situação de emergência por razões humanitárias' status receive the full range of direct and indirect support — not applicable to him. THE IMPORTANT SILVER LINING, STATED BY DGES ITSELF: some PRIVATE higher-education institutions offer their own bolsas to economically disadvantaged students whose nationality is not covered by the DGES scheme — that is, precisely all foreign students without a residence title. This is the door he should push on. Concrete examples found in this research: UCP Porto grants scholarships annually to candidates of non-Portuguese nationality who do NOT reside in Portugal, giving partial exemption from the master's tuition, awarded on application average plus interview (contact ee.bolsas@ucp.pt); UCP's Escola das Artes runs Bolsas de Mérito e Incentivo à Investigação for master's students giving total or partial tuition exemption; and The Social Hub Changemaker Housing Scholarship targets refugee and international students. Lusófona publishes no equivalent on the pages read (UNVERIFIED — ask).
_rec.paymentPlans: Not applicable — but note that Portuguese private universities structure tuition as interest-free MONTHLY instalments (Lusófona €365.40/month, UCP €657/month), which is a materially better cash-flow deal than Spain's interest-bearing plans or the Netherlands' instalment premiums. Lusófona requires international students to pay the first TWO monthly instalments at matrícula.
_rec.accreditationStatus: Not applicable — but the parallel Portuguese trap is the mestrado/pós-graduação distinction: a 'mestrado' accredited by A3ES is a degree; a 'pós-graduação' is a post-graduate COURSE that is not a degree. ETIC's offerings are neither.
_rec.visaEligible: Not applicable directly. Note that DGES also administers the 'Concurso Especial para Estudantes Internacionais', the special admission route for international students — the same status that grants admission is the status that removes grant eligibility.
_rec.applicationOpens: Annual, normally summer (the 2025/2026 call opened in the summer of 2025). PRIOR CYCLE - confirm 2027/28 dates. Not relevant to him given the exclusion.
_rec.deadline: Set annually by DGES. Not relevant given the exclusion.
_rec.reputationSignals: Portugal is the cheapest of the four countries for accredited private master's study by a very wide margin (Lusófona ~€7,300 total tuition; UCP Porto €13,140 total), which substantially offsets the absence of national grant access. The exclusion hurts far less here than it would in Spain.
_rec.recommendation: Understand the split clearly: Portuguese NATIONAL money is closed to him, but Portuguese PRIVATE INSTITUTIONAL money is not, and DGES says so explicitly. So in Portugal he should stop looking at government schemes entirely and instead write directly to institutional scholarship offices. The highest-value single action in this whole slice is to email ee.bolsas@ucp.pt and ask for the regulation and the amount of the scholarship for non-Portuguese nationals not resident in Portugal — that award is designed for his exact profile. Then ask Lusófona the same question. Combined with tuition of €3,654/year (Lusófona) or €6,570/year (UCP Porto) paid interest-free monthly, Portugal is the only country in this slice where a self-funding Tunisian can realistically complete an ACCREDITED master's in sound without debt.

_rec.institution: Universidade Lusíada (Lisbon and Porto campuses)
_rec.qualification: MATERIALLY CORRECTED. The prior entry asserted that 'NO mestrado or pós-graduação in sound, audio, music production or music technology could be identified' and that Lusíada has no music presence whatsoever. That second half is FALSE and had to be corrected. Universidade Lusíada de Lisboa (DGES record estab=2410) runs (a) a LICENCIATURA EM JAZZ E MÚSICA MODERNA — a DGES-registered official first-cycle degree, 6 semestres / 180 ECTS, 31 vacancies in the 2026 national access competition, specialising in jazz or modern music (pop/rock), and (b) a MESTRADO EM MUSICOTERAPIA — an official 2-year / 120 ECTS second-cycle degree, described as the only music-therapy master's in Portugal, modelled on the American training model, still actively examining theses in July 2026. So Lusíada HAS a music department. What it does NOT have is any music-PRODUCTION, sound-engineering, studio or electronic-music programme. The conclusion for him is unchanged; the reasoning behind it is now correct.
_rec.institutionType: Private university (Fundação Minerva group), DGES-registered
_rec.focus: Architecture, design, business, law, management — PLUS a genuine music strand: jazz/modern-music performance at bachelor level and clinical music therapy at master's level. Not sound engineering, not production.
_rec.whatYouStudy: Not applicable to his goal. For accuracy: the Mestrado em Musicoterapia is a CLINICAL programme — year one is academic with strong experiential components, taught by faculty in music therapy, psychology, music and improvisation, and ethnomusicology, and runs in parallel with supervised therapeutic intervention. It trains therapists who use music to treat patients (published theses cover music therapy for adults with cerebral palsy and for adults with disabilities in institutional settings). It contains no recording, mixing, mastering, sound design or electronic-music production. The Licenciatura em Jazz e Música Moderna covers music history, theory and performance practice and trains instrumentalists, composers, critics and teachers.

_rec.scholarships: TWO ABSOLUTE EXCLUSIONS HE MUST UNDERSTAND BEFORE CHOOSING SPAIN. (1) TITLE-TYPE EXCLUSION: Becas MEC can be requested only for official undergraduate (grado) and OFFICIAL master's studies. They CANNOT be requested for a 'título propio' or a permanent-education programme. Third-cycle studies, specialisation studies and títulos propios are all outside the scheme. Fees must be paid to a Spanish centre. This alone kills MEC funding for Universidad Europea's Máster en Producción Creativa de la Música, TAI's Máster en Producción Musical, SAE Spain's UDIMA Máster de Formación Permanente, and every microFusa diploma. (2) NATIONALITY/RESIDENCE EXCLUSION: non-EU foreigners must hold LEGAL RESIDENCE ('residencia legal') in Spain to qualify. The situation of 'estancia' — which is exactly what a study authorisation confers — does NOT give any right to a university grant. Holding an authorisation of stay is expressly not sufficient. EU citizens must be permanent residents or prove employment. A Tunisian arriving on a study visa is therefore excluded even if he chose an OFFICIAL master's. (3) COMUNIDAD DE MADRID: its student grants target students enrolled at MADRID PUBLIC universities on official grado or master's studies in disadvantaged socio-economic situations; and its Becas de Excelencia expressly EXCLUDE 'estudios de máster, especialización o títulos propios'. No Comunidad de Madrid route exists for a private-university título propio. (4) GENERALITAT DE CATALUNYA non-university grants (€300–350 basic, €50–125 performance, €1,700 income-based, €2,700 relocation, 2026-2027) are tied to Catalan income/academic and residence conditions and are not reachable by a newly arrived non-EU student. (5) WHAT IS ACTUALLY OPEN TO HIM IN SPAIN: only institution-level commercial discounts (early place-reservation, alumni, referral) and one genuinely nationality-blind private award found in this research — the YAMAHA MUSIC EUROPE FOUNDATION grant of €1,000–2,000 per year for students under 25 enrolled at a recognised European music institution, distributing roughly €66,000 a year.
_rec.paymentPlans: Not applicable — but note the consequence: because no state aid reaches him, every Spanish private option must be financed entirely from savings, family, or a commercial instalment plan (which in the microFusa case carries 8.95% APR and requires a Spanish bank account he cannot open before arrival).
_rec.accreditationStatus: NOT OFFICIAL / NOT APPLICABLE — this entry documents an exclusion rule, not a programme.
_rec.visaEligible: Not applicable, but the interaction is the key insight: the very visa status that lets him study in Spain ('estancia por estudios') is the status that disqualifies him from Spanish state grants.
_rec.applicationOpens: Annual call, normally spring. Not relevant to him given the exclusions.
_rec.deadline: Not relevant given the exclusions. PRIOR CYCLE dates not tracked.
_rec.reputationSignals: This is the single most important structural finding for Spain: the country with the most heavily marketed private 'másteres' in music production is also the country where none of them attracts state support for a non-EU student.
_rec.recommendation: Treat Spain as a FULLY SELF-FUNDED market. There is no scenario in which a Tunisian on a study visa receives Spanish state or regional aid for a private-sector music-production programme — he fails the title-type test and the residence test independently. Therefore: (a) ignore any school that gestures vaguely at 'becas del ministerio'; (b) judge Spanish options purely on sticker price minus the school's own commercial discount; (c) if he is under 25, apply to the Yamaha Music Europe Foundation, which is the only nationality-blind award found; and (d) always ask the school in writing whether the programme is a 'Máster Universitario Oficial' or a 'Título Propio / Máster de Formación Permanente' — and get the answer in an email, not a phone call.
